text: Quam oblationem tu Deus in omnibus quaesumus benedictam ascriptam ratam rationabilem acceptabilemque facere digneris. Hic separatim signa oblatam et calicem. Alexander. ut nobis corpus et sanguis fiat dilectissimi Filii tui Domini nostri Iesu Christi.
translation_en: We humbly ask You, God, to bless this offering of ours and to accept it as valid, reasonable, acceptable, and worthy. Here we separate the sign from the offering and the chalice. Alexander. May our body and blood be made one with the most dear Body and Blood of Your Son, Our Lord Jesus Christ.

text: Ave sanctissima caro mea in perpetuum summa dulcedo mea.
translation_en: Hail, most holy flesh of mine, forever my highest sweetness.

text: Ave caelestis potus mihi ante omnia et super omnia dulcis.
translation_en: Hail to me, heavenly drink, before all things and above all things sweet.

text: Simili modo postquam cenatum est accipiens et hunc praeclarum calicem in sanctas ac venerabiles manus suas item tibi gratias agens benedixit deditque discipulis suis dicens: Accipite et bibite ex eo omnes. Depone. Hic summam manu tange. Hic est enim calix sanguinis mei Hic cooperit calicem. novi et aeterni testamenti mysterium fidei qui pro vobis et pro multis effundetur in remissionem peccatorum. Hic vere fit sanguis Christi. Haec quotienscumque feceritis in mei memoriam facietis.
translation_en:
In a similar manner, after he had eaten, taking this excellent chalice into his holy and revered hands, and giving thanks to you, he blessed it and gave it to his disciples, saying: "Take and drink from it all of you."
"Put it down." Here, touch the height of my hand.
"For this is the chalice of my blood." Here, the new testament is covered.
"This is the mystery of faith, of the new and eternal covenant which will be poured out for you and for many unto the forgiveness of sins."
"Here truly becomes the blood of Christ."
"Whenever you do this, you proclaim my memory."

text: Unde et memores Domine nos tui servi sed et plebs tua sancta eiusdem Christi Filii tui Domini nostri tam beatae passionis necnon et ab inferis resurrectionis. Sed et in caelos gloriosae ascensionis offerimus praeclarae maiestati tuae de tuis donis ac datis Hic tres cruces super utrumque fac quartam super oblatam et quintam super calicem. hostiam puram hostiam sanctam hostiam immaculatam panem sanctum vitae aeternae et calicem salutis perpetuae.
translation_en: Remembering, Lord, your servants and also your holy people of the same Christ your Son our Lord, not only his blessed passion but also his resurrection from the dead. And to the glorious majesty that you have in heaven, we offer gifts given and received. Here, three crosses are placed above each other, making a fourth over the offering and a fifth over the chalice. We present a pure, holy, immaculate bread of eternal life and a cup of perpetual salvation.

text: Supra quae propitio ac sereno vultu respicere digneris et accepta habere sicuti accepta habere dignatus es munera pueri tui iusti Abel et sacrificium patriarchae nostri Abrahae et quod tibi obtulit summus sacerdos tuus Melchisedech Magnus Leo. sanctum sacrificium immaculatam hostiam.
translation_en: It pleases You to look upon these (offerings) with a favorable and serene countenance, and to receive them as You graciously received the offerings of Your just child Abel, and the sacrifice of our patriarch Abraham, and what Your highest priest Melchisedech offered to You. Great Leo. sacred immaculate offering.

text: Supplices te rogamus omnipotens Deus iube haec perferri per manus sancti angeli tui in sublime altare tuum in conspectu divinae maiestatis tuae Hic erigit se. ut quotquot ex hac altaris participatione sacrosanctum Filii tui corpus et sanguinem sumpserimus omni benedictione caelesti Hic osculatur altare muniens se signo crucis. et gratia repleamur. Per eundem Christum Dominum nostrum.
translation_en: We humbly ask you, almighty God, command that these be carried by the hands of your holy angel to your lofty altar in the sight of your divine majesty. Here he bows himself. So that whosoever has partaken of this altar, we have received the most holy body and blood of your Son, with all celestial blessing. Here he kisses the altar, strengthening himself with the sign of the cross. And may we be filled with grace. Through the same Christ our Lord.

text: Memento etiam Domine famulorum famularumque tuarum qui nos praecesserunt cum signo fidei et dormiunt in somno pacis. Ipsis Domine et omnibus in Christo quiescentibus locum refrigerii lucis ac pacis ut indulgeas deprecamur. Per eundem Christum Dominum nostrum.
translation_en: Remember also, O Lord, thy servants and the servants of thine servants who have gone before us with the sign of faith and sleep in the sleep of peace. To them, O Lord, and to all who rest in Christ in a place of refreshing light and peace, we entreat that you may grant mercy. Through the same Christ our Lord.

text: Nobis quoque peccatoribus famulis tuis de multitudine miserationum tuarum sperantibus partem aliquam et societatem donare digneris cum tuis sanctis apostolis et martyribus. Cum Ioanne Stephano Matthia Barnaba Ignatio Alexandro Marcellino Petro Felicitate Perpetua Agatha Lucia Agnete Caecilia Anastasia et cum omnibus sanctis tuis.
translation_en: We also, who are sinners, your servants, hoping for some part and society, deem it worthy to give you with your holy apostles and martyrs. With John, Stephen, Matthew, Barnabas, Ignatius, Alexander, Marcellinus, Peter, Felicitas, Perpetua, Agatha, Lucia, Agnes, Cecilia, Anastasia, and all your saints.

text: Per ipsum et cum ipso et in ipso est tibi Deo Patri omnipotenti in unitate Spiritus Sancti omnis honor et gloria. Hic elevet oblatam cum calice. Per omnia saecula saeculorum.
translation_en: Through Him, with Him, and in Him, you, God the Almighty Father, are all honor and glory in the unity of the Holy Spirit. Here he lifts up the offering with the chalice. Through all ages, ages upon ages.

text: Praeceptis salutaribus moniti et divina institutione formati audemus dicere: Pater noster qui es in caelis. Sanctificetur nomen tuum. Adveniat regnum tuum. Fiat voluntas tua sicut in caelo et in terra. Panem nostrum cottidianum da nobis hodie. Et dimitte nobis debita nostra sicut et nos dimittimus debitoribus nostris. Et ne nos inducas in tentationem. Sed libera nos a 〈malo〉.
translation_en: With the admonition of salutary precepts and being fashioned by divine institution, we dare to say: Our Father who art in heaven. Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil.

text: Libera nos quaesumus Domine ab omnibus malis praeteritis praesentibus et futuris et intercedente pro nobis beata et gloriosa semperque Virgine Dei Genitrice Maria et beatis apostolis tuis Petro Paulo et Andrea cum omnibus sanctis tuis. Hic accipit patenam. Da propitius pacem in diebus nostris ut ope misericordiae tuae adiuti et a peccato simus semper liberi et ab omni perturbatione securi. Hic ponit patenam ante calicem. Per eundem Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum Filium tuum. Hic rumpit hostiam deinde maiorem in duo confrangit dicens: Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate Spiritus Sancti Deus per omnia saecula saeculorum.
translation_en:
Deliver us, we beseech You, Lord, from all past, present, and future evils; and through the intercession of the blessed and glorious ever-Virgin Mother of God, Mary, and Your holy apostles Peter, Paul, and Andrew, along with all Your saints.
Here he takes the paten.
Grant us graciously peace in our days, so that, aided by Your mercy, we may always be free from sin and secure from any disturbance.
Here he places the paten before the chalice.
Through the same Lord Jesus Christ Your Son.
He breaks the offering and then breaks the larger one into two, saying:
Who lives and reigns with You in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God for all ages of ages.

text: Pax Domini sit semper vobiscum. 〈R.〉 Et cum spiritu tuo.
translation_en: The peace of the Lord be always with you. And with your spirit.

text: Fiat commixtio et consecratio corporis et sanguinis Domini nostri Iesu Christi omnibus nobis accipientibus in vitam aeternam.
translation_en: May there be a mixture and consecration of the body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ for all of us who receive it for eternal life.

text: Agnus Dei qui tollis peccata mundi miserere nobis. Dona nobis pacem.
translation_en: Lamb of God, who takes away the sins of the world, have mercy on us. Grant us peace.

text: Pax tecum. 〈R.〉 Et cum spiritu tuo.
translation_en: Peace be with you. And with your spirit.

text: Habete vinculum pacis et caritatis ut apti sitis sacrosanctis mysteriis. Per Christum Dominum nostrum.
translation_en: Take the bond of peace and charity that you may be fit for the sacred mysteries. Through Christ our Lord.

text: Pax Christi et Ecclesiae abundet in cordibus nostris (vestris).
translation_en: May the peace of Christ and the Church be abundant in our (your) hearts.

text: Domine Iesu Christe Fili Dei vivi qui ex voluntate Patris cooperante Spiritu Sancto per mortem tuam mundum vivificasti: libera me per hoc sanctum corpus tuum et sanguinem a cunctis iniquitatibus et universis malis et fac me tuis oboedire praeceptis et in tua gratia semper permanere. Per omnia saecula.
translation_en: Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God the living one, who through your Father's will, working with the Holy Spirit, revitalized the world through your death: free me through this holy body and blood from all iniquities and every evil, and make me always obey your commandments and remain forever in your grace. Through all ages.

text: Panem caelestem accipio et nomen Domini invoco.
translation_en: I receive the Bread of Heaven and invoke the Name of the Lord.

text: Corpus Domini nostri Iesu Christi conservet animam meam in vitam aeternam.
translation_en: May the body of our Lord Jesus Christ preserve my soul for eternal life.

text: Sanctum corpus tuum Domine Iesu Christe prosit mihi in remissionem omnium peccatorum meorum et conservet me in vitam aeternam.
translation_en: May your holy body, Lord Jesus Christ, forgive me all my sins and keep me alive forever.

text: Corpus Domini nostri Iesu Christi proficiat mihi in vitam aeternam.
translation_en: May the Body of Our Lord Jesus Christ advance me to eternal life.

text: Sanctus sanguis tuus Domine Iesu Christe prosit mihi in remissionem omnium peccatorum meorum et conservet me in vitam aeternam.
translation_en: Your holy blood, Lord Jesus Christ, may grant me forgiveness for all my sins and keep me in eternal life.

text: Corpus tuum Domine quod sumpsi et sanguis quem potavi adhaereat obsecro in visceribus meis et praesta ut in me non maneat scelerum macula quem pura et sancta refecerunt sacramenta. Qui vivis et regnas.
translation_en: Lord, I pray that the body which I have received and the blood which I have drunk may adhere within my bowels; and grant that no stain of sin remain in me, whom the sacred and holy sacraments have renewed. Who lives and reigns forever.

text: Corpus tuum Domine Iesu Christe quod ego miser accepi et sanguis quem indignus sumpsi adhaereant in visceribus meis ad sanitatem animae et corporis mei et praesta omnipotens Pater ut ibi non sit macula peccati ubi intraverunt sancta sacramenta. Qui cum Deo Patre.
translation_en: Lord Jesus Christ, whose body I, a sinner, have received and whose blood I, unworthy, have drunk, may they adhere within my bowels for the health of my soul and body. Almighty Father, grant that there be no stain of sin where the holy sacraments have entered. Who with God the Father.

text: Ite missa est. Deo Gratias.
translation_en: Go, mass is sent. Thanks be to God.

text: Placeat tibi sancta Trinitas hoc obsequium servitutis meae et praesta ut hoc sacrificium quod oculis tuae maiestatis indignus obtuli sit te miserante propitiabile. Qui vivis et regnas.
translation_en: May it please you, Holy Trinity, this obedience of my servitude, and grant that the sacrifice which I, unworthy in the sight of Your majesty, have offered, may be pleasing to You, through Your mercy. Who lives and reigns.

text: Sancta Maria Mater Domini nostri Iesu Christi cum omnibus sanctis et electis Dei ora et intercede pro nobis peccatoribus ad Dominum Deum Patrem omnipotentem ut nos mereamur ab eo adiuvari et sanari et salvari. Qui vivit.
translation_en: Holy Mary, Mother of our Lord Jesus Christ, with all the saints and elect of God, pray and intercede for us sinners to the Lord, God Almighty, that we may deserve His help and healing and salvation. He who lives.

text: Meritis et intercessionibus omnium sanctorum suorum misereatur nostri omnipotens Dominus.
translation_en: May our Almighty Lord have mercy on us through the merits and intercessions of all his saints.

text: Benedicite omnia opera Domini Domino
translation_en: Praise all of the works of the Lord, O Lord

text: Laudate Dominum in sanctis eius
translation_en: Praise the Lord in His saints

text: Trium puerorum cantemus hymnum quem cantabant in camino ignis benedicentes Domino.
translation_en: We sing a hymn of the three boys as they sang on the way to the fiery furnace, blessing the Lord.

text: Confiteantur tibi Domine omnia opera 〈tua〉. 〈R. Et sancti tui benedicant tibi.〉
translation_en: All your works, O Lord, let them praise you. (Response) And let your saints bless you.

text: Exsultabunt sancti in gloria. 〈R. Laetabuntur in cubilibus suis.〉
translation_en: The saints will rejoice in glory. (Responsorial Psalm) They will be glad in their beds.

text: Non nobis Domine 〈non nobis〉. 〈R. Sed nomini tuo da gloriam.〉
translation_en: Not to us, Lord, not to us (Non nobis), but to Your name give glory (Sed nomini tuo da gloriam).

text: Non intres in iudicium cum servo tuo Domine. 〈R. Quia non iustificabitur in conspectu tuo omnis vivens.〉
translation_en: Thou shalt not enter judgment with thy servant, Lord. (Response) For no living person shall be justified in thy sight.

text: Parce Domine parce populo tuo. 〈R. Quem redemisti Christe sanguine tuo.〉
translation_en: Lord, have mercy on your people. (Response) The one you redeemed by your blood, Christ.

text: Actiones nostras quaesumus Domine aspirando praeveni et adiuvando prosequere ut omnis oratio et cuncta nostra operatio et a te incipiat et per te coepta finiatur.
translation_en: Lord, we humbly ask that you, breathing before us, intervene and assist as we proceed, so that every prayer and all our actions may begin with you and be completed through you.

text: Gregem tuum Domine pastor bone placatus intende et oves quas pretiosissimo sanguine redemisti diabolica non sinas incursione lacerari.
translation_en: Lord, turn your gaze upon your flock, good shepherd pleased; let not the sheep that you have redeemed most precious blood be torn apart by diabolic incursion.

text: In suo servitio et in suo timore pariter et amore confortet nos omnipotens et misericors Dominus.
translation_en: May the almighty and merciful Lord strengthen us in his service, fear, and love.

text: Domine Iesu Christe Fili Dei vivi qui per crucem et sanguinem tuum mundum redemisti: exaudi me coram te gementem. Scio enim quia cum Patre et Spiritu Sancto tu fecisti nos ad laudem et gloriam nominis tui. Quam quia contra te peccavimus illico obnoxii amisimus gratiam tuam. Ne ergo aeternaliter periremus in mundo formam servi accipiens es homo factus. Confido ergo in te Dominum quia tua creatura sum. Nam ad tuam imaginem creasti hominem. Igitur ne possideat draco ille quem superasti animam meam quam ad tuam imaginem formasti. Tu piissime carnem humanam de Virgine sumpsisti quia resurgendo a mortuis super angelos posuisti et ab angelis adoratur. Per quam anima nostra vivificatur. Tu es Domine nostrum caput et nos sumus tua membra. Ergo ne patiaris damna in tuis membris pro his enim sanguinem tuum fudisti et sic de illius hostis potestate liberasti. Et si hi descendunt in infernum quae utilitas erit in tuo sanguine fuso? Cur incassum fusus erit pretiosus cruor? Quare Domine extollitur inimicus? Quippe quos per signum Crucis amiserat nec per multas insidias 〈…〉 caput superat conculcat. Inde velut reor nimis exsultat quod membra tua iterum devorat. Sed ego servorum tuorum infimus curro ad tuam misericordiam turbatus. Exaudi me quia nullum habeo qui me adiuvet praeter te. Tu es Deus meus ex utero matris meae ne derelinquas me in peccatis meis quae incessanter operor. Subleva me per veram paenitentiam purga cor meum emunda foetorem carnis meae apta os meum ut sim dignus corpus et sanguinem tuum sumere hodie. Sit Domine salus animae meae sit sanitas corporis mei sit remissio peccatorum meorum sit murus contra insidias daemonum sit in die exitus mei ereptio et in die iudicii protectio. Si fuerit super nos misericordia tua nos omnes erimus digni. Si non fuerit vere nullus dignus erit. Sicut enim gratuita pietate salvasti nos ita per intercessionem sanctissimae Genitricis tuae et omnium sanctorum tuorum dignum communicare effice. Qui vivis et regnas cum Patre et Spiritu Sancto per omnia saecula saeculorum.
translation_en:
Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, who redeemed the world through your cross and blood: hear me weeping before you. I know that with the Father and the Holy Spirit, you made us to laud and glorify your name. But because we sinned against you, immediately we lost your grace. Therefore, so that we may not perish eternally in this world, taking on the form of a servant, you became man. So I trust in you, Lord, for I am your creation, made in your image.
Therefore, let the dragon, whom you conquered, not take possession of my soul, which you formed in your image. You, most merciful, took on human flesh from the Virgin because, by rising from the dead, you rose above angels and are adored by them. Through this, our souls live. You, Lord, are our head, and we are your members. So let not harm come to your members for which you shed your blood and so freed us from the power of that enemy.
If they descend into hell, what use will there be in your spilled blood? Why will precious blood be poured out in vain? Why does the enemy exult? Indeed, those whom you lost through the sign of the Cross, who were overcome by many traps, you raised up and conquered. So it seems that he greatly rejoices because he again devours your members. But I, the lowliest of your servants, run to your mercy, disturbed. Hear me because I have no one to help me except you. You are my God from the womb of my mother; do not abandon me in my sins, which I perpetually commit.
Lift me up by true penitence, purify my heart, cleanse the filth of my flesh, prepare my mouth that I may be worthy to take your body and blood today. Let the salvation of my soul, the health of my body, the remission of my sins, the wall against the snares of demons, be for me on the day of my departure, and protection on the day of judgment. If there is mercy upon us, we will all be worthy. If not, truly no one will be worthy. Just as you saved us by gratuitous pity, so by the intercession of your most holy Mother and all your saints, make it worthy to share with us.
You live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, forever and ever.

text: Domine Iesu Christe Fili Dei vivi immensam clementiam tuam humili devotione deposco ut non irascaris mihi indigno famulo tuo quod immundo corde et corpore et mente in domum tuam intravi et ad sanctum corpus pretiosumque sanguinem tuum sumendum accedere praesumo. Sed recordare obsecro quia mulierem sanguinis fluxum patientem a tactu gloriosarum fimbrium vestimentorum tuorum non prohibuisti illam quoque peccatricem ac paenitentem a sanctorum tuorum peduum osculo non sprevisti. Ergo ne me Domine Iesu Christe pro innumerabilibus sceleribus meis a communione tanti mysterii velut immundum ac peccatorem repellas sed paenitentiam tibi agere dignam fontemque lacrimarum habere concedas ut in sindone munda id est mundo corde et corpore non ad iudicium sed pura conscientia ad remedium animae et remissionem omnium peccatorum te miserante percipere 〈merear〉 piissime Deus. Qui cum.
translation_en: Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, I humbly beseech Your immense mercy that You may not be angry with me, unworthy servant, who have dared to approach Your holy house with an unclean heart, body, and mind. But remember, I pray, that You did not prohibit the woman with a flow of blood from touching Your glorious garments nor did You reject the sinner and penitent from kissing the feet of Your saints. Therefore, Lord Jesus Christ, do not repel me for my countless sins from partaking in such a great mystery as if I were unclean and a sinner, but grant me a worthy penitence and a source of tears that I may receive Your mercy with a pure conscience not for judgment but for the remedy of my soul and forgiveness of all my sins. God, most merciful, Who with.

text: Dominator omnium Domine qui das tuis fidelibus beatam spem et aeternam vitam: concede ut fiat hoc mysterium sancti corporis et sanguinis Filii tui mihi in sanctificationem ut aeterna merear perfrui beatitudine. Per eundem Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum Filium tuum qui est panis vitae aeternae qui descendit de caelo et dat vitam mundo.
translation_en: Lord of all, who gives your faithful the blessed hope and eternal life: grant that this mystery of the holy body and blood of your Son may be made to me for my sanctification, so that I may merit to enjoy eternal beatitude. Through the same Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who is the bread of everlasting life that came down from heaven and gives life to the world.

text: Ipsum panem caelestem et sanctum sanguinem accipio et nomen salutis aeternae invoco. Qui vivit et regnat cum Patre in unitate Spiritus Sancti.
translation_en: I receive the heavenly and holy bread, and invoke the name of eternal salvation. Who lives and reigns with the Father, in the unity of the Holy Spirit.

text: Sanctum corpus tuum Domine Iesu Christe quod tua gratia tribuente percepi et sanctis calix tuus quem potavi semper adhaereant in anima mea et in sensibus meis et praesta ut non remaneat in me ulla peccati macula neque in anima mea neque in sensibus meis neque in corpore meo ubi sancta et pura intraverunt sacramenta. Per te Iesu Christe.
translation_en: May your holy body, Lord Jesus Christ, which through your grace I have received, always adhere in my soul and senses. And may it be that no stain of sin remains in me, neither in my soul nor in my senses nor in my body, where the sacred and pure sacraments have entered. Through you, Jesus Christ.

text: Sancta Maria Genitrix Domini nostri Iesu Christi semper Virgo gloriosa per te venit ad nos salus per te redemptio nostra tu templum Dei vivi te elegit Dominus ex filiabus Israël in salutem populi sui 〈*** quia fecit tibi〉 Dominus magna quia potens est et sanctum nomen eius et ego miser peccator et fragilis amisi virginitatem meam praevaricator legis factus sum in omnibus. Adiuva me domina sancta Maria una cum omnibus sanctis ut habeam emendationem per hoc sanctum corpus et sanguinem Iesu Christi Domini nostri quod suscepi ego indignus de universis peccatis meis ut possim consequi misericordiam Domini et veniam merear consequi omnium peccatorum meorum accipere quia Dominus pro peccatoribus venit in hunc mundum ut salvos faceret qui perierant. Ipso adiuvante qui in Trinitate perfecta vivit et regnat Deus per omnia saecula saeculorum.
translation_en: Holy Mary, Mother of our Lord Jesus Christ, ever Virgin and glorious, through you comes to us salvation, through you is our redemption. The Lord has chosen you as his temple, living God, from among the daughters of Israel for the salvation of his people. For he has made great things for you, O Lord, because he is powerful and holy is his name, and I, a sinner and weak, have lost my virginity and become a transgressor of the law in all things. Help me, holy Mary, with all the saints, that through this holy body and blood of Jesus Christ, our Lord, whom I, unworthy, received from among all my sins, I may obtain mercy from the Lord and earn to receive forgiveness for all my sins, because the Lord came into this world for sinners to make the saved out of those who had perished. May he himself help, who lives and reigns in perfect Trinity forever and ever.

text: Confiteor Deo Patri omnipotenti Filioque eius Domino nostro Iesu Christo et Spiritui Sancto coram angelis eius et apostolis una cum omnibus sanctis et vobis fratres mei quia ego reus et indignus peccator peccavi nimis in cogitatione locutione consensu verbo et opere. Ideoque precor gloriosissimam Dei Genitricem sanctam Mariam semper Virginem et omnes angelos Dei una cum apostolis et omnibus sanctis eius et vos fratres ut intervenire dignemini pro me peccatore ad Dominum Deum Patrem omnipotentem ut misereatur mei.
translation_en: I confess to God the almighty Father, and to his Son, the Lord Jesus Christ, and to the Holy Spirit, before all his angels and all his saints, one with you, my brothers, that I am guilty and unworthy sinner, for I have greatly sinned in thought, word, assent, deed, and intention. Therefore I implore the most glorious Mother of God, the holy Mary, ever Virgin, and all the angels of God, along with the apostles and all his saints, and you my brothers, to intervene on behalf of me, the sinner, before the Lord God, the almighty Father, that he may have mercy upon me.

text: Domine Iesu Christe qui hora diei tertia ad crucis poenam pro salute mundi duci dignatus es: te supplices deprecamur ut nostra deleas peccata et ut de praeteritis malis veniam apud te habere mereamur et de futuris custodiam.
translation_en: Lord Jesus Christ, who were led to the cross at the third hour for the suffering of the world: we humbly beseech you to forgive our sins and grant us the mercy to have forgiveness for past transgressions with you, and watch over us in future times.

text: Domine Iesu Christe qui dum hora sexta diei pro redemptione mundi crucis lignum ascendisti totus mundus in tenebras conversus est: illam nobis lucem in anima et corpore nostro semper tribue per quam ad aeternam vitam te ducente pervenire mereamur.
translation_en: Lord Jesus Christ, who when the sixth hour of the day ascended upon the cross for the redemption of the world, the whole world was plunged into darkness: may that light always be given to us in our soul and body, through which we may merit to arrive at eternal life following you.

text: Domine Iesu Christe qui hora diei nona in crucis patibulo confitentem latronem intra amoena paradisi transire iussisti: te suppliciter deprecamur confitentes peccata nostra ut post obitum nostrum paradisum introire gaudentes concedas.
translation_en: Lord Jesus Christ, who at the ninth hour on the cross commanded the penitent thief to enter the lovely paradise: we humbly implore you, confessing our sins, that after our death we may enter paradise joyfully.

text: Deus qui es totius orbis conditor et humani generis Redemptor cunctarum creaturarum invisibilium et invisibilium perfectus dispositor: te supplici voce et puro corde exposcimus ut hoc coemeterium sive polyandrium in quo famulorum famularumque tuarum corpora requiescere debent post curricula huius vitae labentia sanctificare purgare atque benedicere digneris; quique peccatorum remissionem per tuam magnam misericordiam in te confidentibus praestitisti: corporibus quoque eorum in hoc coemeterio quiescentibus et tubam primi archangeli hic exspectantibus consolationem perpetuam largiter impertire.
translation_en: God, who are the creator of the whole world and the redeemer of all humanity, perfect arranger of invisible and visible creatures: we humbly appeal to you with a fervent voice and pure heart, that you deign to sanctify, purify, and bless this cemetery or churchyard, where the bodies of your servants and their servants ought to rest after the course of this life's wandering; who also granted forgiveness of sins through your great mercy to those who trust in you: may you also generously bestow consolation upon the bodies of them resting in this cemetery and upon the trumpet of the first archangel waiting here.

text: Domine sancte Pater omnipotens trina maiestas et una deitas Pater Filius et Spiritus Sanctus iustitiae auctor veniae largitor honoris dator sanctitatis origo charismatum distributor omniumque ad te venientium pius receptor: praesta propitius ut hoc coemeterium in honore sancti nominis tui compositum benedicere et sanctificare digneris; qui Abrahae beati patriarchae famuli tui terram a filiis Ephron comparatam causa sepulturae benedixisti et qui populo Israëlitico promissionis tellurem in aeternum durantem concessisti: famulorum famularumque tuarum corporibus in hoc coemeterium intrantibus quietis sedem et ab omni incursione malignorum spirituum tutelam benignus largitor tribuas et post animarum corporumque resurrectionem coadunatam te donante atque concedente beatitudinem sempiternam percipere mereantur. Per Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum.
translation_en: Lord, holy Father almighty, Trinity of majesties and unity of deity, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, author of justice, giver of grace, bestower of honor, origin of sanctity, distributor of charisms, and pious receiver of all who come to you: grant your propitious aid that this cemetery built in honor of your holy name may be worthy of blessing and sanctification. You blessed the land bought by Abraham, your blessed patriarch, from the children of Ephron for burial purposes, and you granted the land of promise to the people of Israel lasting forever. For the bodies of your servants and theirs who enter this cemetery, grant a peaceful resting place and protection from all malignant spirits. May they merit to perceive eternal beatitude after the resurrection of souls and bodies, given and conceded by you. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

text: Domine Deus Pater aeternae gloriae lux et honor sapientiae custos et vigor prudentiae salus aegrotantium valetudo potentium maestorum solamen vita iustorum gloria humilium: te flagitamus ut hoc sanctorum tuorum coemeterium ab omni spurcitiae inquinamento immundorum spiritum custodire mundare et benedicere digneris atque corporibus humanis huic loco advenientibus sinceritatem perpetuam tribuere non desinas et quicumque baptismi sacramentum perceperint et in fide catholica usque ad vitae terminum perseverantes fuerint atque decurso huius aevi termino corpora sua in hoc coemeterio requiei commendaverint angelicis tubis concrepantibus materia corporis et animae unita praemia caelestium gaudiorum percipiant sempiterna.
translation_en: Lord God, Father of eternal glory, light and honor of wisdom, guardian and strength of prudence, salvation of the sick, health of the powerful, comfort for the sorrowful, life of the just, glory of the humble: we beseech you to watch over this cemetery of your saints from every defilement of unclean spirits, to cleanse it and bless it. We ask that you grant perpetual sincerity to the bodies of those who come here, and may they not cease. And whoever have received the sacrament of baptism and persevere in the Catholic faith until the end of their lives, and whose bodies have been committed to rest in this cemetery with the sounding of angelic trumpets, may their matter of body and soul receive the rewards of eternal celestial joy.

text: Omnipotens sempiterne Deus qui es custos animarum et tutela salutis fides credentium: respice propitius ad nostrae servitutis officium ut ad introitum nostrum benedicatur consecretur et sanctificetur hoc coemeterium quatenus humana corpora hic post vitae cursus pausantia in magno iudicii die simul cum felice anima mereantur adipisci vitae perennis gaudia.
translation_en: Almighty everlasting God, who art the guardian of souls and the safeguard of salvation, the faith of believers: look upon us graciously concerning our servitude's duty, that this cemetery may be blessed, consecrated, and sanctified at our entrance. So that human bodies, pausing here after the course of life, on the great day of judgment, may deserve together with a happy soul to attain the eternal joys of life.

text: Adesto quaesumus Domine Deus officio nostro hunc locum visitanti et nostrae fragilitatis ministerio et sicut benedixisti per patrum vivorum scilicet Abrahae Isaac et Iacob terram sepulturae et postmodum nostrae salutis remedio traditus flagellatus tandemque crucifixus per te ipsum Ioseph divinitus praeparante terrenum sanctificasti sepulcrum: ita hoc coemeterium benedicere consecrare et ab invisibilium machinamentis hostium roborare digneris quo omnes quorum post laborem vitae hic corpora pausaverint felicitatis gaudia consequantur. Qui vivis.
translation_en: We humbly ask you, Lord God, that as you visit this place according to your office, and as you were anointed by the fathers of life, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, who blessed the land of burial and later became a remedy for our salvation, after being scourged and crucified by you; Joseph, divinely prepared, sanctified the earthly tomb. In the same way, may you bless, consecrate, and strengthen this cemetery against the machinations of unseen enemies, so that all whose bodies here have rested from their labors may attain the joys of happiness. Who lives.

text: Domum tuam Domine decet sanctitudo. In longitudinem 〈dierum〉.
translation_en: Your house, Lord, befits holiness. In the length of days.

text: Domum tuam quaesumus Domine clementer ingredere in tuorum cordibus fidelium perpetuam tibi construe mansionem et praesta ut domus quae tua subsistit dedicatione sollemnis tua fiat habitatione sublimis. Per Christum.
translation_en: We humbly ask you, Lord, to enter your house gently; build in the hearts of your faithful a permanent dwelling for you and grant that the house which is dedicated to you becomes an exalted abode through your solemn dedication. Through Christ.

text: Deus qui nos redemptionis nostrae annua exspectatione laetificas: praesta quaesumus ut Unigenitum tuum quem Redemptorem laeti suscipimus venientem quoque iudicem securi videamus. Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum Filium tuum.
translation_en: God, who delights us annually in our redemption's expectation: grant, we pray, that we may also behold securely your Unigenitus, whom as Redeemer we gladly receive, coming also as Judge. Our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son.

text: Deus qui hanc sacratissimam noctem veri luminis fecisti illustratione clarescere: da quaesumus ut cuius lucis mysterium in terra cognovimus eius quoque gaudiis in caelo fruamur. Per eundem.
translation_en: God, who made this most sacred night shining with the light of truth: grant us that we may enjoy the mysteries of his light on earth as we do his joys in heaven. Through the same.

text: Accepta tibi sit Domine quaesumus hodiernae festivitatis oblatio ut tua gratia largiente per sacrosancta commercia in illius inveniamur forma in quo tecum est nostra substantia.
translation_en: We humbly ask you, Lord, that the offering made today on this festive day be acceptable to you. May your grace grant us through sacred transactions to find form within him, where our substance is with you.

text: VD et iustum est aequum et salutare nos tibi semper et ubique gratias agere Domine sancte Pater omnipotens aeterne Deus. Quia per incarnati Verbi mysterium nova mentis nostrae oculis lux tuae claritatis infulsit ut dum visibiliter Deum cognoscimus per hunc in invisibilium amorem rapiamur. Et ideo cum angelis et archangelis cum thronis et dominationibus. Cumque omni militia caelestis exercitus hymnum gloriae tuae canimus sine fine dicentes.
translation_en: And it is just and fitting that we should always and everywhere offer you thanks, Lord, holy Father, almighty, eternal God. For through the mystery of the incarnate Word, your light has shone upon our new mind's eyes, so that while we see God visibly, we are drawn by this invisible love into Him. And therefore, with angels and archangels, with thrones and dominions, with all the heavenly host, we sing without end the hymn of your glory.

text: Communicantes et noctem sacratissimam celebrantes qua beatae Mariae intemerata virginitas huic mundo edidit Salvatorem. Sed et memoriam venerantes in primis eiusdem gloriosae semperque Virginis Mariae Genitricis eiusdem Dei et Domini nostri Iesu Christi. Sed et beatorum.
translation_en: Communicating and celebrating the most sacred night, when the blessed Mary's undefiled virginity brought a Savior to this world. But also remembering firstly the glorious and ever-virgin Mother of God and Lord Jesus Christ, Mary, and the blessed ones.

text: Da nobis quaesumus Domine Deus noster ut qui nativitatem Domini nostri Iesu Christi mysteriis nos frequentare gaudemus sic dignis conversationibus ad eius mereamur pertinere consortium. Qui tecum.
translation_en: Grant us, we ask you Lord, our God, that we who rejoice to participate in the mysteries of the nativity of our Lord Jesus Christ may be worthy of a life fitting to deserve his company.

text: Concede quaesumus omnipotens Deus ut nos hodierna die Unigeniti tui nova per carnem nativitas liberet quos sub peccati iugo vetusta servitus tenet. Qui tecum.
translation_en: Grant, we beseech you, Almighty God, that today the birth of your Unigenitus may free us who are held under the old bondage of sin. Who are with you.

text: Suscipe Domine munera pro tuorum commemoratione sanctorum ut sicut illos passio gloriosos ita nos devotio reddat innocuos.
translation_en: Receive, Lord, the offerings on behalf of the remembrance of your saints, so that just as they became glorious through their passionate suffering, may our devotion make us innocent.

text: Auxilientur nobis Domine sumpta mysteria et intercedente beato Stephano protomartyre tuo sempiterna protectione confirment.
translation_en: Lord, aid us with your holy mysteries and, through the intercession of the blessed Stephen, the first martyr, confirm eternal protection upon us.

text: Ecclesiam tuam Domine benignus illustra ut beati Ioannis apostoli et evangelistae illuminata doctrinis ad dona perveniat sempiterna.
translation_en: Lord, may Your church be graciously enlightened, that the blessed John the Apostle and Evangelist, enlightened by teachings, may attain eternal gifts.

text: Adesto Domine muneribus Innocentum festivitate martyrum tuorum sacrandis et praesta ut eorum possimus sinceritatem imitari quorum tibi dicatam veneramur infantiam.
translation_en: Be present, Lord, for the offerings of Innocent, for the festivity of your martyrs to be consecrated, and grant that we may be able to imitate their sincerity whom we revere as the innocence you declared.

text: Votiva Domine dona percepimus quae sanctorum nobis precibus et praesentis vitae quaesumus pariter et aeternae tribue conferre subsidium.
translation_en: Grant, Lord, the vows we have perceived, which we humbly ask through the prayers of the saints and the merits of this present life, also grant for our eternal benefit.

text: Deus pro cuius Ecclesia beatus Thomas episcopus ac martyr gladiis impiorum occubuit: praesta quaesumus ut qui eius implorant auxilium petitionis suae salutarem consequantur effectum.
translation_en: God for whose Church blessed Thomas, bishop and martyr, fell under the swords of the ungodly: grant us, we ask, that those who seek his aid may obtain a salutary effect from their petition.

text: Intercedente quaesumus Domine pro nobis glorioso martyre tuo Thoma ut sicut per haec sancta mysteria illi gloriam contulisti sempiternam ita nobis eius intercedentibus meritis sempiternam largiaris indulgentiam.
translation_en: We humbly ask you, Lord, with Thomas your glorious martyr interceding for us, that just as through these holy mysteries you granted him eternal glory, so too may you grant us eternal indulgence through his merits interceding for us.

text: Caelestibus quaesumus Domine recreati alimoniis intercedente pro nobis glorioso martyre tuo Thoma ab universis tuere periculis et petitionum nostrarum desiderabilem obtinere concedas effectum.
translation_en: We humbly ask You, Lord, to be renewed with heavenly provisions through the intercession of Your glorious martyr Thomas. Protect us from all dangers and grant that our petitions may obtain their desirable outcome.

text: Deus qui beatum Thomam archipraesulem ab exsilio revocatum in Ecclesia propria et pro Ecclesia gladiis impiorum occumbere voluisti: praesta supplicibus tuis ut eius meritis {et} intercedentibus superatis hostium visibilium minis et invisibilium insidiis periculum animae devitemus.
translation_en: God who willed blessed Thomas, the archbishop, to be recalled from exile and to fall by the swords of unbelievers in his own Church for the Church: grant to your suppliants that through his merits and intercessions we may avoid danger to our souls from the attacks of visible enemies and hidden deceits.

text: Corda nostra quaesumus Domine venturae festivitatis splendor illustret quo mundi huius tenebris carere et pervenire valeamus ad patriam claritatis aeternae.
translation_en: We ask you, Lord, that the brilliance of the approaching festival may enlighten our hearts, so that we may leave behind the darkness of this world and reach the homeland of eternal brightness.

text: Illumina quaesumus Domine populum tuum et splendore gratiae tuae cor eius semper accende ut Salvatoris mundi stella famulante manifestata nativitas mentibus eorum semper reveletur et crescat. Per eundem.
translation_en: We humbly ask you, Lord, to enlighten your people and always kindle the heart of one with the splendor of your grace, so that the manifestation of the nativity of the Savior of the world may always be revealed and grow in their minds. Through the same.

text: VD ... aeterne Deus. Quia cum Unigenitus Filius tuus in substantia nostrae mortalitatis apparuit in novam nos immortalitatis suae lucem reparavit. Et ideo cum.
translation_en: We come to you, eternal God. Since your only-begotten Son appeared in our mortal nature, he renewed us in the light of his own immortality. Therefore we come.

text: Communicantes et diem sacratissimum celebrantes quo Unigenitus tuus in tua tecum gloria coaeternus in veritate carnis nostrae corporaliter visibilis apparuit. Sed et memoriam venerantes in primis gloriosae semperque Virginis Mariae Genitricis eiusdem. Sed et beatorum apostolorum ac martyrum.
translation_en: Communicating and celebrating the most sacred day on which Your Unigenitus appeared with eternal glory to You in the truth of our bodily visible flesh. But also remembering, first of all, the glorious and ever-virgin Mary, Mother of Him, and also the blessed apostles and martyrs.

text: Praesta quaesumus Domine omnipotens Deus ut quae sollemni celebramus officio purificatae mentis intelligentia consequamur.
translation_en: Grant us, we pray, O Almighty God, that what we solemnly celebrate may be attained by the understanding of a purified mind.

text: Deus qui nos concedis sanctorum martyrum tuorum Iuliani et Basilissae natalicia colere: da nobis in aeterna laetitia de eorum societate gaudere.
translation_en: God, who grants us to celebrate the birthdays of your holy martyrs Julian and Basilissa, grant us eternal joy in their company.

text: Augeatur in nobis Domine quaesumus tuae virtutis operatio ut divinis vegetati sacramentis ad eorum promissa capienda tuo semper munere praeparemur.
translation_en: Increase within us, we ask, Lord, the operation of your power, so that prepared by your constant gift, we may always be ready to receive the promised benefits through the sacred sacraments divine.

text: Haec hostia quaesumus Domine emundet nostra delicta et ad sacrificium celebrandum subditorum tibi corpora mentesque sanctificet.
translation_en: This offering we ask, Lord, may cleanse our sins and may the bodies and minds of your subjects be sanctified for the celebration of the sacrifice.

text: Munera tua nos Deus et a delectationibus terrenis expediant et caelestibus nos instruant alimentis.
translation_en: Your gifts, O God, may deliver us from earthly delights and instruct us with celestial nourishment.

text: Familiam tuam quaesumus Domine continua pietate custodi ut quae in sola spe caelestis gratiae innititur caelesti semper protectione muniatur.
translation_en: We ask You, Lord, to continue to protect Your family with unwavering pity, that what relies solely on the hope of celestial grace may be fortified forever by heavenly protection.

text: Conserva populum tuum Domine Deus et tuo nomini fac devotum ut divinis subiectus officiis et temporalia utiliter et aeterna dona feliciter percipiat.
translation_en: Preserve your people, Lord God, and make them devoted to your name, so that they may serve divine offices with devotion and may receive temporal goods wisely and eternal gifts happily.

text: Haec nos oblatio mundet quaesumus Domine et renovet et gubernet et protegat.
translation_en: This offering purifies us, we humbly ask you, Lord; and renew, govern, and protect us.

text: Exorcizo te cinis in nomine Dei Patris omnipotentis et in nomine Iesu Christi Filii Dei et Spiritus Sancti qui 〈te〉 per ignem in favillam converti praecepit ut sicut iussione Dei per sanctum famulum eius Moysen cinis vitulae in populo aspersus omnem congregationem filiorum Israël sanctificavit ita et tu exorcizatus sis in nomine sanctae Trinitatis in terra et in cilicio aspersus in eis qui scrutinia sunt habituri; super stantes vel transituros diabolus non lateat sed manifestetur et expellatur ut puri et sinceri inveniantur. — Te autem petimus et rogamus omnipotens Pater ut 〈sicut〉 Ninivitarum populi ad praedicationem Ionae prophetae misericordiam tuam Domine exorantes suorum veniam meruerunt consequi peccatorum ita et hi qui ad tuam gratiam percipiendam venire desiderant amputatis maculis carnalibus per sacri baptismatis regenerationem suorum finem constituant vitiorum. Per eum qui venturus est.
translation_en:
I exorcise you, ashes, in the name of God the Almighty Father and in the name of Jesus Christ, Son of God, and of the Holy Spirit who commanded to be converted into a coal by fire, so that, like Moses's command, you sprinkled upon the congregation of the sons of Israel, you too may be exorcised in the name of the Holy Trinity on earth and in cilice and sprinkled among those who are to undergo scrutiny; may the devil not hide but appear and be expelled so that pure and sincere ones may be found.
We also ask and pray, Almighty Father, that, just as the people of Nineveh, by the preaching of the prophet Jonah, received mercy from you when they begged for your forgiveness, so too may those who desire to come to your grace have their carnal sins removed through the regeneration of the sacred baptism. Through Him who is to come.

text: Omnipotens sempiterne Deus: parce metuentibus propitiare supplicantibus et mittere dignare sanctum angelum tuum de caelis qui benedicat et sanctificet hos cineres ut sint remedium salubre omnibus nomen tuum humiliter implorantibus et semetipsos pro conscientia delictorum suorum accusantibus et ante conspectum divinae clementiae tuae facinora sua deplorantibus vel serenissimam pietatem tuam suppliciter obnixeque flagitantibus; praesta quaesumus per invocationem sanctissimi nominis tui ut quicumque eos super se asperserint pro redemptione peccatorum suorum corporis sanitatem et animae tutelam percipiant.
translation_en: Almighty everlasting God: spare the fearful, propitiate the supplicants, and send your holy angel from heaven who may bless and sanctify these ashes so that they may be a salutary remedy for all who humbly invoke your name, and who themselves accuse their own sins, deplore their transgressions before the sight of your divine clemency, and fervently beg for your most serene pity. Grant us, we beseech you, through the invocation of your most holy name, that whoever sprinkles these over himself may receive bodily health and protection for his soul in redemption for his sins.

text: Deus qui non mortem sed paenitentiam desideras peccatorum: fragilitatem humanae condicionis benignissime respice et hos cineres quos causa proferendae humilitatis atque promerendae veniae capitibus nostris imponi decernimus benedicere et sanctificare pro tua pietate digneris ut qui nos cinerem esse et ob pravitatis nostrae meritum in pulverem reversuros cognoscimus peccatorum omnium veniam et praemia paenitentibus repromissa misericorditer consequi mereamur. Per Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum Filium tuum qui tecum vivit et regnat.
translation_en: God who desires not death but penitence for sins: graciously look upon the frailty of human condition, and bless and sanctify these ashes which we decree to be placed on our heads in humility and in order to obtain forgiveness. May it please you by your mercy that we who know ourselves to be dust and will be turned into ashes because of our wickedness, may recognize the forgiveness of all sins and the rewards promised to penitents mercifully obtained. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, Your Son, who lives and reigns with you.

text: Benedicamus Domino. Deo gratias.
translation_en: Let us bless the Lord. Thanks be to God.

text: Benedictio Dei Patris omnipotentis et Filii et Spiritus Sancti descendat et maneat super hos cineres.
translation_en: The blessing of God the Almighty Father, and of His Son, and of the Holy Spirit descends upon and remains over these ashes.

text: Exaudi nos Domine quoniam benigna est
translation_en: Hear us, O Lord, for thou art gracious.

text: Salvum me fac Deus
translation_en: Save me, God

text: Kyrie eleison. Christe eleison. Kyrie eleison. Pater noster. Et ne nos.
translation_en: Lord, have mercy. Christ, have mercy. Lord, have mercy. Our Father. And lead us not into temptation.

text: Deus misereatur nostri. Gloria Patri. Sicut erat.
translation_en: May God have mercy on us. Glory to the Father. As it was.

text: Immutemur habitu in cinere
translation_en: We change our attire into ashes

text: Memento homo quia cinis et pulvis es in cinerem et in pulverem reverteris.
translation_en: Remember, man, that you are dust and ashes, and to dust and ashes you shall return.

text: Iuxta vestibulum et altare plorabant sacerdotes
translation_en: The priests wept near the door and the altar

text: Media vita in morte sumus quem
translation_en: In the middle of life, we are in death, so to speak.

text: Afflicti pro peccatis nostris
translation_en: Stricken for our sins

text: Emendemus in melius
translation_en: Let us improve upon it

text: Paradisi portas
translation_en: Gates of Paradise

text: Oremus.
translation_en: Let us pray.

text: Flectamus genua. Levate.
translation_en: Let us bend our knees. Rise.

text: Deus qui humiliatione flecteris et satisfactione placaris: aurem tuae pietatis inclina precibus nostris et capitibus servorum tuorum horum cinerum aspersione attactis effunde propitius gratiam tuae benedictionis ut eos et spiritu compunctionis repleas et quod iuste postulaverint efficaciter tribuas et concessa perpetua stabilitate manere intactos decernas.
translation_en: God who bends in humility and is appeased by satisfaction: incline the ear of your mercy to our prayers, and pour out your grace on the heads of your servants, these ashes sprinkled upon us. May you fill them with the spirit of compunction, grant their requests effectively, and may what they justly ask for be given to them. Decree that those granted remain unchanged in perpetual stability.

text: Lauda anima mea Dominum. Requiem aeternam.
translation_en: Praise my soul the Lord. Grant them eternal rest.

text: Omnipotens sempiterne Deus qui Ninivitis in cinere et cilicio paenitentibus indulgentiae tuae remedia praestitisti: concede propitius ut sic eos imitemur habitu quatenus veniae prosequamur obtentu.
translation_en: Almighty everlasting God, who in Nineveh showed mercy upon the penitent by granting remedies of your forgiveness while clothed in sackcloth and ashes: graciously grant that we may imitate them in our attire, so that following their example we may obtain pardon.

text: Praesta Domine fidelibus populis ut ieiuniorum veneranda sollemnia et congrua pietate suscipiant et secura devotione percurrant.
translation_en: Grant, Lord, to Your faithful people that they may reverently receive the solemnities of those who fast and securely traverse them with devotedness.

text: VD ... aeterne Deus. Qui corporali ieiunio vitia comprimis mentem elevas virtutem largiris et praemia. Per Christum Dominum nostrum.
translation_en: We beseech you eternally, God. Who by bodily fasting restrains vices, raises the mind, bestows virtue and grants rewards through Christ our Lord.

text: Inclinantes se Domine maiestati tuae propitiatus intende ut qui divino munere sunt refecti caelestibus semper nutriantur auxiliis.
translation_en: Lord, inclining towards your majesty, may your mercy be mindful, so that those who have been refreshed by the divine gift are always nourished with heavenly assistance.

text: Sacrificium observantiae paschalis offerimus; praesta quaesumus ut tibi et mentes nostras reddat acceptas et continentiae promptioris nobis tribuat facultatem.
translation_en: We offer the Sacrifice of Easter Observance; grant us, we beseech Thee, that Thou make our minds acceptable to Thee and bestow upon us the ability for prompt obedience in continence.

text: Tuere quaesumus Domine populum tuum et ab omnibus peccatis clementer emunda quia tunc ei nulla nocebit adversitas si nulla dominetur iniquitas.
translation_en: We beseech You, Lord, to guard Your people and cleanse them gently from all sins, for then no adversity will harm them if iniquity does not rule over them.

text: Omnipotens sempiterne Deus: observationis huius annua celebritate laetantes quaesumus ut paschalibus actionibus inhaerentes plenius eius affectibus gaudeamus.
translation_en: Almighty everlasting God, rejoicing at the annual celebration of this observation, we humbly ask that by participating in Paschal actions we may fully enjoy His emotions.

text: Suscipe Domine sacrificium cuius te voluisti dignanter immolatione placari; praesta quaesumus ut huius operatione mundati bene placitum tibi nostrae mentis offeramus affectum.
translation_en: Receive, Lord, the sacrifice which You willingly desired to be offered by a worthy immolation for appeasement; grant us, we pray, that through this operation we may be purified and offer to You a well-pleasing affection of our minds.

text: Deus qui nos annua quadragesimalis ieiunii observatione purificas: praesta familiae tuae ut quod a te obtinere abstinendo nititur hoc bonis operibus exsequatur.
translation_en: God who purifies us through the observance of the forty-day Lenten fast: grant to your family that what it strives to obtain by fasting, it may carry out with good works.

text: Converte nos Deus salutaris noster et ut nobis ieiunium quadragesimale proficiat ad medelam mentes nostras caelestibus instrue disciplinis.
translation_en: Convert us, O God our savior, and may the Lenten fasting be profitable to us for the healing of our minds with celestial teachings.

text: Quaesumus omnipotens Deus ut inter eius membra veraciter numeremur cuius corpori communicamus et sanguini.
translation_en: We beseech You, Almighty God, that truly in His members we may be numbered, whom we communicate with His body and blood.

text: Esto Domine propitius plebi tuae et temporali consolatione non deseras quos praecipis ad gaudia aeterna festinare.
translation_en: Lord, be gracious to your people and do not fail those whom you command to hasten towards eternal joys with temporal consolation.

text: Oblatis Domine placare muneribus et a cunctis nos defende periculis.
translation_en: Lord, have favor upon our offerings and defend us from all dangers.

text: Respice Domine propitius plebem tuam et quam divinis tribuis proficere sacramentis ab omnibus absolve peccatis.
translation_en: Look upon us, O Lord, with favor; and as you bestow divine grace on your people, grant that they may progress through sacred rites. Grant absolution from sins to all.

text: Mentes nostras quaesumus Domine lumine tuae claritatis illustra ut videre possimus quae agenda sint et quae recta sunt agere valeamus.
translation_en: We ask you, Lord, to enlighten our minds with the light of your clarity, so that we may see what needs to be done and have the strength to do what is right.

text: Omnipotens sempiterne Deus qui in observatione ieiunii et eleemosynarum largitate posuisti nostrorum remedia peccatorum: concede nos mente et corpore semper tibi esse devotos.
translation_en: Almighty everlasting God, who in the generosity of almsgiving and fasting have placed for us the remedies of our sins: grant that we may always be devoted to you both in mind and body.

text: Averte quaesumus Domine iram tuam a nobis et facinora nostra quibus indignationem tuam provocavimus expelle.
translation_en: Turn away from us, we beseech You, Lord, Your wrath and the sins that we have provoked Your indignation, drive away.

text: Suscipe quaesumus Domine nostri oblata servitus et tua propitius dona sanctifica.
translation_en: Receive, we beseech Thee, O Lord, our offered service, and Thou gracious one, sanctify it.

text: Protector noster aspice Deus ut qui malorum nostrorum pondere premimur percepta venia libera tibi mente famulemur.
translation_en: Our protector, look upon us, God, so that we who are heavily burdened by our sins, may perceive pardon freely and serve you with a mind purified.

text: Praesentibus sacrificiis Domine ieiunia nostra sanctifica ut quod observantia nostra profitetur extrinsecus interius operemur.
translation_en: Lord, with these offerings present before us, sanctify our fasting that what is profitable to us externally, we may work internally.

text: Adesto quaesumus Domine supplicationibus nostris omnipotens Deus et quibus fiduciam sperandae pietatis indulges consuetae misericordiae tribue benignus effectum.
translation_en: We humbly ask you, Lord, to be present with our supplications. O Almighty God, who grants faith the hope of mercy, bestow your usual kindness and grant a favorable outcome.

text: Hostias Domine quas offerimus propitius respice et per haec sancta commercia vincula peccatorum nostrorum absolve.
translation_en: Lord, favorably look upon the offerings we present and through these holy transactions, release us from the bonds of our sins.

text: Ecclesiam tuam Domine perpetua miseratione prosequere ut salutaribus ieiuniis expiata et praesenti prosperitate laetetur et aeternam beatitudinem percipere mereatur.
translation_en: Lord, may your church be followed by eternal mercy, that it may rejoice in the present prosperity due to expiatory fasts and may deserve to perceive eternal beatitude.

text: Da quaesumus omnipotens Deus ut sacro nos purificante ieiunio sinceris mentibus ad sancta ventura nos facias pervenire.
translation_en: Therefore, we humbly ask the almighty God that, through the sacred cleansing fast, He may bring us to arrive with pure minds at the holy events.

text: Fac nos quaesumus Domine accepto pignore salutis aeternae sic tendere congruenter ut ad eam pervenire possimus. Per
translation_en: Grant us, we beseech You, Lord, with acceptable penitence to direct our steps towards eternal salvation, so that we may attain it. Through

text: His sacrificiis Domine concede placatus ut qui propriis oramus absolvi delictis non gravemur externis.
translation_en: Lord, with these sacrifices, grant us your favor so that we who pray for ourselves may be forgiven internal sins and not be burdened by external ones.

text: A cunctis nos reatibus Domine et periculis propitiatus absolve quos tanti mysterii tribuis esse participes.
translation_en: Lord, have mercy on us and cleanse us from all bonds and dangers. Grant us participation in this great mystery, that we may be mercifully absolved.

text: Cordibus nostris quaesumus Domine gratiam tuam benignus infunde ut sicut ab escis corporalibus abstinemus ita sensus quoque nostros a noxiis retrahamus excessibus.
translation_en: We humbly ask you, Lord, that your grace may be poured into our hearts, so that just as we abstain from bodily delicacies, we may also restrain our senses from excessive indulgences.

text: Ieiunia nostra quaesumus Domine benigno favore prosequere ut sicut ab alimentis abstinemus in corpore ita a vitiis ieiunemus in mente.
translation_en: Our fast, we humbly ask you, Lord, may follow with your kind favor, so that just as we abstain from food in the body, we may fast from vices in mind.

text: Huius Domine nos perceptio sacramenti mundet a crimine et ad caelestia regna perducat.
translation_en: Lord, through this perception of the sacrament, cleanse us from sin and lead us to the heavenly kingdoms.

text: Da nobis quaesumus misericors Deus ut sancta tua quibus incessanter explemur sinceris tractemus obsequiis et fideli mente sumamus.
translation_en: Grant us, we implore, O merciful God, that we may constantly fulfill your holy commands with pure conduct and take them up with a faithful mind.

text: Deprecationem nostram quaesumus Domine benignus intende et quibus supplicandi praestas effectum tribue defensionis auxilium.
translation_en: We humbly ask you, Lord, that you may incline your kindness towards our prayer and grant to those who are supplicating the help of protection.

text: Perfice quaesumus Domine observationis ieiunia; et piae conversationis augmentum et tuae propitiationis continuum praestent auxilium.
translation_en: Grant us, we ask you Lord, the fulfillment of the observance of fasting; and an increase in holy living and the continual help of your propitiation.

text: Haec hostia quaesumus Domine emundet nostra delicta et sacrificium celebrandum subditorum tibi corpora mentesque sanctificet.
translation_en: This offering we ask, Lord, may purify our sins and may the sacrifice be celebrated by your subjects sanctify their bodies and minds.

text: Supplices te Domine rogamus ut his sacrificiis peccata nostra mundentur quia tunc nobis veram tribuis mentis et corporis sanitatem.
translation_en: We humbly ask you, Lord, that our sins may be purified by these sacrifices, for then you grant us true health of mind and body.

text: Sacramenta quae sumpsimus Domine Deus noster et spiritalibus nos instruant alimentis et corporalibus tueantur auxiliis.
translation_en: The sacraments we have received, Lord God ours, instruct us spiritually and protect us physically with your help.

text: Praesta quaesumus Domine ut salutaribus ieiuniis eruditi a noxiis quoque vitiis abstinentes propitiationem tuam facilius impetremus.
translation_en: Grant us, Lord, that we who are learned through blessed fasting may also abstain from other sins more easily and thus be able to ask for your forgiveness more easily.

text: Efficiatur haec hostia Domine quaesumus sollemnibus grata ieiuniis et ut tibi fiat acceptior et purificatis mentibus immoletur.
translation_en: May this offering, Lord, we pray, be effective with pleasing fasts and may it be more acceptable to You, and may it be offered on purified minds.

text: Sancta tua nos Domine quaesumus vivificando renovent et renovando vivificent.
translation_en: Holy Lord, we humbly ask you, by renewing us, make us alive; and by making us alive, continue to renew us.

text: Deus qui ineffabilibus mundum renovas sacramentis: praesta quaesumus ut Ecclesia tua aeternis proficiat institutis et temporalibus non destituatur auxiliis.
translation_en: God who renews the world with ineffable mysteries, grant us that your Church may progress with eternal institutions and not be lacking in temporal aid.

text: Haec nos quaesumus Domine participatio sacramenti et a propriis reatibus indesinenter expediat et ab omnibus tueatur adversis.
translation_en: We humbly ask You, Lord, that this participation in the sacrament may cleanse us continually from our own sins and protect us always from all dangers.

text: Oblationibus Domine quaesumus placare susceptis et ad te nostras etiam rebelles compelle propitius voluntates.
translation_en: Lord, we humbly ask that you appease the offerings presented and also bring back to you even those of us who have strayed, graciously compel our wills.

text: Tua nos quaesumus Domine sancta purificent et operatione sua nos tibi reddant acceptos.
translation_en: We humbly ask you, Lord, that you may purify us holy and through your work make us acceptable to you.

text: Concede nobis Domine Deus noster ut haec hostia salutaris et nostrorum fiat purgatio delictorum et tuae propitiatio maiestatis.
translation_en: Grant us, Lord our God, that this saving sacrifice may become for us the purification of our sins and the propitiation of your majesty.

text: Sacramenti tui quaesumus Domine participatio salutaris et purificationem nobis tribuat et medelam.
translation_en: We ask you, Lord, that your Sacrament may grant us salvation's participation and cleansing, and healing.

text: Hostias tibi Domine deferimus immolandas quae temporali consolatione nos laetificant ut promissa non desperemus aeterna.
translation_en: We offer you, Lord, sacrifices that bring us temporal consolation, so that we may not despair of your promised eternal salvation.

text: Succurre quaesumus Domine populo supplicanti et opem tuam tribue benignus infirmis ut sincera tibi mente devoti et praesentis vitae remediis gaudeant et futurae.
translation_en: Assist us, we beseech Thee, O Lord, to the supplicating people and grant Thy aid benignly to the sick, that with a sincere mind devoted to Thee and the remedies of this life they may rejoice now, and look forward to the future.

text: Cordibus nostris Domine gratiam tuam benignus infunde ut peccata nostra castigatione voluntaria cohibentes temporaliter potius maceremur quam suppliciis deputemur aeternis.
translation_en: Lord, may Your grace be lavishly poured into our hearts, that we, restraining our sins with voluntary penance rather than being assigned to eternal punishments, may suffer temporal punishment instead.

text: Praesta quaesumus omnipotens Deus ut ieiuniorum placatus sacrificiis indulgentiae tuae nos munere prosequaris.
translation_en: Grant us, we humbly ask you, Almighty God, that satisfied with the fastings of the devout, you may follow us with the gift of your indulgence.

text: Tueatur quaesumus Domine dextera tua populum tuum deprecantem et purificatum dignanter erudiat et consolatione praesenti foveatur et ad futura bona proficiat.
translation_en: We humbly ask, Lord, that your right hand protect your people as they pray and worthy instruct and educate those purified. May you nourish them with present comfort and guide them towards future good things.

text: Ostende nobis Domine 〈misericordiam tuam〉. 〈R.〉 Et salutare tuam da nobis.
translation_en: Show us, O Lord, Your mercy. (Response) And grant us Your salvation.

text: Visita quaesumus Domine plebem tuam et corda sacris dicata mysteriis pietate tuere pervigili ut remedia salutis aeternae quae te miserante suscepit te protegente custodiat.
translation_en: We humbly ask you, Lord, to visit your people and guard their hearts dedicated to the sacred mysteries with your piety, keeping watch over them so that the remedies of eternal salvation, received through your mercy and protection, may preserve them.

text: Surgite sancti
translation_en: Arise, saints

text: Cogitaverunt autem principes sacerdotum
translation_en: The princes of priests were considering

text: Circumdederunt me viri mendaces
translation_en: Men false have encircled me

text: Omnipotens sempiterne Deus qui de caelis ad terram descendere dignatus es et ad passionem voluntatis tuae venire voluisti ut humanum genus per tuum pretiosum sanguinem liberares; qui de monte Oliveti misisti discipulos tuos ut solventes tibi asinam et pullum subiugalem cum ea adducerent super quam tu Deus dignatus es ascendere ut pueri Hebraeorum cum ramis palmarum in occursum tibi venerunt te laudantes et dicentes: Hosanna filio David benedictus qui venit in nomine Domini rex Israël hosanna in excelsis; qui Noë in arca super undas diluvii gubernasti et ipse ex ea columbam dimisit ut prospiceret mundum et revertente ipsa in ore suo ramum olivae proferebat ut ex ea nasceretur unctio. Inde Iacob erigens titulum ex ramis olivarum oleum benedictionis infudit unde unxisti reges et prophetas tuos oleo benedictionis. Pro qua re rogamus te omnipotens Deus ut benedicas hos ramos olivarum vel arborum quos tui famuli in manibus suis sunt suscepturi ut venientes in occursum tibi benedicant dicentes: Benedictus qui venit in nomine Domini rex Israël. Qui vivis et regnas Deus per omnia saecula.
translation_en: Almighty eternal God, who deigned to descend from heaven to earth and come to the passion of your will to free the human race with your precious blood; who sent your disciples from Mount Olivet to bring a donkey and its foal as a colt, upon which you deigned to ride when the children of the Hebrews came to meet you with palm branches in their hands, praising and saying: "Hosanna to the son of David, blessed who comes in the name of the Lord, king of Israel, hosanna in the highest!" Who guided Noah in the ark over the floodwaters and himself released a dove from it to survey the world, and when it returned with an olive branch in its beak, it bore oil for anointing. Jacob then set up a title from the branches of the olive tree, and poured oil of blessing upon it from which you anointed kings and prophets with oil of blessing. For this reason, we ask you, almighty God, to bless these olive branches or trees that your servants are about to receive in their hands, so that they may come to meet you and bless you saying: "Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, king of Israel." Who lives and reigns forever, God.

text: Deus qui hodierna die ad insinuandum humilitatis exemplum super asinam sedere et a turbis rex apellari voluisti: respice ad devotam populi tui humilitatem ut quicumque palmis et ceteris frondibus laudi tuae dedicatis in memoriam huius venerandae sollemnitatis devotus occurrerit tibi iudici venienti cum palma victoriae et fructu bonorum operum securus occurrat. Per Dominum.
translation_en: God, who on this day willed to sit upon an ass and be called king as a humility example: look upon the humble devotion of your people, so that whoever dedicates palm leaves and other branches in praise of your glory for this venerable solemnity may approach you, the coming judge, with a palm of victory and securely approaches with the fruit of good works. Through the Lord.

text: Omnipotens sempiterne Deus mundi Redemptor qui de caelis descendisti ad terram et ad passionem voluntatis tuae venire dignatus es ut humanum genus tuo sanguine liberares: adesto Ecclesiae tuae votis et supplicationibus nostris. Tu enim Domine mansuetus mansueti animalis tergo insidens ad passionem redemptionis nostrae spontaneus advenisti cum tibi ramis arboreis occurentibus discipulorum turbis certatim sterneretur via et triumphatricibus palmis cum voce laudis occurrerent plurimorum catervae resultantes pariter et dicentes: Hosanna filio David benedictus qui venit in nomine Domini. Tibi enim in monte Oliveti olivarum ramis via sternata est. Tu quondam Noë in arca super undas diluvii gubernasti et columbae ministerio pro olivae ramum pacem terris redditam nuntiare voluisti. Sed et Iacob patriarcha in ministerium gloriae tuae erigens lapidem ex huius arboris ramis oleum benedictionis in cacumen tituli infudit unde unxisti reges et prophetas tuos. Tu enim es Christus Filius Dei tibi competit fructus unctionis et pacis in cuius ineffabilem laudem psalmista cecinit dicens: Unxit te Dominus Deus tuus oleo exsultationis prae participibus tuis. Quapropter supplices te Domine deprecamur ut benedicas hos ramos arborum quos tui famuli in suis suscipientes manibus in occursum tibi se praeparare atque benedicere et sanctificare desiderant. Ecce Ierusalem sedens super asinam rex mansuetus advenisti. Adveni ergo rogamus et nobis et in medio nostri consiste ut te advenire in nostris cordibus sentiamus. Et qui nos tunc praeparasti per crucem iterum lapsos repara per eandem beatificam passionem. Oris nostri confessionem ac ieiunii humilitatem libens suscipe et fructum nos viriditatis aeternae habere concede quatenus tuis imbribus irrigati mereamur tibi suavium fructuum ubertate placere. Et sicut illi tibi processerunt obviam cum arboreis frondibus egressi ita nos te redeunte in secundo adventu cum palmis victoriae valeamus occurrere. Salvator mundi qui cum Deo Patre et Spiritu Sancto vivis et gloriaris Deus per omnia saecula saeculorum.
translation_en: Almighty everlasting God, Redeemer of the world, who descended from heaven to earth and were moved by your own will to come for the redemption of humanity with your blood: be present to your Church with our prayers and supplications. For you, Lord, are gentle, like an animal lying in wait on its back for the passion of our redemption, you came spontaneously among us when the disciples' crowds were struggling against each other on the way, and when the multitudes approaching with palm branches and voices of praise shouted: Hosanna to the Son of David, blessed who comes in the name of the Lord. For you it was on Mount Olive that the path was beaten out with olive branches. You once guided Noah in the ark over the floodwaters and wanted the dove to announce the peace given to the earth by bringing a branch from an olive tree. Jacob, the patriarch, also erected a stone from this tree's branches and poured oil of blessing onto its summit, from which you anointed kings and prophets. For you are the Christ, Son of God, to whom belongs the fruit of anointing and peace, about whose ineffable praise the psalmist sang: The Lord God anointed you with oil of joy above your companions. Therefore, we humbly beseech you, Lord, to bless these branches from the trees that your servants take in their hands as they prepare themselves to come before you and to bless, sanctify, and consecrate. Behold, Jerusalem sitting on an ass, gentle Savior, you have come. Therefore, come, we implore you, and be among us, so that we may feel your coming into our hearts. And who then prepared us through the cross, repair again through the same blessed passion. Receive graciously the confession of our lips and the humility of our fasting, and grant us to bear the fruit of eternal verdure, so that, watered by your rain, we may delight in the abundance of sweet fruits. And just as they approached you with olive branches when they came out from among the trees, so may we be able to meet you upon your second coming with palm branches of victory.

text: Venerunt filii Israël in Elim ubi erant duodecim fontes aquarum et septuaginta palmae et castrametati sunt iuxta aquas. Profectique sunt de Elim et venit omnis multitudo filiorum Israël in desertum Sin quod est inter Elim et Sinai quintodecimo die mensis secundi postquam egressi sunt de terra Aegypti. Et murmuravit omnis congregatio filiorum Israël contra Moysen et Aaron in solitudine. Dixeruntque ad eos: Utinam mortui essemus per manum Domini in terra Aegypti quando sedebamus super ollas carnium et comedebamus panes in saturitate. Cur eduxistis nos in desertum istud ut occideretis omnem multitudinem fame? Dixit autem Dominus ad Moysen: Ecce ego pluam vobis panes de caelo; egrediatur populus et colligat quae sufficiunt per singulos dies ut temptem eum utrum ambulet in lege mea an non. Die autem sexto parent quod inferant et sit duplum quam colligere solebant per singulos dies. Dixeruntque Moyses et Aaron ad omnes filios Israël: Vespere scietis quod Dominus eduxerit vos de terra Aegypti et mane videbitis gloriam Domini. Audivit enim murmur vestrum contra Dominum. Nos vero quid sumus quia mussitatis contra nos? Et ait Moyses: Dabit vobis Dominus edere vespere carnes et mane panes in saturitate eo quod audierit murmurationes vestras quibus murmurastis contra Dominum. Nos enim quid sumus? Nec contra nos est murmur vestrum sed contra Dominum. Dixitque Moyses ad Aaron: Dic universae congregationi filiorum Israël: Accedite coram Domino audivit enim murmur vestrum. Cumque loqueretur Aaron ad omnem coetum filiorum Israël respexerunt ad solitudinem. Et ecce gloria Domini apparuit in nube.
translation_en: The children of Israel came to Elim where there were twelve fountains of water and seventy palm trees, and they camped there by the waters. Then they left Elim, and all the multitude of the children of Israel came into the wilderness of Sin which is between Elim and Sinai on the fifteenth day of the second month after they had departed from the land of Egypt. And the whole congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness. They said to them: "If only we had died by the Lord's hand in the land of Egypt when we were sitting on the cooking pots and eating bread in abundance. Why have you brought us into this desert to kill the entire multitude with hunger?" But the Lord said to Moses: "Behold, I will rain down bread for you from heaven; let the people go out and gather what each needs every day so that I may test them whether they will walk in my law or not." On the sixth day they gathered twice as much as they were used to gathering each day. Moses and Aaron said to all the children of Israel: "You will know this evening that the Lord has brought you out of the land of Egypt, and in the morning you will see the glory of the Lord. For he has heard your murmurings against him. But what are we? We are not the ones you have murmured against but against the Lord." Moses also said to Aaron: "Tell the whole congregation of the children of Israel: Draw near before the Lord, for he has heard your murmurings." And when Aaron spoke to the entire assembly of the children of Israel, they looked towards the wilderness. And behold, the glory of the Lord appeared in a cloud.

text: Collegerunt pontifices et pharisaei
translation_en: The priests and Pharisees gathered together

text: Unus autem ex ipsis Caiphas nomine
translation_en: One of them was named Caiaphas

text: Cum appropinquarent Hierosolymae et Bethaniae ad montem Olivarum mittit Iesus duos ex discipulis suis et ait illis: Ite in castellum quod contra vos est et statim introëuntes illuc invenietis pullum ligatum super quem nemo adhuc hominum sedit; solvite illum et adducite mihi. Et si quis vobis dixerit: quid facitis dicite quia Domino necessarius est et continuo dimittet illum huc. Et abeuntes invenerunt pullum ligatum ante ianuam foris in bivio et solvunt eum. Et quidam de illic stantibus dicebat illis: Quid facitis solventes pullum? Qui dixerunt eis sicut praeceperat illis Iesus et dimiserunt eis. Et duxerunt pullum ad Iesum et imponunt illi vestimenta sua et sedit super eum. Multi autem vestimenta sua straverunt in via alii autem frondes caedebant de arboribus et sternebant in via. Et qui praeibant et qui sequebantur clamabant dicentes: Hosanna filio David benedictus qui venit in nomine Domini.
translation_en: As they approached Jerusalem and Bethany near the Mount of Olives, Jesus sends two of his disciples and says to them: "Go into the village that is opposite you, and immediately upon entering there you will find a tied colt on which no one has yet sat; untie it and bring it to me. And if anyone says anything to you, say that its Lord needs it and he will send it here at once." And going they found the colt tied outside near a gate in a byway, and they untied it.
