The Lord gave him a delightful home, namely paradise, but while he remained there, he postponed the commandments of the Lord after being deceived by the devil and eating the forbidden fruit from it. He alone sinned then; if only that danger had been suffered by him alone. But what does the Lord speak to us through Ezekiel the prophet? "Then, fathers, they ate the bitter vine, but now the teeth of the children are hardened." Brothers, you see every day with your own eyes how every day our teeth become hardened when we are daily made bitter by the bitterness of death. Paradise was our dwelling place, not this grave, but our first parents' transgression brought us this habitation. Then we were expelled from that delightful home and fell into the hands of the devil who held us under his power for a long time. But merciful God, remembering that we are dust, descended from heaven to earth and sought the lost man for many years and found him, whom he redeemed with His precious blood, and rejoicing brought him back whence he had first fallen. Therefore, brothers, this grave is not our dwelling place, but as blessed Paul says, it must be believed by us. "Our citizenship," he says, "is in heaven." Brothers, that celestial dwelling place is prepared for you very well. It is reserved for the just and all those who persevere in good works in this age. We are debtors, brothers, to bury one man and pray for him and implore mercy from God for him. Therefore, we ask you, brothers, that as you seek daily mercy and remission for yourselves from God, so you also seek and give today to this wretched man mercy from God and if anyone has sinned, let all of you, for the sake of God, grant him forgiveness.

text: Orate fratres hodie pro eo quatenus Dei misericordia hic eum requiescere faciat et finito mundi termino cum omnis homo resurget quando et Dominus Deus ad iudicium veniet tunc per intercessionem beatissimae Virginis Mariae et omnium sanctorum suorum iste miser homo non ad iudicium sed ad Dei gratiam resurgat. Kyrie eleyson.
translation_en: Pray, brothers today, for him, so that the mercy of God may cause him to rest here and when the end of the world comes, when every man will rise again; then through the intercession of the blessed Virgin Mary and all his saints, this merciful man shall not come to judgment but to the grace of God. Lord have mercy.

text: Omnipotens sempiterne Deus qui hodierna die beatum Adalbertum martyrem tuum atque pontificem merito passionis sanctis tuis coaequasti: tribue quaesumus ut meritis ipsius vitae exempla gradiamur et ad aeternam patriam pervenire mereamur. Per Dominum.
translation_en: Almighty everlasting God, who on this day equated your blessed martyr and bishop Adalbert with the merits of your holy sufferings: grant us that we may be worthy through his merits and examples, and may deserve to reach eternal life. Through the Lord.

text: Munus quod beati Adalberti martyris tui atque pontificis cuius hodie festa celebramus commemoratione tibi humiliter immolamus quaesumus summe Pater ut illius auxilio ad remedium animarum nostrarum proficiat atque 〈ad〉 paradisiacas portas perducat.
translation_en: The office we offer today in honor of the blessed martyr and bishop Adalbert, whom we celebrate on his feast day, we humbly present to you. We entreat the highest Father that through his aid, he may lead us towards a remedy for our souls and guide us to the paradisiacal gates.

text: Hoc sacramentum corporis et sanguinis tui quod sumpsimus Domine quaesumus ut nobis non sit reatus ad poenam sed intercedente beato Adalberto martyre tuo atque pontifice potius prosit ad veniam omnium delictorum nostrorum.
translation_en: This sacrament of your body and blood which we have received, Lord, we ask that it may not be a guilt bringing punishment for us, but rather through the intercession of Blessed Adalbert, your martyr and bishop, may bring forgiveness for all our sins.

text: Deus qui nos annua beati Floriani martyris tui gloriosa passionis sollemnitate laetificas: solita pietatis tuae largitate concede benignus ut cuius honoris famosum victoriae triumphum pio amore veneramur in terris societatis eius laetitiam adipisci te largiante mereamur in caelis.
translation_en: God, who delights us with the solemnity of Your glorious martyr Blessed Florian's anniversary: grant us, according to Your customary grace, to be worthy of his renowned victory and triumphant conquest through pious love on earth. May we merit Your gift of joy in his society in heaven, as You graciously bestow it.

text: Hanc in conspectu gloriae magnitudinis tuae oblationis hostiam quaesumus Domine Pater omnipotens beati Floriani martyris tui digna commendet oratio qui sancto caritatis tuae devictus amore propriam sui corporis hostiam in odorem suavitatis tibi obtulit vivam.
translation_en: We ask you, Lord Almighty Father, in the sight of your great glory, to commend this offering of the Host worthy of your blessed martyr Florian. For he, conquered by the love of your sanctity, offered up his own body as a living sacrifice with an agreeable aroma to you.

text: Custodi nos quaesumus Domine annua beati Floriani martyris tui festivitatis vota reddentes et a cunctis vinculis peccatorum nostrorum nexibus ipso intercedente benignus absolve.
translation_en: We humbly ask you, Lord, to protect us; granting the vows on the annual feast of your blessed martyr Florian, and through his intercession may you be merciful in absolving us from all bonds of our sins.

text: Omnipotens sempiterne Deus: preces populi tui clementer exaudi qui beatum Maiolum confessorem tuum virtutis gratia adornasti et eum in caelesti gloria suscepisti.
translation_en: Almighty everlasting God, graciously hear the prayers of your people. You adorned Blessed Mayol, your confessor, with grace of virtues and took him up into celestial glory.

text: Domine Deus Pater omnipotens: populi tui hostias et vota suscipias quaesumus et per beati Maioli merita nos transferas ad caelestis beatitudinis gaudia. Per Dominum.
translation_en: Lord God Almighty Father: we ask that you accept the offerings and vows of your people, and through the merits of Blessed Mayol, transfer us to the joys of celestial beatitude. Through the Lord.

text: Assit nobis quaesumus omnipotens Deus tuae propitiationis subsidium ut qui ineffabiliter hominem provocas sancti 〈etiam〉 confessoris tui Maxentii animam praeparasti ad gloriam ipso pro nobis apud te iugiter exorante eius vel omnium sanctorum tuorum consortio mereamur.
translation_en: Assist us, we humbly ask you, almighty God, the support of your propitiation, so that you who ineffably summoned mankind, prepared the soul of your confessor Maxentius for glory on our behalf, constantly interceding for us before you, may merit us through his or all your saints' fellowship.

text: Hostias tibi Domine et preces devotas humilitatis nostrae misericordiae tuae praecedat auxilium et interveniente beato Maxentio confessore tuo oblatio quam devotis mentibus immolamus remedium nobis animae conferat et salutem.
translation_en: Offerings to you, Lord, and our devoted prayers preceded by your mercy's aid; may the assistance come first. And with blessed Maxentius, your confessor, intervening, may the offering that we present with most devout minds bring remedy for our souls and salvation.

text: Ut nobis Domine tua sacrificia dent salutem beatus confessor tuus Maxentius quaesumus precator accedat.
translation_en: We ask, Lord, that Your sacrifices grant salvation to Your blessed confessor Maxentius. May the supplicant approach.

text: Deus qui venerabilem beati Martialis confessoris tui atque pontificis festivitatem sollemniter recurrentem hodierna die populo tuo dedicasti: quaesumus ut quem doctorem vitae habuimus in terris intercessorem semper habere mereamur in caelis.
translation_en: God who today on this day have solemnly dedicated the festival of your venerable martyr and bishop Saint Martin, we ask that we may always merit to have him as an intercessor in heaven whom we had as a teacher of life on earth.

text: Suscipe munera quaesumus Domine quae tibi de tua largitate confidimus ut haec sacrosancta mysteria intercedente beato Martiale confessore tuo atque pontifice et praesentis vitae nos conversatione sanctificent et ad gaudia sempiterna perducant.
translation_en: Receive the offerings we ask you, Lord, which we trust in your generosity, that these holy mysteries, through the intercession of Blessed Martial, your confessor and pope, may sanctify our life's conduct in this present world, and lead us to eternal joys.

text: Praesta quaesumus Domine ut sacramenti tui participatione vegetati sancti quoque Martialis confessoris tui atque pontificis precibus adiuvemur. Per
translation_en: Grant us, we beseech Thee, Lord, that by the participation in Thy sacrament, we may be aided with the prayers of Thy saint Martialis, bishop and confessor. Through

text: Praesta quaesumus omnipotens Deus ut beatorum martyrum tuorum Kiliani Colonati et Totnati sollemnia recensentes meritis ipsorum protegamur et precibus. Per Dominum.
translation_en: Grant us, we beseech you, almighty God, that as we celebrate the solemnities of your blessed martyrs Kolanus and Totnanus, we may be protected through their merits and prayers. Through the Lord.

text: Respice quaesumus Domine munera populi tui sanctorum martyrum tuorum festivitate votiva et testificatio veritatis nobis proficiat ad salutem.
translation_en: We humbly ask you, Lord, that the gifts of your holy people, the martyrs, offered in their feast day, may profit us for our salvation through their votive festival and testimony of truth.

text: Repleti Domine martyrum celebritate sanctorum quaesumus ut te semper in eorum commemoratione laudemus et tuam misericordiam iisdem semper deprecantibus consequamur.
translation_en: Filled with the assembly of martyrs and saints, we beseech you, Lord, that we may always praise you in their commemoration, and may always obtain your mercy as they continue to pray for us.

text: Sancti Alexii confessoris tui Domine supplicationibus tribue nos foveri ut cuius venerabilem sollemnitatem celebramus obsequio eius intercessionibus commendemur et meritis.
translation_en: Lord, through the prayers of Your Confessor Saint Alexis, grant us to be protected, so that we who celebrate his venerable feast day may be commended to him through his intercessions and receive mercy through his merits.

text: Hostias Domine quas tibi offerimus propitius suscipe et intercedente beato Alexio confessore tuo vincula peccatorum nostrorum absolve.
translation_en: Lord, we present to You the offerings; graciously receive them. And through the intercession of your blessed confessor, Alexander, remit the bonds of our sins.

text: Caelestibus refecti sacramentis et gaudiis supplices te Domine deprecamur ut cuius gloriamur triumphis protegamur auxiliis.
translation_en: Having been refreshed with heavenly sacraments and joys, we humbly entreat You, Lord, that we may be protected by Your aid during the trials in which we boast of Your glory.

text: Beatorum martyrum remunerator omnipotens Deus: praesta supplicibus tuis ut intercedente beato Christophoro martyre tuo de quacumque tribulatione invocaverint liberentur.
translation_en: O almighty God, rewarder of the blessed martyrs: grant your supplicants that they may be freed from any tribulation when they invoke your blessed martyr Christopher.

text: Oblata sacrificia Domine Deus benignus suscipere dignare ut cuius meritis hoc munus offertur placido vultu assume.
translation_en: Lord, gracious God, deign to receive these offerings of sacrifice. May it please You to accept them as they are offered on account of the merits of the one for whom this gift is given.

text: Descendat super nos famulos tuos benedictio tua Domine Deus et qui beati Christophori dilecti tui martyris intercessionibus se muniri exposcunt tua gratia ab omni malo defende gratiaeque tuae dignos effice.
translation_en: May your blessing, Lord God, descend upon us, your servants; and may we be protected from all evil by the grace of your intercession through the merits of your beloved martyr Saint Christopher. Make us worthy of your grace.

text: Deus per quem fides ignem non sentit et infidelitas sine igne exuritur qui beato Christophoro martyre tuo flamma tui Spiritus succenso superare tribuisti suorum incendia tormentorum: concede propitius per eius intercessionem ut nos famulos tuos non exurat flamma vitiorum sed dilectionis tuae amor ingenitus nostrorum excoquat robiginem peccatorum.
translation_en: God through whom faith does not feel fire and unbelief is consumed without fire, you have granted that the flame of your Spirit kindled over your blessed Christopher the martyr to surpass his tormentors' fires: grant graciously through his intercession that our servants may not be consumed by the fire of vices but may the original love of your affection burn away the rust of sins.

text: Sit nobis Domine intercedente beato Christophoro martyre tuo reparatio mentis et corporis quod de tui sancti 〈altaris〉 benedictione percepimus ut vitia nostra haec medicina expurget nosque a desiderio inflammet atque a totius pravitatis incursibus muniat sanctorumque tuorum faciat esse consortes qua infirmitatis nostrae venisti sanare languores.
translation_en: Grant us, Lord, through the intercession of your martyr Christopher, repair for both our mind and body, which we have received from your holy altar's blessing. May this medicine cleanse our vices, inflame us with desire, and protect us from all attacks of wickedness. May it make the saints your own be our companions in healing the weaknesses that you came to cure.

text: Sanctorum martyrum nos Domine Nazarii et Celsi atque Pantaleonis confessio beata communiat et fragilitatis nostrae subsidium dignanter exoret.
translation_en: Lord, may the blessed confession of the holy martyrs Nazarius, Celsus, and Pantaleon intercede for us and provide worthy support to our weakness.

text: Concede nobis omnipotens Deus ut his muneribus quae pro sanctorum martyrum Nazarii et Celsi atque Pantaleonis honore deferimus et te placemus exhibitis et nos vivificemur acceptis.
translation_en: Grant us, almighty God, that we may offer these gifts in honor of the holy martyrs Nazarius, Celsus and Pantaleon, and that we may please you with them and be revitalized by your acceptance.

text: Da quaesumus omnipotens Deus ut mysteriorum virtute sanctorum Nazarii et Celsi atque Pantaleonis vita nostra firmetur.
translation_en: Grant, we humbly ask you, Almighty God, that through the power of the mysteries, our life may be strengthened by the lives of the Saints Nazarius and Celsus and Pantaleon.

text: Deus qui hodiernam diem sacratissimam nobis beati Germani confessoris tui atque pontificis sollemnitate tribuisti: adesto propitius Ecclesiae precibus ut cuius gloriamur in meritis muniamur suffragiis.
translation_en: God who today have given us the most sacred day of blessed Germanus, your confessor and bishop: be present graciously to the prayers of the Church, that we who boast in his glory may be strengthened by his intercessions.

text: Sacrificium tibi Domine laudis offerimus pro celebritate sancti Germani pontificis; propitiationem tuam quam nostris operibus non meremur pii suffragatoris intercessionibus assequamur.
translation_en: We present to You, Lord, a sacrifice of praise, for the glory of Saint Germanus, the bishop; may we obtain Your mercy, which we do not deserve through our works, by the intercessions of the devout advocate.

text: Sumptis muneribus tuis quaesumus omnipotens Deus intercedente beato Germano confessore tuo atque pontifice nobis misericordiam tuam clementer impende et a cunctis calamitatibus nos propitius respirare concede.
translation_en: Through your gifts we humbly ask, O almighty God, with the intercession of blessed Germanus, your confessor and bishop, that you graciously bestow your mercy upon us and kindly allow us to breathe easily after all troubles.

text: Deus qui beatam ancillam tuam Radegundam in fragili sexu constitutam sanctificatione misericordiae tuae assumpsisti hodierno quondam die felici consummatione: per ipsius merita suscipe propitius preces nostras et praesta ut sicut tecum est illa meritis ita a nobis non recedat exemplis.
translation_en: God, who on this once happy day took your blessed handmaid Radegund into the sanctification of your mercy when she was constituted in fragile flesh; through her merits, receive our prayers graciously and grant that just as she remained with you through her merits, so may her examples not depart from us.

text: Deus qui es sanctorum tuorum omnium inseparabilis fortitudo qui inter mundanae conversationis adversa feminarum nostrarum maxime exemplis consolaris et inter praecipua exempla institutione vel constantiae beatae Radegundae nos consummatione gloriosa quam hodie celebramus accendis: excita Domine in Ecclesia tua illum Spiritum cui ista servivit ut studeamus diligere quod amavit et opere exercere quod ipsa in femineo fragili corpore te auxiliante exercuit.
translation_en: God who art the unseparable strength of all your saints, who console our women especially through adversities of worldly conversation with notable examples, and among the foremost examples, that of blessed Radegunda whom we celebrate today in her glorious consummation, stir up in your Church that Spirit which she served. May we strive to love what she loved and work what she performed in her fragile female body, aided by you.

text: Divinis sacramentis recreati quaesumus Domine Deus noster ut qui nostrae iustitiae fiduciam non habemus in his Radegundae cuius festivitatem celebramus meritis adiuvemur ut ea quae ex tua mensa percepimus intemerata nobis te auxiliante servemus.
translation_en: Through divine sacraments, we are re-created, Lord our God, we humbly ask that you who do not have faith in our justice, help us on the merits of Radegundae whose feast day we celebrate. May we, aided by you, serve unblemished what we receive from your table.

text: Omnipotens sempiterne Deus qui terrenis corporibus Verbi tui Veritatis Filii unigeniti per venerabilem ac gloriosam semperque Virginem Mariam ineffabile mysterium coniungere voluisti: petimus immensam clementiam tuam ut quod in eius veneratione deposcimus te propitiante consequi mereamur.
translation_en: Almighty everlasting God, who willed to unite the Word of your only-begotten Son with the body of the earthly virgin Mary through the ineffable mystery: we ask for your immense mercy that we may deserve to obtain what we ask of you in her veneration, as you are graciously disposed.

text: Deus qui beatum Arnulfum confessorem tuum atque pontificem doctorem praecipuum catholicaeque fidei praedicatorem eligere dignatus es: praesta quaesumus ut ipso intercedente peccatorum nostrorum exui malis et tibi Domino Deo sinceris mereamur mentibus deservire.
translation_en: God, who deemed fit to choose the blessed Arnulf, your confessor, bishop, and eminent teacher of Catholic faith, a proclaimer of the Gospel, grant us, we beseech you, that through his intercession we may be freed from the evils of our sins and may merit to serve you, Lord God, with sincere minds.

text: Omnipotens sempiterne Deus qui beatum Arnulfum confessorem tuum pontificatus officio et fidei munere sublimasti: tribue supplicibus tuis ut quicquid peccati contagione contractum est in nobis ipso pro nobis summo antistite tuo intercedente regatur.
translation_en: Almighty eternal God, who exalted your servant Blessed Arnulf in the office of pontificate and the ministry of faith: grant to your supplicants that whatever has been contracted by contagion of sin within us may be ruled by our highest bishop interceding for us.

text: Repleti sumus Domine muneribus tuis quae de festivitate beati Arnulfi confessoris tui atque pontificis percepimus; tribue quaesumus ut eodem intercedente et eorum mundemur effectu et muniamur auxilio.
translation_en: We have been filled, Lord, with your gifts which we received during the feast of your confessor and bishop, Blessed Arnulf; grant us that through his intercession we may be cleansed by the same effect and strengthened by his aid.

text: Omnipotens sempiterne Deus: da nobis quaesumus sancti martyris tui Genesii precibus adiuvari et praesta ut cuius festa recolimus eius auxilium capiamus.
translation_en: Almighty everlasting God: grant us, we beseech you, through the prayers of your holy martyr Genesius, to be helped and may we obtain his aid, for whose feast day we remember him.

text: Hostias tibi Domine pro sancti martyris tui Genesii commemoratione deferimus suppliciter exorantes; praesta quaesumus ut indulgentiam nobis pariter conferant et salutem.
translation_en: We offer to You, Lord, hosts in remembrance of Your holy martyr Genesius, humbly entreating; grant us we beseech You that they may also grant us forgiveness and salvation.

text: Caelestibus refecti sacramentis et gaudiis supplices te rogamus omnipotens Deus ut sancti martyris tui Genesii cuius gloriamur triumphis protegamur auxiliis.
translation_en: We, who have been refreshed with the sacraments and joys in heaven, humbly ask you, Almighty God, to protect us under the shield of your saint martyr Genesius, whose triumphs we glory in.

text: Salutarem nobis edidit hodierna dies beati Cypriani sacerdotis et martyris in tua Domine virtute laetitiam; praesta quaesumus ut conversationis eius insignia praedicando et intercessione tibi placita iugiter gloriemur.
translation_en: Today's day has brought forth for us the greeting of blessed Cyprian, priest and martyr, in Your divine power, Lord. We humbly ask that You grant us to continually glorify You through the signs of his life and intercession.

text: Deus creator et conservator omnium gentium: misericordiam tuam humiliter postulamus ut hunc diem beatae martyris tuae Iustinae virginis congruis actionibus celebrantes per eius intercessionibus et meritis sempiterna quoque exsultatione laetemur.
translation_en: We humbly beseech you, Creator and Preserver of all nations: grant us your mercy on this day of your blessed martyr, Justin's virgin, that we may rejoice eternally in her intercessions and merits through suitable actions.

text: Sacrificium nostrum Domine quaesumus ipsum tibi sit acceptione placabile cui praesenti †nos mysterio dominicae agimus† de cuius est germine procreata beati Cypriani martyris mox praeclara subiungitur.
translation_en: Our sacrifice, Lord, we humbly ask that it may be acceptable to you, which we offer presently in the mystery of the Dominican Mass. Soon after this germination appears the glorious addition of the blessed martyr Cyprian.

text: Domine Deus omnipotens qui es individua Trinitas et una maiestas qui in altis habitas et humilia respiciendo sanctificas: suscipe quaesumus oblationem nostram quam tibi offerimus in honorem tui nominis vel veneratione beatae Iustinae virginis et martyris tuae; et praesta ut quicumque digne ad altare hoc oblationis libamenta detulerit pietatis tuae gratia cum benignitate reportet.
translation_en: Lord God almighty, who art the indivisible Trinity and one majesty dwelling in high places and beholding lowly ones to sanctify: we beseech you, receive our offering which we present to your name or veneration of the blessed Justina, virgin and martyr of yours; and grant that whoever has fittingly brought the libaments of this oblation to the altar may return with the grace of your piety accompanied by benevolence.

text: Gloriosus nobis Domine praesentatus dies advenit in qua beata Iustina martyr tua sanguine decorata caelestem meruit societatem; proinde deprecamur maiestatem tuam omnipotens Deus ut per ea quae sumpsimus eius martyrium venerantes ipsius quoque meritis mereamur apud te semper misericordiam invenire.
translation_en: A glorious day has been presented to us, Lord, which has arrived, on which blessed Justina, your martyr, adorned with her blood, earned celestial companionship. Therefore, we humbly beseech Your majesty, almighty God, that through the martyrdom of her which we venerate, we may also deserve mercy from You through her own merits, always.

text: Deus qui sanctam nobis huius diei sollemnitatem pro commemoratione beati Domni martyris tui passione fecisti: adesto familiae tuae precibus et da ut cuius hodie festa celebramus eius meritis et intercessionibus adiuvemur.
translation_en: God, who on this day made holy for us the solemnity of your blessed martyr in commemoration of his passion: be present to the prayers of your family and grant that we, who celebrate his feast today, may be helped by his merits and intercessions.

text: Suscipe quaesumus Domine propitius munera quae in beati martyris tui Domni commemoratione deferimus ut cuius honore sunt grata eius nobis fiant intercessione perpetua.
translation_en: Receive, we ask you, Lord, kindly the offerings that we bring on the commemoration of your blessed martyr. May they be pleasing to him, so that through his honor, they become a permanent intercession for us.

text: Beati martyris tui Domni quaesumus Domine gloriosa nobis merita prosequantur quae fragilitatem nostram et precibus tueantur et meritis.
translation_en: We humbly ask you, Lord, that the glorious merits of your martyr may follow us, which may protect our frailty with prayers and uphold with merits.

text: Assit nobis Domine quaesumus santa precatio beati martyris tui Quintini quae nos et a terrenis affectibus incessanter expediat et caelestia desideria perficiat.
translation_en: Lord, assist us we beseech you, holy petition of your blessed martyr Quintinus, which may constantly free us from earthly passions and fulfill our heavenly desires.

text: Intercessio quaesumus Domine sancti Quintini martyris tui munera nostra commendet nosque eius veneratio tuae maiestati reddat acceptos.
translation_en: We humbly ask you, Lord, that the intercession of your holy martyr St. Quintinus may commend our gifts to you and that his veneration may offer them as acceptable to your majesty.

text: Laeti Domine sumpsimus sacramenta caelestia quae nobis intercedente beato Quintino martyre tuo uberius confidimus affutura.
translation_en: With joy, we have received the heavenly sacraments, which we trust more abundantly will be granted us through your martyr Saint Quintinus, interceding for us.

text: Omnipotens sempiterne Deus da populo tuo praesentis diei festivitatem sincero venerari affectu ut qui {per} eam sanctorum martyrum tuorum Vitalis et Agricolae annua celebritate devotis frequentant obsequiis eorundem suffragiis caelestis regni gaudia consequantur.
translation_en: Almighty everlasting God, grant to your people on this festive day a sincere spirit of worship, that those who, through it, celebrate annually the festival of your holy martyrs Vitalis and Agricola, may attain the joys of the celestial kingdom by their intercession.

text: Suscipe Domine sacrificium placationis ac laudis et intervenientibus sanctis tuis Vitale et Agricola nostra quaesumus corda laetificet et fidei nostrae praebeat incitamenta virtutum et multiplici nos suffragia consoletur.
translation_en: Receive, Lord, the sacrifice of propitiation and praise, and through your saints Vitale and Agricola we ask that you cheer our hearts and grant us encouragement for our faith, and that you may console us with abundant intercessions.

text: Omnipotens sempiterne Deus concede nobis habere corpus et sanguinem Domini nostri Iesu Christi intercedentibus sanctis martyribus tuis Vitale et Agricola remissionem omnium peccatorum et praemium vitae praesentis populo tuo ut simul in Ecclesia tua semper et laudes et gratias tibi Deo referre valeamus.
translation_en: Almighty everlasting God, grant us to have the body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ through the intercession of your saints Vitale and Agricola, remission of all sins and reward of present life's prize for your people. May we always be able in your Church simultaneously to render both praises and thanks to you, God.

text: Omnipotens sempiterne Deus sollemnitatem huius diei propitius intuere et Ecclesiam tuam intercessione beati confessoris tui atque pontificis Willibrordi continua fac celebritate gaudere omniumque in te credentium vota perficias.
translation_en: Almighty everlasting God, graciously look upon the solemnity of this day and may your Church enjoy continuous happiness through the intercession of your blessed confessor and bishop Willibrord. Grant that the wishes of all who believe in you are fulfilled.

text: Huius Domine sacrificii munus tua petimus 〈manu〉 contingi quod beati Willibrordi confessoris tui atque pontificis festivitate offerimus exsultantes.
translation_en: We beseech you, Lord, that the office of this sacrifice may touch your hand, which we offer with joy on the feast day of your confessor and bishop Saint Willibrord.

text: Beati confessoris tui Willibrordi atque pontificis Domine gaudia votiva celebrantes da quaesumus ut per haec sancta quae sumpsimus misericordiae tuae auribus nos ipse commendet.
translation_en: Celebrating your confessor Willibrord and the bishop with votive joy, O Lord, we humbly ask that through these holy things which we have taken, may you yourself recommend us to your mercy.

text: Deus qui nobis beati Aniani confessoris tui atque pontificis natalicia gloriosa celebrare concedis: tribue quaesumus eius nos semper et beneficiis praeveniri et orationibus adiuvari.
translation_en: God, who grants us the glorious feast day of your confessor and pope, blessed Anianus: grant us, we ask, always to be preceded by his benefits and to be aided by his prayers.

text: Omnipotens sempiterne Deus: maiestatem tuam suppliciter exoramus ut per intercessionem beati Gregorii confessoris tui atque pontificis cuius hodie annuam recolimus festivitatem cum temporalibus incrementis aeternae prosperitatis 〈capiamus〉 augmentum.
translation_en: Almighty everlasting God, we humbly beseech your majesty that through the intercession of blessed Gregory, your confessor and pope, whose today's anniversary festival we commemorate with temporal increases, we may receive an increase of eternal prosperity.

text: Donis caelestibus da quaesumus Domine libera mente servire munera quae offerimus interveniente beato Aniano confessore tuo atque pontifice et medelam nobis operentur et gloriam.
translation_en: We humbly ask You, Lord, to grant us with heavenly gifts. May our minds be free to serve the offerings we present, through your blessed Anianus the confessor and bishop, and may it bring healing to us. May it also bring glory.

text: Hostias tibi Domine pro commemoratione sancti confessoris tui Gregorii atque pontificis offerimus suppliciter deprecantes ut sicut illi praebuisti sacrae fidei largitatem sic nobis indulgentiam largiaris.
translation_en: We offer to you, Lord, hostias (offerings) for the commemoration of your holy confessor and bishop, St. Gregory, humbly beseeching that, just as you granted him abundance in the sacred faith, you grant us indulgence.

text: Quaesumus Domine Deus noster interveniente beato Aniano confessore tuo atque pontifice quae ore tempore nostrae mortalitatis contingimus immortalitatis tuae gratiam consequi mereamur.
translation_en: We ask you, Lord our God, through the intervention of your blessed confesor and pope Saint Anianus, that we may merit to obtain the grace of eternal life during our time of mortality.

text: Deus fidelium remunerator animarum: praesta ut per haec sancta quae sumpsimus beati confessoris tui Gregorii cuius venerandam celebramus festivitatem precibus indulgentiam consequamur.
translation_en: God, rewarder of the faithful souls: grant that through these holy things which we have received, we may obtain indulgence through the prayers as we celebrate the venerable feast day of your blessed confessor Gregory.

text: Deus qui nos sancti Columbani sacerdotis et confessoris tui annua beatae confessionis sollemnitate laetificas: praesta quaesumus ut callida hostis incursione tua freti virtute devicta pervenire ad gaudia ipso interveniente mereamur aeterna. Per Dominum nostrum.
translation_en: God who joyfully sanctifies us on the annual solemnity of your holy servant and confesor Saint Columbanus: grant, we beseech you, that defeated by your power in the cunning attack of the enemy, we may reach the joys and merit eternal life as he himself intervenes. Through our Lord.

text: Oblatis Domine placare muneribus quaesumus Pater omnipotens propitiatus intende et intercedente beato Columbano confessore tuo et ab occulta insidiatoris incursione fragilitatem nostram tueantur illaesam et angelicis devote manibus suscepta sacris ante conspectum gloriae tuae in odorem suavitatis cum alacritate deferantur.
translation_en: Lord, we beseech You to be propitious towards the offerings. Almighty Father, with Your merciful attention, and through the intercession of blessed Columbanus, Your confessor, protect our frailty from the hidden onslaught of an enemy. May these sacred objects, taken up devoutly by angelic hands, be carried to Your glory with eagerness, and offer a sweet savor.

text: Sumptis Domine sacrosanctae redemptionis mysteriis deprecamur ut et salutaris huius remedii plenitudine roborati et sancti confessoris tui Columbani saluberrimo interventu fulti ad plenae festivitatis gaudia pervenire mereamur aeterna. Per Dominum nostrum Iesum.
translation_en: We beseech You, Lord, in the sacred mysteries of our redemption, that strengthened by the fullness of this salutary remedy and assisted by the beneficial intervention of Your holy confessor Columbanus, we may merit to reach the joyous celebrations of the full feast through eternal life. Through Our Lord Jesus Christ.

text: Intercessio nos quaesumus Domine sanctae Barbarae martyris tuae votiva confoveat ut eius sacra natalicia et temporaliter frequentemus et conspiciamus aeterna. Per Dominum.
translation_en: We humbly ask you, Lord, that the prayer of your holy martyr Saint Barbara may be strengthened by your vow, so that we may celebrate her sacred birthday and occasionally partake in her temporal festivities, and perceive her eternally. Through the Lord.

text: Tribue quaesumus virtutum caelestium Deus ut sacrificia pro sanctae tuae Barbarae sollemnitate delata desiderium nos temporalem doceant habere contemptum et ambire dona faciant caelestium gaudiorum.
translation_en: We ask you, God, to grant us the virtues of the heavenly powers, that the offerings presented for the solemnity of your holy Barbara may teach us to have contempt for temporal desires and make us aspire for the joys of the heavenly realm.

text: Laeti Domine sumpsimus sacramenta caelestia; intercedente pro nobis beata Barbara martyre tua ad vitam quaesumus nobis proficiant sempiternam.
translation_en: We rejoice, Lord, that we have received heavenly sacraments; through the intercession of blessed Barbara, your martyr, we humbly ask for our eternal life to progress.

text: »Domine si fuisses hic« et cetera. (J 1121) Christus qui solus animas in inferno liberavit dedit hominibus potestatem ut succurrere possint positis in purgatorio et ex quo Christus in propria persona hanc legationem implevit non est mirum si orationes et eleemosynas nostras mittamus nos pro ipsis ad Dominum. Unde in hoc evangelio videns suspiria et lacrimas sororum Dominus Lazarum resuscitavit sic precibus fidelium animas a purgatorio liberat. Quod cum posset sine precibus vult quod amicis eius gratiae referantur. Sicut princeps puniendum non exaudit sed eum qui interpellat pro eo. Dicit ergo: »Domine si fuisses hic frater meus non fuisset mortuus.« Mystice intelligitur hoc de morte gehennae. Quoniam si Dominus per gratiam esset cum Lazaro non moreretur morte gehennae. Nota: quidam moriuntur in deserto. Quidam in Aegypto. Quidam in terra promissionis. Primi dies bonae vitae non incipiunt. Secundi dimidiant. Tertii perficiunt. De primis: »Viri sanguinum et dolosi.« (Ps 5424) De secundis: »Dum adhuc ordiret« bene vivere »succidit me.« (Is 3812) De tertiis: »Mortuus Abraham plenus dierum.« (Jer 611) Primi ducuntur in puteum infernum. Secundum illud: »Deduces eos in puteum interitus.« (Ps 54 24) Secundi ad portas inferni in purgatorium. Unde: »Ego dixi in dimidio dierum meorum« et cetera. (Is 3810) Tertii ad gloriam. Unde: »Cum dederit dilectis suis somnum ecce hereditas« et cetera. (Ps 1292–3) Primi cantant triplex vae quia Deum offenderunt quia diabolo consenserunt quia torquebuntur in perpetuum. Secundi lamentum in purgatorio ut per orationes et eleemosynas eis succurramus. Tertii cantant carmen in caelo. Crudeles sunt qui in purgatorio exsistentibus non succurrunt. De quibus dicitur: »Omnes amici eius speverunt eam.« (Thr 12). Animae enim in tormentis clamant: »Miseremini mei miseremini mei saltem vos amici mei.« (Job 1921) Numquam sic probatur amicus quam in tali necessitatis articulo. Magister Hugo post mortem suam cuidam concanonico suo quem prae ceteris dilexit apparuit turpis et graviter afflictus quem duo daemones flagellando et a dextris et a sinistris duxerunt quem cum concanonicus quis esset requireret respondit: Sum quondam tuus socius. Requisitus quare tales poenas toleraret dixit: Propter gnosyas sed si mihi subvenires cito liberarer. Unde postquam ille in vigiliis pro eo laborasset apparuit ei iterum speciosus. Debemus ergo mortuis subvenire et succurere quia et nos sumus morituri. Nihil est certius morte. Quidam burgensis audiens semel a quodam quod utilis esset mortis recordatio feretrum in camera sua positum ferculis impleverat et pauperibus dividebat. Quoniam ut dicit Gregorius necesse est ut iam se reputet mortuum qui se cogitat moriturum. Mortui omnia vana mundi relinquunt quae in tribus consistunt: in carnis suavitate in rerum cupiditate in amicorum societate. Primum relinquit in infirmitate. Secundum in morte. Tertium in sepulcro. Quia »Opera tantum illorum sequuntur illos.« (Act 1413) Attende brevitatem vitae quam multi »messem colligunt« (cf. Jr 4010) »racemos vindemniant« (cf. Mch 71) vestes novas praeparant et tamen illa non gustant istis non induuntur. Quidam considerans se cito moriturum relicto patre et claustrum intravit et cetera. Attende quam »amara mors« (cf. 1Sm 1532) cor enim hominis in morte prae nimio labore in duo dividitur nasus frigescit dentes nigrescunt facies pallescit venae et nervi corporis rumpuntur. Cadaver vero mortuum in aquis non proicitur ne aquae corrumpantur in aëre non suspenditur ne aër inficiatur sed sicut venenum pessimum in foramen proicitur; terra super ipsum velociter tumulatur ne ab hominibus videatur. Ecce gloria mundi quali fine clauditur. Quod considerans quidam philosophus semper flevit. Si quis autem cum dolore aegritudinem vel mortem suscipit signum est quod Deum non diligit. Si aliquis esset in tenebris et incarceratus gauderet si aliquis carcerem confringeret. Ergo enim magna laetitia est infirmitas sucipienda quia in infirmitate carcer noster effoditur. In morte penitus destruitur et anima ad Dominum suum libera progreditur. »Nolite ergo contristari sicut et ceteri qui spem non habent.« (1Th 413) Si contristamini in morte amicorum consolemini quia in caelesti patria ipsos invenietis. Unde Dominus discipulis de morte contristantibus ait: »Si diligeritis me gauderetis utique« et cetera. (J 1428) Est autem triplex mors animae. Nonne gehennae. De prima: »Vidua vivens inde mortua est.« (1T 55–6) De secunda: »Domini Domini exitus mortis.« (Ps 6721) De tertia: »Sicut oves in inferno positi sunt.« (Ps 4815) Infernus est locus quasi pascuosus in quo cibus erit de quo dicit Iob: »Caput aspidis suggeret interficiet eos lingua viperae« (Job 2016) et sicut post prandium solent homines solaciari ita animae in inferno. Unde Iob: »transibunt ab aquis nivium ad calorem nimium et« (Job 24 19) in omnibus his pascuis »mors« peccati mortalis »depascet eos« (Ps 4815). Et notandum quod quattuor sunt viae post mortem. Una adulterorum in mortali culpa decedentium quae ducit eos ad infernum. Alia infantium parvulorum circa septimum et ducit eos in purgatorium. Tertia nondum paenitentiam complentium et ducit in purgatorium. Quarta sine peccati macula decedentium quae ducit ad caeli palatium. Qui »ubi fuerit corpus Christi ibi congregabuntur et aquilae« (Mt 2428 et L 1737) id est animae fideles scilicet corpus Christi in caelo sunt ergo et animae sanctorum illuc congregabuntur. R.
translation_en:
Lord, if you had been here (John 11:21), and furthermore, Christ who alone freed souls in hell gave humans the ability to help those placed in purgatory. Since Christ completed this mission in his own person, it is not surprising that we send our prayers and alms for them to the Lord. In this gospel, seeing the sighs and tears of Lazarus' sisters, the Lord raised Lazarus. Similarly, the souls from purgatory are freed by the prayers of the faithful. Although he could do so without prayer, he wants that his friends receive grace because of it. Therefore, he says: "Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died." Mystically, this is about the death of hell.
Some die in the desert. Some in Egypt. Some in the land of promise. The first days of good life do not begin. The second halves. The third complete them. Of the first: "Men whose blood is guilt." (Psalm 54:24) Of the second: "While he was still speaking, I am cut off." (Isaiah 38:12) Of the third: "Abraham died full of days." (Jeremiah 6:11) The first are led into the pit of hell. According to this: "You lead them to the pit of corruption." (Psalm 54:24) The second to the gates of hell in purgatory. Therefore: "I said in my half of my days," and so on. (Isaiah 38:10) The third to glory. Therefore: "When he gave rest to his loved ones, behold, they inherit." (Psalm 127:3) The first sing a threefold woe because they have offended God, consented to the devil, and will be tormented forever. The second lament in purgatory so that we help them with our prayers and alms. The third sing a song in heaven. It is cruel not to help those who exist in purgatory. They are spoken of as: "All his friends mourned for him." (Lamentations 1:2) The souls in torment cry out: "Have mercy on me, have mercy on me, at least you, my friends." (Job 19:21) Never is a friend proven as much as in such a necessity. After his death, Master Hugo appeared to one of his canon companions whom he loved more than others, appearing filthy and gravely afflicted. Two demons led him, beating him from the right and left. When the canon asked who he was, he replied: "I was once your companion." Asked why he endured such torments, he said: "Because of sins, but if you help me quickly, I would be freed." After the canon labored for him in vigils, he appeared to him again, radiant. Therefore, we should help and support the dead because we are also mortal. Nothing is more certain than death.
One day, a burgher who was told that a reminder of death had been placed in his chamber filled it with dishes and gave them to the poor. Because Gregory says that one must already consider himself dead who considers himself about to die. Mortals abandon everything vanity of the world that consists in three things: in carnal pleasure, in the desire for things, in friendship of men. The first relinquishes in illness. The second in death. The third in the tomb. "For their works follow them." (Acts 14:13)
Attend to the brevity of life, for many "collect grapes" (cf. John 4:10), "harvest bunches" (cf. Mark 7:1), prepare new clothes, and yet they do not taste these nor wear them. One considering himself about to die entered a monastery and so on. Attend how bitter death divides the heart of man in two: his nose freezes, his teeth blacken, his face pales, his veins and nerves break. The corpse of the dead is not thrown into water so as not to corrupt the waters, nor suspended so as not to infect the air, but like the most poisonous venom, it is thrust into a hole; the earth quickly covers it lest it be seen by humans. Thus, the glory of the world closes with such an end. Considering this, a certain philosopher always wept.
If someone receives illness or death with sorrow, it is a sign that he does not love God. If someone were in darkness and imprisoned, he would rejoice if he broke the prison. Therefore, great joy is to be accepted in sickness because our prison is broken in sickness. In death, it is utterly destroyed, and the soul goes freely to its Lord. "Therefore do not grieve as others who have no hope." (1 Thessalonians 4:13) If you mourn for your friends in death, comfort yourselves because you will find them in the celestial kingdom. Therefore, the Lord speaks to his disciples mourning over their dead friends: "If you loved me, you would rejoice." (John 16:28) and so on.

text: 〈...〉 Sigismundi regis et sociorum eius Domni Basilini Petri Pyrrhi Pyrrhini Restituti Basilii Desiderii communicationem corporis et sanguinis Domini nostri Iesu Christi sumpserit ad sanitatem revocetur. Per Dominum nostrum.
translation_en: Sigismund, the king, and his companions, Lord Basilinus Petrus Pyrrhus Pyrrhinus Restitutus Basilius Desiderius, have taken communion of the body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ for their health and recovery. Through our Lord.

text: Deus qui omnibus sanctis tuis ad hanc gloriam veniendi copiosum munus gratiae contulisti: da nobis famulis nostrorum veniam peccatorum ut sanctorum tuorum intercedentibus meritis ab omnibus mereamur adversitatibus liberari.
translation_en: God, who has bestowed upon all your saints a rich gift of grace for coming to this glory: grant us, your servants, forgiveness of sins, so that we may be worthy of being freed from all adversities through the merits of your saints interceding on our behalf.

text: Praesta quaesumus omnipotens Deus ut qui gloriosos martyres Severum Severianum Carpophorum Victorinum fortes in sua confessione cognovimus pios apud te in nostra intercessione sentiamus.
translation_en: Grant, we humbly ask you, Almighty God, that we who have known the glorious martyrs Severus, Severian, Carpophorus, Victorinus, strong in their confession, may feel them pious in our intercession with you.

text: Deus qui beatum pontificem Wolfkangum gloriae sanctorum similem fecisti et beata fide munisti: da nobis eius pia merita devote sectari qui pastor noster exstitit et aeternitatis gloriam promeruit.
translation_en: God, who made the blessed pontiff Wolfgang similar to the glory of saints and equipped him with blessed faith: grant us to devoutly follow his pious merits, who was our pastor and merited eternal glory.

text: Deus qui famulos tuos in hoc loco degentes sub sancta professione de tempestatibus huius saeculi eruisti et ad portum monasterii et quietis venire fecisti: concede propitius ut hic 〈et〉 in perpetuum te auxiliante salventur.
translation_en: God, who rescued your servants dwelling here under a holy profession from the storms of this world and brought them to the port of the monastery and peace, graciously grant that they may be saved here and forevermore with Your aid.

text: Oblatum tibi Domine sacrificium famulos tuos in hoc loco conversantes sanctificet semper et muniat.
translation_en: Offered to You, Lord, is this sacrifice, Your servants, who are turning here. May it be always sanctified and fortified.

text: Divina quaesumus Domine mysteria huius congregationis fratres muniant ubique et protegant et tuis faciant semper inhaerere mandatis.
translation_en: We humbly ask you, Lord, that the brothers of this congregation may uphold and protect the divine mysteries everywhere, and may they always adhere to your commands.

text: Similitudo vultus quattuor animalium facies hominis et facies leonis a dextris ipsorum quattuor. Facies autem bovis a sinistris ipsorum quattuor. Et facies aquilae desuper ipsorum quattuor. Et facies eorum et pennae eorum extentae desuper. Duae pennae singulorum iungebantur et duae tegebant corpora eorum et unumquodque eorum coram facie sua ambulabat. Ubi impetus spiritus erat illuc gradiebantur nec revertebantur cum ambularent. Et similitudo animalium et aspectus eorum quasi carbonum ignis ardentium et quasi aspectus lampadarum. Haec erat visio discurrens in medio animalium splendor ignis et de igne fulgur egrediens. Et animalia ibant et non revertebantur in similitudinem fulguris coruscantis.
translation_en: The likeness of the countenance was that of the four faces: a human face, a lion's face on their right, an ox's face on their left, and an eagle's face above them. The extent of their faces and their wings covered them above. Each of their wings joined together in pairs and covered their bodies, and each one walked before its own face. Wherever the impulse of the spirit was, they moved there and did not return when walking. And the likeness of the animals and their appearance were like burning coals and like the appearance of lamps. This vision shone amidst the animals in a splendor of fire, and from the fire came flashes. The animals went forth and did not return in the likeness of flashing lightning.

text: Ecce confessor magnus qui in vita sua curavit gentem suam et liberavit illam a perditione. Qui praevaluit amplificare civitatem qui adeptus est gloriam in conversatione gentis suae. Quasi stella matutina in medio nebulae et quasi luna plena in diebus suis lucet. Quasi arcus refulgens inter nebulas gloriae sic ille refulsit in templo Dei. Cypri cum nardo nardus et crocus fistula et cinnamomum cum universis lignis Lybani. Et vestiri eum consummatione virtutis in accensu altaris gloriam dedit sanctitatis amictum. Et intravit orationem suam voluit se ostendere sacerdotibus prius pro suis delictis hostias offerre Domino. Et fiat pax in Israël per dies sempiternos.
translation_en: Behold a great confessor who, during his life, cared for his people and freed them from destruction. He prevailed to amplify the city who achieved glory in the conversation of his people. Like a morning star amidst the clouds and like a full moon on its days, it shines. Like a shining rainbow amidst the clouds of glory, he shone in the temple of God. With cypress, myrrh, cassia, calamus, and cinnamon along with all the woods of Lebanon. And he was clothed with the completion of virtues in the burning altar's glow. And he entered his prayer, desired to show himself first to the priests before offering sacrifices for his sins to the Lord. Let there be peace in Israel forever.

text: In principio erat Verbum. Et Verbum erat apud Deum. Et Deus erat Verbum. Hoc erat in principio apud Deum. Omnia per ipsum facta sunt et sine ipso factum est nihil. Quod factum est in ipso vita erat et vita erat lux hominum. Et lux in tenebris lucet et tenebrae eam non comprehenderunt. Fuit homo missus a Deo cui nomen erat Ioannes. Hic venit in testimonium ut testimonium perhiberet de lumine 〈ut omnes crederent per illum. Non erat ille lux sed ut testimonium perhiberet de lumine〉. Erat lux vera quae illuminat omnem hominem venientem in hunc mundum. In mundo erat et mundus per ipsum factus est et mundus eum non cognovit. In propria venit et sui eum non receperunt. Quotquot autem receperunt eum dedit eis potestatem filios Dei fieri his qui credunt in nomine eius. Qui non ex sanguinibus neque ex voluntate carnis neque ex voluntate viri sed ex Deo nati sunt. Et Verbum caro factum est et habitavit in nobis. Et vidimus gloriam eius gloriam quasi Unigeniti a Patre plenum gratia et veritate.
translation_en: In the beginning was the Word. And the Word was with God, and God was the Word. This was in the beginning with God. All things were made through him, and without him nothing was made that has been made. What has been made was life, and the life was the light of men. The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not comprehend it. A man was sent from God whose name was John. This one came as a witness to testify about the light, so that all might believe through him. He was not the light, but he came as a witness to testify about the light. The true light that enlightens every man who comes into this world was in the world, and the world, though it was made through him, did not recognize him. He came to his own, and his own did not receive him. But to all who received him, he gave the power to become children of God, to those who believe in his name, who were born not of blood nor of the will of the flesh nor of the will of man, but of God. And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we have seen his glory, glory as of the only Son from the Father, full of grace and truth.

text: Videte vigilate et orate. Nescitis enim quando tempus sit sicut homo qui peregre profectus reliquit domum suam et dedit servis suis potestatem cuiusque operis et ianitori praecipiat ut vigilet. Vigilate ergo nescitis enim quando Dominus veniat: sero an media nocte an galli cantu an mane; ne cum venerit repente inveniat vos dormientes. Quod autem vobis dico omnibus dico: vigilate.
translation_en: Be watchful, be alert, and pray. For you do not know when the time will come, like a man who has journeyed abroad and left his house to his servants, assigning them tasks and telling the gatekeeper to stay awake. Therefore, be watchful, for you do not know when the Lord will come: at evening, at midnight, at cockcrow, or in the morning; lest he come suddenly and find you asleep. What I say to all I say to you: Be watchful.

text: Optavi et datus est mihi sensus et vocavi et venit in me spiritus sapientiae. Et reposui illam regnis et sedibus et divitias nihil esse duxi in comparatione illius. Nec comparavi illi lapides pretiosos quoniam omne aurum in comparatione illius arena est exigua et tamquam lutum aestimabitur argentum in conspectu illius. Super salutem et speciem dilexi illam et proposui pro luce habere illam quoniam inexstinguibile est lumen illius. Venerunt autem mihi omnia bona pariter cum illa et innumerabilis honestas per manus illius. Et laetatus sum in omnibus quoniam antecedebat me ista sapientia et ignorabam quoniam omnium bonorum mater est. Quam sine fractione didici et sine invidia communico bonis et honestatem illius non abscondo. Infinitus enim est thesaurus hominibus. Quo qui usi sunt participes facti sunt amicitiae Dei.
translation_en: I desired and it was given to me understanding, and I called and the spirit of wisdom came to me. And I rested her in kingdoms and seats and riches, and I considered nothing as compared to her. Neither did I compare precious stones with her, for all gold in comparison to her is like sand and silver will be valued as clay before her. For the sake of her health and beauty, I loved her and chose to have her as light, because her light is everlasting. All good things came to me together with her, and an innumerable honor through her hands. And I was glad in all things because wisdom preceded me and I did not know that she is the mother of all good things. Without any division, I learned her and without envy I share her goodness and do not hide her honesty. For the treasure of men is infinite, those who use it become partakers of the friendship of God.

text: Vigilate quia nescitis
translation_en: Be alert, for you do not know when

text: Exaudi nos Domine Deus noster ut per huius sacramenti virtutem a cunctis nos mentis et corporis hostibus tuearis gratiam tribuens in praesenti et gloriam in futuro.
translation_en: Hear us, O Lord our God, that through the power of this sacrament you may protect us from all enemies of mind and body, granting grace to us now, and glory in the future.

text: Mundet et muniat quaesumus Domine divini sacramenti nos munus oblatum et intercedente beata Virgine Dei Genitrice Maria cum apostolis tuis Petro et Paulo et omnibus sanctis a cunctis nos reddat perversitatibus expiatos et adversitatibus expeditos.
translation_en: We beseech you, Lord, to cleanse and fortify us with the divine sacrament that we have offered. Through the intercession of the blessed Virgin Mary, Mother of God, along with your apostles Peter and Paul, and all the saints, may you grant us, freed from perversity and equipped to face adversities.

text: Clemens et benigna iugi laude digna Maria. Fer spiritalia nobis remedia Maria. Tu plena gratia mater eximia Maria. Solve peccamina relaxa crimina Maria. Felix et beata Deo fecundata Maria. Restaura 〈perdita〉 remitte debita Maria. Parens Dei facta viro sed intacta Maria. Nos a miseria reduc ad gaudia Maria. Tu mundi domina caelorum regina Maria. Sit tibi gloria saecla per omnia Maria.
translation_en: Clement and worthy of high praise, Mary. Grant spiritual remedies to us, Mary. Full of grace, the exalted Mother Mary. Undo our sins, loosen our burdens, Mary. Blessed and happy, made fruitful by God, Mary. Restore what is lost, forgive debt, Mary. Made mother of God, a virgin yet joined to man, Mary. Lead us from misery to joy, Mary. Ruler of the world, queen of heaven, Mary. May glory be yours throughout all ages, Mary.

text: Sonent hymni Deo digni in hac die tam insigni clangore tubae ductili ad haec festa patris tanti voce psallat incessanti tam plebs quam clerus humilis. Nam quod erit tam praeclarum quam ob virum Deo carum 〈laudes sonare gaudii cum applaudit triumphalis lux non mortis sed natalis〉 sancti patris Aegidii. Tibi honor Iesu Christe quo patrante sanctus iste tanta pollebat gratia ut infirmi sanarentur et leprosi mundarentur per ipsius suffragia. Sanat hunc quae serpens laedit solo daemon iussu cedit suum timens imperium. Aegris salus restauratur mare tumens tranquillatur aestus quiescit febrium. Gressu claudus stabilitur dum insignis insignitur fidus Christi vernaculus. In desertum solus fugit et mamillas cervae sugit ceu naturalis hinnulus Diu montis in speleo latens soli vacans Deo sed inde multum doluit ibi pie diffamatur per hunc noxa relaxatur quam rex abscondi voluit. Virtus mira nihil mali sub patrono potest tali quemquam suorum laedere.〉 Sidus dulce confessorum tua prece nos iustorum fac consortes in aethere.
translation_en:
Hymns sound worthy to God on this day of such splendid brass trumpet sound, the choir and the people sing with unceasing voice the praises of our great Father. For what will be as glorious as for the man dear to God, praises sound with joy and applauding triumphant light, not of death but of birth. The holy Father Aegidius celebrates such praises. To you honor, Jesus Christ, through whose intervention this saint possessed such great grace that the sick were healed and lepers were cleansed by his intercession. This one who is bitten only by a serpent flees alone, the demon obeys its command, afraid of its authority. Salvation is restored to the sick, the swelling sea calms down, the fever subsides. The lame man walks steadily and the faithful Christian's native grows strong. In the desert he alone flees like a natural hart, even when hidden in a mountain cave for a long time he feels sad because of his piety, but here he is slandered falsely by sin, which is relaxed much more than the king wanted to hide it. No evil can harm anyone under such a patron.
The sweet star, by your prayer, makes us companions of the just in the ether.

text: Praesta Domine fidelibus tuis ut ieiuniorum veneranda sollemnia et congrua pietate suscipiant et secura devotione percurrant.
translation_en: Grant, Lord, to your faithful ones, that they may honorably receive the solemnities of fasting with reverent devotion and run through them securely with devoted faith.

text: Fac nos Domine quaesumus his muneribus offerendis convenienter aptari quibus ipsius venerabilis sacramenti celebramus exordium.
translation_en: Grant us, Lord, as we humbly ask, to fit ourselves appropriately for presenting these offerings, with whom we begin the venerable sacrament that we celebrate.

text: VD ... Qui corporali ieiunio vitia comprimis mentem elevas virtutem largiris et praemia. Per Christum Dominum nostrum.
translation_en: You who suppress vices with bodily fasting, raise the mind, give virtue, and bestow rewards. Through Christ our Lord.

text: Percepta nobis Domine praebeant sacramenta subsidium ut et tibi grata sint nostra ieiunia et nobis proficiant ad medelam.
translation_en: Grant us, Lord, that the sacraments may be a support to us, so that our fasting may be pleasing to you and that we may profit from them as a remedy.

text: Haec quae nos praeparent quaesumus Domine beata mysteria tuo munere dignos efficiant.
translation_en: We humbly ask, Lord, that those things which we are about to receive may, by your blessing, render us worthy of the holy mysteries.

text: Caelestis doni benedictione percepta supplices te Deus omnipotens deprecamur ut hoc idem nobis sacramenti causa sit et salutis.
translation_en: We humbly ask you, almighty God, that through the heavenly blessing received, this same sacrament be for us and bring salvation.

text: Parce Domine parce populo tuo ut de tuis flagellationibus castigatus in tua miseratione respiret. Per Dominum.
translation_en: Lord, have mercy, have mercy on your people, that, chastised by your scourges, they may breathe again in your mercy. Through the Lord.

text: Sacrificium Domine observantiae paschalis offerimus; praesta quaesumus ut tibi et mentes nostras reddat acceptas et continentiae promptioris nobis tribuat facultatem.
translation_en: We offer the Paschal sacrifice to you, Lord; grant us we pray that you may accept our minds and bestow upon us the ability for prompt obedience.

text: Da famulis tuis Domine abundantiam protectionis et gratiae tuae da salutem mentis et corporis et continua prosperitatis augmenta et tibi semper fac esse devotos.
translation_en: Grant, Lord, to your servants abundance of protection and grace; grant health of mind and body, and continuous increase of prosperity, and may you always make them devoted to you.

text: Adesto Domine supplicationibus nostris et concede ut hoc sollemne ieiunium quod animis corporibusque curandis salubriter institutum est devoto servitio celebremus.
translation_en: Be present, Lord, with our supplications and grant that we may celebrate this solemn fast which has been healthfully established for the care of souls and bodies, in devoted service.

text: Suscipe Domine sacrificium cuius te voluisti dignanter immolari placari; praesta quaesumus ut huius operatione mundati beneplacitum tibi nostrae mentis offeramus affectum.
translation_en: Receive, Lord, the sacrifice which you have willed to be worthy of being offered to appease You; grant us, we entreat, that through this action we may be cleansed and present before You a pleasing mindset.

text: Sacrificium quadragesimalis initii sollemniter immolamus te Domine deprecantes ut cum epularum restrictione carnalium a noxiis quoque voluptatibus temperemus. Per Dominum.
translation_en: We solemnly offer the Quadragesimal sacrifice, Lord, beseeching you that with the restriction of earthly meals, we may also temper ourselves from harmful pleasures. Through the Lord.

text: Super populum tuum quaesumus Domine benedictio tribuatur fides sancta crescat redemptio sempiterna firmetur.
translation_en: Upon your people we humbly ask, Lord, let a blessing be given, may the holy faith grow, may eternal redemption be strengthened.

text: Absolve Domine quaesumus nostrorum vincula peccatorum et quicquid pro eis meremur propitiatus averte.
translation_en: Lord, we humbly ask that you forgive our bonds of sins and turn away whatever merit we have earned for them.

text: Reminiscere miserationum tuarum Domine et misericordiae tuae quae a saeculo sunt ne umquam dominentur nobis inimici nostri; libera nos Deus Israël ex omnibus angustiis nostris.
translation_en: Remember your mercies, O Lord, and your loving-kindness that are from eternity, let them never rule over us our enemies; deliver us, God of Israel, from all our afflictions.

text: Ad te Domine levavi animam meam Deus meus in te confido non erubescam.
translation_en: To you, Lord, I have lifted up my soul; my God, in you do I trust; I shall not be ashamed.

text: Tribulationes cordis mei dilatatae sunt de necessitatibus meis eripe me Domine.
translation_en: My heart's tribulations have been expanded due to my necessities; save me, O Lord.

text: Vide humilitatem meam et laborem meum et dimitte omnia peccata mea.
translation_en: See my humility and my labor, and forgive all my sins.

text: De necessitatibus meis eripe me Domine vide humilitatem meam et laborem meum et dimitte omnia peccata mea. V. Ad te Domine levavi animam meam Deus meus in te confido non erubescam neque irrideant me inimici mei. V. Etenim universi qui te exspectant non confundentur confundantur omnes facientes vana.
translation_en:
From my necessities save me, O Lord; see my humility and my labor, and forgive all my sins.
V. To you, O Lord, I have lifted up my soul, my God, in you do I trust; I shall not be ashamed nor shall my enemies mock me.
V. Indeed, all who wait for You shall not be put to shame; they are the ones who do vain things that will be confounded.

text: Meditabar in mandatis tuis quae dilexi valde et levabo manus meas ad mandata tua quae dilexi.
translation_en: I have meditated on your commandments which I love very much, and I will lift my hands to your commandments that I love.

text: Intellige clamorem meum intende voci orationis meae rex meus et Deus meus quoniam ad te orabo Domine.
translation_en: Understand my cry, attend to the voice of my prayer, King and my God, for I will pray to you, Lord.

text: Omnipotens sempiterne Deus qui in observatione ieiunii et eleemosynarum largitione ∙ posuisti nostrorum remedia peccatorum: concede nos opere mentis et corporis semper esse devotos.
translation_en: Almighty everlasting God, who in the observance of fasting and the distribution of alms have placed remedies for our sins: grant us to be always devoted in mind and body.

text: Sacrificia Domine quaesumus propitius ista nos salvent quae medicinalibus sunt instituta ieiuniis. Per Christum.
translation_en: Lord, we humbly ask that these sacrifices save us, which have been established with healing through fasting. Through Christ.

text: Suscipe Domine quaesumus nostris oblata servitiis et tua dona propitius sanctifica.
translation_en: Receive, Lord, we ask you, our offerings of service, and may your gifts be gracious and holy.

text: Per huius Domine operationem mysterii et vitia nostra purgentur et iusta desideria compleantur.
translation_en: Through the operation of this Lord, our vices will be purged and our just desires fulfilled.

text: Respice Domine propitius plebem tuam et quam divinis proficere facis sacramentis ab omnibus absolve peccatis.
translation_en: Look upon us, Lord, with favor, and as we progress with divine sacraments, absolve us from all sins.

text: Populum tuum quaesumus Domine propitius respice atque ab eo flagella tuae iracundiae clementer averte.
translation_en: We humbly ask You, Lord, look upon Your people with kindness and turn away from them Your rod of anger gently.

text: Deus qui delinquentes perire non pateris donec convertantur et vivant: debitam quaesumus peccatis nostris suspende vindictam et praesta propitius ne dissimulatio prosit ad veniam.
translation_en: God who does not allow the sinners to perish, as long as they convert and live: we humbly ask that you suspend the debt of our sins' retribution and graciously grant that confession may bring forgiveness.

text: Actiones nostras quaesumus Domine aspirando praeveni et adiuvando prosequere ut cuncta nostra operatio et a te semper incipiat et per te coepta finiatur.
translation_en: Lord, we humbly ask that you, by inspiring and assisting us, may proceed and continue our actions. May all our undertakings always begin with you and end through you.

text: Sanctificationibus nostris omnipotens Deus et vitia nostra curentur et remedia nobis aeterna proveniant.
translation_en: In our sanctifications, O almighty God, may our vices be cured and eternal remedies come to us.

text: Haec hostia tibi Domine placationis et laudis nos propitiatione tua dignos efficiat.
translation_en: May this offering, Lord, make us worthy through Your propitiation, for pleasing and praise before You.

text: Perfice quaesumus Domine benignus in nobis observantiae sanctae subsidium ut quae te auctore facienda cognovimus te operante impleamus.
translation_en: Grant us, we beseech Thee, O Lord, Thy gracious help in us, that we may fulfill with Thy aid what we have learned through Thee to be done, and complete it with Thy operation.

text: Sanctificationem tuam nobis Domine his mysteriis placatus operare quae nos a terrenis purget vitiis et ad caelestia regna perducat.
translation_en: Lord, through these mysteries, grant us your sanctification, which cleanses us from earthly vices and leads us to the heavenly kingdoms.

text: Praesenti sacrificio nomini tuo nos Domine ieiunia dicata sanctificent ut quod observantia nostra profitetur exterius interius operetur affectum.
translation_en: In this present sacrifice, Lord, may our fasting dedicated to you sanctify us, so that what our outward appearance profits, may work the affection within us.

text: Adesto Domine famulis tuis et perpetuam benignitatem largire poscentibus ut his qui te auctore et gubernatore gloriantur et congregata restaures et restaurata conserves.
translation_en: Be present, Lord, to your servants and grant them eternal kindness as they ask. May those who glory in you as author and governor be restored and preserved when they are gathered and restored.

text: Haec in nobis sacrificia Deus et sanctificatione permaneant et operatione firmentur.
translation_en: These sacrifices in us (remain) God, and are strengthened by sanctification.

text: Sacramenti tui Domine libatio penetralia nostri cordis infundat et sui participes potenter efficiat. Per Dominum.
translation_en: May your Sacrament, Lord, pour into the innermost parts of our hearts and make us powerful participants. Through the Lord.

text: Haec hostia Domine quaesumus mundet nostra delicta et sacrificium celebrandum subditorum tibi corpora mentesque sanctificet.
translation_en: This offering, Lord, we humbly ask that it purifies our sins, and may the sacrifice be celebrated by your subjects, who offer their bodies and minds to you.

text: A cunctis nos Domine reatibus et periculis propitiatus absolve quos tantis mysteriis tribuis esse participes.
translation_en: Lord, propitiated towards all, absolve us from all retributions and dangers. You who grant us to be participants of such great mysteries.

text: Subveniat nobis Domine misericordia tua ut ab imminentibus peccatorum nostrorum periculis te mereamur protegente salvari.
translation_en: May the Lord's mercy be upon us, that we may be delivered from the dangers of our sins which we may deserve to be saved through His protection.

text: Tua nos Domine protectione defende et ab omni iniquitate custodi.
translation_en: Lord, defend us with Your protection and guard us from all wickedness.

text: Suscipe Domine quaesumus preces populi tui cum oblationibus hostiarum et tua mysteria celebrantes ab omnibus nos defende periculis.
translation_en: Receive, Lord, we humbly beseech You, the prayers of Your people with the offerings of sacrifices and while celebrating Your mysteries, protect us from all dangers.

text: Sanctificet nos Domine qua pasti sumus mensa caelestis et a cunctis reatibus expiatos supernis promissionibus reddat acceptos.
translation_en: Sanctify us, Lord, as we partake of the table in heaven, and may He grant that we are accepted by all divine promises and purified from all sins.

text: Sacramenti tui Domine veneranda perceptio et mystico mundet effectu et perpetua virtute defendat.
translation_en: May Your sacred rite, Lord, be received with reverence and cleansed by a mysterious effect. May it protect us by its eternal power.

text: Miserere Domine populo tuo et continuis tribulationibus laborantem propitius respirare concede.
translation_en: Have mercy, Lord, on Your people and grant them relief from continuous tribulations; be gracious and let them breathe again.

text: Deus qui et iustis praemia meritorum et peccatoribus per ieiunium veniam praebes: miserere supplicibus parce peccantibus ut reatus nostri confessio indulgentiam valeat percipere delictorum.
translation_en: God who provides rewards for the merits of the just and forgiveness through fasting to sinners: have mercy on the penitent, spare the guilty ones, that our confession may worthily receive forgiveness for our offenses through indulgence.

text: Praesta quaesumus Domine ut salutaribus ieiuniis eruditi a noxiis etiam vitiis abstinentes propitiationem tuam facilius impetremus.
translation_en: Graciously hear us, Lord, that we may, through penitential fasting, being enlightened by it, may easily obtain your forgiveness, even as we abstain from harmful vices.

text: Populi tui Deus institutor et rector peccata quibus impugnatur expelle ut semper tibi devotus et tuo munimine sit securus.
translation_en: God, instigator and ruler of your people, drive away the sins that attack, so that they may always be devoted to you and secure within your protection.

text: Deus qui ineffabilibus mundum renovas sacramentis: praesta quaesumus ut Ecclesia tua aeternis proficiat institutis et temporalibus foveatur auxiliis.
translation_en: God who renews the world with ineffable sacraments: grant us, we ask, that your Church may progress with eternal institutions and be fostered with temporary aids.

text: Huius nos Domine quaesumus participatio sacramenti et a propriis reatibus indesinenter expediat et ab omnibus tueatur adversis.
translation_en: Lord, we humbly ask that this participation in the sacrament may cleanse us continually from our own sins and protect us from all dangers.

text: Fiat Domine quaesumus per gratiam tuam fructuosus nostrae devotionis affectus quia tunc nobis proderunt suscepta ieiunia si tuae sint placita pietati.
translation_en: Lord, we humbly ask through Your grace may our devout feelings be fruitful, for then our fasting will benefit us if they please You according to Your piety.

text: Oblationibus nostris Domine quaesumus placare susceptis et ad te nostras etiam rebelles compelle propitius voluptates.
translation_en: Lord, we humbly ask that you accept our offerings. May those presented be pleasing to you, and even our rebellious selves, graciously move us towards you with your loving indulgence.

text: Sanctifica quaesumus Domine nostra ieiunia et per Christi tui passionem cunctarum nobis propitius indulgentiam largire culparum.
translation_en: We humbly ask you, Lord, to sanctify our fasting and through the Passion of your Son grant us merciful forgiveness for all our sins.

text: Da quaesumus Domine populo tuo salutem mentis et corporis ut bonis operibus inhaerendo tua semper mereatur protectione defendi.
translation_en: Grant, we ask You, Lord, health of mind and body to Your people, so that always meriting Your protection, they may be defended by it through good works.

text: Nostra tibi sint quaesumus Domine accepta ieiunia quae et nos per Unigeniti tui passionem expiando gratia tua dignos efficiant et ad remedia perducant aeterna.
translation_en: We humbly ask You, Lord, that our fasting may be acceptable to You. May it be, through the Passion of Your Only-Begotten Son, that we are worthy of Your grace and may lead us to eternal remedies.

text: Hostias tibi Domine deferimus immolandas quae temporalem quaesumus consolationem nobis impendant ut promissa certius speremus aeterna.
translation_en: We offer You, Lord, sacrifices that we implore may bestow temporary comfort upon us, so that we may more certainly hope for the fulfilment of eternal promises.

text: Exaudi Domine quaesumus gemitum populi supplicantis ut qui de meritorum qualitate diffidimus non iudicium sed misericordiam consequi mereamur.
translation_en: Hear us, O Lord, we humbly ask that you accept the groans of the supplicating people. May those who doubt their merit not receive judgment but mercy, so that we may deserve it.

text: Concede nobis Domine quaesumus celebraturi sancta mysteria non solum abstinentiam corporalem sed quod est potius habeamus mentium puritatem.
translation_en: Grant us, Lord, we humbly ask, not only bodily abstinence but especially mental purity as we celebrate the holy mysteries.

text: Vegetet nos Domine semper et innovet tuae mensae libatio quae fragilitatem nostram gubernet et protegat et in portum perpetuae salutis inducat.
translation_en: Nourish us, Lord, always and renew the offering on your table that may guide and protect our frailty, and lead us to the harbor of eternal salvation.

text: Cordibus nostris Domine Spiritus Sancti donum benignus infunde ut peccata nostra castigatione voluntaria cohibentes temporaliter potius maceremur quam suppliciis deputemur aeternis.
translation_en: Lord, generously pour out the gift of the Holy Spirit upon our hearts, that we may through voluntary penance restrain our sins, rather to be temporarily chastised than assigned to eternal punishments.

text: Da nobis quaesumus Domine observantiam ieiuniorum devote peragere ut cum abstinentia carnalis alimoniae sancta tibi conversatione placeamus.
translation_en: Grant us, we ask you, Lord, the diligence of the fasting ones, that we may faithfully carry it out. May our holy behavior please you through abstinence from carnal nourishment.

text: Adesto Domine fidelibus tuis et quos caelestibus reficis sacramentis a cunctis defende periculis.
translation_en: Be present, Lord, to your faithful ones and those whom you refresh with heavenly sacraments. Defend them from all dangers.

text: Tueatur quaesumus Domine dextera tua populum tuum deprecantem et purificatum dignanter erudiat ut consolatione praesenti foveatur et bona perficiat.
translation_en: We ask you, Lord, may your right hand protect your people as they pray and worthily educate those who are purified, so that they may be nourished with consolation and complete what is good.

text: Omnipotens sempiterne Deus qui humano generi ad imitandum humilitatis exemplum Salvatorem nostrum carnem sumere et crucem subire fecisti: concede propitius ut et patientiae ipsius habere documenta possimus et resurrectionis consortia mereamur.
translation_en: Almighty everlasting God, who for our imitation made it that our Savior should take on human flesh and bear the cross: grant us graciously that we may have the examples of his patience and merit the fellowship of his resurrection.

text: VD ... aeterne. Qui salutem humani generis in ligno crucis contulisti ut unde mors oriebatur inde vita resurgeret. Et qui in ligno vincebat in ligno quoque vinceretur. Per Christum Dominum.
translation_en: We beseech You, eternal one... Who bestowed the salvation of the human race upon the wood of the cross, so that where death arose, life might rise again. And who was conquering in the wood, there also He was to be conquered. Through Christ, the Lord.

text: Respice Domine quaesumus super hanc familiam tuam pro qua Dominus noster Iesus non dubitavit manibus tradi nocentium et crucis subire tormentum.
translation_en: Look upon us, Lord, we entreat you, on this family of yours for whom our Lord Jesus did not hesitate to deliver wicked hands over and suffer the torture of the cross.

text: Deus a quo et Iudas proditor reatus sui poenam et confessionis suae latro praemium sumpsit: concede nobis tuae propitiationis effectum ut sicut in passione sua Iesus Christus Dominus noster diversa utrisque intulit stipendia meritorum ita nobis ablato vetustatis errore resurrectionis suae gratiam largiatur.
