translation_en: Lord Jesus Christ, for whose love the blessed Eugenia, forgetting her possessions, wealth, and family (including siblings and relatives), having fled from her parents' home with disheveled hair, joins herself to your followers, desiring to subject her neck to your commandments. She longs to be with you, Church of yours, be present mercifully and easily appeased, so that, like this martyr of yours, we may abandon the world, scorn vain allurements, fleeting pleasures, parental concerns, and earthly cares, unhindered, most willingly overcome the trials of the present age, just as this virgin overcame the deceitful temptations of Melantius.

text: Domine Iesu Christe propitius esto mihi peccatori quia misericordia tua primus indigeo et pro consacerdotibus meis exorare praesumo quia tu es immortalis et sine peccato. Tu solus Dominus Deus noster. Tu es benedictus qui benedicis omnia. Tu es sanctus qui sanctificas omnia. Universa nobis indulge indignis famulis tuis quia peccatores sumus et indigni quod praesumimus ad sanctum altare tuum invocare te quia peccavimus coram te et coram angelis tuis sed tribue nobis indulgentiam delictorum et confirma sanctam Ecclesiam tuam in fide orthodoxa et doce nos facere voluntatem tuam omnibus diebus nostris.
translation_en: Lord Jesus Christ, have mercy on me, a sinner, for I first need your mercy and presume to pray for my priests, for you are immortal and without sin. You alone are our Lord God. You are blessed who blesses all things. You are holy who sanctifies all things. Grant us all indulgence, unworthy servants of yours, because we are sinners and unworthy that we presume to invoke you at your holy altar, because we have sinned before you and before your angels. But grant us forgiveness for our offenses and strengthen your holy Church in the orthodox faith and teach us to do your will all our days.

text: Domine Iesu Christe quem venturum esse credimus iudicem qui iamdudum in primo adventu gloriae tuae propter nostra scelera humilis venire dignatus es petimus ut dum adventus clementiae tuae secundus advenerit nostra nomina absterso peccato cum sanctis tuis facias praenotari.
translation_en: Lord Jesus Christ, whom we believe to be the coming judge, who humbly came in the first advent of Your glory due to our sins, we ask that when the second coming of Your clemency draws near, our names may be wiped clean of sin with those of Yours, and be announced among the saints.

text: Domine Iesu Christe qui beatissimo primoque martyri tuo Stephano post ictus lapidum concessisti praemium sempiternum tu sereno vultu respice hoc sacrificium nostrum et praesta nobis famulis tuis ut prece huius martyris tam viventibus quam defunctis donetur indulgentia criminum per quem olim confutata est infidelitas Iudaeorum.
translation_en: Lord Jesus Christ, who granted the eternal reward to your blessed first martyr Stephen after he was struck by stones, look upon this sacrifice of ours and grant us, your servants, that the prayer of this martyr may be given to both the living and the dead, bestowing the indulgence of sins through whom once the infidelity of the Jews was overthrown.

text: Domine Iesu Christe qui de caelis ad terram de sinu patris descendisti et in ligno crucis quinque plagas sustinuisti et sanguinem tuum pretiosum in remissionem peccatorum nostrorum effudisti te suppliciter deprecamur ut in die iudicii ad dexteram tuam statuti a te audire mereamur: »Venite benedicti in regnum patris mei«.
translation_en: Lord Jesus Christ, who descended from heaven to earth from the breast of the Father and sustained five wounds on the cross and poured out your precious blood for the remission of our sins, we humbly entreat you that on the day of judgment we may be worthy to hear from you: "Come, blessed, into the kingdom of my Father."

text: Domine Iesu Christe qui {dum} hora sexta pro redemptione mundi crucis adscendisti lignum <dum> universus mundus in tenebras conversus est illam nobis lucem in anima et corpore nostro semper tribue per quam ad aeternam vitam pervenire mereamur.
translation_en: Lord Jesus Christ, who when the sixth hour ascended upon the cross for the redemption of the world, when the whole world was turned into darkness, may that light forever be granted to us in soul and body, through which we may merit to attain eternal life.

text: Domine Deus Iesu Christe qui hora sexta pro redemptione mundi crucis lignum adscendisti ut universus mundus qui in tenebris erat illuminaretur te supplices deprecamur ut illam lucem in anima et corpore nostro semper tribuas per quam ad vitam aeternam pervenire mereamur.
translation_en: Lord God Jesus Christ, who at the sixth hour ascended the cross for the redemption of the world, that all who were in darkness might be illuminated; we humbly beseech You to always grant that light within our soul and body, through which we may merit eternal life.

text: Domine Iesu Christe qui pro mundi redemptione crucis lignum adscendisti ut universus mundus qui in tenebris erat illuminaretur illam quaesumus lucem in animas et corpora nostra semper infunde per quam ad aeternam lucem pervenire mereamur.
translation_en: Lord Jesus Christ, who ascended on the cross for the redemption of the world to enlighten all that was in darkness, we humbly ask that you pour this light into our souls and bodies, through which we may be worthy to reach eternal light.

text: Domine Iesu Christe qui hora diei sexta pro redemptione mundi crucis patibulum adscendisti et sanguinem tuum pretiosum in remissionem peccatorum nostrorum fudisti te humiliter deprecamur ut per tuae passionis et vulnerum tuorum merita post obitum nostrum paradisi ianuam gaudenter introire mereamur.
translation_en: Lord Jesus Christ, who at the sixth hour of the day ascended upon the cross for the redemption of the world and poured out your precious blood for the remission of our sins, we humbly beseech you that through the merits of your passion and wounds, after our death, we may merit to enter happily into paradise.

text: Omnipotens Deus Christiani nominis
translation_en: Almighty God of the Christian name

text: Domine Iesu Christe qui es ineffabilis bonitas et invicta potestas pro cuius nomine beatissimus Saturninus praesul et martyr dum litari aris daemonicis renuit ad Capitolium a turbis attrahitur furentisque tauri supplicio consecratur tu eius meritis et offerentium suscipe vota et omnes in commune pro tua miseratione iustifica quo exauditi pro nobis requiem etiam apud te mereamur impetrare defunctis.
translation_en: Lord Jesus Christ, who are the ineffable goodness and invincible power, for whose name the blessed Saturninus, bishop and martyr, refused to write to the demonic altars and was dragged by the furious crowd towards the Capitolium where he was consecrated by the bull of the enraged bull. Through his merits and those offering, receive his vows and all for your sake be justified, so that, heard on our behalf, we may deserve to implore rest even with you for the departed.

text: Domine Iesu Christe qui es testis fidelis primogenitus mortuorum tu requiem dona spiritibus fidelium defunctorum quo verus pontifex per hoc sacrificium populi delicta omittens sicut olim te moriente mortua corpora surrexerunt ita nunc in hac resurrectionis tuae festivitate sepulti in aeternam requiem transferantur.
translation_en: Lord Jesus Christ, who are the faithful witness and firstborn of the dead, grant to the spirits of the faithful departed the rest that, as true High Priest, through this sacrifice, you may forgive their sins, just as once the bodies of the dead rose when you died, so now on this festivity of your resurrection, those buried be transferred into eternal rest.

text: Domine Iesu Christe qui ex virgine natus unicus virginum permanes sponsus quarum tu coetui praebuisti ducatum ad caeli sedem ubi caput illarum esse voluisti assumendo matrem gloriosissimam Mariam virginem te quaesumus et rogamus ut obtentu illarum nigredine careamus omnium nostrorum facinorum.  Divina namque illa et ineffabilis mansio quae virginem hodie sumpsit sic permansuros in ea nos dextera tuae virtutis censeat ut laetos gnaviter lumen speciei tuae ibidem sine fine instituat. Nam si discreta donorum merita ibidem praerogant loca summa et ineffabilia hodie adeptura noscitur virgo mater per te Domine cui adsunt possibilia universa.  Tu es itaque Domine qui omnia ista disponis qui etiam caelestia ac terrestria pretio pacificasti sacri livoris et filios dignatus es facere gratuitae bonitatis.
translation_en:
Lord Jesus Christ, who were born from the virgin and remain as the unique spouse of all virgins, whom you granted leadership to your heavenly court where it was your will to be the head of them by assuming the most glorious virgin Mary. We humbly ask and implore that through their intercession we may be freed from the stains of our sins.
For that divine and ineffable dwelling which today took the virgin, may your right hand's virtue deem us worthy to continue residing there forever, instilling joyfully the light of your appearance without end. For if the merits of gifts are discerned there today at the highest and ineffable places, it is known through the virgin mother by you, Lord, that all things are possible.
Thus, Lord, who arranges all these things and even pacified both heavenly and earthly things with price, and who were worthy to make sons of gratuitous goodness,

text: Domine Iesu Christe qui ex voluntate patris cooperante spiritu sancto super Lazarum flere compassione humili voluisti concede nobis peccatoribus tibi in carne passo ac proximis nostris compati in hac vita tali lacrimarum rore cum tantae humilitatis radice ac tantae caritatis fervore ut post luctus et suspiria mereamur ad gloriam supernae felicitatis pervenire.
translation_en: Lord Jesus Christ, who by the will of the Father and with the help of the Holy Spirit wept over Lazarus in compassion and humility, grant us sinners that we may feel compassion for you in your flesh that suffered, and for our nearest neighbors in this life, with tears like this dew of such deep humility and intense love. May we deserve to reach the glory of supreme happiness after sorrow and sighs.

text: Domine Iesu Christe qui illuminatione tua fecisti fidem laudari martyris tui illius fac nos eius intercessione apud te commendari ut sicut ille a te caritatis amore inflammatus mundum blandientem evicit comminantem contempsit saevientem pertulit et sic ad caelum triumphator accessit ita eius intercessione placatus facias nos et despicere saeculi huius errores et vincere atque indulgentiam peccatorum nostrorum apud te ex abundanti misericordiae tuae munere obtinere.
translation_en: Lord Jesus Christ, who made the faith of your martyr shine forth to be praised, may his intercession commend us before you, so that, as he was inflamed with the love of charity and triumphed over the world with gentleness and threats unheeded, scorned the savage, bore it, and thus as a triumphant victor ascended to heaven; so may his intercession make us please you, disdain the errors of this age, conquer, and obtain indulgence for our sins through your abundant mercy.

text: Domine Iesu Christe qui in patibulo crucis suspensus patrem ex forma servi quam susceperas ut quid te derelinqueret acclamasti et ut persecutoribus veniam tribueret postulasti tuam supplices imploramus clementiam ut quod tunc pro suscepta carnis humilitate a patre expetere videbaris nunc cum eodem connexa semper divinitatis potestate consistens praestare digneris.
translation_en: Lord Jesus Christ, who, suspended on the cross, cried out to your Father in the form of a servant, asking what He had abandoned and requesting mercy for your persecutors. Now we humbly ask for your clemency, that what seemed to be asked of the Father at that time for the humility you assumed in flesh, now consistently united with the same divine power, you would deign to fulfill.

text: Domine Iesu Christe qui in patibulo crucis suspensus patrem ex forma servi quam susceperas iisdem fuisti verbis deprecatus et ut quid te derelinqueret cum ab eo non recederes acclamasti et ut iniquis ac sceleratis persecutoribus veniam tribueret postulasti atque ut spiritum tuum in suis gloriosis tibi tantummodo cognitis susciperet manibus indicasti {unde} nos exigui famuli tui tuorum sermonum tramitem secuti tuam supplices imploramus clementiam ut quod tunc pro susceptae carnis humilitate a patre expetere videbaris nunc cum eodem connexa semper divinitatis potestate consistens praestare digneris ut Ecclesiam tuam catholicam quam pretioso sanguine redemisti numquam derelinquas nobisque indignis in eandem concurrentibus et crucis tuae sollemnia celebrantibus ut criminum indulgentiam concedas precamur atque ut animas nostras in conspectu tuo semper suscipias custodias et benedicas humillima prece deposcimus. Et qui latronis tecum in cruce pendentis confessionem iustificare dignatus es omnium recte in te credentium fidem augeas multiplices et solita pietate conserves.
translation_en: Lord Jesus Christ, who on the cross were hung as a servant before the Father according to the form you had assumed for them, you prayed with those same words what would abandon you when you did not withdraw from him; you acclaimed and asked for forgiveness of iniquitous persecutors, and that your spirit be received by their hands only in its glorious knowledge; we, Your humble servants who have followed Your way, humbly implore Your clemency, that what then appeared to seek on behalf of the assumed flesh's humility from the Father, now always being united with the same divine power, You would deign to provide for Your Church which You redeemed at a precious price. We pray that You never abandon us and for the unworthy ones striving for the same, and for those celebrating the solemnity of Your cross, You grant forgiveness of sin. We also pray and humbly ask that You always receive, guard, and bless our souls. And he who deigned to justify the robber hanging on the cross with You, increases the faith of all righteously believing in You, and preserves it with His usual piety.

text: Omnipotens Deus fac nobis tibi semper devotam
translation_en: Almighty God, make us ever devoted to you

text: Domine Iesu Christe qui ita verbum caro factus es ut et conceptionem tui virginalis uterus altissimi obumbratione susciperet et ad pariendum te porta materni corporis non pateret sollemnitatis huius obsequia propitius suscipe ac nostrum quoque cor dignatus ingredere. Tibi soli sit pervium cui soli id esse cupimus praeparatum ut cum nostrarum mentium puritatem bene placitam tibi ipse perfeceris operis tui custos et perpetuus habitator esse digneris.
translation_en: Lord Jesus Christ, who became flesh in such a way that even your virginal conception was received by the utmost shadow of obedience and the gateway of your mother's body did not open for this solemnity; propitiously receive us as well, worthy to enter your court. May it be only for you who alone we desire to be prepared, that with the purity of our minds pleasing to you, you yourself may perfect the work and be worthy to be the eternal guardian and perpetual dweller.

text: Domine Iesu Christe qui mortalitatis hominem sic assumpsisti ut mortem nostram consumeres sic iugum legis in tua carne suscepisti ut a nostra carne discuteres sic circumcisus in carne corporis es ut nos sine vulnere carnis in corde purgares atque utrique sexui proficeret circumcisio spiritualis cum ex virginitate genitricis ipse vir tamquam sponsus procederes et utrumque sexum in sacramento incarnationis amplecteres suscipiens scilicet virum natum ex femina Unde veneranda illa senectus in Simeone atque Anna purgata iam aetas et defaecata sinceraque etiam in viro feminaque canities te suscipiens non destitit collaudare. Te quaesumus ut sacrum circumcisionis diem sollemnitate votiva nobis prosequentibus orationes supplicum placatus exaudias et offerentium sacrificia sanctificanda suscipias atque spiritus quiescentium quorum est facta commemoratio nominum in requiem electorum perducas.
translation_en: Lord Jesus Christ, who took upon yourself human mortality so as to consume our death, and who assumed the yoke of the law in your flesh so as to separate from our flesh, and who were circumcised in the flesh of your body so as to purify us without wounding our flesh, and who progressed in both sexes with a spiritual circumcision, as you advanced from virginity of the mother like a groom, and embraced both sexes in the sacrament of incarnation, receiving indeed the man born of woman. From where that venerable old age in Simeon and Anna was purified, the age defaced, and sincere even in man and woman, taking upon themselves gray hair, did not cease to praise you. We beg you that on this day of holy circumcision, you hear our prayers offered by us with a vow, as you graciously accept the sacrifices of the offerings and lead the spirits of those whose names are remembered in commemoration of the elect to rest.

text: Domine Iesu Christe qui olim hunc mundum incarnationis tuae visitasti praesentia quemque venturum ad iudicium cum sanctis exspectat omnis anima christiana tu nos in die adventus tui solita miseratione iustifica ut qui recurrentis anni festum incarnationis tuae hodierna die in laudibus inchoamus veniente te ad iudicium sanctorum coetibus aggregemur.
translation_en: Lord Jesus Christ, who once visited this world with your incarnation, which every Christian soul awaits as it comes to judgment with the saints. On this day of the annual festival of your incarnation, have mercy on us and justify us so that as we begin to laud you on this coming day, we may be joined with the assembly of the saints at your judgement.

text: Domine Iesu Christe qui olim venisti occultus cum apparueris manifestus assiste propitius liberaturus populum tuum ab impiorum imperio a criminum iugo ut tibi plebs tua serviat in aequitate a quo liberatur ab omni malorum oppressione.
translation_en: Lord Jesus Christ, who once came hidden and appeared manifestly, propitiously assist to free your people from the empire of the impious, from the yoke of sin, so that your people may serve you in justice, from whom they are freed from every oppression by evil.

text: Domine Iesu Christe qui sacratissimam virginem Mariam in matrem dignissimam elegisti cuius benedictam animam in vita et in morte tua doloris gladius pertransivit per passionem tuam amarissimam ac eiusdem matris tuae dilectissimae dolores et angustias nos quaesumus in vita et in morte misericorditer tueri digneris quatenus a cunctis cruciatibus et doloribus post mortem liberi resurrectionis tuae gloria perfruamur.
translation_en: Lord Jesus Christ, who chose the most worthy Virgin Mary as your mother, whose blessed soul was pierced by the sword of sorrow during your most bitter passion, and whose most beloved sorrows and anguish of your own mother, we humbly ask that you graciously protect us in life and death. May we be worthy to enjoy the glory of your resurrection, free from all sufferings and pain after death.

text: Domine Iesu Christe qui temetipsum in cruce holocaustum immaculatum Deo patri spontaneum obtulisti quaesumus ut eiusdem sacrificii quod perfecimus oblatio veneranda indulgentiam nobis obtineat et gloriam sempiternam.
translation_en: Lord Jesus Christ, who offered yourself as a spotless holocaust on the cross to the eternal Father, we humbly ask that the offering of the same sacrifice which we have made may obtain for us a worthy indulgence and eternal glory.

text: Domine Iesu Christe qui vera es vita credentium tibi pro defunctis fidelibus sacrificium istud offerimus obsecrantes ut regenerationis fonte purgatos et temptationibus mundi exemptos beatorum numero digneris inserere et quos fecisti adoptionis participes iubeas hereditatis tuae esse consortes.
translation_en: Lord Jesus Christ, who are truly the life of believers, we offer this sacrifice to you on behalf of the faithful departed. We humbly ask that you cleanse them with the font of regeneration and free them from the trials of the world. May you graciously include them in the number of the blessed, and command those whom you have made your adopted children to be heirs of your inheritance together with you.

text: Domine Iesu Christe qui vivificaturus occideris qui resurrecturus sepeliris dum morte tua mortuos solvis dum poenam superas crucifixus tu ad preces nostras illa qua totum pateris pietate converte et nostris iam calamitatibus finem pone sicque reddita nobis indulgentia miserere ut qui adversante gravium culparum impressione nos egisse sentimus iterum te ad nos misericordia parcente conversum redeunte quietis statu et meliorum rerum commodis potiamur.
translation_en: Lord Jesus Christ, who vivifies while you die, who resurrects while you are buried, as your death releases the dead, and as you endure the cross to atone for our sins; turn with your paternal compassion towards our prayers. Grant an end to our calamities, so that, receiving mercy, we may rejoice once again in your return, feeling your merciful presence converting us and returning to us a state of peace and better circumstances.

text: Domine Iesu Christe rex aeterne qui pulchritudinem animarum nostrarum omnimodis et concupiscis et perficis praesta nobis quaesumus famulis tuis virginis et martyris tuae Marinae intercessu ut et honorem et timorem quo te veneremur et timeamus in nobis pius ac benignus infundas.
translation_en: Lord Jesus Christ, eternal King, who delight in the beauty of our souls in all ways and satisfy and perfect it, grant us, your servants, we pray, through the intercession of your virgin and martyr Marina, that you may imbue within us a pious and kind fear, the honor and reverence with which we revere and fear you.

text: Domine Iesu Christe sanctarum cogitationum suspirator qui servos tuos gloriosam matrem tuam honorare docuisti concede propitius ipsius sollemni cum sacrificio laudem debita cum devotione celebrare in terris ut eius intercessione regnando iubilare mereamur in caelis.
translation_en: Lord Jesus Christ, who taught your servants to honor your glorious mother with holy thoughts and sighs, graciously grant that we may celebrate the fitting praise with devotion on her solemnity with sacrifice here on earth. May we deserve to rejoice in heaven because of her intercession while ruling.

text: Domine Iesu Christe sanctorum claritas meritorum et vera beatificatarum felicitas animarum dona ut qui tuae resurrectionis diem laetando colimus et litando resurgere ipsi per gratiam tuam bene sancteque vivendo et paci tuae consentiendo ante nostrum obitum mereamur. Et sicut tibi pro tantae festivitatis officio amictus in nobis candidos exhibemus ita per indulgentiam tuam dealbati supra Nivern atque mundati et geminae dilectionis dulcedine satiati universi criminis nigredine careamus.
translation_en: Lord Jesus Christ, brightness of the saints and true beatific happiness of souls, grant that we who rejoice in your resurrection day may merit to rise ourselves through your grace by living well and holy and consenting to your peace before our death. And just as you, for such great festivity, present yourself clothed in us with pure garments, so too may we, through your indulgence, be made white above Nivardus (Nivern) and cleansed, and satiated with the sweetness of double love, be freed from all stain of sin.

text: Domine Iesu Christe tuarum pastor ovium suscipe placatus hoc nostrae devotionis sacrificium quod tuae offerimus maiestati in eorum recordatione de quorum sollemniter hodierna congaudemus divisione.
translation_en: Lord Jesus Christ, Shepherd of Your sheep, receive our offering, pleasing to You, which we present to Your majesty in remembrance of those whom we joyfully remember today by their division.

text: Domine Iesu Christe unigenitus Filius Dei patris qui Lazarum suscitaturus elevatis sursum oculis patri tuo gratias agis praesta nobis famulis tuis ut eo fremitu spiritus quo illum suscitasti ad vitam ea quoque modificatione digneris haec oblata tibi sanctificare libamina ut percipientes gratiam corporis et sanguinis tui in visceribus nostris habeamus partem tecum in saeculis sempiternis.
translation_en: Lord Jesus Christ, only-begotten Son of God the Father, who raised Lazarus with a lifted gaze to your Father, grant us, your servants, that we may be made partakers of the same breath by which you raised him to life. Deign also, by this offering, to sanctify these gifts, so that receiving the grace of your body and blood, we may have a part with you in eternal ages.

text: Domine misericordiarum et Deus summae perfectaeque bonitatis qui peccatorum propitiationem ieiuniis orationibus et eleemosynis quaerendam et obtinendam esse monstrasti respicere dignare ad hanc humilitatis nostrae confessionem ut qui inclinamur conscientia nostra erigamur misericordia tua.
translation_en: Lord of mercy and God of supreme perfect goodness, who have shown that the atonement for sins is to be sought and obtained through fasting, prayers, and alms, deign to look upon this humility of ours. Regard our confession, so that we, who bend with a guilty conscience, may rise up with your mercy.

text: Domine quem vocantem sancti apostoli Iacobus et Ioannes fide integra sunt secuti et quem sequentes ex caritate integra sunt electi ut mundi piscatores fierent qui profundi retia reliquissent auribus percipe quaesumus orationem nostram et tribue ut dum apostolicos triumphos admiramur et colimus si assequi eorum facta non possumus implere saltem monita contendamus.
translation_en: Lord, who are called the holy apostles James and John, have followed with an unwavering faith. Those following them with an integral love are chosen to become fishers of men, leaving their nets in the depths behind their ears. Hear our prayer, we beseech you, and grant that while we admire and worship the apostolic triumphs, if we cannot achieve their deeds, at least let us strive for their teachings.

text: Domine qui ambulanti de virtute in virtutem sancto Stephano martyri tuo aperuisti caelos ad gloriam contemplationis quos ei aperueras ad meritum sanctitatis ut confessionis suae fructum caperet ostende nobis suffragio eius misericordiam tuam.
translation_en: Lord, who opened the heavens to Your saint Stephen, the martyr, as he walked in virtue to virtue, show us Your mercy through his intercession, so that we may reap the fruit of his confession.

text: Domine qui beatissimis apostolis tuis Iacobo et Ioanni gloriam martyrii bibitione tui calicis praedixisti ut et confirmares responsionem quam fides pura protulerat et conferres virtutem quam caritas devota praesumpserat hanc eorum passionis memoriam Ecclesiam tuam sollemniter celebrantem placatus intende. Prosit quaesumus commemoratio sanctorum beatissimorum ad obtinendum tuae miserationis auditum. Prosit apostolorum titulos recolere ut maiestatis tuae aures oratio nostra valeat inclinare. Prosit supplicare patrociniis ut digneris exaudire suffragiis.
translation_en: Lord, who foretold the glory of your martyrdom to the most blessed apostles James and John through the drinking of your chalice, so that you might confirm the response which pure faith had proclaimed and confer the power which devout charity had presumed. May this remembrance of their passion move your Church, celebrating it solemnly, to be favorable. We pray that the commemoration of the most blessed saints may help us to obtain the hearing of your mercy. May remembering the titles of the apostles make our prayer worthy to bend your majesty's ear. May supplication through their patronage move you to grant us hearing through our prayers.

text: Domine qui beatissimos apostolos tuos Petrum et Paulum diverso tempore vocationis beneficio elegisti et uno die passionis merito coronasti quorum admirabilis singulorum fides ante obitum mortis illatae unum fecit claves regni caelestis accipere alium usque ad caelum tertium penetrare cum ille censor credentium constitutus intromittendi illic probos et excludendi improbos ius teneret hic in excessu supra nubium raptus recessus ineffabilia divinorum secreta verborum futurus gentium doctor hauriret quodque ne alii sanctorum passi hoc isti meruere passuri. Hos nobis Domine facito esse patronos quos fecisti esse magistros ut eorum obtentu veniae nostrae suffragia sentiamus quorum in ducatu gratiae tuae instituta suscepimus.  In Petro peccatorum nostrorum numerum amplificatae modus remissionis excedat; in Paulo viam obstructam perfidiae Christi sermo lumine nobis veritatis aperiat. In illo nobis praestetur nutantis saeculi fluctibus non dimergi; in isto antiqui serpentis morsibus non noceri ut nec naufragio malorum perditi nec veneno vipereo sauciati eodem auctore salvemur quo ille undas superavit hic viperas conculcavit.
translation_en:
Lord, who chose your blessed apostles Peter and Paul at different times through the blessing of calling, and on one day merited to crown them with martyrdom; whose admirable faith before the death of their martyrdom made one receive the keys of the kingdom of heaven until the third day he entered there, with him appointed as the judge of believers, entering in to sift the good from the bad. He, being taken up beyond the clouds, withdrew into ineffable divine secrets; who would gather teachings for the nations. Those same sufferings that others saints merited to undergo, these two earned.
Lord, make these be our patrons whom you made masters, so that we may feel their intercession's support through their mercy's grant, which we have accepted in your grace's government.
In Peter, let the number of our sins exceed the measure of remission; in Paul, let the way obstructed by the treachery of Christ open for us with light of truth. Let him not be harmed by the fluctuating waves of this world; may he not be bitten by the ancient serpent's venom such that neither those shipwrecked by evil nor those poisoned by the viper perish, but may we be saved by the same author who overcame the waves and trampled the vipers.

text: Domine qui per os David locutus es: »Vovete et reddite Domino Deo vestro« te suppliciter exoramus ut famulum tuum illum vigilanter custodias tuearis ac defendas et oblationem quam pro ipso tibi offerimus interveniente sancto archangelo Michaele clementer ac benigniter suscipias; accende igitur Domine cor famuli tui illius igne timoris tui vel desiderii tui ut et sanctorum patriarcharum exempli imitator efficiatur et in boni operis testimonio firmus ac stabilis perseveret.
translation_en: Lord, who spoke through the mouth of David: "Vow and pay to the Lord your God," we humbly beseech you to watch over, protect, and defend your servant, and graciously and benevolently receive the offering which we present on his behalf with Saint Michael the Archangel intervening. Therefore, Lord, kindle the heart of your servant with the fire of your fear or desire, that he may become an imitator of the examples of the holy patriarchs and be firm and stable in the testimony of good works, persevering.

text: Domine qui sanctis pro merito servitutis in caelo praemia excelsa donasti ut laetarentur sancto conspectu tuo perpetuae lucis gratia pateretur praesta ut sacerdotes tui te credentes simili dignatione respecti per baptismum sacrationis corporum peccata deponant ut ad laetitiam aeternam perveniant. Commemorationem facientes defunctorum fidelium illis praeteritorum noxa laxentur et aeternae vitae praemia condonentur ut et vivis haec oblatio prosit ad salutem et defunctis ad requiem.
translation_en: Lord, who have given rewards fitting for the merits of service in heaven to the saints, grant that they may rejoice before your face with the grace of perpetual light. Provide that your priests, believing in you, may be respected with a similar dignity through baptism and lay aside their sins, so that they may attain eternal joy. As we make commemoration for the departed faithful, let the past offenses be loosed for them, and let their rewards for eternal life be forgiven, so that this offering may also profit the living for salvation and the dead for peace.

text: Domine qui virtute spiritus tui et eorum qui veteris confusionis superbiae turrem aedificabant proturbasti auditum et surgentis Ecclesiae tuae novitatem diffusis linguis multiplicasti insignibus ut quod fuerat in condemnatione esset in munere atque inde construere; fidem unde destruxeras vanitatem da super hunc familiae tuae supplicem coetum Spiritus Sancti tui quem es pollicitus et largitus adventum qui in nobis et contrariae molitionis studia adversa dispergat et meritum sanctificationis accumulet. Sitque munerator in promissione qui est promissus in munere quo Ecclesia tua eius igne succensa in ipso veram teneat fidem a quo omnem percipit veritatem. Ipseque offerentium nomina caelestibus scribat in paginis ac requiem dignetur praestare defunctis qui in unitate deitatis tecum permanet semper aequalis.
translation_en: Lord, who with the power of your Spirit and those who were building the tower of Babel in their pride of the ancient confusion, overthrew and scattered the news of your Church with various tongues to make what was in condemnation a gift, and from there construct; grant faith where you destroyed vanity for this humble assembly of your Holy Spirit, which you have promised and bestowed. May he disperse contrary desires and accumulate the merit of sanctification among us. May he be the giver in the promise who is promised in the gift, through which your Church remains with true faith in him from whom all receives truth. And may he write the names of those offering on heavenly pages and grant them rest who in the unity of the Trinity remain always equal to you.

text: Domine rex gloriae qui patefactis prophetarum oraculis tamquam elevatis aeternalibus portis paternam repetis sedem quia dum tua deitas eo quo numquam discessit regreditur humano generi caelorum aditus aperitur dona ut illic extendatur nostra intentio quo praecessit nostra redemptio nec inhaereamus captiva delectatione terrenis qui te regnantem confitemur in caelis quo prece humilitatis nostrae placatus ex illa maiestatis qua resides sede et viventes repleas donis et pausantium spiritus consoleris.
translation_en: Lord, King of glory, who unveiled the prophecies of the prophets as if opening eternal gates and returned to your Fatherly throne when your divinity never departed from there. The gates of heaven are opened for the human race, so that our intention may be extended there where our redemption has preceded. May we not cling to the captivating delight of earthly things, but confess you as reigning in the heavens; and may you be appeased by our humble prayer from the majesty where you reside and fill us with gifts while we live, and comfort the spirits of those who rest.

text: Domine Salvator noster qui de fluctibus huius saeculi bonorum animas suscipere dignatus es animam quoque famuli tui illius assumere dignare et eum ad portum aeternae quietis admitte ut caelestibus fruatur bonis et gaudeat se malis evasisse tormentis.
translation_en: Lord, our Savior who has deigned to receive the souls of the good from the storms of this world, deign also to assume the soul of your servant and admit him into the port of eternal peace. May he enjoy heavenly goods and rejoice that he has escaped the torments.

text: Domine sancte Pater aeterne omnipotens Deus in cuius nomine beatae Eulaliae virginis ac martyris tuae sollemnia celebramus quae dum ad confessionem duceretur non illam mortis timor intravit nec vultus pallor obsedit non ira terruit comminantis non dira vox non cruenta manus non etiam torvus adspectus a proposita passione submovit tu nobis martyris huius gaudentibus de triumpho et ad te convertendi aditum praebe et sanctae conversationis tribuito dignitatem concedens per hanc oblationem a nobis tibi oblatam et offerentibus perennis gratiae lucrum et defunctis aeternae repausationis solatium.
translation_en: Lord, holy Father eternal, almighty God, in whose name we celebrate the feast of the blessed Eulalia, virgin and martyr. When she was led to confession, neither fear of death entered her, nor did paleness overtake her face, nor did anger terrify her as threats were made, nor did a terrible voice nor bloody hands nor even an harsh gaze move her from her proposed passion. Grant us, rejoicing in the triumph of this martyr, the means to turn and return to you, and grant to the holy way of life dignity. Graciously conceding through this offering we bring to you and those who offer, the eternal reward of grace and the eternal rest for the dead.

text: Domine sancte Pater omnipotens aeterne Deus creator humanae substantiae qui Verbum tuum in virginis uterum venire voluisti supplicantium tibi preces benignus intende.
translation_en: Lord, holy Father, almighty and eternal God, creator of the human substance, who willed that your Word should come into the womb of the Virgin, listen kindly to our prayers.

text: Domine sancte Pater omnipotens aeterne Deus cuius spiritu totum corpus ecclesiae multiplicatur et regitur conserva in nova familiae tuae progenie sanctificationis gratiam quam dedisti ut corpore et mente renovati puram tibi animam cum securitate pacis et purum pectus semper exhibeant.
translation_en: Lord, holy Father almighty eternal God, whose spirit the whole body of the Church is multiplied and governed, conserve in your new family the grace of sanctification which you have given, so that renewed in body and mind, they may always present to you a pure soul with the security of peace and a clean heart.

text: Domine sancte Pater omnipotens aeterne Deus da nobis gratia tuae dignationis augeri et mortalitatis conscientia trepidos pietatis eruditione confirma ut te omnia in omnibus operante profectus gregis tui sit forma pastoris.
translation_en: Lord, holy Father, almighty eternal God, grant us the grace of your mercy to be increased, and confirm our awareness of mortality with the learning of piety, so that in all things, the progress of your flock may be the form of a shepherd.

text: Domine sancte Pater omnipotens aeterne Deus da servis tuis hunc caritatis affectum ut bona pro malis reddere tuo incitentur exemplo et de inimicis suis correctione magis cupiant quam ultione gaudere.
translation_en: Lord, holy Father, almighty and eternal God, grant your servants this affection of charity, that they may be moved to render good for evil by your example, and may desire the correction of their enemies more than to rejoice in vengeance.

text: Domine sancte Pater omnipotens aeterne Deus de abundantia misericordiarum tuarum famulos et famulas tuas praesta locupletes praesta securos ut confirmati benedictionibus tuis abundent in omni gratiarum actione teque perpetua exsultatione benedicant.
translation_en: Lord, holy Father, almighty and eternal God, from the abundance of your mercies, grant us, your servants, both men and women, to be abundantly blessed, grant us security, so that confirmed by your blessings, we may abound in every act of gratitude, and bless you perpetually with endless exultation.

text: Domine sancte Pater omnipotens aeterne Deus gratiae tuae in nobis dona prosequere et quod possibilitas non habet fragilitatis humanae tuo spiritu miseratus impende ut sacris altaribus servientes et fidei integritate fundati et mentis sint claritate conspicui.
translation_en: Lord, holy Father, almighty eternal God, grant Your grace upon us and follow through where human frailty cannot. Bless us with Your compassion so that those serving at the sacred altars, founded in the integrity of faith, may be conspicuous in spiritual clarity.

text: Domine sancte Pater omnipotens aeterne Deus oblationes familiae tuae propitiatus intende ut haec piae devotionis obsequia et rectores sanctificent et regendos.
translation_en: Lord, holy Father, almighty and eternal God, incline Your attention towards the offerings of Your family, so that these acts of pious devotion may consecrate and guide those who lead and govern.

text: Domine sancte Pater omnipotens aeterne Deus propitiare digneris supplicationibus nostris et mitte angelum tuum sanctum nobiscum qui nos a cunctis adversitatibus protegat et in servitio sancti nominis tui ubique custodiat ut nullus nos iri via nostra decipiat inimicus sed ut mereamur ab omni hoste triumphum et tuae miserationis semper subsidium quatenus tua iussa complentes sospites ad propria redeamus.
translation_en: Lord, holy Father, almighty and eternal God, have mercy on our supplications and send your holy angel to be with us. May he protect us from all adversities and guard us wherever we serve in your holy name, so that no enemy may deceive us on our way. Instead, may we deserve the triumph over every foe and always find support in your mercy. Grant that as we fulfill your commands we may return safely to our own.

text: Domine sancte Pater omnipotens aeterne Deus qui benedictionis tuae gratiam aegris infundendo corporibus facturam tuam multiplici pietate custodis ad invocationem nominis tui benignus assiste et hunc famulum tuum illum liberatum ab aegritudine et sanitate donatum dextera tua erigas virtute confirmes potestate tuearis et Ecclesiae tuae sanctisque altaribus tuis cum omni desiderata prosperitate restituas.
translation_en: Lord, holy Father almighty eternal God, who pour out your blessing's grace upon the sick bodies, and preserve them with Your abundant mercy, be gracious in response to Your name's invocation. Assist this, Your servant, released from illness, and grant him health. Raise him up with Your right hand, confirm him with virtue, protect him, and restore him and all that is desired for the Church and Your holy altars to prosperity.

text: Domine sancte Pater omnipotens aeterne Deus qui contulisti fidelibus tuis remedium vitae post mortem ut somnum esse sentiant quibus paradisus patet da ut coniunctio labiorum copulum efficiatur animarum et ministerium osculi perpetuae proficiat caritati et praesta ut quod in nomine electi tui Sigismundi pro infirmantibus petimus celeriter consequamur.
translation_en: Lord, holy Father, almighty everlasting God, who have provided a remedy for life after death to your faithful ones so that they may feel sleep when the paradise is open to them, grant that the union of lips might make the union of souls and that the ministry of the kiss might perpetually advance charity, and grant that what we ask in the name of your chosen one Sigismund for the sick, may be swiftly fulfilled.

text: Domine sancte Pater omnipotens aeterne Deus qui contulisti fidelibus tuis remedium vitae post mortem ut somnum esse sentiant quibus paradisus patet praesta quaesumus ut quod fideliter in nomine electi tui Sigismundi pro infirmantibus petimus celeriter consequamur.
translation_en: Lord, holy Father, almighty and eternal God, who have given remedy of life after death to your faithful, so that they may sense sleep when paradise is open for them, grant us, we pray, that what we faithfully ask in the name of your chosen one, Sigismund, for the sick may be swiftly attained.

text: Omnipotens et misericors Deus quaesumus immensam pietatem
translation_en: Almighty and merciful God, we humbly ask for your immeasurable compassion.

text: Domine sancte Pater (omnipotens aeterne Deus) qui contulisti fidelibus tuis remedium vitae post mortem et sanitatis donum post languoris taedium da ut haec celebrata mysteria famulo tuo illi proficiant et ministerium hoc omnibus cum gratiarum (actione) perpetua proficiat caritate et praesta ut quod fideliter in nomine electi tui Sigismundi pro infirmantibus petimus celeriter consequamur.
translation_en: Lord, holy Father (omnipotent eternal God), who have given to your faithful a remedy for life after death and a gift of health after the weariness of illness, grant that these mysteries celebrated may profit your servant and that this service may benefit all with perpetual gratitude. And pray that what we ask for faithfully in the name of your chosen one, Sigismund, for those who are sick, may be swiftly obtained.

text: Domine sancte Pater omnipotens (aeterne) Deus qui dignaris infima et abiecta non despicis attolle quos suscitas et guberna quos erigis; da mihi famulo tuo sufficientiam commissi moderaminis; da Ecclesiae tuae pacem cui me praeesse voluisti ut in uno eodemque spiritu sit tibi grata devotio et plebis et praesulis.
translation_en: Lord, holy Father almighty (eternal) God, who deigns not to despise the lowly and humbled, lift up those whom you raise and govern those whom you establish; give to your servant sufficientness for the commission entrusted to me; give peace to your Church, where you willed me to preside, so that in one and the same Spirit may there be pleasing devotion both to you and to the people and bishops.

text: Domine sancte Pater omnipotens aeterne Deus qui es ductor sanctorum et dirigis itinera iustorum dirige angelum pacis nobiscum qui nos ad loca destinata perducat. Sit nobis comitatus iucundus ut nullus viae nostrae subripiat inimicus. Procul a nobis sit malignorum accessus et comes nobis dignetur esse Spiritus Sanctus.
translation_en: Lord, holy Father, almighty and eternal God, who art the guide of saints and directest the paths of the righteous, direct the angel of peace towards us, that he may lead us to our predestined places. May our companionship be pleasant, so no enemy may rob us on our way. Far from us be the approach of the wicked, and may the Holy Spirit graciously be our companion.

text: Omnipotens et misericors Deus qui benedixisti horrea
translation_en: Almighty and merciful God, who has blessed the granaries

text: Domine sancte Pater omnipotens aeterne Deus qui fragilitatem condicionis nostrae infusa virtutis tuae dignatione confirmas ut salutaribus remediis pietatis tuae corpora nostra et membra vegetentur super hunc famulum tuum propitiatus intende ut omni necessitate corporea infirmitatis exclusa gratia in eo pristinae sanitatis perfecta reparetur.
translation_en: Lord, holy Father almighty eternal God, who confirm our fragile condition with the dignity of your power that our bodies and members may grow healthily upon this your servant. Direct your attention so that all bodily necessities are excluded due to infirmity and the grace in him is restored perfectly to the pristine state of health.

text: Domine sancte Pater omnipotens aeterne Deus qui me nulla praeditum fiducia meritorum ineffabilis gratiae munere familiae tuae praesidere tribuisti attolle quos suscitas et guberna quos erigis ut quorum auctor tu bonorum sis ipse perfector.
translation_en: Lord, holy Father, almighty and eternal God, who have bestowed upon me, unworthy as I am, the ineffable grace of your family's protection; exalt, uphold, and guide those whom you raise up and rule over. Let yourself be the author of their good works and the perfector thereof.

text: Omnipotens et misericors Deus qui es doctor cordium
translation_en: Almighty and merciful God, who art the teacher of hearts

text: Domine sancte Pater omnipotens aeterne Deus respice super hunc famulum tuum qui ab infesta saeculi tempestate demersus flebili lamentatione suos accusat excessus ut fletus ac gemitus eius pie suscipias eumque de tenebris ad lumen revoces et medelam confitenti salutem paenitenti et vulnerato auxilium sanitatis indulgeas. Nec ultra inimicus in eius habeat animam potestatem. Cuiusque confessionem libenter admittens Ecclesiae tuae purificatum restitue ac tuo altario repraesenta ut ad sacramentum reconciliationis admissum una nobiscum nomini tuo gratias agere mereatur.
translation_en: Lord, holy Father, almighty and eternal God, look upon this, your servant, who submerged in the hostile tempest of this world laments his excesses with weeping and groans. May you graciously receive him, and bring him out of darkness into light, give him health to the penitent and help to the wounded. Indulge him with salvation for the confessing, healing for the afflicted, and may no enemy have power over his soul. Willingly accepting his confession, the Church restores the purified and presents him on your altar, so that he may join us in giving thanks to your name after receiving the sacrament of reconciliation.

text: Omnipotens et misericors Deus qui famulos tuos in hac domo
translation_en: Almighty and merciful God, who has servants in this house

text: Domine sancte Pater omnipotens aeterne Deus supplices te deprecamur ut misericordiam tuam iugiter nobis concedas sufficienter messium copias et fructuum omnium largiter tribuas vineae quoque substantiam abundantem arborum fetus proventus omnium rerum atque ab his omnibus pestiferum sidus tempestatis universas procellas et grandines amovere digneris.
translation_en: Lord, holy Father, almighty and eternal God, we humbly beseech you to always grant us your mercy sufficiently abundant harvests and fruits of all kinds, lavishly bestow the rich yield of the vine, a bountiful produce from all trees, and from all things, remove the harmful star, all tempests, storms, and hailstorms.

text: Omnipotens et misericors Deus qui necessitatem humani generis
translation_en: Almighty and merciful God, who is the necessity of the human race

text: Domine sancte Pater omnipotens aeterne Deus te fideliter deprecamur ut accipienti fratri nostro illi sacrosanctam hanc eucharistiam corporis et sanguinis Domini nostri Iesu Christi Filii tui tam corporis quam animae sit salus.
translation_en: Lord, holy Father almighty eternal God, we humbly beseech You to grant our brother this most sacred Eucharist of the body and blood of Our Lord Jesus Christ, Your Son, be it for his body and soul a salvation.

text: Domine sancte Pater qui nobis ore Filii tui quidquid orantes te petituri simus exaudiri nos promisisti exaudi quaesumus preces nostras et fac nos dignos tuae interesse frequentationi.
translation_en: Lord, holy Father, who promised us that we should be heard when we pray to Your Son, hear our prayers and make us worthy to participate in Your presence.

text: Domini ac Dei nostri sempiterni gloriam deprecemur orantes uti hoc sacrificium sua benedictione benedicat et Sancti Spiritus sui rore perfundat ut accipientibus universis legitima sit eucharistia.
translation_en: We pray to our Lord and God, the eternal one, that He may bless this sacrifice with His blessing and anoint it with the dew of His Holy Spirit, so that for all who receive it, the Eucharist may be legitimate.

text: Dominum Deum nostrum fratres carissimi in hac nostri humiliatione ieiunii supplices deprecemur ut observantia quam corporaliter exhibemus mentibus etiam valeamus exercere sinceris et castigatio nostrorum corporum <ad> profectum militet animarum.
translation_en: We humbly beseech our dear brothers, the Lord our God, during this humiliation and fasting, that not only do we show observance corporally but also that we are able to exercise it sincerely with our minds, so that the discipline of our bodies may contribute to the progress of our souls.

text: Domum tuam Domine quaesumus propitiatus illustra et subditorum tibi fidelium corda purifica ut bene placitis inhaerendo cuncta quae bona sunt mereantur accipere.
translation_en: Lord, we humbly ask that your graciousness shines upon your house. Purify the hearts of your faithful subjects so that they may merit to receive all good things as they strive to please you well.

text: Domum tuam quaesumus Domine clementer ingredere et in tuorum tibi corda fidelium perpetuam constitue mansionem ut cuius aedificatione subsistit huius fiat habitatione praeclara.
translation_en: We humbly ask you, Lord, to enter your house gently and establish a permanent dwelling in the hearts of your faithful, so that through this building, it becomes a distinguished abode.

text: Domum tuam quaesumus Domine clementer ingredere et in tuorum cordibus fidelium perpetuam tibi construe mansionem.
translation_en: We humbly ask you, Lord, to enter your house gently and build a permanent dwelling place for you within the hearts of your faithful people.

text: Domum tuam quaesumus Domine continuis auge subsidiis eamque de lapidibus vivis id est fidelibus tuis ita semper aedifica ut eam in perpetuum possidere digneris.
translation_en: We ask you, Lord, to continually increase your household with continual support and build it from living stones, that is, your faithful ones, so that you may always deem worthy of possessing it forever.

text: Omnipotens et misericors Deus qui sacerdotum ministerio
translation_en: Almighty and merciful God, who through the ministry of the priesthood

text: Dona Domine virtutem populo tuo et effice nos templum Spiritus Sancti ut tibi de corde puro holocaustum acceptabile praeparemus.
translation_en: Lord, grant thy power to thy people and make us a temple of the Holy Spirit, that we may prepare for thee from a pure heart an acceptable holocaust.

text: Dona nobis Domine Deus noster in custodienda pace tuum donum tuumque depositum custodire et sic in omnibus sequi quam ipse iubeas et tribuis caritatem ut in aliquibus culpas noverimus odisse non animas finem optare criminis non salutis; sic cunctis concordia sit amore ut discordiam nec inferre ulli liceat nec referre.
translation_en: Grant us, O Lord our God, the ability to keep your peace and your gift that you have entrusted to us, and thus in all things follow as you command, and bestow charity so that we may know not to desire the end of souls through sins, but rather salvation; thus let harmony be with love among all, so that no one is allowed to inflict discord or refer it.

text: Omnipotens et misericors Deus qui ubique praesens es
translation_en: Almighty and merciful God, who art everywhere present

text: Dona nobis omnipotens Deus martyris tui illius celebrantibus festum sincerae pacis et caritatis affectum ut qui in honorem eius tibi sacrificium deferimus laudis nobis a te impetremus donaria caritatis.
translation_en: Grant to us, almighty God, the feelings of sincere peace and charity during the celebration of your martyr's feast, so that we who offer you a sacrifice in his honor may through him request from you gifts of charity for ourselves.

text: Dona nobis omnipotens Pater per mysterium crucis unigeniti tui ut venenum serpentis antiqui quod fideles nititur propinare per illud medicamentum quod Christi manavit latere possit a fidelium pectoribus expurgari quosque transgressio praecepti de paradiso expulit confessio nominis Christi in paradiso reformet.
translation_en: Grant to us, Almighty Father, through the mystery of your only-begotten Son, the Cross, that the venom of the ancient serpent which the faithful are obliged to drink might be purged from their hearts by the medicine of Christ's Passion; and that those whom the transgression of the commandment drove out of Paradise may be restored through confession of the name of Christ in Paradise.

text: Dona quaesumus omnipotens Deus cunctae familiae tuae hanc voluntatem Christo filio tuo domino nostro venienti in operibus iustis apte occurrere ut eius dexterae sociati regnum mereantur possidere caeleste.
translation_en: We humbly ask you, Almighty God, that for all your families this will (their) desire meet appropriately the coming Christ, your Son, our Lord, in just works, so that they may deserve to possess the heavenly kingdom on his right hand.

text: Donis caelestibus cum sanctorum tuorum recordatione satiati gratias tibi referimus.
translation_en: With the gifts from heaven, having been satisfied with the remembrance of your saints, we offer our thanks to you.

text: Donis caelestibus da quaesumus Domine libera mente servire ut munera quae deferimus et medelam nobis operentur et gloriam.
translation_en: We humbly ask you, Lord, to grant us freedom of mind to serve with gifts from heaven, that the offerings we bring and the remedy may work for us, and bring glory.

text: Omnipotens sempiterne Deus a cuius facie caeli
translation_en: Almighty everlasting God, from whose face the heavens

text: Donis caelestibus da quaesumus Domine libera mente servire ut munera quae deferimus interveniente evangelista tuo Luca et medelam nobis operentur et gloriam.
translation_en: We humbly ask you, Lord, to grant us through your heavenly gifts, a free mind to serve, so that the offerings we bring, with your Evangelist Luke present, may work on us and bring glory.

text: Dono pacis ac tuae dilectionis rogamus Deus ut ieiunantium corda praemunias et huius oblationis nostrae libamina benedicas. Gratuita quoque nos sanctificatione perlustrans et votivae abstinentiae hanc suscipe hostiam et corda nostra tuae semper caritatis ubertate multiplica.
translation_en: We ask you, God, to bestow peace and grant us your favor. Protect the hearts of those who fast and bless the offering we present. May you also sanctify us with your grace and accept this votive offering made by our abstinence. Multiply our hearts always with the abundance of your love.

text: Donorum omnium Deus auctor et largitor qui sanctorum virtute multiplici Ecclesiae tuae sacrum corpus exornas da eam in ipsorum defendi prece membrorum de quorum excellentia gloriatur.
translation_en: God, the author and bestower of all gifts, who adorns Your Church with the multiplied virtue of the saints, grant her to be defended by their prayers through the excellence of whose members she boasts.

text: Omnipotens sempiterne Deus adesto magnae pietatis
translation_en: Almighty everlasting God, be present in great mercy

text: Dulcedinem tui amoris immitte quaesumus Domine mentibus nostris ut perceptione corporis et sanguinis tui laetificati beati Taurini meritis mereamur semper ab omnibus periculis defendi.
translation_en: We humbly ask, Lord, to send the sweetness of your love into our minds, that being enlightened by the perception of your body and blood, we may deserve through the merits of blessed Taurinus to be always protected from all dangers.

text: Ecce antistes verissimus et martyr tuus Babilas incomparabili illo tuae Christe dilectionis affectu permotus gliscit animo exsultat voto ac laudationis iucundatur tripudio quod pro tuo nomine boiarum ponderibus illigatus pedibusque revinctus in rota quasi luiturus quod professus fuerat iubetur urbe monstrari quo potius plus inde sumeret gaudii quod pro tuo nomine dignus esset contumeliam pati.  Ob hoc in tanti martyris gloriosae celebritatis sollemnitate offerentes tibi Christe sacrificium humiliati cordis et vivorum vota offerimus et sepultis requiem flagitamus rogantes ut qui martyrem tuum liberum effecisti ab illatis suppliciis et viventes et defunctos a tormentis eruas et praesentibus et futuris.
translation_en:
Behold, the most genuine bishop and your martyr Babylas, moved by an incomparable affection for Christ, trembles with joy, is filled with desire and delight in vows and praise, dances with jubilation because for your name he was bound with weights like a bull on a wheel, as if he were about to be slaughtered, which he had been declared. He is ordered to be shown in the city so that he might take more joy from it, since he was worthy to endure contempt for your name.
For this reason, in the solemnity of this glorious martyr's renown, we offer you, Christ, a sacrifice of humbled hearts and living vows, and we implore rest for the dead. We pray that you who have made your martyr free from afflictions and have released the living and the dead from torments, may be present now and in the future.

text: Ecce Domine de te Caiphae pontificis vaticinium ignarum sibi ipsi in populis est prolatum ut unus occumberet pro gente ne cuncti pariter interirent et tu singulare granum in terra morereris ut seges plurima nasceretur; supplices te ipsum qui pro mundi salute es hostia caesus deprecamur ut nobis de te ipso veniam dones qui te ipsum obtulisti pro nobis et hos quos recitatio commemoravit ante sanctum altare qui in pace iam tua ab his sunt vinculis corporeis translati quaesumus Domine ut te habeant ereptorem quem per baptismum meruerunt redemptorem habere sed et si qui inter hos adstantes ad baptismi salutaris sacramenta praeparentur quaesumus Domine Deus noster ut imbutos in fide instructos in sensu confirmatos in gratia ad percipiendam plenitudinem gratiae tuae spiritus tui munere iubeas praeparari ut sancti lavacri sonte desiderato mereantur renasci.
translation_en: Behold, Lord, the prophecy of Caiphas the high priest, unknown to him and his own people, has been brought forth: that one should die for the people lest all perish together; and you, a single grain on earth, should die so that a great harvest may be born. Humbly we beseech you who were sacrificed for the salvation of the world, grant us forgiveness through yourself whom you offered up for us, and those mentioned in the recitation before the holy altar, who are now translated from bodily bonds by your peace. We humbly ask, Lord, that they may have you as their redeemer, whom they merited to have through baptism. And for those among them preparing for the saving sacrament of baptism, we humbly ask, Lord our God, that you command the ones soaked in faith, instructed in sense, confirmed in grace, to be prepared, so that the sound of holy laundering may merit them to be reborn.

text: Ecce Domine dilecti tui Iuliani vel spiritalis coniugis suae Basilissae miraculorum insignia praedicantes has hostias divinitati tuae benedicendas offerimus qui se tibi exhibentes in sacrificium verum alios tibi exemplo suo in holocaustum veri sacrificii litaverunt cum et per Iulianum multorum monachorum millium patrem et per Basilissam sanctarum virginum choros tuentem copiosam utriusque sexus monachorum scilicet ac virginum in caelestem gloriam susceperis congregationem.  Ex hoc igitur immensam bonitatis tuae potentiam obsecramus ut qui per utrosque electa animarum munera suscepisti per nos humiles tuos hanc hostiam pro nostris peccatis oblatam dignanter suscipias impendens et benedictionem oblatis et expiationem sumpturis.
translation_en: Behold, Lord, here your beloved Juliani and his spiritual wife Basilissa, proclaiming the signs of miracles, offer these sacrifices to be blessed by your divinity. They presented themselves to you as a true sacrifice, just like others who offered themselves to you as holocausts in the true sacrifice of Christ. Through Juliani, father of countless monks, and through Basilissa, guardian of choirs of holy virgins, rich in both male and female monastics whom you have received into celestial glory, we humbly ask for your immense power to be invoked. May you receive graciously this offering made on our behalf for our sins, bestowing upon it your blessing and absolution.

text: Ecce Domine festo cathedrae confessoris tui Martini sanctissimi uberius gratulamur dum hunc diem quo ipse in sacerdotium adscitus est prona devotione excolimus. Is quippe dum catervas aufugeret hominum praesul effectus est populorum ut qui iam motus carnis compresserat in deserto evectu gratiae utilius in populo perficeretur salvando quo pacis cuius in deserto avidus fuerat adsecutor post largius exsisteret praerogator.  Ex hoc igitur tuam pie Deus exoramus clementiam ut quidquid doctrinae eius promanavit ex lumine te opitulante nos impleamus in caritate.
translation_en:
Behold, Lord, on the feast of Your confessor Martin, the most holy, we joyously congratulate this day when he was taken up into the priesthood with humble devotion. Indeed, when he fled the multitude as a bishop, he became a shepherd to the people so that he who had already restrained his carnal movements might more usefully fulfill his grace among the people by saving them. Afterward, he pursued the desirer of peace in the desert more abundantly because he would exist more openly as a petitioner for him.
From this, we humbly ask You, God, to bestow Your mercy so that whatever has been produced by his teaching under Your guidance may be filled in us with charity.

text: Ecce fratres carissimi sollemnitas nobis hodie claruit summi nuntii quam olim quondam nostrorum meruit obtinere fides maiorum. Quia cum sit ministerio eminens angelorum non abhorrent animas aestuare nostrorum ut fruantur potius illius intercessione suorumque et sociorum.  Nam in condicione omnium creaturarum individua Trinitas quae est una deitas sempiterna maiestas cum conderet angelorum agmina quae primi operis lux est appellata et eminentior angelus cum praeferretur ceteris superba turgidus voluntate ruit profundior immanissima omni crudelitate. Cuius adversio sicut auctori culpae applicavit interitum ita permansuris in servitute donavit regnum beatitudinis indefessum tantoque solidior aucta est fides manentium quanto crudelior est facta damnatio delinquentium. Amissa claritate interiit qui humilitatem servare nequivit et sublimis in gloria pollet qui in ministerio perfectior manet.  Apostata etenim angelus ab aeterna beatitudine proiectus factus est humano generi insidians inimicus ne locum quem perdiderat gloria humana potiretur fragilis glutinatio plasmae. Prius enim decepit quam sexu fragilem vidit et per illam letale virus rudi et incauto obtulit viro. Cuius protinus parens culpa iustae damnationis intulit poenam a quo disseminata ex illis progenies obnixe maneret districta.  Sed vicit pietas creatoris et callidi anguis suadelam decipulam et trangressoris admissa piacula. Redemit enim misericorditer quem dudum culpa damnaverat condecenter; libero arbitrio heredem contulit caelo quem olim fore beatum plasmaverat in paradiso. Nam quia primus homo conditus angelorum fuerat societate locandus si non fuisset inoboediens factus. Post vero suadenti obtemperat et creatoris iussa relinquit etiam consortium angelorum amisit. Quod quidem iam manet restauratum per Dei patris omnipotentis verbum unicum caro factum in cuius incarnatione angeli gloriam cecinerunt et omnes bonae voluntatis consimili laude secum sociandos denuntiaverunt.  Horum etenim militia angelorum Michael eminentior manet in officio actionum ut ordinatim dispositi maneant in obsequio conditoris et vota deferam populi communi omnium creatori.
translation_en:
Behold, dear brothers, today solemnity has shone upon us through the high messenger, which our faith of old times deserved to obtain. For since the service of angels is eminent, souls do not shrink from being moved by ours, rather they prefer to be helped by his intercession and those of his companions.
Indeed, in the condition of all creatures, the individual Trinity which is one eternal deity, eternal majesty, created the host of angels, the first work of light, called the highest angel, who was set above others with proud and arrogant will, fell deeper into the abyss of immeasurable cruelty. His opposition, as the author of guilt applied death, so he gave everlasting kingdom of beatitude to those remaining in servitude, and the faith of those remaining increased as much as the damnation of the disobedient became more cruel. The one who lost his brightness perished because he could not keep humility, but the exalted one blooms in glory who remains perfect in service.
An angel indeed fell from eternal beatitude and became an enemy to the human race, striving not to let a place that he had lost due to human glory be occupied by fragile humanity. First, he deceived before he saw the weak sex, and through it, he offered a deadly virus rough and careless to man. Immediately, his parent imposed the punishment of just damnation on him from whom the progeny spread out and remained firmly rooted among them.
However, the Creator's piety conquered the sly serpent and transgressors admitted penance. Mercyfully, He redeemed whom guilt had once damned; to the free will, He gave an heir to heaven, whom He had foreseen as blessed in paradise. For if the first man created among angels was to be placed in society, he would not have been disobedient if he had not been. After yielding to temptation and abandoning the Creator's commands, even the companionship of angels was lost. What remains now is restored through God the Father Almighty's word, made flesh in whose incarnation angels sang glory and all the good will proclaimed their desire to join them in similar praise.
The service of angels, indeed, Michael remains eminent in office, arranging that those duly disposed remain obedient to the Creator and fulfilling the wishes of the common people to all Creators.

text: Ecce Iesu his diebus salutaris abstinentiae mediatis deferimus tibi hoc sacrificium nostrae redemptionis. Ob hoc te poscimus et rogamus ut per huius sacrificii oblationem gratissimam et vivis donorum tribuantur spiritalium incrementa et defunctis fidelibus requies concedatur aeterna.
translation_en: Behold, on these days of salutary abstinence, we offer this sacrifice of our redemption to you. For this, we ask and beseech you, that through the offering of this sacrifice may spiritual increments be bestowed and eternal rest granted to the faithful departed.

text: Omnipotens sempiterne Deus apud quem nihil obscurum est
translation_en: Almighty everlasting God, in whom there is no secret thing

text: Ecce Iesu mediator Dei et hominum Christe redemptor ac Domine hominem illum quem cum patre et spiritu sancto unus Deus sexto die ad tuam condidisti imaginem sexta demum aetate per assumptam visitans carnem reformationem mentis eidem tribuisti per evangelii veritatem.  Proinde in hoc die tam pro condicione quam pro redemptione humani generis hanc tibi offerimus victimam sacrificii singularis in quo ipse pro nostra salute ligno confixus es crucis aceto potaris lancea latere perfoderis inferna moriens penetrans resurgendo spolians. Pro quibus mysteriis ac miraculis hunc diem apud tuam clementiam sacrificiis commendantes petimus a te redemptore pio et domino ut hodierni mysterii recordatus spolians nos vetere homine cum actibus suis induas illo qui secundum Deum creatus est in iustitia et sanctitate veritatis.  Decidant in nobis carnalium libitus voluptatum et intereant exstinctae passiones variae vitiorum. Qui nobis te dedisti esse in munere non nos sinas nobis ipsis esse ulterius in dolore ut in novitate vitae ambulantes sicut tuo redempti sumus ex sanguine ita cruci tuae affixi perenniter et perditionis ab inceps respuamus errorem et concessae dignitatis retineamus absque crimine libertatem.
translation_en:
Behold Jesus, mediator between God and man, Christ the Redeemer and Lord, who on the sixth day created man in your image during his sixth age through the assumed flesh, granting him reform of mind through the truth of the gospel. Therefore, today, both for the condition and the redemption of the human race, we offer this unique victim in sacrifice, in whom you yourself were fixed to the cross with wood for our salvation, pierced by a spear on your side, dying in agony but rising again, stripping off death. For these mysteries and miracles, commending this day to your mercy, we ask you, our Redeemer and Lord, to remember us clothed in the old man with his deeds, who was created second to God in justice and holiness by truth.
May our carnal desires and pleasures fade away, and may the varied passions of sin cease. He who gave himself as a gift to us shall not allow us to be any further in sorrow, so that walking in the newness of life as your redeemed, we are fixed perpetually by your blood to your cross, and from the beginning reject error and retain the dignity granted without guilt, freedom.

text: Ecclesia ecce tua Deus omnipotens quae te ac si sparsa in toto mundi alveo uno tamen agglomerata complexionis globo pro omnibus tam qui adsunt quam etiam qui corporis praesentia desunt voce imprecatur unica et sacrificiorum oblata offert devotione cernua ut et pro his qui in hac casura degunt vitam intercedente tanti antistitis prece ne ullatenus dilabantur impetretur auxilia et pro animabus pausantium ut tartareo exuantur ab igne gratuletur se aeterna obtinuisse solatia.
translation_en: Your church, indeed, O almighty God, scattered throughout the whole world in one single alveolus, is yet gathered into one spherical complexion for all – both those present and those absent from bodily presence. A single voice imprecates, and offerings of sacrifices are presented with conspicuous devotion. It is prayed that for those dwelling in this fall, life may be interceded by the powerful prayer of such a bishop, that no one may be dispersed by any means. It is also requested for the souls resting, that they may be freed from the fire of Tartarus with eternal consolation.

text: Ecclesia tua Domine caelesti gratia repleatur et crescat atque ab omnibus vitiis expiata percipiat sempiternae redemptionis augmentum ut quod in membris suis copiosa temporum prorogatione veneratur spiritalium capiat largitate donorum.
translation_en: May your church, Lord, be filled and grow with celestial grace, and be cleansed from all sins by everyone. May it receive the increase of eternal redemption, so that what is delayed in its members by the prolongation of time may receive spiritual abundance of gifts.

text: Ecclesia tua Domine caelesti gratia repleatur atque ab omnibus vitiis expiata percipiat sempiternae redemptionis augmentum.
translation_en: May your church, Lord, be filled with heavenly grace and purified from all sins, receive the increase of eternal redemption.

text: Ecclesia tua quaesumus Domine quae pia celebritate ad beati Pantaleonis martyris tui concurrit sollemnia a cunctis liberari adversis mereatur et ad eiusdem perveniat martyris societatem quam precatur.
translation_en: We beseech your church, Lord, that it may deserve to be freed from all adversities at the solemn occasions which gather at the shrine of your blessed martyr Pantaleon, and may attain to the fellowship of his martyrdom which he prays for.

text: Ecclesiae tuae Domine munera placatus assume quae et misericors offerenda tribuisti et in nostrae salutis potenter efficis transire mysterium.
translation_en: Lord, in Your church, graciously receive the gifts You have bestowed and mercifully grant that we may effectively pass through the mystery for our salvation.

text: Ecclesiae tuae Domine munera sanctifica et concede ut per eum cuius veneramur sollemnia nobis fiant tua virtute salutaria.
translation_en: Lord, sanctify the offerings for your church and grant that through him whom we are honoring with solemnities, may they become salvific for us by your power.

text: Ecclesiae tuae Domine munera sanctifica et concede ut per haec veneranda mysteria pane caelesti refici mereamur.
translation_en: Lord, may your Church's gifts be sanctified, and may we merit to be refreshed through these venerable mysteries of the heavenly bread.

text: Ecclesiae tuae Domine munera sanctifica et concede ut pane caelesti refici mereamur.
translation_en: Lord, sanctify the gifts for your church and grant that we may be worthy to receive the heavenly bread.

text: Ecclesiae tuae Domine munera propitiatus sanctifica et concede ut per haec veneranda commercia intercedente beato Mauro confessore tuo atque abbate pane caelesti refici mereamur.
translation_en: Lord, grant your grace to the Church you have favored. Sanctify her offerings and grant that through these revered transactions, with the intercession of blessed Maurice, your confessor and abbot, we may be worthy to receive heavenly bread.

text: Ecclesiae tuae Domine quaesumus tua benedictione dona sanctifica nosque per haec a culpis expediens illi configurari tribue qui olim suis discipulis gloriose transfiguratus apparuit.
translation_en: We beseech Your church, Lord, may Your blessing grant us and make us holy through these. May the one who once gloriously appeared to his disciples after being transfigured on the mountain, cleanse us of sins and make us worthy of configuration to Him.

text: Omnipotens sempiterne Deus cuius iudicio universa
translation_en: Almighty everlasting God, whose judgment governs all things

text: Ecclesiae tuae Domine voces placatus admitte ut destructis adversantibus universis secura tibi serviat libertate.
translation_en: Lord, accept the voices of your Church, pleased, that with all opposing forces destroyed, it may serve you securely in freedom.

text: Ecclesiae tuae Domine preces placatus admitte ut destitutis adversitatibus universis secura tibi serviat libertate.
translation_en: Lord, graciously accept our prayers in your church, that with freedom from all adversities, the destitute may serve you securely.

text: Ecclesiae tuae quaesumus Domine dona propitius intuere quibus non iam aurum thus et myrrha profertur sed (quod) iisdem muneribus declaratur immolatur et sumitur.
translation_en: We humbly ask you, Lord, to grant favorably look upon your church, where no longer gold and myrrh are offered, but which is declared, sacrificed, and received with the same offerings.

text: Omnipotens sempiterne Deus cuius sapientia hominem
translation_en: Almighty eternal God, whose wisdom created man

text: Ecclesiae tuae quaesumus Domine oblationem propitius intuere et intercedente gloriosa virgine Dei Genitrice Maria unitatis ac pacis semper eidem dona concede.
translation_en: We humbly ask you, Lord, to look favorably upon the offering of your church. Through the intercession of the glorious Virgin Mary, Mother of God, may you always grant unity and peace.

text: Ecclesiae tuae quaesumus Domine preces et hostias apostolica commendet oratio ut quod pro illorum gloria celebramus nobis prosit ad veniam.
translation_en: We humbly ask you, Lord, that your prayers and the apostolic offerings commend to prayer, so that what we celebrate for their glory may also bring us forgiveness.

text: Ecclesiae tuae quaesumus Domine preces et hostias beati Petri apostoli commendet oratio ut quod pro illius gloria celebramus nobis prosit ad veniam.
translation_en: We humbly ask you, Lord, that the prayers and offerings of the blessed Apostle St. Peter may be presented by your prayer, so that what we celebrate in honor of his glory may bring us forgiveness.

text: Ecclesiae tuae quaesumus Domine preces et hostias beatae Brigidae commendet oratio ut qui pro illius meritis maiestatem tuam indefessam atque exorabilem humiliter imploramus eius precibus adiuti misericordiam tuam sentiamus.
translation_en: We humbly ask you, Lord, that your prayers and offerings to your church of the blessed Brigid may be commended by your prayer. May we, who implore your majesty with unceasing and fervent supplication because of her merits, feel your mercy through her intercession.

text: Ecclesiae tuae quaesumus Domine preces exaudi ut quae de beati pontificis ac martyris tui Aelfegi sacra festivitate laetatur et patrociniis ipsius muniatur et gratiae tuae dona consequatur.
translation_en: We humbly ask you, Lord, to hear our prayers, that your Church may rejoice during the sacred feast of the blessed bishop and martyr Alfege, and be strengthened by his patronage, and may obtain your gifts.

text: Ecclesiae tuae quaesumus Domine unitatis et pacis propitius dona concede quae sub oblatis muneribus mystice designantur.
translation_en: We humbly ask You, Lord, to graciously bestow upon Your church the gifts of unity and peace which are mysteriously signified by the offerings presented.

text: Ecclesiae tuae quaesumus omnipotens Deus placatus intende conventum et misericordia tua nos potius quam ira praeveniat quia si iniquitates nostras observare volueris nulla poterit creatura subsistere sed admirabili pietate qua nos fecisti ignosce peccantibus ut opera manuum tuarum non facias interire.
translation_en: We humbly ask you, Almighty God, pleased one, to direct your attention towards your Church. May your mercy precede your wrath for us, because if you wish to observe our iniquities, no creature can stand.
