text: Simili modo posteaquam cenatum est accipiens et hunc praeclarum calicem in sanctas ac venerabiles manus suas item tibi gratias agens benedixit dedit discipulis suis dicens: »Accipite et bibite ex eo omnes; hic est enim calix sanguinis mei novi et aeterni testamenti – mysterium fidei – qui pro vobis et pro multis effundetur in remissione(m) peccatorum.«
translation_en: Likewise, after eating, taking and blessing this excellent chalice with his holy and venerable hands, he also thanked you, and giving it to his disciples, he said: "Take and drink from it all of you; for this is the chalice of my new and eternal testament – a mystery of faith – which will be poured out for you and for many for the remission of sins."

text: Simili modo posteaquam cenatum est accipiens calicem elevavit oculos ad caelos ad te Deum patrem suum omnipotentem item tibi gratias agens benedixit tradidit discipulis suis dicens ad eos: »Accipite et bibite ex eo omnes; hic est enim calix sanguinis mei novi et aeterni testamenti – mysterium fidei – qui pro vobis et pro multis effundetur in remissionem peccatorum.«
translation_en: In the same way, after having eaten, taking the cup, he lifted his eyes to heaven to you, God his all-powerful Father, giving thanks to you he blessed it, handed it over to his disciples, saying to them: "Receive and drink from it all of you; for this is indeed the chalice of my new and eternal testament - the mystery of faith - which will be poured out for you and for many for the forgiveness of sins."

text: Similiter etiam calicem postquam cenatum est pridie quam pateretur accepit respexit ad caelum ad te sancte Pater omnipotens aeterne Deus gratias agens benedixit apostolis et discipulis suis tradidit dicens: »Accipite et bibite ex eo omnes; hic est enim sanguis meus.«
translation_en: Likewise, also the chalice after supper on the night before he was to suffer, he took, looked up to heaven, and said to you, holy Father, almighty, eternal God: giving thanks, he blessed it, handed it over to his apostles and disciples, saying: "Take and drink from it all of you; for this is indeed my blood."

text: »HAEC QUOTIENSCUMQUE feceritis in mei memoriam facietis.«
translation_en: "Whenever you make mention of me, you will do so."

text: Mandans quoque et dicens ad eos: »Haec quotienscumque feceritis in meam commemorationem facietis mortem meam praedicabitis resurrectionem meam annuntiabitis adventum meum sperabitis donec iterum de caelis veniam ad vos.«
translation_en: Also commanding and saying to them: "Whenever you do this in remembrance of me, you will proclaim my death, announce my resurrection, anticipate my coming, and hope until I come again to you from heaven."

text: Unde et memores sumus Domine nos tui servi sed et plebs tua sancta Christi Filii tui Domini Dei nostri tam beatae passionis nec non et ab inferis resurrectionis sed et in caelos gloriosae a<d>scensionis; offerimus praeclarae maiestati tuae de tuis donis ac datis hostiam puram hostiam sanctam hostiam immaculatam panem sanctum vitae aeternae et calicem salutis perpetuae
translation_en: And remembering, Lord, your servants and also the holy people of Christ your Son our God, blessed of his passion, raised from the dead, and exalted in glorious ascension; we offer to your splendid majesty from your gifts and grants, a pure, holy, immaculate bread of eternal life and the cup of perpetual salvation.

text: Unde et memores sumus Domine nos tui servi sed et plebs tua sancta Domini nostri Iesu Christi passionis necnon et ab inferis mirabilis resurrectionis sed et in caelos gloriosissimae a<d>scensionis; offerimus praeclarae maiestati tuae de tuis donis ac datis hostiam puram hostiam sanctam hostiam immaculatam hunc panem sanctum vitae aeternae et calicem salutis perpetuae
translation_en: Indeed, we remember you, Lord, our servant, and your holy people, the servants of Jesus Christ, your Passion, the marvelous Resurrection from the dead, and the glorious Ascension into heaven; we offer to your majesty this pure, holy, immaculate gift - this Holy Bread of eternal life and the Cup of everlasting salvation.

text: Ergo memores gloriosissimae eius passionis et ab inferis resurrectionis et in caelum adscensionis offerimus tibi hanc immaculatam hostiam rationabilem hostiam incruentam hostiam hunc panem sanctum et calicem vitae aeternae.
translation_en: Therefore, remembering his most glorious passion, resurrection from the dead, and ascension into heaven, we offer to you this immaculate rational unbloody host, this holy bread and chalice of eternal life.

text: Supra quae propitio ac sereno vultu respicere digneris et accepta habere sicuti accepta habere dignatus es munera pueri tui iusti Abel et sacrificium patriarchae nostri Abrahae et quod tibi obtulit summus sacerdos tuus Melchisedech sanctum sacrificium immaculatam hostiam.
translation_en: It pleases You to look upon these [offerings] with a gracious and serene countenance and deign to accept them, as You deigned to accept the offerings of Your righteous child Abel, the sacrifice of our patriarch Abraham, and that which Your high priest Melchisedech offered to You, a holy and spotless sacrifice.

text: Supplices te rogamus omnipotens Deus iube haec perferri per manus angeli tui in sublime altare tuum in conspectu(m) divinae maiestatis tuae ut quotquot ex hac altaris participatione sacrosanctum Filii tui corpus et sanguinem sumpserimus omni benedictione caelesti et gratia repleamur. Per Christum Dominum nostrum.
translation_en: Humbly we ask you, Almighty God, command that these be borne by the hand of your angel to your high altar in the sight of your divine majesty, so that whatever from this altar's participation we have received the most sacred body and blood of your Son, may we be filled with every heavenly blessing and grace. Through Christ our Lord.

text: Et petimus et precamur ut hanc oblationem suscipias in sublimi altari tuo per manus angelorum tuorum sicut suscipere dignatus es munera pueri tui iusti Abel et sacrificium patriarchae nostri Abrahae et quod tibi obtulit summus sacerdos tuus Melchisedech.
translation_en: And we ask and pray that you receive this offering on your high altar by the hands of your angels, as you were worthy to receive the offerings of your righteous son Abel, and the sacrifice of our patriarch Abraham, and what was offered by your high priest Melchizedek.

text: Haec facimus haec celebramus tua Domine praecepta servantes et ad communionem inviolabilem hoc ipsum quod corpus domini sumimus mortem dominicam nuntiamus. Tuum vero est omnipotens Pater mittere nunc nobis unigenitum Filium tuum quem non quaerentibus sponte misisti qui cum sis ipse immensus et inaestimabilis Deum quoque ex te immensum et inaestimabilem genuisti ut cuius passione redemptionem humani generis tribuisti eius nunc corpus tribuas ad salutem. Per eundem Christum Dominum nostrum.
translation_en: We make this, we celebrate this, O Lord, keeping your commandments and approaching the inviolable communion; for what we ourselves receive as the body of the Lord, we proclaim the death of the Lord. Indeed, it is yours, Almighty Father, to send now to us your only-begotten Son whom you have sent freely to those who do not seek him. Although you yourself are immeasurable and inestimable, from you you have generated an immeasurable and inestimable Son that through whose passion you gave redemption to the human race; now grant us his body for our salvation. Through the same Christ our Lord.

text: Memento etiam Domine et eorum nomina qui nos praecesserunt cum signo fidei et dormiunt in somno pacis… Ipsis et omnibus in Christo quiescentibus locum refrigerii lucis et pacis ut indulgeas deprecamur. Per Christum Dominum nostrum.
translation_en: Remember also, Lord, and those whose names went before us with the sign of faith and are sleeping in the sleep of peace... To them and all in Christ who rest a place of refreshing light and peace, we humbly ask that you be merciful. Through Christ our Lord.

text: Memento etenim Domine famulorum famularumque tuarum et beatissimae virginis Mariae omniumque sanctorum tuorum intercedentibus meritis suppliciter quaesumus omnipotens Deus ut famulos ac famulas tuas quorum eleemosynas recepimus seu qui nobis familiaritate coniuncti sunt larga misericordia tua protegas et ab omnibus impugnationibus defendas ut tua protectione ubique salventur et animabus famulorum famularumque tuarum videlicet omnium orthodoxorum quorum commemorationem agimus et quorum corpora hic requiescunt vel quorum nomina hic in libro vitae scripta esse videntur indulgentiam et remissionem peccatorum tribuas et in consortio electorum tuorum habere digneris.  Istis et omnibus in fide catholica quiescentibus locum pacis refrigerii et requiei ut indulgeas deprecamur. Per Christum Dominum nostrum.
translation_en: Remember, O Lord, Thy servants and the servants of Thy servants, and the most blessed Virgin Mary, and all Thy saints interceding on their merits, we humbly ask The Almighty God that He may protect and defend Thy servants and handmaidens, whose alms we have received or who are connected to us by familiarity, with His bountiful mercy. May they be protected from all attacks and, under Thy protection, safe everywhere. For the souls of Thy servants, handmaidens, that is, all orthodox ones, whose commemoration we make and whose bodies here rest or whose names are written in this Book of Life, grant indulgence and remission of sins, and may He find them worthy to be with the elect. For these and all who sleep in faith in the Catholic Church, a place of peace, refreshment, and repose, we humbly ask for indulgence. Through Christ our Lord.

text: Nobis quoque peccatoribus famulis tuis de multitudine miserationum tuarum sperantibus partem aliquam societatis donare digneris cum tuis sanctis apostolis et martyribus cum Ioanne Stephano Matthia Barnaba Ignatio Alexandro Marcellino Petro Felicitate Perpetua Agatha Lucia Agnete Caecilia Anastasia et cum omnibus sanctis tuis intra quorum nos consortium non aestimator meriti sed veniae quaesumus largitor admitte. Per Christum Dominum nostrum
translation_en: Graciously grant to us, the sinners, your servants, a part of your great mercy, hoping for fellowship with your holy apostles and martyrs, along with John, Stephen, Matthias, Barnabas, Ignatius, Alexander, Marcellinus, Peter, Felicity, Perpetua, Agatha, Lucia, Agnes, Cecilia, Anastasia, and all your saints. We ask that you admit us into their fellowship, not by estimating our merit, but by granting forgiveness. Through Christ our Lord.

text: PER QUEM haec omnia Domine semper bona creas sanctificas vivificas benedicis et praestas nobis. PER IPSUM et cum ipso et in ipso est tibi Deo patri omnipotenti in unitate Spiritus Sancti omnis honor et gloria per omnia saecula saeculorum. AMEN.
translation_en: Through whom, O Lord, you always create, sanctify, vivify, bless and grant to us. Through Him and with Him and in Him, to You, God the omnipotent Father, is all honor and glory through all ages of ages. AMEN.

text: Per quem haec omnia Domine semper bona creas sanctificas vivificas benedicis et nobis famulis tuis largiter praestas ad augmentum fidei et remissionem omnium peccatorum nostrorum.  Et est tibi Deo patri omnipotenti ex ipso et per ipsum et in ipso omnis honor virtus laus (et) gloria imperium perpetuitas et potestas in unitate Spiritus Sancti per infinita saecula saeculorum. AMEN.
translation_en: Through whom, O Lord, you always create, sanctify, vivify, bless, and generously bestow upon us, your servants, for the increase of faith and remission of all our sins. And to you, God Almighty, is every honor, virtue, praise (and) glory, empire, eternity, and power in the unity of the Holy Spirit, throughout infinite centuries of centuries. AMEN.

text: Adsistat huic sanctificationi illa benedictio qua Dominus noster Iesus Christus sacrificium tale instituit atque benedixit. Hosanna in altissimis. Te pro refrigerio spirituum defunctorum omnipotens aeterne Deus humiliter exoramus praecipue pro animabus famulorum tuorum et famularum tuarum illarum inlessa commemoratione ut ab infernali manu liberatas in sinu patris requiescant patriarchae.
translation_en: May this sanctification be assisted by that blessing which our Lord Jesus Christ instituted and blessed for such a sacrifice. Hosanna in the highest. We humbly beseech you, almighty eternal God, especially for the souls of your servants and their servants, that they, unburdened, may be freed from the hand of the infernal one and rest in the bosom of the father, among the patriarchs.

text: Benedictus Deus et clementi proposito pro erudiendis mortalitatis nostrae facinoribus infertis ipse etiam unigenitus pro parte quae caro factus est abitus est mortalis ultro se subdens ludibriis et colomna sui corporis dilectionis nostrae ruinas fulcirit ac sui casus condere hostes arma conterens forciore rubore quam eclesiam ruiramus erigit.
translation_en: Blessed is the God and merciful, who has undertaken to educate our corrupt deeds. Even His only-begotten Son, though He became flesh and suffered death, willingly submits Himself to mortal derision, and supports the ruin of His own body by a column of love for us. He turns the events that brought about His own fall into weapons against His enemies, with a stronger redemption than we have ruined the church.

text: Benedictus Dominus noster qui nos in labore reficit pascit in fame visitat in dolore qui non erubuit corpus nostrae humilitatis suscipere.
translation_en: Blessed is our Lord who refreshes us in labor, feeds us in famine, visits us in sorrow, who was not ashamed to receive the body of our lowliness.

text: Benedictus es Nazarene qui ex ore infantium et lactentium perfecisti laudem ut non humana sed divina confessio nasceretur et immatura loquendi aetas agnosceret quem periti lege nescirent.
translation_en: Blessed are you, Nazarene, who through the mouths of infants and nursing babies have perfected praise so that not human but divine confession would be born, and immature age of speech would recognize Him whom the wise in the law did not know.

text: Benedictus plane qui venit in nomine domini; benedictus Deus rex Israel. Pax in terra; gloria in excelsis.
translation_en: Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord; blessed is God, the king of Israel. Peace on earth; glory in the highest.

text: Benedictus qui venit in nomine domini; benedictus e caelis. Ut conversaretur in terris caro factus est; ut delicta carnis ablueret hostia assumptus est; ut nos faceret sacerdotes sacerdos <fieri> dignatus est; ut nos patri quos liberare venit reconciliaret; ut terrenos crederemus in caelis cui caelorum Dominus esset in nobis.
translation_en: Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord; blessed is he from heaven. In order to turn flesh into earth, he was made flesh; in order to cleanse the offenses of flesh, he was assumed as a sacrifice; in order to make us priests, he deigned to become a priest; in order to reconcile for us the Father whom he came to free; in order that we may believe in heavenly things, to whom the Lord of Heaven is in us.

text: Benedictus qui venit in nomine domini. Deus scientiarum dominus qui praestat adinventiones suas et disponit omnia suaviter; qui adscendit super occasum Dominus nomen est illi. Hic panis vivus et verus qui de caelo descendit ut daret escas esurientium immo et ipse esset esca viventium. Fiat nobis in pane quo corda firmantur ut in virtute panis huius per hos quadraginta dies sine impedimento carnis et sanguinis ieiunare valeamus ipsum panem habentes qui pauperes pascit panibus qui Moysi et Eliae per quadraginta dies ieiunantibus quadragesima dedicavit. Deinde etiam in suo ipso ieiunio eundem nobis numerum dierum ieiunii sollemnitate signavit ut quod ipse Dominus in nostri corporis infirmitate pro nobis iugiter in quadraginta diebus explevit id nos vel minutatim eodem numero dierum calculo distributa observantia vespertinis refectionibus studeamus imitare.
translation_en: Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord. God, Lord of knowledge, who provides inventions and arranges all things gently; who ascends on the west, the name is his. Here is the living bread that has come down from heaven to give food to the hungry, even to be food for those who live by faith. Let this bread strengthen our hearts so that, in the power of this bread, we may be able to fast without hindrance for these forty days, having this bread which feeds the poor. The same bread, which Moses and Elijah ate during their forty-day fasts, consecrated Lent for them. Then even in its own fast, he marked out the same number of days of solemn fast for us to observe with diligence, imitating how, in our bodily weakness, he has constantly fulfilled this in forty days. We should strive to follow this number of days of fasting calculated by the evening meals.

text: Cantabimus tibi Domine cum angelis et sanctis uno cordis affectu canticum individuae Trinitatis quod omnis ecclesia per totum diffusa orbem terrarum decantat principaliter tibi filiique tui ac Spiritus Sancti dignam praeferens gloriam maiestatis.
translation_en: We will sing to you, Lord, with angels and saints, with one heartfelt affection, the song of the individual Trinity which the whole church dispersed throughout the earth's sphere sings primarily to you, to your Son, and to the Holy Spirit, giving precedence to the glory of your majesty.

text: Deus qui culpa offenderis paenitentia placaris da nobis Domine flere mala quae fecimus ut tuae consolationis gratiam consequamur.
translation_en: God, who is appeased by penitence for the offense we have caused, grant us, Lord, to weep for the evil that we have done, so that we may follow the grace of your consolation.

text: Deus qui nos caelestium numquid hymnum tibi vis offerri sed meritum et sanctorum angelorum tam loca tenere quam carmina dona ut qui supernarum virtutum concentum in tua praedicatione sumimus etiam superioris vitae affectum ex correctione sumamus.
translation_en: God, who would we offer a hymn to you from the celestial realm, but we offer it with merit and the songs of the holy angels. We hold such places as these, and we receive such songs from you. For we take on the affection for higher life through your teachings, and even from correction, we take on its superior nature.

text: Deus rerum omnium conditor atque creator qui unus in Trinitate et trinus in unitate cognosceris cuius magnitudinem deficiens est lingua humana narrare quem sine cessatione proclamant angeli sanctum. Ideo nos minimi famuli tui ore quidem indigno non tres »Sanctus« sed ter »Sanctus« praeconio vocis attollimus ut consono modulamine proclametur ter repetatur laudatio. Ob hoc pietatem tuam clementissime Domine exoramus optata tribuas praesumpta indulgeas ut detersa nube peccaminum pura et libera conscientia tuam mereamur opulentiam collaudare.
translation_en: The Creator and maker of all things, one in Trinity and three in unity, whom the human tongue is unable to fully describe but whom the angels proclaim without ceasing as holy. Therefore, we, your least servants, though our voice may be unworthy, raise the "Sanctus" three times not three "Sanctuses," in a fitting hymn, so that the praise is sung and repeated three times with harmonious modulation. For this reason, we humbly beseech your mercy, most merciful Lord, to grant what is sought and forgive what has been presumed, so that, cleansed by the cloud of sins, we may be worthy to praise your bounty with a pure and free conscience.

text: Dignus es Domine Iesu ab omnibus accipere gloriam et honorem qui pro nobis dignatus es improperium passionis suscipere. Dignus es praedicari per mundum qui per crucem pereunti subvenire dignatus es mundo. Dignus es paternae dexterae aequalitate sustolli qui pro servulis non es dedignatus occidi. Dignus es a caelestibus et terrestribus in veritate cum patre et spiritu sancto adorari qui caelum et terram ab initio cum patre creasti. Digne quoque illud adeptus es quod esset super omne nomen qui supernam moriendo ac resurgendo praeparasti humano generi mansionem.  Totum tibi omnipotens Pater quod sibi redemit acquiris cui totum quod in te est nihil amittendo naturaliter tradidisti.
translation_en:
Worthy are You, Lord Jesus, to receive glory and honor from all, who deigned to bear the reproach of our passion. Worthy are You to be proclaimed throughout the world, who condescended to succor those who perish by the cross. Worthy are You to be raised to the equality of the Father's right hand, who did not scorn to die for Your servants. Worthy are You to be worshiped in truth with the Father and the Holy Spirit by both celestial beings and humans, who created heaven and earth with the Father from the beginning.
Also worthy is what was achieved by You that was above all names: You prepared a dwelling for the human race by dying and rising again.
All that the omnipotent Father redeemed, He acquires; You have given nothing of what is in You naturally without losing it.

text: Dignus es Domine Iesu Christe aeternis angelorum et hominum collaudari praeconiis qui terrena cupiens caelestibus sociari humanum genus pretio tui sanguinis redemisti. Etenim pro nobis omnibus mortem crucis excipiens latus illud tui corporis sacri confossum lancea aperitur et continuo duo illa magnifica sacramenta sanguis scilicet et aqua fluxerunt. Sanguis ille plane qui in remissionem effusus est peccatorum et aqua quae salutare temperans poculum et lavacrum pariter praestat et potum. Hac et originalis primoplastorum noxa detergitur et reconciliationis gratia exhibetur.  His proinde fluminibus ex latere tuo fluentibus quibus olim nos regeneratos ac salvatos meminimus pro noviter regeneratis infantibus postulamus ut te opitulante ita fidei nutrimento proficiant ut cum bonorum operum effectu nobiscum pariter ad te remunerati perveniant.
translation_en: You are worthy, Lord Jesus Christ, to be praised eternally by the choirs of angels and men, who desiring earthly things, longed to associate with the heavenly. You have redeemed the human race with the price of your blood. Indeed, for our sake you accepted death on the cross; your side was pierced with a spear, and from it there flowed out two most magnificent sacraments, blood certainly, and water. This blood clearly shed for the remission of sins, and the water which temperately provides both the cup and the cleansing bath, likewise bestows and offers the drink. With these rivers flowing from your side, which we remember regenerating and saving us in times past, we now plead for the newly-baptized infants that, with your help, they may progress by the nourishment of faith so as to reach you, rewarded together with us for good works.

text: Domine Deus noster nos quoque hodiernam diem inhonorem tui sancti nominis et in commemoratione beatissimorum martyrum cum ceteris sanctis annua festivitate percolimus altaribus tuae pietatis assistimus tibi enim Domine laudes et gratias referimus in nomine et honore sanctissimi Filii tui Dei ac Domini nostri Iesu Christi.
translation_en: Lord God, we also today honor your holy name and remember the blessed martyrs along with all the saints in the annual feast. We assist you, Lord, as we offer lauds and thanksgiving in the name and honor of the most sacred Son of God, our Lord Jesus Christ.

text: Domine Deus Sabaoth pleni sunt caeli et terra <gloria> maiestatis tuae. Hosanna in excelsis. Benedictus qui venit in nomine domini.
translation_en: Lord God of hosts, heaven and earth are full of your glory. Hosanna in the highest. Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.

text: Gloria in excelsis Deo et in terra pax hominibus bonae voluntatis quia appropinquavit redemptio nostra venit antiqua exspectatio gentium adest promissa resurrectio mortuorum iamque praefulget aeterna exspectatio beatorum.
translation_en: Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace to people of good will. For there is news of great joy for all the people: For today in the city of David a Savior has been born to you, who is Christ the Lord. And this will be a sign for you: You will find a baby wrapped in swaddling clothes and lying in a manger. And suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly host praising God and saying: Glory to God in the highest heaven, and peace on earth to those whom God favors! (Luke 2:14). The redemption of our salvation has drawn near, the ancient expectation of nations is fulfilled, the promised resurrection of the dead is present, now the eternal expectation of the blessed shines forth.

text: Haec est Domine tua laudatio quae est nostra confessio. Hoc est tuum sacrificium quod nostrum pretium. Haec tua victima nostra vita. Quae nobis in unitate Spiritus Sancti donata cum filio et iterum redonata per filium.
translation_en: This is Your, Lord, the praise that is our confession. This is Your sacrifice which is our redemption. This is Your victim, our life. Which was given to us in unity of the Holy Spirit, with the Son and again returned through the Son.

text: Haec est sine fine felicitas haec est beatitudo sine termino; sic Deo indesinenter haerere ut ipse sit spes ipse sit requies in ipso vigilet negotium in ipso otium conquiescat. Sic nobis cibum praebendum vel poculum ut quidquid praefiguravit in mysteriis reddat in praemiis.
translation_en: This is endless happiness, this is beatitude without end; thus to adhere continually to God that He Himself is our hope, that He Himself is our rest, that vigilance takes place in Him, that work finds repose in Him. Thus may a food and drink be given to us such that whatever has been foreshadowed in the mysteries returns as rewards.

text: Haec te vox Domine mystica luce comitatur quae cum in supernis dominicae perennitatem laudis exerceat celebrationem tanti nominis invexit in terris ut huiusmodi praeconia si homines tacerent saxa clamarent. Viderunt te inferi Deus viderunt te et tremuerunt a voce tonitrui tui dicentes: »Absorpta est mors in victoria tua. Ubi est mors aculeus tuus?« Propter quod attonita paululum miserorum stetere supplicia nec habuerunt tormenta cruciatum sic vicisse cernentia crucifixum. Et iudicem suum ipsa etiam poena contremuit quia natura terribilium tenebrarum praesentia tui fulgoris hebetata iam tunc timuit iudicari.  Exsultaverunt sancti in gloria laetantes in cubilibus suis quod auctorem promissae sibi lucis agnoscerent. Quorum tu Domine stipatus agminibus et tibi tantum noti splendoris candore perfusus sacrificia per te instituta sanctifica non invocantis merito sed instituentis magisterio vel exemplo ut cunctis rite perfunctis Salvatore nostro ab inferis iam re?gresso et mors se intellegat victam et vita tripudiet revocatam.
translation_en:
This mystical voice, O Lord, accompanies thee, which in the heavens exercises eternal praise of thy perpetual dominion, has brought such proclamations on earth that even if men were silent, stones would cry out. The infernal regions have seen thee, God, and trembled at the sound of thy thunderous voice, saying: "Death is swallowed up in thy victory. Where is death, thy sting?" Therefore, for a brief moment, the torments of the damned stood still in awe, seeing the crucified one. Even the punishment itself quaked, for the presence of thy radiant glory had weakened the terrible darkness it was accustomed to.
The saints rejoiced in their glory, exulting in their beds, because they recognized the author of the promised light. Thou, O Lord, art arrayed with their ranks and bathed in the brightness of their splendor, hast sanctified sacrifices instituted by thee, not through merit but through teaching or example, that all may be properly completed and our Savior returned from hell, the dead aware of their defeat, and life recalling its captured victim.

text: Hanc igitur oblationem familiae tuae tibi adstantis quorum tibi epulis excitatis.
translation_en: Therefore, this offering of your family standing before you, whom you have excited with your feasts.

text: Hanc in excelsis gloriae tuae laudem supernarum creaturarum voce resonante nobis quoque famulis tuis cognitam fieri pietas tua voluit et haec praeconia sedibus celebrata sidereis magnificentiae tuae donum non solum noscendam famulis tuis sed etiam imitandam patuerunt.
translation_en: Your glory in the highest is made known to us, your servants, by the resounding voice of the supernal creatures. Your mercy has wanted it to be recognized, and these praises sung by the celestial seats are not only meant to be understood by your servants but also imitated by them.

text: Hic inquam Christus Dominus noster et Deus noster qui sponte mortalibus factus assimilis per omnem hunc aevi diem immaculatum tibi corpus ostendit veterisque delicti idoneus expiatur sinceram inviolatamque peccatis exhibuit animam quam sordentem rursus sanguis elueret abrogataque in ultimum lege moriendi in caelum corpus perditum atque ad patris dexteram relevaret.
translation_en: Here, I say, Christ our Lord and God who freely became like us and assumed a body immaculate for all days, offered to you as an expiation for the ancient sin. He showed an innocent, unblemished soul, which again the blood would cleanse. Thus, under the abolished law of death, he raised his body lost in heaven and restored it to the Father's right hand.

text: Hiis te hymnis Domine patriarcharum tuorum fides; hiis te hymnis Domine prophetarum tuorum spes; hiis te hymnis Domine apostolorum tuorum caritas; hiis te hymnis Domine angelorum tuorum chorus; hiis te hymnis Domine martyrum tuorum candidatus laudat exercitus; hiis te hymnis Domine nostra ( cetera desiderantur )
translation_en: In these hymns, Lord, faith acclaims the patriarchs of yours; in these hymns, Lord, hope praises the prophets of yours; in these hymns, Lord, love honors the apostles of yours; in these hymns, Lord, the choir of angels extols you; in these hymns, Lord, the army of your martyrs acclaims you; in these hymns, Lord, the rest (desire to be) ours.

text: Hiis te hymnis Domine patriarcharum tuorum virtus; hiis te hymnis Domine apostolorum tuorum chorus; hiis te hymnis Domine martyrum tuorum candidatis laudat eiecimus; Hiis te quoque hymnis Domine qua possumus voce benedicimus.
translation_en: With these hymns, Lord, we praise the virtues of your patriarchs; with these hymns, Lord, we sing the choir of your apostles; with these hymns, Lord, we shout praises to the white-robed martyrs whom we have ejected; With these hymns also, Lord, as much as we can, we bless you with our voice.

text: Hoc cantant angeli hoc resonant caeli; Benedictus qui venit in nomine domini. Benedictum quod venit regnum patris nostri David. Hosanna in excelsis.
translation_en: These sing the angels, these echo the heavens; Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord. Blessed is the kingdom that comes from our Father David. Hosanna in the highest!

text: Ipse Dominus est sanctorum virtus et ipse victoria est martyrum qui formam sacrificii perennis institueris eam primus obtulit et a nobis iussit offerri.
translation_en: The selfsame Lord is the power of saints, and He is the victory of martyrs; He first established the form of perpetual sacrifice and commanded it to be offered by us.

text: Iste hymnus Domine in excelsis ab angelis iste hymnus a sanctis praecinitur omnibus; Vere sanctus vere benedictus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus a quo sanctus roboratur Pelagius ut nec mori timeret nec veritatem interrogatus taceret. Persuasus namque a praeside ut copiosa regni munera acciperet et Christum negaret et ita regis lenociniis fieret aptus qui iam ante divinitus exstabat illuminatos tuus ille intrepido animi rigore: »Nam paratus sum magis mori quam Christum Dominum meum negare. Porro haec transitoria quae demonstras o rex non amo quia regnum aeternum consequi cupio. Ventuosa haec enim sunt omnia et ideo exspectata non concupisco vivens internis Deo affectibus qui me sibi animum corpusque intactum servare multis edocuit sermonibus. Quapropter est mihi mori lucrum et vivere praemium cui Christus promisit dare interminabile sanctis cum omnibus bravium.«  Qui utique Domine pro te occisus non solum tecum meruit regnum sed magnum etiam in ecclesia obtinet principatum. Impetravit quippe ad honorem sepulcrum quem exponi tyrannus praeceperat piscibus vel canibus in pastum. Impertite adclines itaque petimus aeterne Deus huius martyris tui plebi catholicae patrocinium cuius sancti Cypriani coemeterium caput ac ruricula beatissimi Genesii corpus servat honorandum. Unde petimus per huius interventum haec sanctificentur munera ac multiplicius ditentur altari sacrificia imposita qualiter omnis qui ex his libaverit muneribus per te semper tueatur ab adversis.
translation_en:
This hymn, Lord, in the heights is sung by angels; this hymn is sung by saints to all. Verily holy, verily blessed is our Lord Jesus Christ, Son of yours, from whom sanctity draws strength, Pelagius, so that he neither feared to die nor remained silent when questioned about truth. Convinced by the leader to receive abundant gifts of the kingdom and deny Christ and thus become fit for the king's intrigues, who already before divinely stood firm and illuminated with undaunted spirit: "For I am ready rather to die than to deny my Lord Jesus Christ. Moreover, these transitory things that you show, O king, I do not love because I desire an eternal kingdom. These things are fleeting and thus I do not covet them living with inner feelings for God who has taught me through many sermons to keep my spirit and body unblemished. Therefore, dying is a gain for me and living is a reward which Christ promised to give eternally to the saints along with all rewards."
Indeed, Lord, he who was killed for you not only merited your kingdom but also holds a great principality in the church. He obtained the honor of the tomb which the tyrant had ordered to be exposed as food for fish or dogs. Grant, we pray, eternal God, the patronage of this martyr's people, the Catholic Church, whose holy Cyprian's cemetery preserves the head and body of the blessed Genesius worthy of honor. Therefore, we ask through his intervention that these gifts may be sanctified and multiplied, and that whoever partakes of these offerings may always be protected by you from adversities.

text: O quam gloriosum est nomen Filii tui Deus pater in sanctis in quo beatus hic martyr Sebastianus cum sociis martyribus suis et obstrusa mutorum ora resolvit et contractionibus podagricae nodositatis medelam infundit.
translation_en: O how glorious is the name of Your Son, God, Father, in the saints, in which blessed here martyr Sebastian, together with his fellow martyrs, and clogged mouths opened up, and poured out a remedy for the swellings of gout.

text: O vere excelse eminentissimus insolitis solitus fluctus quod de velociori insufflatione ortus in milibus hominis recreavit omne mundum! Sic divinae sapiens sapientiae penetrabilior omni gladio ancipiti vigens quod stultorum atque infantium tam dissertas effecit sui flatus vehementia linguas et universa mundana sapientia huic prostrata colla submiserit adinventione mendax.  O Deus qui vere ignis consumens es exurendo videlicet peccata et renovando quae sunt venustate collapsa! O quam immensa huius ignis potestas quamque efficax fortitudo! Quod male aestuantes bene refrigerans ardor ut gehennae hunc inexstinguibilem madefaciat ignem et corda mortalium gelida accendendo illuminet et illuminando vivificet mentes. O ignis exurendo fecundans quod vinum sobrietatis esse credentibus inebrians propinando credimus!  Te hunc igitur omnipotentem esse Deum quem omnis intellectualium creaturarum suae vivificatione fatetur cuius etiam seraphim ferventes copiosius igne speciali eius sortiti vocabulo sanctitatis divino magnificantes aequalitatem atque omnipotentiam Trinitatis.
translation_en:
O truly exalted and exceedingly magnificent one, accustomed to extraordinary surges, who, rising from swift inspiration, has refreshed the world in countless men! Thus, the divine wise wisdom, penetrating more than any sharp sword, vigorously prevails over the foolish and infantile, making them speak confused languages and submit their necks in prostration to this false wisdom invented by deceit.
O God who truly are a consuming fire, burning undoubtedly sins and renewing what has been collapsed in beauty! O how immense is the power of this fire, and how effective is its strength! The one who cools the malicious ardor, refreshing it, makes the fire of hell inextinguishable; illuminating the cold hearts of mortals with it, enlightening and reviving their minds.
O the fertile burning, believed by those who believe in sobriety to be a wine, intoxicating them! Therefore, we acknowledge you as the almighty God, to whom all intellectual creatures confess their life, and even the seraphim, inflamed with special fire of his, praise him vocally, extolling the equality and omnipotence of the Trinity with divine magnificence.

text: Oremus fratres dilectissimi ut Dominus ac Deus noster speciem istam nostro ministerio consecrandam caelestis gratiae inspiratione sanctificet et humanam benedictionem plenitudine divini favoris accumulet.
translation_en: Let us pray, dearest brothers, that our Lord and God may sanctify this appearance with the inspiration of celestial grace through His consecration in our ministry, and may He increase its human blessing with the fullness of divine favor.

text: Hosanna in excelsis. Benedictus qui venit de caelis ut conversaretur in terris; caro factus ut per passionem suam vitam credentibus daret.
translation_en: Hosanna in the highest! Blessed is he who comes from heaven, to redeem us on earth; made flesh, so that through his passion he might give life to believers.

text: Hosanna in excelsis. Benedictus qui venit in nomine domini. Deus Dominus et illuxit nobis.
translation_en: Hosanna in the highest! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord. God, Lord, and savior of us.

text: Hosanna in excelsis. Benedictus qui venit in nomine domini. O vere beata nox quem angelorum et archangelorum concinunt virtutes quae nos hodie in passione beati martyris tui Leudegarii vox una prorumpit in laude ut tu Deus pater omnium nobis veniam tribuas de peccatis. Quaesumus da oblivionem praeteritorum facinorum qui dedisti martyribus post triumphum coronam.
translation_en: Hosanna in the highest! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord. O truly blessed night, which the virtues of angels and archangels sing! The voices of us all break forth together in praise that you, God, Father of all, may grant us forgiveness of sins. We ask that you give oblivion for past transgressions, which you granted to martyrs after their triumph and crown.

text: Hosanna in excelsis. Haec Domine maiestatis tuae iugis et superexcelsa laudatio est quam ex huius terrenae sedis habitaculo suppliciter audemus imitari habentes tuto hanc fiduciam per Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum qui nos impios perpetui celebrandi praeconii tui vocare dignatus est.
translation_en: Hosanna in the highest! This, Lord, is a praise of your majesty that dwells on high and even higher we dare to imitate from this earthly abode, having safely this faith through our Lord Jesus Christ, who deemed us unworthy sinners worthy to be called for the eternal proclamation of your glory.

text: Hosanna in excelsis. Idem excelse in excelsis idem humilis in terris Christe Filius Dei. Qui nebulosa magicae artis in Simonis praesumptione prestigia apostolicae concertationis veritate prodita destruxisti. Quem frustra caelorum adscensum aeris monitionibus appetentem decepta daemonum illusione iactantia altius extulit gravius elidendum ut quo eum paulo longius sursum volandi audacia permissa sustolleret multo validius in deorsum volantis insania dimissa disrumperet; nescientem utique quod nisi laudatam Petri confessionem nisi creditam Pauli fidem teneret caeli cuius claves Petrus habebat et cuius Paulus intima penetraverat ianuam non intraret. Immemor etiam illius severitatis atque censurae qui Ananiam et Saphiram sancto spiritui mentientes praevaricationis et perfidiae reos praesentis mortis animadversione damnavit. Paris quoque Pauli in evangelio potestatis ignarus qui doctrinae suae contradicentem Elymam magum iusta protinus caecitate percussit et seducentem Pythonis garrulum spiritum imperata illico discensione migravit. Totum illis caelestium athletarum viribus pro Iesu nomine pro Salvatoris divinitate pro Christi insinuatione pugnantibus divina est clementia praestitum.
translation_en:
Hosanna in the highest! The same who is exalted in the highest, is humble on earth. Christ, Son of God.
You shattered the illusions of magical arts, demonstrated through the presumption of Simon, in the truth of the apostolic gathering. The one whom the air's warnings attempted to draw upwards towards heaven, was lifted higher by a deceiving demonic illusion, only to be dashed down more violently, when allowed to fly a little further upwards with audacious confidence, so that the madness of falling faster would break apart; unaware that unless he held onto the laudable confession of Peter or believed in the credited faith of Paul - for Peter had the keys of heaven and Paul had penetrated its inner door - he would not enter.
Forgotten too is the severity and scrutiny of him who, condemning Ananias and Sapphira for lying to the Holy Spirit, imposed a sentence of present death upon them. Also forgotten is Paul's ignorance of power in Paris, who struck Elymas the magician with sudden blindness when he contradicted his teachings, and cast out the seducing spirit of Python when commanded to do so.
All these powers of celestial athletes were given by divine mercy for fighting under the name of Jesus, for the divinity of the Savior, for the insinuation of Christ; indeed, all of this was granted.

text: Hosanna in excelsis. Quanta nobis omnipotens Pater hoc sacrificium reverentia metuendum quo adeundum tremore quo honore sit celebrandum! Istae dominicis laudibus perenniter servientes caelestium voces admonent potestatum quibus nos agere officii sui similitudinem contestantur ut ad faciendam Dei voluntatem eos pro nostris viribus imitemur quos ad praedicandam Dei maiestatem nostris vocibus imitamur.  Ad instar superni altaris hoc nobis ad quod accedimus constitutum panem nos angelorum accipere manducandum cum illorum statum meritis gloriosum nostrum peccatis obsitum noverimus. Illi et numquam peccant et semper laudant; nos et crebro peccamus et raro laudamus rei per frequentiam criminum rei per neglegentiam gratiarum. Sed ab his nos conscientiae peccatricis debitis unici tui hostia in sanguine tuo tibi oblata mundavit. Illa nobis etiam post redemptionem delinquentibus hac spe et confessione subveniat quae etiam usque ad ultimum iudicii diem solum in spiritu non peccantibus revertendi aditum reseravit ut qui ad redimendos nos se dedit pretium ad excusandos nos se faciat advocatum.
translation_en:
Hosanna in the highest! How awesome is the almighty Father to us, who this sacrifice should be approached with reverence feared, trembling with awe, and honored with utmost respect! The voices of heavenly beings, serving these eternal praises of the Lord, remind us of the powers we imitate in our service. We must strive to imitate those whom we imitate when preaching God's majesty with our own voices.
We know that the bread given for this purpose, like that of an altar in heaven, is received by angels to be eaten, with a glorious status due to their merits, which is obscured by our sins. They never sin and always praise; we often sin and seldom praise due to the frequency of crimes and negligence of thanks.
But from these sinners, we have been cleansed by the atoning sacrifice of your only-begotten Son offered in your blood. May this also aid us, even when straying after redemption, with this hope and confession, which opened to the return to those who do not sin in spirit until the last day of judgment. He who gave himself as a price to redeem us may become our advocate.

text: Hosanna in excelsis. Vere dignum satis et iustum est omni quidem tempore sed praecipue in honorem sanctorum tuorum nos tibi gratias agere consempiterna et consubstantiva et cooperatrix bonorum omnium Trinitas Deus et pro beatissimi martyris tui Laurentii celeberrimo die laudum hostias immolare.  Cuius gloriosum passionis triumphum anni circulo revolutum Ecclesia tua laeta concelebrat apostolis quidem tuis in doctrina imparem sed in dominica confessione non imparem qui niveam illam stolam leviticam martyrii cruore purpureo decoravit.  Cuius cor igne tuo quem veneras mittere super terram ita flammam ut ignem istum visibilem non sentiret et appositas corpori flammas mentis intentione superaret ardentemque globum fide validus non timeret.  Quique cratulae superpositus novum sacrificium tibi semetipsum castus minister exhibuit et veluti super aram holocausti more decoctus saporem domino suavitatis ingessit.  In qua incomparabilis martyr praecordiis pariter ac visceribus medullis liquescentibus desudavit ac defluentia membra torreri invicta virtute patientiae toleravit; in qua extensus ac desuper fixus subditis iacuit ac pependit incendiis et holocaustum pietatis cruda coxit impietas.  Quae sudorem liquescentium viscerum bibulis vaporibus suscepit; supra quem velut super altare corpus suum novi generis sacrificium celebrandus minister imposuit et levita praedicandus ipse sibi pontifex et hostia fuit et qui fuerat minister dominici corporis in offerendo semetipsum officio functus est sacerdotis.  Tuam igitur Domine in eo virtutem tuamque potentiam praedicamus. Nam quis crederet corpus fragili compage glutinatum tantis sine te sufficere conflictibus potuisse? Quis incendiorum aestibus aestimaret membra non cedere nisi flagrantior a te veniens interiorem hominem lampas animasset?  Cuius potentia factum est ut laeta rore suo anima coctione proprii corporis exsultaret dum versari se martyr praecipit et vorari ne et paratam coronam uno moriendi genere sequeretur et si lenitate cruciatum vitalis tardaret interitus non exsisteret gloriosius coronatus.
translation_en:
Hosanna in the highest! It is truly fitting and just at all times, but especially for the honor of your saints that we should continually and forever offer you thanks, Trinity of God who is the cooperatrix of all good things. And on this most famous day of praise, we offer up hostias (sacrifices) for your most blessed martyr Lawrence.
The Church rejoices in the glorious triumph of his passion that has been returned to us again throughout the yearly cycle. In the apostles' teaching he remained unsurpassed, but not in their confession, for he adorned the snowy priestly robe of Levi with the purple blood of martyrdom.
His heart, which you sent to burn upon the earth, did not feel this visible fire and surmounted the flames of his body by the intention of his mind. He was unconcerned about the fiery globe and did not fear the valid faith.
Placed upon the little cart (cratula), he offered himself as a pure minister for a new sacrifice to you, and like a meal offered on the altar of holocaust, he infused the flavor of sweetness into his Lord.
In this incredible martyr, the marrow of his heart and entrails melted together, and with an invincible power of patience, his limbs remained unscathed while boiling. He endured to be placed under and suspended over the fires and to be roasted as a holocaust of piety by cruelty.
The sweat of his melting entrails he drank like steam, and upon him, as if on an altar, he offered his body as a new kind of sacrifice, becoming both priest and victim himself, who had been the minister of your divine body in offering himself up for the role.
Therefore, O Lord, we proclaim your power and your might in him. For who would believe that a fragile body glued together could withstand such battles without you? Who would estimate that his limbs would not yield to the heat of the fires unless the inner man had been animated by a more powerful flame from you?
His power made it so that his soul, exulting in its own boiling, rejoiced as the martyr plunged and followed after the prepared crown with one kind of death. If he were delayed by cruelty, there would be no more glorious coronation.

text: Hosanna in excelsis. Vere sanctus vere benedictus Dominus Deus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus manens in caelis manifestatus in terris.
translation_en: Hosanna in the highest! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord. Our Lord God Jesus Christ, your Son, remaining in heaven, revealed on earth.

text: Hosanna in excelsis. Vere sanctus vere benedictus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui sanctus in sanctis pro morte vitam pro poena gloriam pro confessione victoriam praestare dignatus est.
translation_en: Hosanna in the highest! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord. Truly, our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, has been deemed worthy to save life for death, to give glory for punishment, victory for confession, in the presence of the saints.

text: Hosanna in excelsis. Vere sanctus vere benedictus vere gloriosus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui beatum Andream apostolum primum electione exinde certamine consecravit.
translation_en: Hosanna in the highest! Truly holy, truly blessed, truly glorious is our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who first consecrated Blessed Peter, the apostle, through a divine election following that contest.

text: Per hunc te Domine deprecamur per quem formam sollemnitatis et spem securitatis accepimus qui super hoc sacrificium fidei divi spiritus tui respectu tantummodo benedicere et sanctificare dignetur.
translation_en: Through you, Lord, we humbly beseech You, by whom we received the form of solemnity and hope of security. May Your divine Spirit regard it with blessing and sanctification as regards this sacrifice of faith.

text: Sanctus in sanctis benedictus in terris Dominus noster Iesus Christus.
translation_en: Blessed are you, holy one, in the holy places; blessed is our Lord Jesus Christ on earth.

text: Suscipe Domine inter angelicae vocis officium nostrae quoque servitutis obsequium.
translation_en: Receive, Lord, within the service of the angelic voices, also our service in submission.

text: Te Domine sancte Deus petimus et oramus quod cum pro omnibus qui per universum mundum in pace tua requiescunt; tum pro his specialiter quorum commemorationem facimus deprecamur uti eos inter electos tuos recipi iubeas quorum numerum et nomen nosse dignaris; peculiariter pro caro nostro illo cuius hodie depositionem facimus deprecamur ut eum in sinu Abrahae Isaac et Iacob collocare digneris et in prima anastasi cum sanctis tuis facias suscitari ( ... cetera desiderantur ... )
translation_en: We ask and pray to you, Lord, holy God, that you would consider all who throughout the world rest in your peace; and particularly those whose commemoration we make known, we beseech you to command that they be received among your chosen ones, whom it is worthy for us to know by number and name. In a special way, we pray for our dear one whose departure we are celebrating today, that you would grant him a place in the bosom of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and that you would make him rise with your saints at the first resurrection ( ... other desires are desired ... ).

text: Te laudat Domine omnis virtus caelorum et innumerabilis multitudo sanctorum. Tibi omnis creatura famulatur et te sequitur beatorum exercitus angelorum.
translation_en: All power in heaven lauds you, Lord, and an innumerable multitude of saints. Every creature serves you, and the blessed army of angels follows you.

text: Tu summe Deus (h)a(c)ios ipse sanctus omnipotens Sabaoth qui venisti ab excelsis pati pro nobis miserere nobis; tu trinae potentiae pater inclite qui moenia excellentissima Ierusalem divinis ornas lapidibus et eius agmina sanctorum sanguine pingis libera nos tuo valido brachio et salva nos per auxiliatricem dexteram tuam et defende in nobis pretium pretiosi sanguinis tui quos redemisti.
translation_en: O supreme God, holy yourself, all-powerful Sabaoth who came from the heights, have mercy on us; you, the illustrious father of the trinity, adorned the most excellent walls of Jerusalem with divine stones and painted its holy army with its own blood. Deliver us by your mighty arm, save us through your helping right hand, protect within us the price of your precious blood that you have redeemed.

text: Tuo iussu Domine condita sunt universa in caelo et in terra in mari et in omnibus abyssis. Tibi patriarchae prophetae apostoli martyres confessores atque omnes sancti gratias agunt. Quod et nos facientes has hostias spiritales et sincera libamina ut libens exaudias deprecamur. Te oramus uti hoc sacrificium tua benedictione benedicas et Spiritus Sancti tui rore perfundas ut sit omnibus legitima eucharistia.
translation_en: By Your command, Lord, all things in heaven and on earth, in the sea and in all abysses, have been established. To You, patriarchs, prophets, apostles, martyrs, confessors, and all saints, thanks are given. We also offer these spiritual sacrifices and sincere libations, praying that you may graciously hear our humble petition. We beseech You to bless this sacrifice with Your blessing, and to anoint it with the dew of Your Holy Spirit, that it may be a legitimate eucharist for all.

text: Utinam ad hoc opus mens humana per misericordiam tuam illuminata sufficiat ut Domini nostri unigeniti tui per quem facti ac redempti sumus qui saeculorum est conditor credentium liberator doctrinam recolamus et gratiam. Qui humiliatus usque ad mortem mortem autem crucis pati pro nobis voluit tecum regnare non distulit idem hostia et sacerdos verus.
translation_en: May it be pleasing to this work, that the human mind, enlightened by Your mercy, may suffice; so that through our only-begotten Lord, by Whom we were made and redeemed, who is the founder of the ages and the liberator of believers, we may recall the doctrine and grace. He Who humbled Himself even unto death, death indeed He willed to suffer for us, yet did not delay to reign with You. The same He, the true sacrificial offering and priest.

text: Vere admirabilis et sanctus Dominus noster Iasus Christus Filius tuus qui nobis instituit nostrum coram hominibus non ostentare ieiunium ne labentis vitae transitoria laude bona male uteremur nec iam esset his retributio futura quos hic subsecuta fuisset merces vanitatis admissa.  Ob hoc praelargissime te Deus pater exposcimus ut te propitiante et ieiunium nostrum habeatur a vanitate disiunctum et merces nobis non hic ore hominum sed post in concilio praelargiatur sanctorum.
translation_en: Verily admirable and holy is our Lord Jesus Christ, Your Son, who has instituted for us not to show our fasting before men, lest by praise of transitory life we misuse good things, nor should reward for such be granted. Therefore most generously do we entreat you, God the Father, that with You being propitious, our fasting may be separated from vanity, and may our reward not here be given in the mouth of men but later in the council of saints.

text: Vere benedictus Dominus Deus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui cum humanum genus ab exitiabilis damnatione peccati terrenae carnis assumptione revocasset et per gratiam quae ducit ad vitam tua hostia in interitum legis vincula laxasset ut aeternam vivificatis salutem etiam sacrificii permutatione sanciret dum conversatione terrena et doctrina caelesti hominem quem assumpserat dignatus est instituere per has principales tuorum munerum creaturas mysterii ordinem quo te veneremur instituit.
translation_en: Blessed indeed is our Lord God Jesus Christ, your Son, who with the assumption of the human race recalled from the destructive damnation of earthly sin and loosed the bonds of the law through the grace leading to life by his sacrifice. He also sanctified eternal salvation even through the change of the sacrifice, while he deigned to institute mankind whom he had assumed, through these principal creatures of your gifts, in the order of the mystery whereby we venerate you.

text: Vere benedictus et gloriosus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus cuius nos gratia liberavit a pondere legis et fecit filios suae esse adoptionis. Qui ad suscitandum veniens Lazarum »Tollite lapidem« clamat ut pressuram auferret ab eo damnationis quem iam foetidum reddiderat horrenda actio sepulcralis. Tollite Iesus ait ab eo pondus legis quod eum deprimit in morte ut succurrat illi gratia vocis meae. Gratia quippe Dei est cum vocem eius audivimus ut cum Lazaro rectis Iesum gressibus assequamur.
translation_en: Verily blessed and glorious is our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, whom by grace we have been freed from the burden of the law and made sons of adoption. He coming to raise Lazarus shouts "Take away the stone," so that the pressure of damnation, which already his horrible burial had rendered him, might be removed from him. Jesus says, "Lift off from him the load of the law," which holds him down in death, to help him by grace through my voice. For indeed it is the grace of God when we hear His voice, so that we may follow Jesus with righteous steps as Lazarus.

text: Vere benedictus et sanctus et admirabilis Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui praedictum sacerdotem suum trino fultum comite coronavit et in eculei poenis positum non reliquit.  Is igitur veri pontificatus peragens cursum lotis inter innocentes manibus verum divino sacrificium litavit altario dum se cum his quos nutrierat salutarem victimam per gladii animadversionem obtulit.
translation_en: Verily blessed and holy and wonderful is our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who adorned His ordained priest with the triple fullness of the Holy Spirit and crowned him, and did not abandon him when placed in the prison of sins. Therefore, carrying out the true pontificate with hands washed among the innocent, he truly offered divine sacrifice on the altar while offering himself along with those he nourished as a saving victim through the scrutiny of the sword.

text: Vere benedictus et vere sanctus es Domine Deus noster propitiatio fidelium et redemptio animarum. Tu enim sanctus omnia sanctificas et sanctificata ad te conversa perlustras. Quem recte et vere totius caeli militia conclamat sanctum cuiusque incorruptum ut sancti simus habemus praeceptum.  Unde nos tibi rerum conditor quamlibet impuris offeramus hostiam meritis ad instar tui corporis et sanguinis in tuorum tamen gemino martyrum festo precibus deprecamur immensis ut ad tuorum sanctificationem servorum placido et sereno intuitu tuum mereamur cum benedictione respectum.
translation_en:
Blessed and truly holy art Thou, Lord our God, propitiation of the faithful and redemption of souls. For thou, O holy one, sanctifyest all things, and those consecrated to Thee, thou dost inspect. The whole heavenly militia rightly and truly acclaimeth Thee as holy, whose incorruptible body and blood we have as a commandment that we may be made holy like unto Thee.
Wherefore we, the creator of all things, offer to Thee from ourselves whatever is free from impurities, an offering worthy of Thy merits, in likeness to Thy body and blood, yet on the twin feast of martyrs we beseech Thee with immense prayers that by a peaceful and serene gaze upon Thee we may deserve a respectful look with Thy blessing.

text: Vere bone Deus vere pie et une Deus te solum laus te solum hymnus te solum gloria decet qui pro nobis te ipsum a teipso uno eodemque Christe ante saecula filio Dei et in fine saeculorum filio hominis super aram crucis Deo patri in expiationem peccatorum nostrorum offerri voluisti docens nos celebritatem huius sacramenti et pia fide et munda operatione gratissime frequentare.  Largire ergo ut quidquid in occasu diei quidquid in defectu mundi quidquid in resolutionis confinio labimur totum pietas tua et indesinenti consolatione confoveat et aeternae exsultationis participatione adducat.
translation_en: Verily, a good and truly pitiful God, you alone are worthy of praise, hymns, and glory who, for our sake, desired to offer yourself, your very self, the same Christ, before the ages as the Son of God, and in the end of ages as the Son of Man, upon the altar of the cross to God the Father, as an expiation for our sins. Teaching us to celebrate this sacrament with a pious faith and a pure operation, we gratefully wish to frequent it. Therefore, grant that whatever we stumble upon in the course of the day, whatever we lack in the world, whatever we encounter at the boundary of resolution, may our devotion be nourished by your every care and incessant consolation, and may it lead us to a share in eternal exultation.

text: Vere dies sempiternus vere lucifer verus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui sic luce divinitatis suae claruit mundo ut cum a tenebrarum eriperet dominatu ut nos qui aliquando eramus tenebrae efficeremur in eo verum lumen qualiter eum cognosceremus per illuminationem fidei suae qui pro nobis omnibus animam suam tradidit usque ad mortem.
translation_en: Verily, this is the eternal day, verily, the true light, our Lord Jesus Christ, Your Son, who so shone with the light of His divinity upon the world that He might deliver us from the dominion of darkness. We, who were once in darkness, were made into Him as true light. How may we come to know Him? Through the illumination of His faith, who for our sake gave His life even unto death.

text: Vere Domine sanctus vere Domine quia pleni sunt caeli et terrae gloria maiestatis tuae. Caro factum est ut habitaret
translation_en: Truly, Lord, truly you are holy; truly, Lord, the heavens and earth are full of your glory. Flesh was made to dwell in you.

text: Vere gloriosus et admirabilis Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui plasmatis sui praevidens miseratus occasum captivum hominem a destinata mortis sententia compassus exemit. Formam accipiens servi contubernium carnis assumpsit ne operis ratio suo moreretur auctori. Ipse quippe hominem dignatus induit humiliatus erexit traditus redemit crucifixus absolvit; innovavit resurgens consecravit adscendens.
translation_en: Verily glorious and wonderful is our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who, foreseeing the formation of His own, moved by compassion for the captive human being facing a predestined sentence of death, released him. Taking on the form of a servant, He assumed the companionship of flesh so that the work of creation would not perish in its Author. Indeed, He deigned to humble Himself, raised up what was low, gave what was given, redeemed what was betrayed, absolved what was crucified; renewing, He consecrated, ascending.

text: Vere gloriosus et admirabilis es Deus Pater omnipotens qui beatissimum martyrem tuum Felicem ita magisterio fecisti evangelicae praedicationis instructum ut dum relicta patria exsul te luminum patrem quaereret et non obtecta modio sed super candelabrum lucerna fidei cunctis in ecclesia perluceret saeviente fidei persecutione inimicum non quaesitus aufugeret sed quaerens cum quo certaretur inveniret.  Qui cum comprehensus cruentis tribunalibus ob confessionem tui nominis sisteret et primum lenocinatione sermonum sanctum tuum suasionibus inimicus illecebrare tentaret pectus quod tu sera gratiae tuae firmaveras tela reserare non valuerunt inimici.  Ingerit itaque insatiata crudelitas squalorem carceris ferri pondera inediae tabem flagellorum sulca ungularum lacerationem maris naufragia totaque perversitate meritis terrere militem tuum attentat.  Sed tu adiutor fortis dum in omnibus facis victorem martyrem tuum deficientibus poenis fatetur se etiam adversarius victum ut sentiret se divino iudicio poenis subditum qui vanis superstitionibus deditus cogebat tormentis subdi martyrem tuum.  Insaniens itaque victa crudelitas sanctum interfici iubet carcere trusum sed Felix triumphator dominum Deum confessus in terris felicem animam triumphantibus angelis praemisit in caelis.
translation_en:
Indeed, glorious and wonderful is God, Almighty Father, who made your most blessed martyr Felicity so well-versed in the evangelical teaching that while leaving his native land he sought you as the light of fathers and shone with uncovered lampstand as a beacon of faith for all in the church amidst savage persecution of faith. Yet, his enemy was not sought but fled from him, and found to engage in combat.
When apprehended before bloody tribunals because of his confession of your name, at first his enemy tried to seduce your saint with enticing words, but the weapons that you had strengthened with your grace could not open his steadfast heart.
Therefore, unquenchable cruelty inflicts upon him the stench of prison, the weight of iron chains, hunger, illness, scourges on his limbs, wounds from lashes, shipwreck, and all perversity to terrify your soldier. But you, mighty helper, in all things you make your martyr a victor who confesses himself defeated even in the face of decreasing penalties; and thus his enemy, vanquished, is forced to submit to divine judgment who had been leading your martyr astray with false superstitions.
Thus, insane cruelty orders that the saint be killed within prison, but Felicity, the triumphant conqueror, gives up his happy soul on earth to rejoicing angels in heaven.

text: Vere gloriosus et pius Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui suam pro nobis posuit animam et tribuit mundo novam per effusionem sui sanguinis vitam.  Ipsi ergo hodie humiliatum cor in laudis sacrificium offeramus petentes ab eo ut hodie vel cras seu cunctis vitae nostrae diebus ablutis criminibus calicem supplicii sui expiati bibere mereamur.
translation_en: Verily glorious and pious is our Lord Jesus Christ, Your Son, who set His own soul for us and gave the world a new life through the shedding of His blood. Therefore, today we offer to Him our humbled heart as a sacrifice of praise, asking Him that we may worthy to drink from the cup of His suffering's atonement today or tomorrow, or in all the days of our life, washed clean of sins.

text: Vere gloriosus vere benedictus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui sanat contritos corde et maerentes erigit sospitate qui cor contritum et humiliatum non spernit in nobis qui per spiritalis parsimoniae abstinentiam et animam salvat et corpus liberat a ruina.
translation_en: Verily glorious, verily blessed is our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who heals the contrite heart and raises up those who weep with salvation. He does not disdain a contrite and humble spirit in us. Through spiritual parsimony (or frugality) he saves the soul and frees the body from ruin.

text: Vere incomparabiliter te esse sanctum Domine omnis profitetur a te condita creatura a quo et creantur et sanctificantur omnia.  Hinc te quaesumus ut quibus iussis praeceptisque ad instar sanctitatis tuae iubes esse sanctos ob circumcisionis unigeniti tui diem cum oblatis sacrificiis sanctifices indignos.
translation_en: Indeed, everyone confesses you to be incomparably holy, Lord, from whom all creation is made and sanctified. Therefore, we humbly ask you to command and instruct them to be holy like your own unigenitor's circumcision day with unworthy offerings presented.

text: Vere sanctum ac magnificum nomen gloriae tuae cuius iussu condita sunt omnia in caelo et in terra in mari et in omnibus abyssis. Tibi patriarchae et prophetae et apostoli martyres omnesque sancti gratias agunt; quod et nos facimus Domine sancte Pater omnipotens Deus; hostias spiritales et sincera libamina quae tibi offerimus ut libens suscipias deprecamur. Adsit huic sanctificationi illa benedictio quam Filius tuus instituit ac benedixit.
translation_en: Truly, your name is holy and magnificent, to whom all things in heaven and earth, in sea and in all abysses were created by your command. To you, patriarchs, prophets, apostles, martyrs, and all saints, gratitude is given; which we too do, Lord, holy Father Almighty God. We offer you spiritual sacrifices and sincere libations that we present to you willingly. May this sanctification be accompanied by the blessing that your Son established and blessed.

text: Vere sanctum et benedictum nomen gloriae tuae Deus quod et in caelis et in terra omnis a te condita creatura concelebrat. Sit laus tua refectio infirmorum qui est gloria felicium et gratia sanitatum ut ex te sumat in huius carnis labore nostrae mortalitatis refrigerium ex quo beatissimum spiritum perfruatur quod est super omnia gloriosum.
translation_en: Verily, the holy and blessed name of your glory, God, is praised by all created beings, both in heaven and on earth. May your praise be the recovery of the sick, a joy for those who are happy, and grace for those receiving health. Let it provide refreshing from our mortal labor, drawing from you the most blessed spirit which surpasses all things, that is most glorious.

text: Vere sanctum pium ac magnificum nomen gloriae tuae omnipotens Deus cuius iussu condita sunt omnia in caelo et in terra in mari et in omnibus abyssis qui mirificus sanctorum omnium adoratur in terris et gloriosior prae cunctis angelis collaudatur in caelis.  Qui sic nos hic tribulationum censura contundit adversantium stimulis erudit lacerantium adversitatibus frangit ut post dolores veniamus ad requiem post laborem inveniamus mercedem.  Hic tibi Deus pater haec sacrificia inferat; hic tibi haec commendabilia reddat; hic nostris precibus faveat; hic servos tuos omnes fideles captivos ac tribulatos pro quibus haec tibi offerimus dona ab omnibus pressuris absolvat ac redimat et gratia tua eis quantocius multiplex solamen impertiat.
translation_en:
Verily, the holy and mighty name of your glory, O almighty God, whose command has established all things in heaven and on earth, in sea and in all depths, who is miraculously adored by all saints on earth and more glorious than all others above the angels in heaven.
Who thus crushes us here with trials, educates us with adversaries' stimuli, breaks us with lacerating adversities, so that after suffering we may come to rest and after labor we may find reward.
Here to you, God, Father, may these sacrifices be offered; here may these commendable things be returned to you; here may you favor our prayers; here may all your faithful servants, captives and troubled, for whom we offer these gifts, be freed from all pressures, redeemed and may the multiplying grace of yours quickly comfort them.

text: Vere sanctum vere benedictum est nomen tuum omnipotens Pater qui unigenitum Filium tuum ad hoc misisti ut perditos repararet errantes revocaret vivificaret aeternitatis suae participes efficeret crucis suae contrarias fortitudines vinceret.
translation_en: Truly your name is blessed and holy, Almighty Father, who sent your only-begotten Son for this purpose: to heal the lost, lead back the straying, give life to the lifeless, make participants of eternal life, overcome the opposing powers of the cross.

text: Vere sanctus atque in excelsis mirabilis Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus per quem tibi Deus Pater omnipotens famulantes offerimus sacrificium laudis et simplicem cordis nostri devotionem. Non enim hic horrido mugitu pecudum tristis hostia aut taurus occiditur aut hircus de gregibus immolatur sed hostia quam verus Dominus et sacerdos instituit omnipotens.
translation_en: Verily, holy and miraculous is our Lord Jesus Christ, Your Son, whom we, the servants of God Almighty Father, offer You a sacrifice of praise and a simple devotion of our heart. For here no sorrowful victim of beasts roars, nor bull is slain nor goat from flocks is immolated; but that which the true Lord and priest established, the Almighty has ordained.

text: Vere sanctus Deus pater sanctus unigenitus filius sanctus quoque unus utriusque spiritus.  Huius ecce virtute inaestimabili discurrit evangeliorum toto orbe ardentium quadriga rotarum radiorumque flammigerantium rutilans fulgoribus axis gestatur animalium circumquaque corporibus ocularis. Cuius in rotis auriga ipse vitae spiritus manens propriae potestatis imperio cunctum subiecit Christi pedibus mundum; divinis scilicet perhibens testimonium virtutibus patris unigenito verbo quia caro factum est et habitavit in nobis.  Hoc illud est paterni pignoris sibi simile munus quod se filius pollicitus fuerat transmissurum dum suos ad patrem regrediens orphanos diceret nullatenus relinquendos; in eius scilicet praesentia suam patrisque docens consistere maiestatem.  Hoc illud unguentum est quo prae consortibus unctus est Christus a patre cuiusque vetus illud chrisma praetendebat figuris transeuntibus veritatem; quo delibuti quoque sacerdotes prophetae constituebantur et reges unius veri regis et sacerdotis et prophetae imaginem prosignantes.
translation_en:
Verily, the holy God, Father, holy only-begotten Son, and also the holy Spirit of both substances. Behold, by this inestimable power, the Gospel's chariot with its burning wheels and flaming rays is whirling throughout the entire world, shimmering with its glorious axles, surrounded by bodies of animals, with eyes everywhere. The charioteer himself, the spirit of life, remains within the power of his own dominion, subjecting the whole world to the feet of Christ; indeed, bearing witness to divine truths, he declares that flesh was made and dwelt among us through the word of the only-begotten Son.
This is a likeness of the Father's pledge that his Son had promised to transmit when returning to the Father, saying that orphans would never be abandoned; in his presence, he teaches the majesty to remain stable.
This is the unguent with which Christ was anointed by the Father, whose ancient chrism prefigured truth through passing figures; and as priests and prophets were consecrated with this ointment, so kings were set in the image of one true king, priest, and prophet.

text: Vere sanctus es Domine et sanctorum omnium sanctitate praeclarior quem caelestium et terrestrium creatura suum dominum confitetur et laudat. Tu enim es propitiatio peccatorum et omnium fidelium Deus Dominus et redemptor aeternus.
translation_en: Truly, you are holy Lord and more holy than all the saints with your sanctity. Whereas both celestial and terrestrial creatures confess and praise their own lord. For indeed, you are the propitiation for sins and God, Lord and Redeemer of all eternity.

text: Vere sanctus es Domine Iesu Christe qui apostolum tuum Petrum firmissimam statuens petram aedificari tibi in ea sanctam pronuntiasti ecclesiam cui portae inferi minime praevalerent et caeli iugiter absque ambiguitate paterent. Caelorum etenim claves a te accipere meruit ut veniendi ad te desiderium habentes vitae portas aperiat et ad caeleste tuae maiestatis palatium introducat.
translation_en: Verily, you are holy, Lord Jesus Christ, who firmly established your apostle Peter on the rock, proclaiming that in him you would build your church, to which the gates of hell shall not prevail, and the gates of heaven shall ever without ambiguity open. For indeed, the keys of the heavens were worthy for him to receive, so that desiring to come to you, he might open the doors of life, and guide us into the palace of your divine majesty.

text: Vere sanctus et admirabilis es Deus summe qui te in his tribus sanctis perfecta Trinitatis unitas demonstrasti; non corporum visibilium dissimilitudine sed unita mentium voluntate; non officiorum distantium ordine sed concertantium militum inseparabili caritate; non aetatum alternantium tempore sed animorum persistentium indiscreta virtute.  Condecet enim ut hii qui bella domini praeliant sui secum regis exhibeant in abditis simulacra; quia et illic certa sperabitur ex hoste victoria ubi armorum victricium signa fuerint comitata.  Hii igitur cum principe glorioso levitae animo paterno consimiles effecti sunt continuo caelestis gloriae coheredes; in quibus bonae voluntatis immutabilem manere concordiam furibundus carnifex cernens nihilque posse in eis praevalere poenarum conspiciens mox atrocibus exurendos deputat flammis. Sed eo fit militum tuorum fides ardentior quo fuit acrior sententia cruentorum.  Quos tamen ita indisrupto sibimet vinculo tua caritas vinxit ut nec aestuantia camini dum traherentur procul conspecta formidarent incendia nec tristia saltem dum illic proicerentur contraxerint ora. Quin potius solvendae stationis tempus adesse cernentes caelestium dapum desiderio tacti propere perveniunt ad suae compendia mortis. Cumque mediis urerentur sacra corpora flammis acceptabilia Deo reddunt hymnis sonantibus vota.  Necdum quae fuerant ignibus divina sacrificia concremata et iam animae angelorum ovantibus gregibus chorisque consertae perpetim conscendunt aetherea in arce volatu ut apud te Deum solverent servatam esuriem a quo se fidenter speraverant refici perpetua caritate.
translation_en:
Verily, holy and wonderful is the God supreme who has shown the unity of the perfect Trinity in these three holy ones; not through the dissimilarity of visible bodies but through the united will of minds; not through the order of distant offices but through the inseparable charity of soldiers; not through alternating ages but through the persistent virtues of spirits.
It is fitting that they who carry into hiding the images of wars for the Lord's kingdom should expect certain victory from their enemy, where the symbols of triumphant arms will be accompanied.
Therefore, those who have been made alike to the glorious prince in a paternal spirit have become continuous co-heirs of celestial glory; in whom, seeing the unchangeable harmony of good will raging executioner cannot prevail, and sensing that nothing can conquer them by the tortures of punishment, he soon assigns them to be consumed by fierce flames. But their faith becomes more ardent because of the cruelty of the executioners.
Yet your love has bound them with an undissevered bond so much that even when they approach burning fires they do not fear the sight of them nor do they frown when they are thrown there. Rather, perceiving the time for the fulfillment of their station, they hasten to the feast of heaven with a desire touched by longing and promptly arrive at their reward for death. And when their sacred bodies are burning with acceptable flames, they return vows with resounding hymns.
Not yet have the divine sacrifices consecrated by fires ascended perpetually on ether to the citadel where they offer eternal hunger to God from whom they confidently hoped to be replenished with eternal love.

text: Vere sanctus et benedictus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui se pro peccatis nostris crucifigendum impiorum manibus tradidit qui proprias manus in cruce pro nobis extulit qui principatus et adversarias potestates per crucis mysterium abdicavit ac totius humani generis delicta iri ipsa cruce transfigens tibi se immaculatam hostiam obtulit et a nobis exiguis servis pro sua commemoratione indesinenter offerri praecepit.
translation_en: Verily holy and blessed is our Lord Jesus Christ, Your Son, who willingly gave Himself to be crucified by the wicked for our sins, who raised His own hands on the cross for us, who renounced principalities and adversarial powers through the mystery of the cross, and who, Himself sinless, offered You an immaculate sacrifice upon the cross, and commanded to be incessantly offered by us, Your unworthy servants, for His remembrance.

text: Vere sanctus et clemens vere benedictus et iustus vere admirabilis et gloriosus Dominus noster Iesus Christus qui inaestimabili clementiae suae dono nullum perire iubet sed omnes pietatis gremio convocat ad salutem.
