text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui mulierem illam sollicitam fecit quae habuit decem denarios; secundum quod in sancto evangelio legitur quia cum perdidisset unum ex eis accendit lucernam <et> scopa domum suam mundavit donec inveniret eum; rogavit amicos et vicinos suos dicens: »Gaudete mecum quia inveni denarium meum qui perierat.«  Mulier hic pactum legis ostendit; decem denarii decem capita sunt sancti a Deo electi id est filii primae legis;  Primum elegit Adam quem de pulvere terrae sibi similem fecerat.  Secundum elegit Noe ipsumque invenit iustum quem liberavit aqua diluvii.  Tertium elegit Abraham ex fide credentium et fecit eum multarum gentium patrem.  Quartum elegit Isaac ex promissione Dei natum.  Quintum elegit Iacob accipere benedictionem.  Sextum elegit Ioseph ipsiusque castitatem custodivit et accusatricem dominam suam spernere confudit.  Septimum elegit Lot ipsumque invenit iustum et hospitem angelorum et liberavit eum a sententia Sodomorum.  Octavum elegit Moysen ducem populorum ut educeret filios Israel per mare rubrum.  Nonum elegit IesuNave ipsumque fecit ingredi in terram repromissionis.  Decimum elegit David ut in regem ungeret eum.  Id est; Noe servavit iustitiam Abraham fidem Isaac repromissionem Iacob benedictionem Ioseph castitatem Lot hospitalitatem Moyses ducatum IesuNave integrum successorem David regalem unctionem. Ex his omnibus denarius unus qui perierat Adam qui derelinquendo pactum domini erraverat quia praeceptum quod acceperat non custodivit.  Modo lex sancta se ostendit lux sancta est quia cum lucerna in inferno descendit. Scopa enim immunditias omnes attrahet de domo paenitentiae. Adam vero post quinque milia quingentos annos dum legitimae esset paenitentiae in resurrectione Domini nostri Iesu Christi meruit accipere indulgentiam.
translation_en:
Verily holy, verily blessed is our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who made the woman troubled, who had ten coins; according to what is read in the holy gospel, because when she lost one of them, she lit a lamp and cleaned her house until she found it; she rejoiced with me and said: "Rejoice with me because I have found my lost coin."
This woman shows the law's pact here; ten coins represent ten heads chosen by God, that is, the sons of the first law. First, Adam was chosen whom He had formed from the dust of the earth. Second, Noah himself was chosen and found him righteous whom He saved from the flood. Third, Abraham was chosen from among those who believed, and made him the father of many nations. Fourth, Isaac was chosen by the promise of God born to him. Fifth, Jacob was chosen to receive the blessing. Sixth, Joseph was chosen, and he preserved his chastity and humiliated his accuser, the lady of his house. Seventh, Lot was chosen, whom He found just and a host to angels, and saved him from the judgment of Sodom. Eighth, Moses was chosen as leader to lead the children of Israel through the Red Sea. Ninth, Joshua was chosen to enter the land of promise. Tenth, David was chosen to anoint him king. In other words: Noah preserved justice, Abraham faith, Isaac God's promise, Jacob his blessing, Joseph chastity, Lot hospitality, Moses leadership, Joshua a whole successor, and David the royal unction. From all these, one coin that was lost was Adam, who, by abandoning the covenant of the Lord, erred because he did not keep the commandment that he had received.
Now, the holy law shows itself as light, because when the lamp went down to hell. A broom, however, attracts all impurities from the house of penitence. Adam, therefore, after five thousand and five hundred years, at the resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ, merited to receive indulgence for legitimate penitence.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui nobis hunc diem et sanctorum Macchabaeorum passione illustrem et Felicis sui felicitate reddidit enitentem.  Te proinde Deus pater exoramus adclines ut in hac concreta martyrum tuorum festivitate supplicantibus nobis et amorem implendae legis tuae pro qua illi passi sunt tribuas et Felicis tui suffragio tempora feliciora concedas.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily blessed is our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who has made this day and the Passion of the holy Maccabees illustrious and joyful for us. Therefore, we pray to you, God Father, that in this feast of your martyrs, you would incline towards us; granting us love for fulfilling your law for which they suffered, and that through the intercession of your happy one, happier times may be granted.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui nobis praecepta salutaris abstinentiae dedit per quam cum adiuncta oratione et incursus daemonum pelleremus et mundati a vitiis in sanctitate et iustitia serviremus.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily blessed is our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who gave us the salutary precepts of abstinence. By them, along with an added prayer and repelling the attacks of demons, we may drive away and cleanse ourselves from vices, serving in sanctity and justice.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui non ex virili semine natus sed ex spiritu est tuo Deus pater conceptus; qui dedit mundo per incarnationem adventus sui novum fidei lumen reserans viam quae obstrusa fuerat hominis primoplasti ex culpa.
translation_en: Truly holy, truly blessed is our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who was not born from a human father but conceived by your Spirit, God the Father; who gave to the world through incarnation his advent, new light of faith, uncovering the way that was obstructed for man's first creation due to sin.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui nos et vitiis abstinere et cibis edocuit. Ab illo quippe et abstinendi docemur exemplis et abstinentiae remuneramur ex donis.  Proinde te Deus pater rogamus ut per illum sit nobis et in praesenti huius mundi labore consolatio et in aeterna vita donetur beatitudinis plenitudo.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily blessed is our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who taught us to abstain from sins and to be instructed with food. Indeed, we learn to abstain through his examples, and are rewarded for abstinence by gifts. Therefore, we ask God the Father on your behalf that through Him may be to us consolation in the trials of this world, and eternal life be granted the fullness of blessedness.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui nos per abstinentiam reddit caelo quos homo primus gula praecipitante miserat in profundo.  Ipsi ergo servitutis reddamur obsequia qui mundum sanguine suo liberavit ex poena; ipsi nos in hostia ieiunii offeramus qui solus patri hostia pro nobis est immolatus.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily blessed is our Lord Jesus Christ, Your Son, who by abstinence returns us to heaven, whom man first sent down to the deep by the urging of gluttony. To Him then let us render obedience, who freed the world with His blood from punishment; to Him we offer ourselves as sacrifice in the fast, who alone was immolated for us as an offering to the Father.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui ortu suo mundum illuminavit passione sua redemit morte propria nos a mortis imperio eruit et resurrectione sua spem resurgendi credentibus praebuit. Adscensione sua in caelis polorum regna nobis clementer aperuit ut illic nos coheredes faceret vitae suae qui hic particeps fieri voluit mortis nostrae.  Ipsius namque praecepto compulsus hic sanctus Thomas apostolus cuius hodie natalicium ovantes celebramus regna Indorum devotus adiit ubi ineffabilia miraculorum signa divino munere ditatus patravit restituens caecorum oculis visum surdis auditum claudicantibus gressum et exanimatis corporibus potiorem vivendi usum.  Fugavit ab obsessis corporibus hostem cum satellitibus suis antiquissimum et a cunctis languoribus curavit populum Christo domino fideliter crediturum. Leprosos mundavit confortavit debilia membra orationibus crebris animasque salvificans praedicationibus sacris innumerabilem plebem acquisivit Christo propter quam fuerat directus ab ipso inter barbaricas nationes.  Plerumque insidiis affectus carcerali vinculo crudeliter addictus Senticitiam fidelissimam feminam ad usum vivendi restituit quam per ternos annos caecitate detentam praedicationis suae verbo corde et corpore mirifice illuminavit. Adeo profuit cunctis audientibus sermo divinus apostolico ore prolatus ut etiam regum coniuges regalia horrerent cubilia et immaculato gressu sequerentur eum qui omnes in se credentes ad supernum perducit regnum.
translation_en:
Verily holy, verily blessed is our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who with his birth enlightened the world, with his passion redeemed, with his death freed us from the power of death, and with his resurrection gave hope of resurrection to believers. Ascending into heaven, he opened for us by his mercy the kingdoms of the heavens of the skies, so that there he might make us co-heirs of his life, which he wished to share in our humanity here.
Indeed, compelled by his command, this holy Thomas the apostle, whose birthday we celebrate today, devoted himself to the kingdoms of the Indians, where, endowed with divine miracles, he performed wonders: restoring sight to the blind, hearing to the deaf, making the lame walk, and giving a more abundant life to the lifeless bodies.
He drove away the enemy from besieged bodies with his satellites, the oldest one, and cured all infirmities of the people who believed faithfully in Christ as their Lord. He cleansed lepers, comforted the weak limbs with frequent prayers, saved countless souls with sacred preachings, and acquired an immense crowd for Christ, whom he was directed to among barbarian nations because of them.
Often threatened by cunning traps, Thomas was cruelly bound by a carceral chain. However, he restored the most faithful woman, Senticia, to life, whom he illuminated miraculously with his word, both in heart and body, for three years held captive by blindness. The divine speech proclaimed by apostolic mouth produced such effect on all who listened that even the beds of kings trembled, and they followed him with immaculate steps who leads all those who believe in him to the heavenly kingdom.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui parvulorum suorum Iusti et Pastoris roboravit infantiam quo eorum tenera aetas persequentis posset sustinere tormenta quique in illis cum se invicem ad passionem exhortarentur fari dignatus est per gratiae donum qui non vigore corporis sed spiritus optatum continuo adepturi erant martyrium.  Propter quod debitas illi tecum atque sancto spiritui gratias referentes qui solus abundans in dono gratiae ex ore infantium et lactentium perfecisti laudem precamur ut horum innocentiam mereamur tenere dum vivimus quorum hodie festa sollemnia celebramus.
translation_en:
Verily holy, verily blessed is our Lord Jesus Christ, Your Son, who strengthened the infancy of His just and Shepherd children, so that their tender age, pursuing them, could bear torments. And He was willing to grant martyrdom through the gift of grace not by the strength of the body but of spirit.
Therefore, referring back to You and the Holy Spirit the debt of thanks that is due for this, who alone abounds in the gift of grace from the mouths of infants and sucklings, You perfected praise. We pray that we may deserve to keep their innocence as long as we live, whose feast day we celebrate today.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui per clausa ostia dum discipulos visitaret introivit ut Deus et cum de veritate corporis sui dubitantibus peteret panem et manducaret homo est verus inventus. Illud faciens mirabiliter hoc misericorditer; illud ad glorificandam potentiam divinitatis hoc ad asserendam substantiam carnis.  Oportebat quippe eos illum in utraque natura conspicere quem mediatorem iubebantur Dei atque hominum praedicare cui favum mellis simpliciter offerentes fidem suam locuti sunt donis mysticis nos docentes. Sic est enim ex duabus rebus simplex favi confecta materia sicut ex naturis duabus una Christi creditur exstitisse persona.
translation_en:
Verily holy, verily blessed is our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who, while visiting the disciples through locked doors, entered as God. With those questioning about His true bodily presence, He asked for bread and ate as a man. Truly this was found to be real. This marvelously and mercifully did; this for the glory of divine power, this for asserting the substance of flesh.
 It was indeed necessary that they should perceive Him in both natures, whom they were commanded to preach as Mediator between God and man. Speaking simply of honeycomb (mead), they offered their faith in mystic gifts, teaching us. For just as the simple matter of honeycomb is made from two substances, so too one person of Christ is believed to have existed from two natures.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui potentissimus sanctorum omnium veneratur in terris et gloriosior prae cunctis angelis gloriatur in caelis.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily blessed is our Lord Jesus Christ, Your Son, who is the most powerful of all saints and is revered on earth, and is more glorious than all angels and glorified in heaven.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui praedictos martyres suos et medicaminis arte industrios et crucis efficit patibulo gloriosos. In utroque igitur capitis sui imitantes exemplum et curationum enitent gratia et crucifixionis mulctati sunt poena.  Sic sic delitescenda virtus martyrum quae terris occulitur  in crucis porrecta patibulo exaltatur. Tenuit illic humilitas in abditis ne vanitati patesceret quod hic crux patula omnibus admirandum fore monstraret. Nec tamen hoc cruciatu martyrum elabitur vita quo sua mortificari redemptor voluit membra ut quibus cruce crucifixi vita promittebatur in cruce positi non deficerent sed gauderent.
translation_en:
Verily holy, verily blessed is our Lord Jesus Christ, Your Son, who makes the prophesied martyrs glorious on the cross by their diligence in medical arts and the use of the cross. In both head and sufferings they imitate His example, receiving grace and being chastened by crucifixion as a penalty.
Thus, thus may the virtue of the martyrs be hidden on earth but exalted on the cross. There, humility held back so that it would not reveal itself to vanity, what here the open cross would show admirable to all. Yet, this crucifixion of the martyrs does not destroy life, for as their Redeemer willed to mortify members, so those who were placed on the cross promised life in Christ would not fail but rejoice.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui quadraginta diebus vel noctibus ieiunavit et postea esurivit. Tantorum quippe dierum ieiunando protelationem explens quia Deus erat; et postea esuriens quia hominem verum assumpserat.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily blessed is our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who fasted for forty days or nights and afterwards ate. For indeed these days of fasting He prolonged because He was God; and afterwards He ate because He had truly taken on human nature.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui repudiata immundorum contagione libaminum simplicem ritum novae sanctionis instituit docuitque discipulos suos inter haec sacrosancta sollemnia innocentia pura vivere et Deo soli hostiam laudis offerre.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily blessed is our Lord Jesus Christ, Your Son, who, rejecting the contagion of the unclean, instituted a simple and new-sanctioned rite, and taught His disciples to live innocently pure among these sacred solemnities, and to offer the offering of lauds only to God.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui sanctae tuae illius virginis arcana possidens ei et virginitatis pudorem et passionis ruborem tribuisti dum et pudica in secreto et invicta in foro et illic manet ut te promereatur et hic vincit ut a te coronetur.  Annue igitur precibus eius ut conscientiam nostram pudor possideat nec deserat fortitudo quo per illud tranquilla maneat ne contaminetur; per hoc vincere studeat ut probetur.
translation_en:
Verily holy, verily blessed is our Lord Jesus Christ, Your Son, who possessing the secrets of that same virgin, grants her both the modesty of virginity and the glow of passion. He remains pure in secret and invincible in public, so that he may be promised to you and here he conquers so that he may be crowned by you.
Grant, therefore, his prayers, so that our conscience may possess modesty and fortitude, lest it forsake tranquility or become defiled; through this, let him strive to conquer in order to be proven.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui se in visceribus athletae sui Cucufatis et misericordem probat et admirabilem manifestat cum sic in illis semel illapsus est ut nec inclusa corpore fidem amitterent nec effusa miraculi novitate carerent.  Quin potius fusa pro se martyris Christus in suppliciis viscera inaestimabili miraculo revocaret ad vitam seque in illis viventem ostenderet quae foris ferus carnifex avulsisset ut in quibus semel fuerat infusus per gratiam non pateretur deperire penitus per naturam.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily blessed is our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who was within the bowels of the athlete Cucufatus and proved his mercy and manifested his marvelous act, when once falling upon them, neither did they lose their enclosed faith nor lacked they the novelty of miracles that were poured out for Him. Rather, the martyr Christ was poured out for himself in the tortures with an inestimable miracle recalling them to life and showing Himself living within them whom the cruel butcher outside had torn apart, so that in whom He once was infused by grace would not allow to perish utterly by nature.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui solus est vita mortalium et immortalitas redemptorum.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily blessed is our Lord Jesus Christ, Your Son, who alone is the life of the mortal and the immortality of the redeemed.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui solus servientium tibi et primordia consecrat et fines glorificanter exornat qui illorum commendat exitum signis quorum vitam ambitio exornaverit sanctitatis quique huius confessoris sui ita est glorificatus in opere ut non pateretur eum confundi inimicis in porta loquentem.  Hic quippe vir cuius mundo vita in testimonium discipulis exstitit in exemplum vidit eminus se obviante consistere adversarium quem eo apertis oraculis exprobravit quo se continuo in sinu Abrahae recipi veridica inspectione praescivit. Hunc tu Deus summe coram te pro nostris facinoribus intercessorem statue quem dono gratiae tuae et vita perlustrem et mortis interminatione constituisti insignem.
translation_en:
Verily holy, verily blessed is our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who alone sanctifies those serving you and adorns the beginnings gloriously and the ends. He commends to them an exit marked by signs, whose life ambition has embellished with holiness; and this confessor of his is so glorified in deeds that he could not be shamed before enemies while speaking at the gate.
Indeed, this man, whose life in the world served as a testament to disciples and appeared as an example, saw the enemy confronting him from afar; and with open oracles, he reproached him whom he clearly foresaw receiving in true inspection into the bosom of Abraham.
May you, O God most high, establish this man as an intercessor for our sins before you, whom you have made prominent by your grace and life, and who, having been constituted by your mercy, is a beacon against the termination of death.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui solus verbo virtutis cuncta moderans et omnia crucis destina portans vectes ferreos comminuit portarumque aerearum claustra perfregit tartara profunda descendit sedentibus in umbra mortis ignotae lucis claritate resplenduit et sol iustitiae de tumulo corpore suscitato procedens radiis suis tenebras nostras mirabiliter illustravit.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily blessed is our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who alone with the power of his word governs all things and carries on the cross everything iron-hard; he crushed the gates, broke through the bronze-clad bars, descended into the depths of Tartarus, shone in the unknown shadow of death with the brightness of light, and from the body raised up proceeded, miraculously illuminating our darkness with his rays.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui suorum martyrum illorum passiones ponit ad cultum perducit ad praemium porrigit ad exemplum proponit ad fidem glorificat laude exornat honore ut illorum mors dedicetur in laudibus quorum4 fuit vita compta virtutibus; ut mentio adscribatur laudi quorum vita confixa est cruci; ut quod perierat passione revivescat laude et quod affectum est contumeliis dedicetur obsequiis; ut perpetuus vivat honor in sanctis et merces in miseris cum quidquid martyribus impenditur ad honorem obsequentibus proficiat ad salutem.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily blessed is our Lord Jesus Christ, Your Son, who places the sufferings of His martyrs for use, leads them to reward, offers them as an example, glorifies them with praise, adorns them with honor, so that their death may be dedicated to praise, whose life was filled with virtues; so that mention may be ascribed to the laud of those whose life was fixed on the cross; so that what perished in Passion may revive with praise and what was dedicated to contumely may be consecrated with obedience; so that eternal honor may live among the saints and mercy among the miserable, with whatever rewards are bestowed upon martyrs, may progress towards salvation for those who render obedience.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui testis sui Saturnini cuius fuerat et voce praedicatus et sanguine victorem spiritum extulit caelo corpus condidit in sepulcro; illius demum cineres glorificando translationis honore cuius olim animam passionis laureaverat munere.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily blessed is our Lord Jesus Christ, Your Son, who was the witness of Saturninus, whose voice was proclaimed and victorious through blood, raised spirit to heaven, laid down body in the tomb; indeed, his final ashes were glorified by the honor of translation, whose soul had once been rewarded with the gift of passion's laurel.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui traditus ac mortuus est propter peccata nostra et resurrexit propter iustificationem nostram.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily blessed is our Lord Jesus Christ, Your Son, who was handed over and died for our sins and rose again for our justification.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui ut mortalium sordes elueret opprobrium mortalitatis accepit; ut nos a poenis perpetuis liberaret poenarum cruciamenta sustinuit; ut mortem in nobis vita perimeret ad mortem usque cunctorum vita pervenit; ut viam nobis caelestis patriae reseraret aeris liquidi viam ipse devicta morte transcurrens supra caelos in tua parte dextera regnaturus adscendit. Per quem te supplices exoramus ut haec typica sacramenta respiciendo sanctifices et sanctificando respicias ut corporis et sanguinis sui mysteria percepturis ipse fautor exsistat ad veniam qui liberalis exstitit redemptor ad vitam.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily blessed is our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who took on the filth of humanity to wash away the shame of mortality; who suffered eternal punishment to free us from perpetual penalties; who conquered death by dying so that life might conquer death in us; who opened for us the way to the heavenly homeland by passing over the waters of liquid air, vanquished by death, ruling above the heavens at your right hand; through whom we humbly beseech you to look upon these typical sacraments and sanctify them, and in sanctifying, to look upon us so that we may perceive the mysteries of his body and blood. May he, our advocate and generous redeemer, be present to grant forgiveness and eternal life.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui venit e caelis ut conversaretur in terris; caro factus est ut habitaret in nobis.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily blessed is our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who came from heaven to dwell on earth; flesh was made for him to live among us.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui venit de caelis ut conversaretur in terris; homo factus ut habitaret in nobis; hostia effectus ut nos faceret sacerdotes.
translation_en: Truly holy, truly blessed is our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who came from heaven to dwell on earth; made man to live among us; fashioned as a sacrifice to make us priests.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui venit quaerere et salvum facere quod perierat.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily blessed is our Lord Jesus Christ, Your Son, who comes to seek and save that which was lost.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui veridicam humilitatem generi humano demonstrans surgens a cenae convivio aqua in pelvim missa suorum laverit pedes discipulorum magister et Dominus et linteo quo erat praecinctus extersit.  Atque ut totius mundi mortis chirographum deleret nullius peccati conscius omnium pro delictis hominum voluntarie adstitit immolandus.
translation_en:
Truly holy, truly blessed is our Lord Jesus Christ, Your Son, who, demonstrating genuine humility to the human race, rising from the dinner party of the supper, washed His disciples' feet with water in a basin and dried them with a towel which was girded around Him.
And that He might destroy the legal instrument of death for the entire world, being conscious of no sin, voluntarily stood up to be sacrificed for the sins of all men.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui voluntatem timentium se facit et orationes eorum exaudit quique admirabili clementia ita se diligentium desideriis favet ut eorum votis postulata non deneget.  Etenim ingenita bonitas eius sacratissimam Dorotheam virginem exaudire non destitit imprecantem cum non solum de propriae passionis attollitur palma sed etiam de sororum quas Christo acquisierat tripudiatur corona.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily blessed is our Lord Jesus Christ, Your Son, who makes the wishes of those fearing Him come true and listens to their prayers. He shows such great kindness that He favors their desires so much that He does not deny what they ask for in their prayers. Indeed, His innate goodness did not neglect to hear Dorothea, the most sacred virgin, who prayed, not only was her palm raised because of her own passion but also her crown danced because of her sisters whom Christ had acquired.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus quo inspirante ianuam praesentis anni in confessione intramus; quove tacti compungimur ut reliquos excursus temporum in divinis obsequiis transigere delectemur. Ipse est vere Salvator noster et dominus Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui est et consecratio temporum et conditor saeculorum.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily blessed is our Lord Jesus Christ, Son of yours. With Him inspiring us, we enter the door of the present year in confession; where we are touched, we are moved to penitence so that we delight to pass through the remaining courses of time in divine service. He truly is our Savior and Jesus Christ, Son of yours, who is both the consecrator of times and the creator of ages.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus Dominus noster Iesus Christus qui est Filius tuus natura non adoptione neque gratia sed generatione; qui in utraque natura unus filius creditur et tertia in Trinitate persona tecum et cum spiritu unus Deus creditur et adoratur.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily blessed is our Lord Jesus Christ, who is Your Son not by adoption or grace but by generation; who, in both natures, is believed to be one son and, in the Trinity, the third person is believed and worshipped as one God with You and the Holy Spirit.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus Dominus noster Iesus Christus qui esurienti multitudini in quinque panibus et duobus piscibus cibus esse dignatus est non ut milium convenientia quod factum mirifice sacra evangeliorum testantur eloquia sed per librorum volumina quinque per quae insatiata populi pectora Moysen canente replentur. Proinde apostolis congregatum iussit fenum adspargere id ignorantiam plebis replendam dominicis praeparare praeceptis.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily blessed is our Lord Jesus Christ who was pleased to provide food for the multitude with five loaves of bread and two fish, not according to the convenient measure as testified by the miraculous words of the sacred gospels, but through the books of five which, through the insatiable people's hearts being filled by Moses singing, are prepared to dispel ignorance among the assembly of apostles.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus Dominus noster Iesus Christus qui in adventu iudicii sui et tremendus ab impiis et gloriosus visurus est ab electis; cuius nos incarnatio reparavit ad vitam mors redemit a poena resurrectio innovavit ad gloriam.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily blessed is our Lord Jesus Christ, who in His coming judgment will be terrible to the unrighteous and glorious to the chosen; whose incarnation restored us to life, death redeemed us from punishment, and resurrection renewed us to glory.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus Dominus noster Iesus Christus unigenitus tuus qui martyrem suum Stephanum caelestis aulae collegio muneravit; qui corporis nostri infirmitatem suscepit et qui priusquam pium sanguinem pro humana salute funderet mysterium sacrae sollemnitatis instituit.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily blessed is our Lord Jesus Christ, your only-begotten one, who appointed his martyr Stephen to the heavenly court; who took upon himself the infirmity of our body and who instituted the mystery of the sacred solemnity before spilling his precious blood for the salvation of mankind.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus es Christe redemptor qui nostrorum dissolvisti vincula peccatorum et triumphans de inferis liber remeasti ad solium tuum.
translation_en: Truly holy, truly blessed are you, Christ, redeemer, who have dissolved the bonds of our sins and, triumphing over death, have freed us to sit on your throne.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus es Domine Deus Iesu Christe qui et vivis praestas salutem et defunctos perducis ad requiem. Te ergo poscimus mentis intentione ut hoc sacrificium acceptans digneris sanctificare et famulorum tuorum illorum pro quibus offertur locum lucis aeternae tribuas possidere.  Nobis quoque te orantibus praesentis temporis concede salutem et aeternam fac perfrui lucem.
translation_en:
Verily holy, verily blessed are you, Lord God Jesus Christ, who both live provide salvation and lead the dead to rest. Therefore we humbly ask you with our mental intention that accepting this sacrifice, you may deign to sanctify it and grant everlasting light for those for whom it is offered a place in eternal light.
Grant us too at this present time the salvation and may the eternal light shine upon us.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus es Domine Deus noster auctor vitae et conditor qui futurae resurrectionis es redemptor reparator et indultor; qui promissae immortalitatis dispensator es atque largitor; qui posuisti praesentis vitae terminum ut aeternitatis reserares introitum et per finem praesentium principia panderes futurorum; qui necessitatem animarum recedentium a corporibus non interitum voluisti esse sed somnium ut dissolutio dormiendi roboraret fiduciam resurgendi dum in te credentium vivendi usus non amittitur sed transfertur et fidelium tuorum mutatur vita non tollitur.  Cuius institutionem nulla diversitas mortis nullum iudicium indictae mortalitatis illudit et ita opera digitorum tuorum perire non pateris ut quidquid hominum per mortis varietatem tempus labefecerit aura dissolverit ignis consumpserit avis rapuerit fera discerpserit terra obsorbucrit pulvis involverit gurgis immerserit piscis exscreaverit bellua exhauserit vel quidquid in vetustissimum mare fuerit redactum te iubente terra restituat induatque incorruptionem deposita corruptione.  Te exoramus Domine ac supplices petimus ne spiritus fidelium sepultorum aut tristibus tenebris aut ignitis gehennae caminis aut perpetuis tartari frigoribus deputati poenalem locum ad habitandum accipiant sed in sinu Abrahae et in gremio patriarcharum requiescentes tempus resurrectionis diemque iudicii cum gaudio secuturae immortalitatis exspectent.
translation_en:
Verily holy, verily blessed art thou, Lord God our maker and creator, who art the redeemer, restorer, and grantor of the future resurrection; who art the dispensator and giver of promised immortality; who didst set a limit to this present life in order to open the entrance to eternity and through the end of the present, didst show the principles of the future; who hast desired that the departure of souls from bodies is not death but sleep, so that the faith of those believing in thee, whose living usage is not lost but transferred, and the life of thy faithful ones is changed not destroyed.
Whose institution no diversity of death nor judgment of the appointed mortality hinders and thus work of thine fingers perishes not, but whatever time has been shaken by the variety of death shall be dissolved by air, consumed by fire, carried off by birds, torn apart by beasts, swallowed by fish, exhaled by whales, or whatever has been reduced to the oldest sea, thou hast commanded the earth to restore and clothe with incorruption what was laid low with corruption.
We beseech thee, Lord, and suppliantly ask that the spirits of thy faithful ones buried may not receive a penal place to dwell in, either in sad darkness or fiery gehenna's chimneys or perpetual frosts of tartarus, but resting in the bosom of Abraham and in the embrace of patriarchs, they may await the day of resurrection and the judgment with joyful expectation of eternal life.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus es Domine Deus noster in cuius manu est ultionis censura et sanitatis medela; qui paenitentibus parcis; qui lacrimosis indulges; qui gementes exaudis; qui ieiunantium contritionem comprobas; qui votum contriti cordis acceptas.  Quiescat iam quaesumus indignatio tua et placare super haec sacrificia tibi oblata ut totius delicti nostri delens chirographum institutum a te hoc nostrum ieiunium acceptetur.
translation_en:
Verily holy, verily blessed are You, Lord God our Savior in whose hand is the judgment and remedy of vengeance and health; who shows mercy to the penitent, who forgives the weeping, who hears those who mourn, who approves the contrition of those who fast, who accepts the vow of a contrite heart.
We humbly ask that Your indignation rest now and that You be appeased regarding these sacrifices offered to You, so that this our penance, instituted by You, may be accepted as erasing the entire contract of our sin.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus es Domine Deus noster qui corona es martyrum et perpetua claritas angelorum.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily blessed are you, Lord our God, who are the crown of martyrs and the perpetual light of angels.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus es Domine Deus noster qui cum nullius cibi indigeas alimenti initia tamen messium ac vinearum offerri tibimet in sacrificium voluisti ut quae de manu tua erant accepta reddantur tibi.  Ecce et nos acceptas de tuis manibus primitias nostrarum frugum tibi litamus in sacrificium ut ab omnibus frugibus nostris repulsis cunctis incommodis et terrae nostrae fructum multiplices et animas benedictione perlustres.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily blessed are you, Lord God our Savior, who, needing no food of your own, yet have desired that the beginnings of grain and vine offerings be made to you in sacrifice; so that what has been received by your hand may be returned to you. Indeed, and we, accepted from your hands, offer the first fruits of our crops to you as a sacrifice, so that from all our crops, rejected are all the troubles, and may the produce of our land be abundant and our souls be blessed with your benediction.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus es Domine Deus noster qui cum totum quod habemus nobis videaris dedisse decimam tamen a nobis videris repetere nec tibi sed nobis procul dubio profuturum cum si a nobis tibi fideliter detur et abundantiam frugum et salutem corporum nihilominus consequimur.  Praesta his famulis tuis offerentibus tibi suorum decimas frugum temporalium in rebus augmentum ut multiplex rerum quas tibi nunc deferunt ex voto tibi per multa curricula <annorum> animo offerant voluntario et corde perfecto.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily blessed art Thou, Lord our God, who seemeth to have given us all that we possess, yet Thou seemest to reclaim a tithe from us; but it is undoubtedly profitable for us, if faithfully we give unto Thee. Even though we gain abundance of crops and health of bodies, nevertheless we follow these offerings which they bring Thee as their tithes of temporal fruits in things, that multiplying the things which Thou now receive from them by vow, they may offer it with a willing heart and perfect spirit through many rounds of years.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus es Domine Deus noster qui ex omnibus gentibus gloriosam tibi assumis ecclesiam quae tuae passionis et resurrectionis gloriam praedicando et augmentum capit per fidem et gloriae suscipit retributionem cum tibi indesinenter beneplacitam exhibet operationem.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily blessed are you, Lord God our Savior, who from all nations have assumed a glorious church for yourself, which, by preaching and spreading the glory of your Passion and Resurrection, increases through faith and accepts recompense in glory, continually presenting to you an operation pleasing to you.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus es Domine Deus noster qui nec per spatia locorum nec per intervalla temporum ab his quos tueris discedis.  Adesto quaesumus famulis tuis illis in te ubique fidentibus et per omnem quam ituri sunt viam dux eis atque protector esse dignare. Nihil adversitatis eis noceat. Cuncta eis sint prospera ut sub ope dexterae tuae quidquid iusto expetierint desiderio celeri consequantur effectu.
translation_en:
Truly holy, truly blessed are you, Lord our God, who do not depart from those whom you protect, neither by distances of places nor intervals of time.
We humbly ask that you be present to your servants among those who trust in you everywhere, and grant to be their guide and protector through all the ways they may go. May nothing harm them. Let all things be prosperous for them so that whatever they desire justly, under the power of your right hand, they may quickly attain by effect.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus es Domine Deus noster qui percutis et sanas vulneras et mederis; quique nos sic castigas verbere ut refoveas pietate; sic languoribus tangis ut sanitatibus consoleris.
translation_en: Truly holy, truly blessed are you, Lord our God, who heals and soothes wounds; you who chastise us with a rod to renew us with kindness; you who touch us with weakness to comfort us with health.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus es Domine Iesu Christe quies fidelis in verbis tuis et sanctus in omnibus operibus tuis; qui nos iam nunc eodem coram te facis spiritu gemere cuius praesentiam praecipis exspectare.  Hinc igitur quia quid oremus nescimus ipse te Dei Filius pro nobis interpellet gemitibus inenarrabilibus quo ineffabili pietate prius nos idem spiritus ex donis praeveniendo sanctificet et post adveniens beatiores inveniet quos coronet.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily blessed art Thou, Lord Jesus Christ. Thy faithful peace rests in Thy words and Thou art holy in all Thy works; who makest us now to groan the same Spirit whose presence Thou biddest us eagerly to await. Hence, because we know not what to pray for, Thine own Self, the Son of God, intercedes for us with inexpressible groans, with an unfathomable pity, which Spirit preceding as gifts sanctifies us, and following makes us more blessed to be crowned.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus es tu Filius Dei vivi quia multum es incomparabiliter pius et inaestimabiliter gloriosus. Et ideo tuae pietatis gloriam imploramus et hanc tibi placationis hostiam immolamus ut nostras nunc orationes exaudias crimina laxes et omnia peccata dimittas vel quidquid a te secundum tuam voluntatem exposcimus velociter clementerque impertias quatenus nos a malis omnibus eruas et bonis repleri concedas.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily blessed are you, Son of the Living God, for you are greatly incomparably merciful and inestimably glorious. And therefore we implore the glory of your mercy and offer this sacrifice of propitiation to you, that now you hear our prayers, forgive our sins, and remit all our transgressions; or whatever we ask of you according to your will, grant it swiftly and mercifully, so that you deliver us from all evil and fill us with good things.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus et gloriosus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui nos et in priori adventu gratia reparavit et in secundo daturum se nobis regnum cum suis angelis repromisit.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily blessed and glorious is our Lord Jesus Christ, Your Son, who restored grace to us at His first coming, and has promised that He will give us a kingdom with His angels at His second coming.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus Iesus Christus Filius tuus Dominus noster qui sub hodiernae exspectatione virtutis redeunti ad te homini viam praestitit ipse dum via est; qui indemutabili divinitatis suae in se manente substantia peracto incarnationis nativitatis passionis resurrectionis adscensionis officio eum in caelis regnaturus imponit quem in infernis liberaturus intravit nihil dubitationis volens relinquere nihil erroris si cum eo visibiliter adscenderet pro quo invisibiliter descendisset ut incredula plebs iudaicae multitudinis esset confusa dum reverteretur quae non fuerat confessa dum nasceretur et quae non meruit credere dum venisset possit erubescere dum rediret ut videret in Deo hominem quae Deum in homine non vidisset non quod paeniteret dum ostenditur sed ut erubesceret dum miratur.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily blessed is Jesus Christ, your Son, our Lord, who under today's expectation of returning virtue made a way for mankind; He himself walked the way while it was there, who, maintaining unchangeable divinity within Himself, completed incarnation, nativity, passion, resurrection, ascension, and will rule Him in heaven, whom He will free from hell. He desires to leave no room for doubt and error when visible ascending with Him, who invisibly descended, so that the unbelieving Jewish multitude would be confused, returning what had not been confessed when it was born and did not deserve to believe when it came; It can blush when it returns, seeing in God a man which did not see God in man; Not because it repents when it is shown but because it blushes when it marvels.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus in altissimis Iesus Christus Filius tuus Dominus noster qui assumpta humanae fragilitatis natura non solum infidelium sterilitatem convertendo fecundavit verum etiam antiquissimum serpentem seductionibus blandis illecebrantem totiusque mundi copiam promittentem sterilitate cibi praemissa post ieiunii peracta sollemnia omnipotenti brachio supplantavit docens discipulos suos apostolos nostros non numerositate taurorum aut hircorum non vitulorum ubertate non agnorum pinguium victimis tuam placare clementiam posse sed puris mentibus lotisque innocentiae manibus sacrificia delibare tuae serenitati simplicia.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily blessed in the highest Jesus Christ, Your Son, our Lord, who assuming the fragile nature of humanity not only converted the sterility of unbelievers into fruitfulness but also subdued the oldest serpent, enticing with sweet allurements, and promised the whole world's abundance with food after fasting, performed miracles through omnipotent arm, teaching Your apostles our disciples that it is not the numerical strength of bulls or goats, nor the wealth of oxen or sheep, nor the fat victims of rams that can appease Your clemency but pure minds washed with innocence that can offer simple sacrifices to Your serenity.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus in excelsis Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus rex Israel qui sicut ovis ad occisionem ductus et sicut agnus coram tondente sine voce sic non aperuit os suum.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily blessed in the highest is our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, the King of Israel. Who, led as a sheep to slaughter and behold, as a lamb before the shearer, opened not his mouth.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus qui venit in nomine domini rex Israel. Qui iam venit humilis et adhuc venturus est in maiestate terribilis; qui iam venit ut iudicaretur in mundum et adhuc venturus est ut iudicet mundum; qui iam venit ut redimeret a morte quos ad vitam praedestinavit et adhuc venturus est ut remuneret quos redemit.
translation_en: Truly holy, truly blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, King of Israel. He has come humbly and will still come in terrible majesty; he has come to be judged in the world and will still come to judge the world; he has come to redeem from death those whom he had predestined for life and is still coming to reward those he has redeemed.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus unigenitus Filius tuus Dominus noster qui passione crucis suae allevat pondus iniquitatis nostrae et dat finem piaculis per oblationem sacrificii singularis. Unde tali spei robore solidati cum magna fiducia ea quae non reprobet salubriter impetremus et ea quae diligit gratissime deferamus.  Ponamus interim in illo spem nostram confidentes de misericordia sua. Ipse enim qui hos ieiuniorum dies fecit nos pietatis suae beneficiis mediare faciet ad calicem passionis suae et nunc immaculatos accedere et ad sanctum pascha ablutis delictorum sordibus pervenire.
translation_en:
Verily holy, verily blessed is the only-begotten Son of yours, our Lord, who alleviates the burden of our iniquity through his passion of the cross and gives an end to our sins by the offering of a single sacrifice. Therefore, strengthened with such hope, we pray confidently for what he will not refuse healthily and offer gratefully what he loves most.
Meanwhile, let us place our hope in him, confident in his mercy. For he who has made these days of fasting for us by his goodness will mediate us to the chalice of his passion, and now let us approach immaculate and reach the holy Easter, having been purified from the stains of sins by washing.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus unigenitus tuus Dominus noster et medicus qui non solum aegritudinem nostram quam paradisi exsules dolebamus absolvit verum etiam mortem primi parentis errore contractam pro sua pietate miseratus divina potestate superavit dum nobis et formam morum vivendo praebuit et peccatorum remissionem moriendo concessit.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily blessed, unigeniture thou art, our Lord and physician. Not only did he absolve our sickness, which we lamented as exiles of paradise, but also the death contracted by the first parent through error, out of pity he overcame with divine power. While living, he gave us the form of morals, and while dying, he granted us forgiveness for sins.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus unigenitus tuus primogenitus noster; primogenitus in gratia unigenitus in natura; primogenitus quia nemo ante ipsum unigenitus quia nemo post ipsum; qui cum in forma Dei esset non rapinam arbitratus est esse se aequalem Deo sed semetipsum exinanivit formam servi accipiens; perfectus in tuis et verus in nostris.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily blessed, only-begotten is your only-begotten one, our firstborn; only-begotten in grace, only-begotten in nature; firstborn because no one before him was begotten, because no one after him; who, being in the form of God, did not consider it robbery to be equal with God, but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, being born in human likeness; perfect in your nature and true in our humanity.

text: Vere sanctus vere benedictus vere mirabilis in sanctis suis Deus noster Iesus Christus; ipse dabit virtutem et fortitudinem plebi suae. Benedictus Deus quem benedicimus in apostolis et in omnibus sanctis suis qui placuerunt ei ab initio saeculi.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily blessed, verily marvelous is God our Jesus Christ in his saints. He himself will give power and courage to his people. Blessed be the God whom we bless in the apostles and in all his saints who pleased him from the beginning of the age.

text: Vere sanctus vere gloriosus Domine Deus noster. Te in caelestibus spiritalia te in terrenis humana venerantur. Et dum in supernis maiestas gloriae tuae attollitur in imis potentia virtutis augetur. Hic proferuntur obsequia mentium illic gaudia relaxantur animarum. Christum igitur rogemus auctorem quem scimus nobis celebrandum esse post mortem.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily glorious Lord, God our Creator. In heaven and on earth, you are honored with spiritual worship and human adoration. While in the heavens your majesty and glory are exalted, on earth your power and virtue are increased. Here the obeisance of minds is offered; there the joy of spirits is relaxed. Therefore we implore Christ, the author whom we know must be celebrated by us after death.

text: Vere sanctus vere gloriosus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui est custos virginitatis et virginale decus immensi pudoris; qui et in matre Maria virginitatem servavit et in martyre Eugenia integritatem virgineam contulit cum et illam virginem ipsa sui nativitate adsignat et istam per deceptricia accusantis Melantiae verba virginem manifestat.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily glorious is our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who is the guardian of virginity and the incomparable honor of immense modesty; who also preserved virginity in Mother Mary and bestowed unblemished virginity in Saint Eugenia during martyrdom. Moreover, he himself assigns her as a virgin at his own nativity and manifests her as a virgin through the words of accusing Melantia.

text: Vere sanctus vere gloriosus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui subsistendi nobis in labore fortitudinem donat cum inediae nostrae ubertatem suae dulcedinis administrat.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily glorious is our Lord Jesus Christ, Your Son, who gives us strength to endure in labor and administers the abundance of His sweetness in the face of our hunger.

text: Vere sanctus vere gloriosus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui trium martyrum hodie in passione laudatur.Vincentius quippe cum Sabina et Christeta sororibus in hoc die pro eius nomine viriliter agonizans contemnendo labilem vitam pretiosae mortis adeptus est gloriam. Cuius vestigium lapis in terra victoriam gestat remunerationem post supplicium custodia caelitus delata demonstrat. Tu igitur Domine in horum passione laudabilis tu gloriosus rn horum supplicio celebraris qui sanctorum tuorum quorum animas in aethereis locaveris regnis inhonora in terris corpora non relinquis.
translation_en: Verily, holy and verily glorious is our Lord Jesus Christ, Your Son, who today is praised in the passion of the three martyrs. Indeed, Vincent with Sabina and Christeta his sisters, on this day bravely struggling for his name, scorned the fragile life and achieved the glory of precious death. Whose footsteps a stone in the earth carries the victory as a reward after suffering, which heavenly guardianship reveals demonstrates. Therefore, Lord, in their passion you are worthy of praise, your glorious one, who celebrates their supplication in their suffering, who place the souls of Your saints in heavenly kingdoms, but do not abandon their bodies on earth.

text: Vere sanctus vere gloriosus es in sanctis tuis Christe Deus qui pro redimendis servulis passionis ludibria sustines et sustinentes sanctos perpetuitatis decore glorificas dans illis pro te et velle et posse voluntarie et mori et passionum tolerantia quasi diadematum pulchritudine decorari ut mundo dantes repudium te solum et vitae suae et mortis habeant lucem.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily glorious art thou in thy saints, Christ God, who for the redemption of your servants sustainest the mockeries of passion and, sustaining, glorifieth the saints with perpetual beauty, making them to desire and will, and to be able and to die, and to bear the torments of passions as a decoration of beauty, so that to the world you give a reproach, they having only you and life and death may have light.

text: Vere sanctus vere gloriosus potens et admirabilis Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus cuius confessionem in martyribus illatus furor non adimit cuiusque amorem insanientium cruciatio non exstinguit.  Huius itaque nomen beatissimus Saturninus et martyr tuus et ante supplicium praedicavit et inter supplicia non negavit cum persequentium circumdatus obicibus coactusque sacrificare daemonibus te unum et verum Deum voce clara se testatus est credere pro quo etiam et animam posuit usque a mortem.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily glorious, powerful and wonderful is our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, whose confession angered by the furor of martyrs could not be stolen, whose love for the insane could not be extinguished through crucification. Therefore, this name is most blessed: Saturninus, your martyr, who proclaimed it before suffering and did not deny it during suffering, surrounded by objects and compelled to sacrifice to demons, he declared with a clear voice to believe in you, the one and true God, even to the point of laying down his soul until death.

text: Vere sanctus vere gloriosus unigenitus tuus Dominus noster Iesus Christus qui cum ’de suo’ genitori esset aequalis ’de nostra’ factus est minor ab angelis et ex patre habens immortalitatem ex matre quod moreretur assumpsit ut in se liberaret genus humanum de tartaro dum ipsum mors non tenuit in sepulcro.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily glorious, your only-begotten Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, who, being equal with his own Father, was made less than the angels, and having immortality from the Father, took upon himself mortality in order to free mankind from the devil; while death itself did not hold him in the tomb.

text: Vere sanctus vere gloriosus vere multae pietatis Dominus unigenitus Iesus Christus Filius Dei vivi qui cum patre manem aeternitatis tuae prospectu definieras unam tibi de gentibus congregandam ecclesiam copulare; cuius copulationis mysterium in hoc sacramento corporis et sanguinis tui vera exhibitione complesti ad inhaerendum tibi emundans illam aqua baptismatis exhilarans oleo unctionis satiaris pane corporis et laetificans vino effusi cruoris.  Ipse redemptor eius ipse pro ea factus pretium emptionis non dans pro ea quamlibet pretiosam rem quae tamen esset quacumque vetustate solvenda quoniam et haec emenda erat nec vetustatis putredine nec vilitatis sorde poterat quandoque fatescere; sed vere teipsum dans aeternum atque immortalem ad mortem humilians emisisti illam ita eruens eam a ditione mortis ut conformares eam ad immortalitatis tuae gloriam et beatitudinem sempiternam.  Unde et haec talium beneficiorum indesinenter memor exsistens cum fide et gratulatione sincera tuae institutionis et suae redemptionis verba commemorat.
translation_en:
Verily holy, verily glorious, verily full of great piety, the Lord, only-begotten Son Jesus Christ, the Son of God living, who with the Father remains in eternal glory, you have defined one church to be gathered from among the nations for yourself, whose mystery of union is completed in this sacrament by a true exhibition of your body and blood, to cling to you. This Church is purified with water baptism, made glad with oil of unction, satisfied with bread of the body, and joyful with wine poured out, the shedding of whose blood.
This Redeemer himself, himself was made the price for this Church, not giving for it any precious thing that might be sold, yet something that could be bought with money; since this also needed to be redeemed, nor could putrefaction of age nor filth of lowliness cause it to perish. But truly you gave yourself eternal and immortal, humbling yourself unto death, releasing it so that you might raise it up from the power of death, making it conformable to your glory and everlasting beatitude.
Therefore, this Church continuously remembers such beneficences existing with faith and sincere gratitude, recounting in its words the institution and redemption of yours.

text: Vere sanctus vere haec illa praeclara et admirabilis supernarum creaturarum aeterna laudatio quae in caelestibus sine defectu psallitur ab angelis et hic sollemniter decantatur a populis. Illic collaudant caelestia hic adorant terrestria.  Illic sanctis tuis aeterna retribuis praemia hic fidelibus largam praestas misericordiam. Illa non deseris ista non despicis quia redemptorem nostrum piissime pater pro totius mundi salute ad nos misisti.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily that which is praiseworthy and wonderful, the eternal praise of the supernal creatures, which in heaven without fault is sung by angels, is here solemnly chanted by the people. There they bless the celestial beings; here on earth they adore them. There you reward your saints eternally with prizes, here you generously bestow mercy upon your faithful. There you do not forsake or despise, because most mercifully Father, you have sent our Redeemer to us for the salvation of the whole world.

text: Vere sanctus vere in altissimis gloriosus cuius melior est misericordia super terram qui dives est in misericordia. Ille etenim ieiunis visceribus spiritalis alimenti epulum donat et animabus vitio abstinentibus gratiae caelestis donaria subministrat.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily exalted, glorious in the heights, whose mercy is superior on earth who is rich in mercy. Indeed, He gives spiritual food as a feast to those who fast and grants celestial gifts to souls abstaining from sin.

text: Vere sanctus vere in altissimis gloriosus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus a quo Stephanus martyr primus atque levita coronari promeruit passione suscepta dum et curri ceteris consecrandus apostolorum electione in ministerio eligitur septimus et singulariter pro Christo martyrium adeptus est primus; qui ideo lapidari se voluit saxeis ictibus perfidorum ut facilius pervenire possit ad lapidem pretiosum.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily exalted, glorious is our Lord Jesus Christ, Your Son, from whom Stephen, the first martyr and Levite, was promised to be crowned in his passion when he was chosen seventh among the apostles for election in ministry. He singularly achieved martyrdom for Christ; therefore, he wanted to become a stone by blows of treacherous stones, so that he might more easily reach the precious stone.

text: Vere sanctus vere in altissimis gloriosus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui certatricem pro nomine suo Columbam inter suprema supplicia emissa de caelis voce ad se vocat: »Veni quippe ait Columba; aperti sunt tibi caeli.«  Ecce vox fit ad virginem similis quae super baptizatum dominum exstiterat singularis. Singularis plane vox illa quia illum dilectum Dei filium nuntiabat; communis vel similis quia ex ipso caeli climate processerat quae pretiosam mortem virginis populis commendabat.  Hinc igitur quia nostris non debentur meritis talia te Deus quaesumus ut vox quam audivimus ab initio in nobis permaneat ut dum apparueris habeamus fiduciam et non confundamur in ea cum manifestata cunctis fuerit gloria tua.
translation_en:
Verily holy, verily exalted, glorious Lord our Jesus Christ, Son of yours, who called the dove, a contender for your name Columba, from the highest suffering released from heaven to himself: "Come indeed, saith Columba; the heavens are opened unto you."
Lo, a voice is made like unto the virgin which stood over the baptized Lord, unique. This voice plainly because it proclaimed the beloved Son of God; common or similar because it proceeded from the climate of heaven, which recommended the precious death of the virgin to the people.
Hence, since such things are not due to our merits, we pray to you, O God, that the voice which we have heard from the beginning may remain in us; so that while you appear we may have faith and not be confounded by it when your glory is manifested to all.

text: Vere sanctus vere in altissimis gloriosus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui est esurientium cibus sitientibus potus. Ab ipso enim et infirmitati nostrae defectus reficitur et defessae animae spiritale robur augetur.  Proinde rogamus te Deus pater ut per illum concedas nostris offensis veniam qui mortuus est propter peccata nostra et suscitatus est ex virtute sua.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily glorious Lord, our Jesus Christ, Your Son who is the food for the hungry and drink for the thirsty. For from Him our infirmity recovers strength and the weary soul receives spiritual vigor. Therefore, we ask you, God the Father, that through Him You grant us forgiveness for our offenses, who died for our sins and was raised by His power.

text: Vere sanctus vere in excelsis admirabilis et praeclarus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui beatissimum martyrem suum Tirsum prius martyrio consecravit quam lavacro prius fide quam regeneratione prius etiam supplicio quam baptismo ostendens illi inter poenas constantiam inter carceres lumina inter adversantes vindictam cum caesores suos ante poena consumeret quam ipsum poenaliter lacerarent; ante caedentes deficerent quam caeso vitam exstinguerent.  Is etenim incomprehensibili sinus tui illustratus arcano trino persecutus iudice vita non caruit in qua tamen ludibriosum eorum finem ante praedixit. Sicque eos horribili mortis exitu citius praemisit ad poenam quam sibi extorquerent vitam. Deinde tuis adiutus omnipotens Pater iudiciis placito tibi tempore sacratum consignavit spiritum quem inter adversa mundi constantia servaverat illaesum pariter et invictum. Unde te in huius martyris sollemni festo rogamus ut precibus ipsius dones tibi confitentibus veniam qui manifestam ostendisti in persecutoribus eius vindictam.
translation_en:
Verily holy, verily exalted, wonderfully and glorious is our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who consecrated his most blessed martyr Tirrus with martyrdom before washing with faith, regeneration, or even suffering before baptism. Showing him constancy among torments, light amidst prisons, vengeance against adversaries, and his helpers preceded death rather than extinguish his life. Before they struck him down, they faltered, for they had failed to end his life when they killed him.
Indeed, illuminated by your incomprehensible embrace of the trinity, he was pursued by a judge; yet in that life, he predestined their ridiculed end. So, with a horrible death, he hastened them to punishment sooner than they could extort his life from him. Then, empowered by you, the Almighty Father, consigned his spirit to sacred judgement, which he had maintained unscathed and invincible amidst the world's adversities.
Hence, on this martyr's solemn feast, we implore you with his prayers that you give forgiveness to those confessing their sins, who have made manifest vengeance upon his persecutors.

text: Vere sanctus vere in excelsis benedictus Dominus Deus noster (Iesus Christus Filius tuus) per quem te supplices deprecamur uti hanc oblationem quam tibi offerimus pro Ecclesiae tuae catholicae fide stabilitate <et> concordia pro emundatione vitiorum et remissione peccatorum pro gloria martyrum et requie defunctorum propitiatus adspicias adspiciendo sanctifices sanctificando benedicas.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily exalted, blessed is the Lord our God (Jesus Christ, Your Son) through whom we humbly beseech You to behold this offering that we present to You on behalf of the stability and unity of Your Catholic Church. May You purify us from sins, forgive our offenses, look favorably upon the glory of martyrs, and grant rest to the departed. May You, propitiated, look upon us, sanctifying and sanctifying us, bless us.

text: Vere sanctus vere in sanctis suis gloriosus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus cuius potentia virtutis pro nomine suo certantibus Iuliano athletae sociisque suis tantum donum attribuit laudis ut omnia quae vellent fiducialiter in eo ac per eum facere possent.  Illi enim praedicti martyres credendo atque sequendo ardentibus dimersi in cupis illaesi post ignes rutilante claritate resplenduere fulgoris. E quibus Iulianus admirabili virtutum specialitate praepollens in nomine eius cuidam se caedenti oculum evulsum reformat; corpus exanime suscitat praesentiaque sua in pulverem redigit idolorum vanissima simulacra. Huius sane martyris dimicationem atque victoriam elementa ipsa testata sunt humana laudaverunt caelestia per emissam desursum vocem potentialiter intonarunt.  Per hos ergo martyres quibus tantam praestitisti magnificentiam laudis indivisa Trinitas Deus sit tibi gloria. Sit nobis obsequentibus peccatorum venia exoptata ut quorum passionibus collaudaris eorum precibus delecteris exaudiendo eos pro nobis qui pro omnibus ipse incarnari voluisti in terris.
translation_en:
Verily holy, verily in the holy ones, glorious is our Lord Jesus Christ, Your Son, whose power of virtues contending for His name, grants such a gift of praise to Julian the athlete and his companions, that all things which they confidently desire to do in Him and through Him are able to do.
Indeed, the aforementioned martyrs, burning with faith and following, were torn apart by lions unharmed, shining in brilliance after fires; and Julian, excelling in marvelous speciality of virtues in his name, healed the eye of one who was being slain. He raised the lifeless body and reduced its presence to dust, the worthless images of idols.
Indeed, the martyrdom and victory of this very martyr were testified by the elements themselves, human beings praised them, heavenly powers powerfully sang in praise of him.
Therefore, through these martyrs, who have shown such great magnificence of praise, the undivided Trinity, God, may glory be to You. May we, who are obedient, the forgiveness of sins be desired for us, that you may delight in their prayers and hear them on our behalf, for whom He Himself willingly became incarnate on earth.

text: Vere sanctus vere inaestimabilis Dominus Deus noster et immense gloriosus qui scientiae lumen totis sic in singulorum corda illabitur totus ut integer exstans totus portionaliter scindi non patiatur.
translation_en: Verily, the holy is verily immeasurable; our Lord God is immense and extremely glorious. He who illuminates all knowledge with such a light that it penetrates every heart whole, yet remains entire, cannot be divided portionally.

text: Vere sanctus vere inaestimabiliter gloriosus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus ob cuius fidem fortissimus athleta tuus Romanus animam posuit et puerulus Theodulus furenti gladio lactentis infantiae collum subiecit.  Propter quod Deus pater soli tibi debetur honor virtutis et aeternae gloria potestatis quem et elinguis Romanus voce concelebrat et infantulus Theodulus adorandum piis documentis insinuat.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily inestimably glorious is our Lord Jesus Christ, Your Son, for whose faith your strongest athlete, the Roman, gave his soul, and the child Theodulus submitted his neck to a raging sword during the play of infancy. Therefore, only to you should God the Father be due honor, virtue, and eternal glory of power, which even the eloquent Roman acclaims in voice, and the child Theodulus suggests to be adored with pious documents.

text: Vere sanctus vere inaestimabiliter gloriosus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus sub quo et fortes decidunt et humiliata eriguntur cum et de se praesumentes colliduntur ad terram et de se diffidentes provehuntur ad aethera; qui est salutaris inchoantibus via et perficientibus remuneratio copiosa. Ipse ergo Deus pater tibi pro nobis intercessor exsistat pro quibus suam posuit animam quo eo adiuvante et haec inchoata ieiunia expleamus et ad dies passionis eius mundatis pectoribus accedere mereamur.
translation_en: Verily, the Holy and immeasurably glorious Lord, our Jesus Christ, Your Son, under whom both the mighty are brought low and the humble exalted; those who presume from themselves fall to the earth, and those who doubt themselves rise to heaven. He is salvation for beginners and a plentiful reward for the faithful. Therefore, let this God, our Father, be for us an intercessor, especially on behalf of those who have dedicated their souls to Him; by His aid, we may complete these begun fasts and with clean hearts approach the days of His passion. We deserve to do so.

text: Vere sanctus vere ineffabilis unigenitus tuus Dominus noster qui cum esset aequalis tecum assumendo nostra paulo minus minoraretur ab angelorum toga ut ab universis populis glorificaretur in terra. Ille inquam ex te vero patre quamquam ineffabilem habens immortalitatem nostrae ex huius Mariae unde moreretur formae assumpsit aequalitatem. Sit tibi ob inde laus genitoque tuo cum spiritu sancto qui nostro ver(a)e destruxisti mortis dominio tuamque post matrem glorificasti in transitu suo.
translation_en: Verily holy, verily ineffable, your only-begotten Son, our Lord, who though equal to you, assumed our human form to be a little less than you, and thereby was veiled by the angelic robe so that he might be glorified by all peoples on earth. I say truly from you, the Father, although ineffable, possessing immortality, he took the likeness of our flesh from this Mary from whom he would take on form. Therefore to you is praise given and to your Son born with the Holy Spirit who destroyed for us the true power of death, and glorified you after his mother's transit.

text: Vere sanctus vere pius vere inaestimabiliter gloriosus Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus qui profluentibus ex ventre suo fluminibus recumbentem in sinu suo dilectum Ioannem sic irrigavit sic docuit sic replevit ut cor ipsius illuc ad enarrandum incorruptibile principium adscendere posset quo alius non valuit penetrare.  Hic vera de Verbo sentiens praedicamenta conscripsit cui idem unigenitus Filius tuus et matrem moriens commendavit. Et rursum eum materno honori consimilem reddidit cum uno eodemque munere et matrem glorificat et discipulum inter fratres exaltat cum matrem gloria pariendi honorat et discipulum recumbendi honore glorificat.  O quam felix venter qui talem genuit prolem! Quam honorabile caput quod talius recubavit in pectore! Gloriosa quidem Maria quae genuit Christum; sed et Ioannes qui recubuit supra Christum. O parile praemium in utrisque virginitatis quod sic commendatur in exitu finis cum et Maria nullo persecutionis mortis suae congustata tormento latenter ex hac vita subducitur et Ioannes diem recessus sui ante praesciens effodiri ipse sibi praecepit loculum sepulcri in quo valedictis fratribus sine ullo mortis dolore ingressus requiescit usque ad adventum domini incorruptus; tam extraneus a tormento mortis quam alienus a corruptione exstitit carnis.  Hinc igitur quia pretiosa est in conspectu tuo Domine mors horum sanctorum tuorum te deprecamur ut haec holocausta nostra suscipiens nostris criminibus veniam praestes quo ad instar apostoli tui et te incorrupto sequamur ex corde et tu ad nos veniens apud nos facias mansionem.
translation_en:
Verily holy, verily kind, verily inestimably glorious is our Lord Jesus Christ, Your Son, who lying on His breast irrigated, taught, and filled John so that his heart could ascend to the unutterable beginning of the incorruptible principle, which no other was able to penetrate. Here truly sensing the properties of the Word, he (John) wrote what was committed to him, and Your only begotten Son commended both himself and his mother in death. Again, he returned a similar honor to his mother when he glorified her and exalted the disciple among brothers with the mother's glory of giving birth, and he glorified the disciple with the honor of lying down, as he glorified the mother with the honor of giving birth.
O how blessed is the womb that gave birth to such a progeny! How honorable is the head that lay on the breast! Indeed, Mary is glorious who gave birth to Christ; but also John, who lay upon Christ. O equal reward in both virginities, which is committed in the exit of its end, with Mary, who is secretly withdrawn from this life without any torment of death's persecution, and John, who himself commanded before his departure to be buried in a tomb prepared for him by brothers without any sorrow of death. Entering there, he rests until the coming of the Lord, remaining as foreign to the torment of death as alien to the corruption of flesh.
Therefore, because death is precious in Your sight, Lord, we humbly pray You to accept this holocaust of ours, granting us forgiveness for our sins, so that following in the steps of Your apostle and You being incorruptible, You may come to us and dwell among us.

text: Vere sanctus verus aeternusque pontifex et solus sine macula sacerdos cuius sanguinem omnium fidelium corda mundantem placationis hostiam non solum pro delictis populi sed etiam pro nostris offensionibus immolamus.
translation_en: Verily, the holy true and eternal priest, and the sole priest without blemish, whose blood purifies the hearts of all faithful as an offering for reconciliation, we not only offer on behalf of the people's sins but also for our own offenses.

text: Vere satis praeclarum et satis est dignum omnique devotionis intentione iucundum tibi Iesu Domine gratiarum actiones persolvere tibi gloriam et honorem perenniter dare qui haec caelestium sacramenta mysteriorum dum in te consummas in nobis commendas et ita per resurrectionis gloriam in te clarificata conservas ut in nobis clarificanda semper intendas.  Da ergo ut sicut his sacrificiis officio ministrationis innectimur ita eorum sanctificationibus pietatis remedio misceamur.
translation_en:
Indeed, these actions of thanksgiving are quite splendid and worthy enough to be pleasing to you, Jesus Lord, in every intention of devotion. It is fitting that we should pay back the glory and honor to you, who bestow upon us these heavenly sacraments of mysteries as they are fulfilled within us and entrusted to us, and thus through the glory of resurrection, we are kept bright in you so that we may always strive to be brightened within ourselves.
Grant, therefore, that just as we are bound by these sacrifices and their ministerial service, we may also be mixed with their sanctifications by the remedy of piety.

text: Vere terribilis sanctus metuendus amandus conditor instructor moderator tutor oper(a)tor qui proprium genitum per quem virtute paterna tunc adolescentis formasti exordia mundi mittere sede poli demum dignatus es orbi qui reparator et pastor adest nostrarum animarum.
translation_en: Verily terrifying, holy, fearful yet lovable, creator, instructor, moderator, guardian, helper, worker who formed the beginning of the world by your own paternal power through your own begotten one when the adolescence was established, you were deemed worthy to send from the throne of heaven to this world, which is repairer and shepherd, who is present for our souls.

text: Accepturi fratres carissimi intra mortalia viscera caeleste sacrificium et intra cubiculum humani pectoris hospitem Deum mundemus conscientias nostras ab omni labe vitiorum ut nihil sit in nobis subdolum vel superbum sed in humilitatis studium et caritatis adsensum per escam et sanguinem dominici corporis fraternitas copuletur ut cum magna fiducia dicere mereamur;
translation_en: Our dear brethren, we receive the heavenly sacrifice within our mortal bodies and cleanse our consciences from all stains of sin so that nothing in us may be crafty or proud. Instead, let us be in the pursuit of humility and agreement in love. Thus, fraternity will be bound by the bread and blood of the Lord's body, enabling us to say with great confidence that we are worthy.

text: Accipe Deus nostrorum confessionem labiorum omniumque ligamenta solve facinorum quo huius virginis tuae Leocadiae prece et vitiis careamus et muneribus ampliemur cum ad te proclamaverimus e terris; ...
translation_en: Receive, O God, the confession of our lips and dissolve all the bonds of sins, so that we may be free from faults in Your Virgin Leocadia's prayer and be enriched with gifts as we call upon You from the earth; ...

text: Ad fontem lucis et originem bonitatis te summe Deus concurrentes precamur ut arentem ieiunio carnem tuae foveas castitatis amore; effectum quoque nobis donans petitionis exaudi nos de caelis cum ad te proclamaverimus e terris; ...
translation_en: At the font of light and origin of goodness, we, most high God, humbly entreat you. Cleanse the channels of your flesh with the love of chastity through fasting. Also, grant us the effect of our petition from heaven, as we have called out to you from earth; ...

text: Ad terribilem thronum altaris cursu concito Pater omnipotens properantes vestigia Agni viventis cum lacrimis osculantes unguentorum ac fletuum libamenta offerimus.  Poscimus itaque piissime Deus ut paenitentiae fletibus omnium peccata laventur et indulgentiali unguento ossa ecclesiastici corporis solidentur quo possimus omnes cum renatis infantibus respirare et cum mortuis suscitatis Ierusalem caelestem medullata portantes sacrificia introire proclamantes e terris;
translation_en: To the awesome throne of the altar, we hasten our course, O Almighty Father, running in the footsteps of the Living Lamb with tears, we offer kisses of the unguents and the balm of tears. Therefore, we most humbly ask you, God, that through the tears of penitence all sins may be washed away and that the bones of the Church's body may be softened by the indulgent ointment, so that we may breathe with the renewed infants and proclaim, while carrying the meat of heavenly Jerusalem, to enter the sacrifices from earth.

text: Aeterne Dei Filius Domine Iesu quem Stephanus dum lapidaretur ut eius susciperes invocat; quem positis genibus pro inimicis exorat tu nos facito et amicos in te fidenter diligere et pro inimicis te sinceriter postulare quo dum debentibus nobis ex corde dimittimus ea quae praecepisti fiducialiter proclamemus;
translation_en: Eternal Son of God, Lord Jesus, whom Stephen called out to as he was being stoned and invoked you; whom he humbly asked for on behalf of his enemies.
