Make us do the same: to confidently love our friends as we sincerely ask for things on behalf of our enemies. That when we forgive them from our hearts as we ought, we may boldly proclaim what you have commanded.

text: Agnosce Domine verba quae praecepisti; ignosce praesumptioni quam imperasti; ignorantia est enim non nosse meritum contumacia non servare praeceptum quo iubemur
translation_en: Lord, acknowledge the words you have commanded; forgive the presumption that you have ordered; ignorance indeed is not knowing the merit, contumacy is not keeping the commandment which we are ordered to observe.

text: Apostolo tuo Iacobo Domine edocente praemonimur ut si quis nostrum indiget sapientia postulet a te qui das omnibus affluenter et non improperas. Sed quia ad te pervenire cupimus per Christum qui est virtus tua et sapientia id agere praeoptamus poscentes clementiam tuam ut per eum qui apud te advocatus factus est noster et pervenire nos ad te facias et orationem quam ipso domino instruente didicimus ad te introire permittas proclamantes e terris;
translation_en: We are warned by your Apostle James, Lord, that if any of us needs wisdom, he should ask you, who gives generously to all and does not reproach. However, since we desire to reach you through Christ, your power and wisdom, we prefer to ask for your clemency that, through him who was made our advocate before you, he may lead us to you, and that you permit the prayer which we have learned from him teaching the Lord to enter into you. We proclaim from the earth;

text: Attende Domine nostram propitius precem et iter famulorum tuorum illorum in prosperitate et salute dignare dirigere quo et illis et nobis prospera impetremus cum ad te nunc proclamaverimus e terris;
translation_en: Hear, O Lord, our supplication graciously, and guide the way of your servants among prosperity and health. May you direct them where we are asking for prosperity from you as we call upon you now from the lands.

text: Attendite dilectissimi fratres quid sanctorum oratio valeat quidve pro impiis oppositae iustorum intercessiones obtineant cum orante Urbano et virginis Caeciliae vota implentur et Valeriani atque Tiburtii fides aucta martyrii gloria decoratur.  Proinde extensis ad caelum palmis petamus nobis auxilium de supernis invocantes eum ex pietate patrem quem terribilem venturum expavescimus iudicem.  Profecto etenim erit per illum nobis vita aeterna per quem virgo Caecilia non fuit in ardoribus concremata. Qui enim illos in martyrii certamine positos exaudivit exaudiet nos cum ad eum fuderimus clamorem gemitus nostri proclamantes atque ita dicentes;
translation_en: Pay attention, dear brothers, what the prayers of the saints are worth, and what the intercessions of the righteous opposed to the impious may obtain, as the vows of Urban and the virgin Cecilia are fulfilled, and the faith of Valerian and Tiburtius is strengthened by martyrdom's glory. Therefore, with outstretched palms towards heaven, we ask for help from above, invoking Him as a Father whom we trembled at the thought of coming as a terrible judge. Indeed, it will be through Him that we will have eternal life, through Whom the virgin Cecilia was not consumed by the flames. For He who heard them in the contest of martyrdom will hear us when we pour out to Him our cry, groans, and so saying:

text: Audi Domine vocem nostri clamoris et effectum dona petitionibus nostris abstinentiae labore. Adiutor esto promptissimus et in periculis liberator assiduus. Pelle a nobis dolum interime vitium praesta alternae dulcedinis incrementum ut cum ea quae praecipis impleverimus in nullo confundamur cum ad te proclamaverimus e terris;
translation_en: Hear us, O Lord, the voice of our supplication and grant the result of our petitions through abstinence and labor. Be swift to help and a constant deliverer in perils. May deceit depart from us, let vice be ended, grant an increase of sweetness as an alternative, that we may not be confounded with those who have proclaimed themselves unto you from the earth.

text: Auxilium misericordiae tuae nobis petentibus Domine Deus omnipotens semper impertire ac solita pietate sacrificia quae offerimus propitiatus accepta.  Scimus enim pie Domine quod non vis mortem peccatoris sed ut revertamur et vivamus prophetica admones voce.  Et inde omnipotens Deus qui operis confessionem superne holocaustum amplectaris quaesumus ut cordis nostri gemitum libens accipias et oris nostri confessionem tibi placitam efficias ut digne tibi proclamemus;
translation_en: We humbly ask you, Lord God Almighty, to continually bestow upon us the help of your mercy. May the sacrifices we offer be accepted with your customary compassion. We know, Lord, that you do not wish the death of a sinner but rather that we return and live, as prophetically advised through your voice. And so, Almighty God, who embraces the confession of our work as a heavenly holocaust, we humbly ask that you graciously accept the groanings of our heart and make our confession pleasing to you, so that we may proclaim worthy praises to you.

text: Christe amator castitatis et collator aeternae possessionis qui beatissimum martyrem Iulianum ad te pro corpore exanimato clamantem exaudire dignatus es precibus eius per caelestem vocem sine mora respondens quod eundem dilectum tuum in nullo contristari volueris in quo sic ipse cum patre et spiritu sancto laetabaris tu nobis concede ut ita in veritate vivamus ne sanctum spiritum contristemur in quo signati sumus quo ab eo per momenta compuncti et recreati per eum tibi relatura exhibeamus orandi verba quae ipse nos docuisti ut dicamus;
translation_en: Christ, lover of chastity and giver of eternal possessions, who deigned to hear the prayers of the most blessed martyr Julian on behalf of his lifeless body, respond promptly in heavenly voice, that you do not wish your beloved one to be saddened in any way, whereby yourself with the Father and the Holy Spirit rejoice. Grant us that we may live truly, so that we are not grieved by the Holy Spirit in whom we have been signed. May we, moved and refreshed by him, bring reports to you about him, through whom you teach us what words to say.

text: Christe Dei Filius cuius testimonio instructi manemus eo quod unaquaeque anima ad suum tutamentum custodem habeat angelum deputatum quaesumus ut assidue nobiscum manente angelo pacis procul efficiatur refuga ille quondam angelus auctor iniquitatis ut corde et corpore purificati ad corporis et sanguinis tui sacramenta mereamur accedere beatificandi. Et sic aurem cordis tuis inclinemus praeceptis ut semper ad te fiducialiter clamemus e terris;
translation_en: Christ, Son of God, by whose testimony we are instructed, we remain in the one who assigns an angel to each soul as its guardian. We humbly ask that the angel of peace may always be with us and drive away that former angel, the author of wickedness, so that purified both in heart and body, we may deserve to approach your sacraments and beatification. And thus, let our ears turn towards your precepts, so that we may always trustingly call out to you from the earth.

text: Christe Dei Filius qui victoriam martyris in ultionem persecuturum eius propagatam ostendis dum eo superstite et paratos ignes exstinguis et cruentos carnifices perimis conceptum in nobis fomitem exstingue libidinis et flammas tuae incende perpetuae caritatis quibus respersi per momenta in intimis ad te et verbis et cordibus proclamemus e terris;
translation_en: Christ, Son of God, who shows the victory of the martyr which is avenged upon his persecutors, you extinguish the fires prepared and destroy the bloodthirsty executioners in him that remains with us. Quench the germ of lust in us, and fan the flames of your perpetual charity within us, by which we are sprinkled in moments, and proclaim both in words and hearts to you from the earth.

text: Christe Deus in quo non est inventum peccatum et <qui>tamen pro peccatoribus oblatus es Deo patri in sacrificium respice gemitum nostrum suscipe humilitatis nostrae ieiunium ut qui nos a te ob proximitatem festivitatis tuae mortis sanctificari volumus sanctificationem tuae gratiae impetrasse nos gratulemur;
translation_en: Christ, God, in whom no sin has been found, yet offered up for sinners to God the Father as a sacrifice, look upon our groaning, receive our humility, accept our fasting. May we who desire to be sanctified by you for proximity to your festivity of death, rejoice that we have obtained your sanctification through your grace.

text: Christe Deus qui ieiunii non renuis votum qui nobis per te magnum abstinendi praebuisti exemplum quique docuisti te per orationem petere per lectionem quaerere eleemosynis etiam vel lacrimis propulsare accipe nostram petitionem quae in nobis et amorem lectionis enutriat et lacrimas nostras tibi commendabiles reddat ut cum te petierimus orando te nos invenisse gratulemur quaerendo cumque lacrimando pulsaverimus a te exaudiri promereamur;
translation_en: Christ, God, who does not refuse the vow of those who fast, you have given us through you a great example of abstaining. You also taught us to seek you through prayer, to find alms through reading, and even to drive away through tears. Receive our petition which nourishes love for reading in us and makes our tears commendable to you. So that when we ask you through prayer, we may rejoice that we have found you; and when we seek and weep, we may promise to be heard by you.

text: Christe Deus qui per apostolum tuum oris confessionem ad salutem prodesse dixisti confessoris tui illius precibus consule nostrae saluti ut cum ea quae corde credimus ore professi fuerimus a te exaudiri ocius mereamur e terris;
translation_en: Christ, God, who through your apostle said that confession of your mouth brought salvation to your confessor, we pray that with what we believe in our heart and confess with our mouth, we may be swiftly heard by you for the salvation of our souls.

text: Christe Deus qui virginali prodiens ex utero novum hodie lumen apparuisti in mundo agnitus in stella adoratus per munera ciba nos favo mellis et sermonibus bonis orationibus iustis ac responsionibus pietatis ut dulcedo auditus tui sanitas sit animae vel corporis nostri ut gustantes et videntes quam suavis es Domine nequaquam percogamur ad amaritudinem saeculi declinare sed caelestibus suspensi oraculis cordibus et vocibus per te patrem impetremus e terris;
translation_en: Christ, God, who today appeared in the world as a new light coming forth from the virginal womb, recognized in a star and adored by gifts, nourish us with honeyed words, good sermons, just prayers, and answers of piety. May the sweetness of your voice bring health to our soul or body. Since we taste and see how sweet you are, Lord, may we never be led to the bitterness of this world, but rather be raised with celestial prayers and voices through you, we may implore the Father from the earth.

text: Christe Iesu bone qui ad patrem de cruce clamasti tu nos in hac die qua ipse de tumulo surrexisti ad te clamantes exaudi quo resurrectionis tuae hilaritate gaudentium ora repleantur iubilo laudis et corda effectum percipiant exorationis cum nunc exoraverint ea quae praecepisti;
translation_en: Christ Jesus, good one who cried out to the Father from the cross on this day when you rose again from the tomb, hear us as we cry out to you. May our lips be filled with joyful praise for your resurrection and our hearts understand the petition as they now pray according to what you have commanded.

text: Christe qui beatissimis apostolis tuis orandi praecepta instituis praesta ut suffragio apostoli tui Thomae digni effecti ipsa tua deifica verba proclamantes mereamur exaudiri e terris;
translation_en: Christ, who gave the prayer instructions to your most blessed apostles, grant that we may be worthy through the intercession of your apostle Thomas, and by proclaiming your divine words, deserve to be heard from the earth.

text: Christe qui es omnium creaturarum conditor et redemptor repara quaeque sunt in nobis lassa virtutis tuae potentia ut qui te duce retroactae abstinentiae dies peregimus futura quae supersunt ieiuniorum obsequia te adiuvante celebrius impleamus quo te et in bonorum principiis laus a nobis debita subsequatur et in mediis vel ultimis obsequelis honorificentiae tibi gratiae deferantur.  Accipe igitur quaesumus huius ieiunii tempore mediante prolatam a nobis hanc praeceptionis tuae hostiam tribuens nobis per illam et praesentibus non deici in aerumnis et futuris relevari de gaudiis cum ad te proclamaverimus e terris;
translation_en: Christ, who art the creator and redeemer of all creatures, restore in us what is weary of your power, so that we, having passed the days of abstinence in your leadership, may perform the future days of fasting more devoutly with your assistance. May the praise due to you for good deeds follow from us, and honors of gratitude be offered to you in the midst or end of our obligations. Therefore, we humbly ask that during this time of fasting, you accept from us this offering, presented according to your command, granting us relief both now and in the future, and releasing us from sorrows as we call out to you from the earth.

text: Christe qui humani conservator es corporis et collator dignitatis conserva nos beneficiis profluis et miserationibus consuetis quo sicut praedicti martyris corpus sub erecta fastigii tecta digne sepeliri promeruit ita nos te miserante obtecti mercamur per omnia exaudiri cum ea quae praecipis proclamaverimus;
translation_en: Christ, who are the conservator of the human body and bestower of dignity, preserve us with your flowing blessings and customary mercies, so that just as the body of the predicted martyr was worthy to be buried under the raised roofs of a church, we who are covered by your mercy may be heard in all things, along with her whom we have proclaimed with what you command;

text: Christe salus omnium concede cordi nostro pietatis affectum quo te veridicente et carnis nostrae tympanum per abstinentiam pungat et mens per multiplicem dilectionem exorare non desinat oratione qua nos docuisti orare et dicere;
translation_en: Christ, salvation of all, grant to our heart a feeling of pity whereby, as you have promised, and our flesh's drum is stung by abstinence, and mind continues to pray and exhort with multiple acts of love according to the prayer and teaching that you have taught us.

text: Christe vita nostra vitis vera saturitas sempiterna refice inediam nostram. Da nobis dulcedinem tuam qua satiati et compuncti futuros ieiuniorum labores expediamus interriti et in hoc parsimoniae nostrae initio mereamur a te audiri;
translation_en: Christ, our life, the true vine's everlasting satiety, revive within us the quenching of our hunger. Grant us your sweetness, by which we may accomplish the labors of the fasting and prepare the timid, and in this begin the merit to be heard by you.

text: Ciba nos Domine pane salutis et poculo benedictionis ut eo amplius te sitiamus quo affatim de tuis visceribus biberimus;
translation_en: Feed us, Lord, with the bread of salvation and with the cup of blessing, that we may thirst for you more abundantly as we drink from your depths.

text: Clemens immense et admirabilis Deus cui omnia elementa famulantur et omnes elationes maris deserviunt libera nos de aquis multis et de manu filiorum alienorum ut qui per te renati sumus ex aqua et spiritu sancto non patiamur ab ethnicis et irregeneratis divelli a sancto proposito sed arcum eorum inconvertibilem contere sagittas destrue pharetras retrude gladios perime lanceas divelle consilia quae in nobis agunt maligna confunde et in ipsis si credere noluerint ea ipse retorquendo converte atque semper fidei scuto nos protege.  Qualiter qui hic propter nomen Filii tui novum quem in margaritam fulgidam id est in calculum candidum scripsisti diversa a gentibus sustinemus opprobria portamus infanda ludibria illic pro fide qua credimus et pro ea quidquid ad mendicitatem et mortem distrahimur concedatur remissio peccatorum et potiatur infinitus locus iustorum cum ea quae filio tuo docente didicimus proclamaverimus e terris;
translation_en:
Clement and admirable God, to whom all elements serve and all the exaltations of the sea submit; free us from many waters and from the hand of foreign sons, that we who are reborn by you through water and the Holy Spirit may not be torn away from the holy purpose by the heathens and the unregenerate. May their impenetrable bow break, arrows be destroyed, torches be extinguished, swords be shattered, lances be broken, plots that are working against us maliciously be confused, and if they do not want to believe in these things, may you yourself turn them back and convert them. And always protect us with the shield of faith.
For how we here, because of the name of your Son new, whom you have written on the radiant pearl, that is, on the white marble, sustain insults different from the nations; bear infamous portals; suffer ridicule for faith which we believe and for whatever is dragged toward beggary and death by it, may the forgiveness of sins be granted and let an infinite place of the just be attained with those things that we have learned from your Son teaching us proclaimed from the earth.

text: Cogitationes et delicta nostra cernentes non cruentas tibi Domine victimas immolamus et simplicibus votis tibi sempiterni sacerdotis corpus offerimus.  Memorare itaque Domine quid pro nobis pertulerit qui peccata nostra portavit. Indue ergo nos iustitiae stola ut incena tua sine veste nuptiali nullus adcumbat gaudiisque caelestibus novi testamenti convivium floreat.  Procul absit dolus quo deceptus est malus ille discipulus. Sit omnibus fides vera spes certa et caritas pura ut spiritalibus sacramentis non damnetur conscientia sed per pacis caritatisque tuae dulcedinem ab omnibus emundati vitiis ad te proclamemus e terris;
translation_en:
Recognizing our thoughts and sins, we do not offer to you, Lord, bloody sacrifices, but with simple vows we present our bodies as a perpetual priest. Therefore remember, Lord, what was borne for us by him who carried our sins. Clothe us, then, with the robe of justice, so that no one approaches your banquet without the wedding garment. Let the feast of the new covenant flourish.
Let deceit far removed from us, as it deceived the wicked disciple. May true faith, certain hope, and pure charity be with all, so that through spiritual sacraments our conscience may not be condemned but purified by your sweetness and kindness, turning away from all vices to proclaim you on earth.

text: Completis Domine sacrificiorum tuorum pro tua laude et nostra salute mysteriis plenam nos habere tuam gratiam praesta ut quia nostrum non agnoscimus meritum sed tuum praeceptum audeamus tibi proclamare dicentes;
translation_en: Complete, Lord, Your sacrifices for Your glory and our salvation. Grant us to be filled with Your grace that we, who do not recognize our worthiness, might dare to proclaim Your commandment to You, saying:

text: Concede Domine famulis tuis ut orantes cum fiducia dicamus sicut ipse iubere dignatus es dicere;
translation_en: Grant, O Lord, to your servants that, with confidence, we may say as you have been pleased to command.

text: Congregati universi fratres carissimi qui in peccatorum mole depressi et mundanis onerati cogitationibus suspiramus consideremus qualiter noster mediator ignominiosam deportans ad mortem sustulit manibus crucem nihil persequentibus aut interrogantibus inimicis respondens sed humilitate piissima dum pro nostris laboraret iniquitatibus tacens.  Ob hoc ergo quia mitis et humilis corde est discamus in hoc quid oporteat fieri. Mortificemus cum vitiis membra nostra crucifigamus desideria carnalia resurgamus in anima sicut ille iustus surrexit in gloria quia tunc paschalis unanimiter poterit honorari sollemnitas cum haec sacrificia eidem Deo summo vitae nostrae commendaverit probitas qui nos in terris positus sic docuit orare et dicere;
translation_en: Let us consider how our mediator, despite being treated shamefully and lifted the cross with no pursuers or questioners among his enemies, responded humbly. Since he is gentle and humble at heart, let us learn what we must do in this regard. Let us mortify our members along with our vices, let us crucify our carnal desires, let us rise again in spirit as the just man rose in glory, for then the solemnity of Easter can be appropriately honored with these sacrifices, to which he commended his life on earth. He taught us how to pray and speak while placed on earth.

text: Confortamini manus fatigatae; roboramini pusillanimes; hilarescite et nolite timere; extollite ad Deum manus vestras et excitate corda quia ecce iam in proximo est redemptio nostra.  Cuius incarnatio nos redemit cuius processio nativitatis illuminavit cuiusque etiam praeceptum nos docuit orare semper et dicere;
translation_en:
Take heart, you weary-handed ones; strengthen, you faint-hearted ones; be cheerful and do not fear; lift up your hands to God and awaken your hearts, for behold, our redemption is already near.
Whose incarnation redeemed us, whose procession illuminated the nativity, whose precepts taught us to pray always and say:

text: Conscientiarum nostrarum errore suspecti vel peccatorum recordatione confusi omnipotens Deus indignos nos ad invocationem tui nominis iudicamus ut orationem quam praecepisti dicere audeamus sed quia permittis et dicimus;
translation_en: Due to the suspicion of our conscience straying from the right path or being confused by memories of our sins, Almighty God, we who are undeserving, judge ourselves worthy to invoke your name. Yet, since you allow it and we say so:

text: Conserva nos Domine in timore nominis tui qui societatem trium martyrum tuorum Fausti Ianuarii et Martialis inimici persuasionibus non passus es dividi. Quique illorum animas post eculeum inter flammas suscepisti nostras voces post libitus carnis inter commotiones saeculi fluctuantis exaudi cum ea ad te nunc proclamaverimus quae nobis ipse instituisti;
translation_en: Preserve us, Lord, in the fear of your name, who did not allow the fellowship of your three martyrs Faustus, Januarius, and Marcellus to be divided by the persuasions of their enemies. And may you receive their souls after death among the flames, hear our voices after the cravings of the flesh amidst the turbulence of the fluctuating world. Answer us now as we proclaim to you what you yourself have instituted for us.

text: Cum ex lege tua Domine noverimus in memoria aeterna esse iustum non pro illius sed pro nostri commendatione hoc tibi offerimus holocaustum petentes ut qui eius animam fecisti in passione victricem nostrum votum efficias in confessione victorem quo eodem suffragante clamorem nostrae accipias vocis cum ad te proclamaverimus e terris;
translation_en: Since we have known from your law, Lord, that the just one exists forever in eternal memory not for his own sake but for our commendation, we offer you this holocaust, praying that you who made him victorious in his passion will fulfill our vow in confession, making us victors. May the same one, interceding for us, receive our cry when we proclaim to you from the earth.

text: Da pacem Domine tribue caritatem impertire gratiam ut cum fiducia dicamus ea quae docuisti;
translation_en: Grant peace, Lord, bestow charity that we may extend grace, so that with confidence we may say what you have taught us.

text: Descendat Domine ad nos Spiritus Sanctus per quem et mundata pectora nostra cum eo ipse possideas et institutam a te orationem suscipias ut ita non per nos sed per illum nostra accipias postulata sicut per illum non per nos nostra deles facinora quo eo qui tecum et cum patre regnat aequalis interpellante pro nobis per eum ad te proclamemus e terris;
translation_en: Let the Holy Spirit come down upon us, O Lord, through whom our hearts may be purified so that You possess and receive the prayer instituted by You. In this way, let our petitions not be received through us but through Him, just as our sins are not forgiven through us but through Him. Through Him who, with You and the Father, reigns equally, we intercede for us before You.

text: Desiderantes Christe Deus mundi pervenire ad cenam tuam postulamus ut nostra iubeas abolere peccata tribuasque nobis munditiam carnis atque spiritus pellens a corde dolum a carne libitum a lingua mendacium ab actu scandalum; renovando nos gloria passionis vulnere crucis atque gloria resurrectionis quo largam impendens misericordiam miseris ieiuniumque acceptans nostrae humilitatis exaudies vocem nostri clamoris quo dicimus;
translation_en: Desiring to come to Your supper, Christ, God of the world, we ask that You command our sins to be abolished and grant us cleanliness both of flesh and spirit. Driving away deceit from the heart, desire from the flesh, falsehood from the tongue, scandal from the act; renewing us by the wound of Your passion's glory and the glory of Your resurrection, where You lavish mercy upon the wretched and accept fasting, may You hear the voice of our supplication because we say:

text: Deum cuius magnitudo divinitatis capi non potest quique sine initio Deus summus et pater est deprecemur dilectissimi fratres ut idem pater qui nasci filium suum voluit ex utero virginis matris mundet nos ab omni inquinamento carnis et sanguinis quo sicut divina obumbratione concepit virgo ut pareret ita nos divina inspiratione accensi conceptum Sancti Spiritus quem domino nostro Iesu Christo docente accepimus proferamus publice et dicamus;
translation_en: We pray to the God whose greatness of divinity cannot be comprehended, who is supreme and father from the beginning. Beloved brothers, we implore that the same Father who willed to be born His Son from the womb of the Virgin Mother, cleanse us from every defilement of flesh and blood. Just as the Virgin conceived by divine shadow was able to give birth, so may we, inflamed by divine inspiration, conceive the concept of the Holy Spirit, which our Lord Jesus Christ teaches us to receive, bring forth publicly and say:

text: Deum qui est resurrectio mortuorum et vita animarum fidelium fratres carissimi deprecemur ut mundet nos propitius a peccatis nostris et a passionibus liberet quatenus bonorum filiorum in numero copulati idoneo ad eum corde clamemus e terris;
translation_en: We entreat the God who is the resurrection of the dead and the life of the faithful brothers, dearly beloved, that He would purify us kindly from our sins and free us from passions, so that as good sons joined in number, we may cry out to Him with a pure heart from the earth.

text: Deum vitae nostrae auctorem fratres carissimi et creatorem rerum omnium dominum agnoscentes pietatem eius supplici confessione poscamus ut et peccatis nostris clementer ignoscat et ex toto cordis affectu ad se semper clamare nos faciat ita dicentes;
translation_en: Recognizing our life's Creator, the most beloved brothers, and the Lord of all creation, we humbly confess our piety and ask for His mercy. May He graciously forgive our sins and make us always long to call upon Him with a whole heart's devotion. Thus, let us say:

text: Deus a quo docente nos spiritu paterno tuo sancto te nomine invocare praesumimus crea in nobis fidelium corda filiorum ut promissam hereditatem mereamur ingredi per debitam servitutem clamantes e terris;
translation_en: We presume to call upon you, God, from whom we are taught by your holy Father's spirit, create in us the hearts of faithful children so that we may deserve to enter into the promised inheritance through fitting service, crying out from the earth.

text: Deus a quo unicus tuus in hunc mundum missus ac pro nobis in cruce suspensus nostrae redemptionis pretium dedit sanguinem suum ut reconciliati per eius mortem filiorum apud te promereremur adoptionem eiusdem nostri mediatoris obtentu nobis nec merentibus tribue ut possimus te patrem fiducialiter appellare et orationem quam ipso docente didicimus ad te non solum vocibus sed et meritis proclamare et dicere;
translation_en: God from whom your only one was sent into this world and suspended on the cross for us, gave his blood as a price of our redemption, that we might be worthy through his death to obtain adoption as his children through the same mediator. Grant it to us, not because we deserve it, but grant it so that we may call you faithfully our Father, and proclaim the prayer which he taught us, not only with words, but also with deeds, and say:

text: Deus aeterne qui beatissimos martyres tuos Fructuosum Agorium et Eulogium igne examinasti eorumque animas perustis membris ad aeternam requiem perduxisti dum in illis tribus Trinitas vera inhabitas quos unitos in passione unitas sancta coronas respice nos de excelso throno gloriae tuae dans nostris criminibus finem et terrae nostrae finibus pacem.  Ardeamus spiritu sanctificemur ex actu; operemur iustitiam teneamus et castimoniae disciplinam ut eo fervore cordis quo te praedicti martyres in medio ignis positi laudaverunt nos quoque institutionis divinae oraculum compuncti coram te depromere mereamur ita dicentes;
translation_en: Eternal God, who examined your most blessed martyrs Fructuosus and Eulogius with fire, and led their souls to eternal rest while in them the true Trinity dwelled, look upon us from your high throne of glory, putting an end to our sins and granting peace to our land. May we be burned with the Holy Spirit, purified by action; may we work justice, hold fast to righteousness and discipline, that with the fervor of heart with which the aforesaid martyrs praised you in the midst of fire, we may also deserve to present the divine institution's oracle before you. So let us say:

text: Deus auctor caelestium et terrestrium et sanctorum remunerator piissimus omnium qui ante mundi constitutionem apostolos eligis quos acquisitos cruore vel a populo instituis ut ipsi ostenderent populo caerimonias et colendi te ritus demonstrarent hominibus in quibus abs te datus requiescit Spiritus Sanctus et per ipsos fundares ecclesiam; in quorum vocatione tuam demonstras gratiam gratuitam; et ipsi regni caelorum acciperent claves quos tecum cum ad iudicandum sederis supra sedem maiestatis tuae duodecim tribus Israel constituis iudices nobis quaesumus sancti Matthaei apostoli et evangelistae vel martyris memoriam celebrantibus adesto placatus et occurre propitius.  Obtentu eius nostrum iustifica coetum et merito suscipe votum ut quos propria non fulciunt merita hos prex ad superna sustollat sancti tui apostoli gloriosa ut qui non meremur exaudiri impediente mole delicti eius exaudiamur merito cum ad te proclamaverimus e terris;
translation_en:
God, author of the heavens and earth and the rewarder of saints, most compassionate of all, who before the constitution of the world chose apostles whom you acquired either through blood or from the people to show the people the ceremonies and the way to worship you. In which the Holy Spirit, given by you, rests. And through them, you founded the church; in whose vocation, you demonstrate your gratuitous grace; and they received keys of the kingdom of heaven, whom you will sit with on the throne of your majesty as the twelve tribes of Israel were constituted judges for us. We humbly ask that the memory of the holy apostle and evangelist or martyr Matthias be celebrated, that you are present graciously and approach propitiously.
May his prayer lift our righteous congregation to the supreme powers and may you accept our vow deservedly, that those whom their own merits do not support may be raised by the glorious prayers of your apostle so that we who are not worthy to be heard can be heard justly when we proclaim ourselves from the earth.

text: Deus collator iustitiae et castimoniae prorogator a quo praedicta famula tua visitatam se fore praespiciens et in vulneratis membris recepit sanitatem et noctis medio revincta carcere caelesti promeretur illustrari ex lumine tu luce illa Sancti Spiritus nostram irradians mentem ad videndum te et corpore valentes et animo puriores nos effice quo dum spiritalis affectus in interno se diffuserit corde fidelia ad te ora collaudando proclament;
translation_en: God, the giver of justice and chastity, looking ahead and foreseeing that your servant would be visited, received healing in her wounded members during the middle of the night and was promised to be illuminated by the light from you, shining on our mind through the light of the Holy Spirit. May this light irradiate our mind to see you, and may it make us stronger both physically and spiritually pure, so that when spiritual affection spreads within our heart, we faithfully pray with a loud voice in praise of you.

text: Deus cuius magnitudinis fuit ut contra naturam beatissimus martyr tuus liberam de sub aquis emitteret vocem cum constipato capite cervice tenus vase pelvis arctatus consisteret libera nos de aquis multis et de manu filiorum alienorum quo lingua nostra ab undis odiorum sit extera et in sola sibi tui nominis confessione sufficiat ita proclamans e terris;
translation_en: God whose greatness was such that your blessed martyr emitted a voice freely from under the waters with his constricted head and neck held tightly to a closed vessel, may free us from many waters and from the hand of foreign sons so that our tongue be distant from the hateful waves and only in the sole confession of Your name suffice on earth.

text: Deus Dei Filius qui cum ad patrem adscenderes venturum te iterum ad nos voce propria promisisti veni ad nos et apud nos facito mansionem manifestans teipsum nobis quibus praecepisti ad te proclamare e terris;
translation_en: God, Son of God, who promised to come again to us when you ascended to the Father with your own voice, come to us and make a dwelling among us, manifesting yourself to us whom you commanded to proclaim you from the earth.

text: Deus in cuius manu est correctionis iudicium et salvationis ac misericordiae votum quique flagellas peccatores ut redeant et occasionem admonendi tribuis ne recedant praesta nobis quaesumus supplicibus tuis ut eo momento famulo tuo illi integritas salutis a te dirigatur e caelis qua fide et quo momento nos clamaverimus e terris;
translation_en: God, whose hand holds the judgment of correction and the vote for salvation and mercy, who scourges sinners so they may return and gives opportunity for admonishing lest they depart, grant us we beg, your suppliant ones, that at this moment the integrity of salvation for your servant may be directed towards him from heaven, with the faith and the very moment we have cried out from earth.

text: Deus Pater omnipotens qui in expiatione parturientium duos tibi offerri pullos praecipis columbarum tu precibus Columbae martyris tuae ab omni nos lava sorde pollutionum ut huius virginis suffragio a te culparum possimus veniam promereri cum nunc orationem coram te deprompserimus Filii tui proclamantes atque ita dicentes;
translation_en: O Almighty Father God, who commands the two doves to be offered to you in expiation during childbirth, through the prayers of your martyr dove, wash us from every stain and pollution that we may deserve forgiveness for our sins, now as we present this prayer before you, proclaiming your Son, and saying;

text: Deus quem scimus vitam esse viventium et requiem defunctorum preces nostras placatus suscipe et cuncta nobis peccata dimitte defunctis fidelibus requiem tribue et nos ad te collaudandum idoneos effice;
translation_en: God whom we know to be the life of the living and the rest for the dead, accept our prayers and graciously forgive all the sins of the faithful departed. Grant them eternal rest and make us worthy to praise you.

text: Deus qui ad salutem humani generis Filium tuum destinasti ad terras cuius exemplum praedicti martyres et virtute miraculorum et passione ipsa secuti sunt respice nos horum propitiatus suffragio et confessionis propriae voto per hos infirmo nostro subveniens corpori quos spiritales medicos elegisti quo nostra his intervenientibus a te accipiatur oratio quibus curationum attributa est optio ut per hos medicamine divino compuncti a te cum oraverimus mereamur ocius exaudiri;
translation_en: God, who destined Your Son for the salvation of the human race to come down to earth, whose example these predicted martyrs and through virtue, miracles, and their own passion followed; look upon us with their propitiatory intercession and our own confession's vow. Help our infirm body in response. You have chosen spiritual physicians for us, so that with them intervening on our behalf, may our prayer be received by you, to whom the power of healing is attributed. May it be our choice, through them moved by divine medicine, that when we pray to you, we may deserve to be swiftly heard.

text: Deus qui animam viri sancti ac confessoris tui Martini soluta carnali compage caelesti collocasti in requie ut tuorum consors exsisteret angelorum qui vita calcaverat mundum essetque paradisi possessor qui eremi exstiterat habitator haberetque caelestis gloriam vitae qui increpato diabolo triumphaverat in morte tu nos praedicti viri obitus memoriam celebrantes actu placabiles cogitatione facito esse felices quo nec opere nec cogitatione sordentes et corde et lingua proclamemus ad te ita dicentes;
translation_en: God, who placed the soul of your holy martyr and confessor Martin freed from carnal form in rest among your own, so that he existed as a consort of angels who had trodden upon the world, was a possessor of paradise who dwelled in the wilderness, and possessed heavenly glory who triumphed over death when rebuked by the devil; we, who remember his death, celebrate him in deed and thought. Make us happy so that neither in action nor thought do we become unclean, and with heart and tongue proclaim to you thus:

text: Deus qui beatam Eulaliam antequam passionis gradum scanderet quid crederet quid oraret misericorditer docuisti dum in ea non facis perire quidquid a te edocta fortiter credidisset da nobis ut quod de te scimus et credimus ad aeternam profecisse nobis laetitiam gratulemur ut quod illa effusione promeruit sanguinis nos in his Filii tui Domini nostri mereamur adipisci verbis;
translation_en: God, who before the steps of passion taught blessed Eulalia what to believe and pray mercifully, when in her you did not let perish whatever she firmly believed that you had taught; grant us that we may rejoice forever for the joy that we know and believe comes from you because of her. Let us be worthy, through the outpouring of her blood, to receive through your Son our Lord the rewards of what she has merited.

text: Deus qui concedis orandi mysterium tribue orationis effectum. Orationum suscipe votum et tribue propitius remedium postulatum ut non nobis abneges quod precamur dum inspicis quod oramus cum ad te ore proprio proclamaverimus e terris;
translation_en: God, who grants the mystery of prayer, grant the effectiveness of our prayers. Receive our vow of prayers and graciously give the remedy we have asked for, that you may not deny us what we ask for as we look to what we pray for when we have proclaimed it with our own mouth from the earth.

text: Deus qui delictis nostris provocatus irasceris miserere nostri inflexus miserationibus tuis. Non obsorbeat poena quibus pro delictis nostris subtracta est pluvia nec arbori terrae imbrium copiam deneges quam nostris cernimus criminibus obduratam sed pone iam Domine finem malis et da pluviam in terris;
translation_en: God, who is provoked to anger by our sins, have mercy on us, bent with your compassion. May the punishment not overwhelm those from whom the rain for our sins has been withdrawn, nor deny to the earth's tree the rain we see stubborn in our crimes, but rather, Lord, put an end to evil and send rain upon the lands.

text: Deus qui es collator et conditor vitae humanae accipe vocem confessionis nostrae et ieiunia nostra sanctifica dorio gratiae tuae ut oratio quam nos docuisti orare aditum nobis reseret indulgentiae. Quo iubente dicimus;
translation_en: God, who art the giver and creator of human life, receive the voice of our confession and sanctify our fasting with the grace of yours, that the prayer which you have taught us to pray may open for us an entrance through your mercy. By whose command we say:

text: Deus qui in sancti tui illius corde flammam accendisti dilectionis tuae da mentibus nostris eadem fidei caritate perfrui ut cuius gaudemus triumphis eius provocemur exemplis ad te proclamantes e terris;
translation_en: God, who in the heart of your saint kindled the flame of your love, grant that our minds may be filled with the same faith and charity. May we, who rejoice in his triumphs, be spurred on by his examples to proclaim you from the earth.

text: Deus qui in veri holocausti hostiam igne examinatum levitam suscepisti Laurentium quo more holocausti decoctus ad te perveniret integer pro miseris rogaturus eius quaesumus suffragiis in nobis omnibus ignis caelestis faces accende ut purgata conscientia ad te mereamur proclamare et dicere;
translation_en: God, who examined Leviticus as a burnt offering in the fire and received Lawrence, when he came to you in the manner of a burnt offering, whole despite being cooked; we beseech you through his intercession that the faces of celestial fire may be kindled within us all, so that with a purified conscience we may deserve to call out to you and say:

text: Deus qui individua divisione connecteris et in uno quod non solus es approbaris triplex exaudi supplices tuos benignus ut iniquitatis vinculis ligatum saltem gratia confessionis
translation_en: God, who connects by individual division and who is approved as the one who is not alone, hear the prayers of your supplicants graciously, so that bound by the chains of iniquity at least the grace of confession may free him.

text: Deus qui levitam tuum Vincentium tanto virtutum munere decorasti ut ministerii sacri fretus officio qui Filium tuum Dominum nostrum secuturus esset in passione eiusdem Christi tui calicem ministraret prius credentibus in salutem tu nos facito coram te digne tractare suscepta ministeriorum officia quorum gestandam suscepimus obsequelam.  Quo martyr tuus Vincentius divino auctus spiritu qui persequentem Datianum obiectibus duris aggreditur cum contra eum Valerium episcopum suum leviter musitasse conquereretur meritis suis tribuat omnibus in hac vita feliciorem excursum et in futura regione regnum beatitudinis infinitum ut sicuti eum inter poenas suscepisti te confitentem ita nunc iubeas exaudire pro nobis orantem cum ad te proclamaverimus e terris;
translation_en:
God, who adorned your servant Vincent with such a great gift of virtues that, entrusted with the office, he would serve him who was to follow your Son our Lord in his passion by first ministering the cup to him. Make us worthy to handle the duties of the offices we have undertaken in your presence.
Your martyr Vincent, strengthened by divine spirit, who confronts Datianus with hard objects, is justified for mocking Valerius, his own bishop, mildly. May he grant him a happier course in this life and an infinite kingdom of beatitude in the future realm. So, just as you received him confessing among tortures, now command that we may hear him praying for us when we have proclaimed him from the earth.

text: Deus qui nolentes praevenis fide atque credentes subsequendo facis non frustra te credidisse quique beatissimum Genesium prius gratia praevenisti dulcedinis quam regeneratione baptismatis te suppliciter deprecamur ut iam praeveniamur miserationibus tuis quo ad te fiducialiter possimus clamare e terris;
translation_en: God, who overtakes the unwilling by faith and follows the believers making it not in vain that they have believed in you; we humbly pray that you precede us with your mercies so that we may confidently call out to you from the earth.

text: Deus qui nos infirmitate relevas in pressuris exaltas dona precantibus nobis in tuam plebem venire optabilem sanitatem ut quos culpa in languorem induxit miseratio in salutem restituat quo animorum vel corporum repulsis morbis te nobiscum possint orare a terris;
translation_en: God who lifts us up from our infirmity in times of pressure, grant to those praying among your people the desirable health, so that the one whom guilt has caused to fall into weakness may be restored by mercy to salvation. May we, having been delivered from physical and spiritual diseases, be able to pray to you from the earth.

text: Deus qui nos inspicis ob legis tuae mandatum offerre primitias frugum in his oblatis tibi sacrificiis attende et frugibus nostris parce a grandine et ab omni aerum incommoditate ut cuncta nobis in commune veniant bona cum ad te nostra proclamaverit lingua;
translation_en: God, who sees us according to Your law's commandment to offer the firstfruits of our crops, pay attention to these offerings made to You as sacrifices. And be merciful to our crops from hail and from every kind of atmospheric distress, so that all things may come to us in common good when our tongue has proclaimed them to You.

text: Deus qui nos spe repromissae beatitudinis foves et panem illum caelorum e sedibus porrectum nostrae abstinentiae ariditati impertis atque concedis tu pius nobis et in praesenti ieiunii aerumna consolationem attribue et orantibus atque clamantibus ad te verba doctrinae tuae patulae pietatis accommoda aurem;
translation_en: God, who nourishes us with the promise of future beatitude and bestows upon our abstinence the bread of heaven from your throne, grant us, your merciful one, consolation in this present fast, and accommodate to us the words of your doctrine open to the ears of those praying and crying out to you.

text: Deus qui olim in hoc die beatissimum confessorem tuum Martinum et confessionis gloria et sacerdotii consecrasti corona eius interventu virtutum nos decore circumda eoque suffragante nostra deleantur facinora cui potestatem solvendi contulisti peccata ut emaculatis conscientiis ad te proclamemus e terris;
translation_en: God who once on this day consecrated your blessed confessor Martin with the glory of confession and the priesthood, adorn us with his virtues' intervention. May we be freed from our sins through his intercession, for whom you granted the power to forgive sins. May pure conscience proclaim us to you from earth.

text: Deus qui peccatores sine merito salvas et iustos ex gratia praecedente glorificas quique Adrianum ex infidelitate revocasti ad fidem et Nataliam obsequiali coronasti ex munere nostris quaesumus in eorum festo et iniquitatibus parce et spiritali nos ardore accende quo spiritaliter accensi iri intimis ad te proclamemus e terris;
translation_en: God who saves sinners without merit and glorifies the just by grace preceding, who called Adrian back from unbelief to faith and crowned Natalia in obedience from our gift, we ask that on their feast day you be merciful and kindle us with a spiritual fire so that spiritually kindled we may proclaim ourselves unto you from the earth.

text: Deus qui per beatissimum Ioannem praecursorem et martyrem tuum gentibus universis lumen baptismatis intulisti ut infidelitatem populorum quam profanae observantiae ritus intulerat regeneratio caelestis aboleret praesta ut intercessio tanti vatis quae nobis est indulta per lavacrum purae conscientiae proficiat ad exemplum ut salutaribus edocti praeceptis sic dicere mereamur e terris;
translation_en: God, who through the blessed John the Baptist and martyr brought light of baptism to all nations, that the regeneration of heaven might abolish the infidelity of the people which had been imposed by profane observances of rites, grant that the intercession of such a great prophet, which has been granted to us through the laundry of pure conscience, may profit for our example, so that we may deserve to speak righteously and be worthy to remain on earth.

text: Deus qui sacris tribusque martyribus Vincentio Sabinae et Christetae id gratiae contulisti ut qui pestiferi anguis evincerant morsum eorum serpentis custodia inhumata corpora servarentur quo illius vel ob custodiam sui uterentur obsequiis quam in paradiso deceptricem noverant homines nostris quaesumus precibus imploratus antiqui serpentis iri nobis perime virus et ea nos semper propitius tuere custodia quo nullis impellamur vitiis ad ruinam.  Etenim cum omne quod cupimus noveris misericorditer tamen quid oremus ostendis. Placabilem ergo accommoda precibus nostris aurem et sicut orandi quibus postuletis dedisti praecepta ita affectum quo impetreris accommoda cum ad te et corde nunc proclamaverimus et lingua;
translation_en: God, who granted grace to the three martyrs Vincent, Sabina, and Christeta, so that they who overcame the poisonous snakes by evading their bites, were able to preserve their bodies in an unburied state as a result of guarding them or using their guardianship for service, just as people in paradise knew; we humbly ask through our prayers that the ancient serpent's venom may be removed from us and that you may always watch over us with favor so that we are not driven by vices to ruin. Indeed, since you know all that we desire, you show us what to pray for. Therefore, make our prayers acceptable to your ear, and just as you have given the precepts of prayer to those who ask, provide us with the disposition with which to obtain it. Now that we have proclaimed our hearts to you and spoken with our tongues,

text: Deus qui sanctos apostolos tuos exemptos ab huius saeculi fluctibus angelicis iussisti coetibus aggregari quos etiam tuis praeceptionibus inhaerentes qualiter te deprecarentur exhortator piissimus informasti supplices quaesumus ut qui illos hilari affatu salubriter imbuisti nobis ipsam precem cum fiducia permittas clamare et dicere;
translation_en: God, who commanded your holy apostles to be gathered together from the fluctuations of this world by angels, and who, being most compassionate instructed them in their supplication on how they should approach you; we humbly ask that you permit us, with confidence, to imbibe the very same prayer with which you blessed them, and allow us to say and pray;

text: Deus qui te in spiritu et veritate adorare mandasti virtute nos obumbra Spiritus Sancti. Veniat iam super nos misericordia tua et salutaris tui gratia repromissa quo per quem nobis a te credimus peccata dimitti per eum ad te dirigatur precatio oris nostri;
translation_en: God, who commanded you to be worshipped in spirit and truth by your virtue, may the shadow of the Holy Spirit come upon us now. May your mercy and the promised grace of your salvation soon descend upon us, through whom we believe that our sins are forgiven; through Him may our prayer be directed towards You.

text: Deus qui virginum agmine saeptus quocumque ieris ab eisdem solis prosequeris collaudandus qui te illo virginitatis cantico laudant quod electi ceteri audire queunt promere nequeunt te votis supplicibus imploramus ut sic per ea quae nos te exorare docuisti emundes et cantici ipsius canentium numerositati adsocies ut per compunctionem hic deflendo quae gessimus per dilectionem quoque te patrem invocemus atque dicamus;
translation_en: God, who is enclosed by the rank of virgins wherever you go, you are worthy of praise from the same sun that follows you. You are lauded by them with that song of virginity, which others can hear but cannot promise. We implore you with supplicant vows to cleanse us through those whom you have taught us to invoke, and to associate with the number of their singing, so that through compunction we may appeal to you in our sorrow through love, and call upon you as father.

text: Deus sanator noster qui et virginum integritatem custodis et corruptorum scisse carnis rupturam mira indulgentiae compositione resarcis quique in hac virgine sic servasti collatum a te virginitatis unicae donum ut eam faceres ad destinatum pervenire martyrium te quaesumus ut eius obtentu ita nos eluas libidinum incentivis quo cunctis resistendo adversis fiducialiter ad te proclamemus e terris;
translation_en: Our Healing God, who keeps the integrity of virgins and miraculously restores the breakage of corrupt flesh with wondrous compositions of mercy, we ask that you preserved in this Virgin the unique gift of virginity so that she may reach her predestined martyrdom. We beseech You to free us from the temptations of lust through her merits and, by resisting all adversities, may we confidently proclaim ourselves devoted to You from the earth.

text: Devotione geminata carissimi fratres passo pro nobis domino maestificati cordis hostias offeramus maeroris operibus fructum laetitiae comparantes ut dum paschale sacrificium sedulitatis studio agere procuramus in adventum ipsius strenuae servitutis testimonium reportemus. Per ipsum quo iubente dicimus;
translation_en: With a doubled devotion, dear brothers, we offer the Lord, humbled in spirit, sacrifices of our hearts through works of mourning, comparing fruit of joy. In doing so, as we strive diligently to perform the Paschal sacrifice, we aim to present evidence of our strong service as he approaches. Through him, whom we obey at his command, we say:

text: Diligentes Deum fratres carissimi pietatis eius in nobis petamus operari dilectionem ut divinae virtutis dono repleti orationem dominicam in qua spes est nostrae salutis sic dicere mereamur e terris;
translation_en: Dear brothers, we who love God, ask that His pity work in us, so that filled with the gift of divine virtue, we may be worthy to pray the Lord's prayer in which our salvation's hope lies. Thus on earth, we may deserve to say.

text: Divino magisterio edocti et divina institutione formati audemus dicere;
translation_en: We dare to say, having been taught by divine teaching and formed by divine institution;

text: Divino magisterio edocti et salutaribus monitis instituti audemus dicere;
translation_en: Having been taught by divine guidance and instructed by beneficial admonishments, we dare to say:

text: Domine Deus omnipotens in quo certatrix Euphemia veraciter credens nec argumento lapidum nec morsibus laniata est bestiarum fac nos nec de adversis deici nec de prosperis elevari quo discreto aequitatis iudicio gradientes tuaque monita promptissime observantes sicut illam in omnibus persecutionibus suis te precantem exaudisti de caelis sic nos semper exaudias ad te proclamantes e terris;
translation_en: Lord God Almighty, in whom the wrestler Euphemia truly believes and was not harmed by stones or torn apart by beasts, make us neither fall from adversity nor be lifted up from prosperity; according to a just judgment of equity, may we promptly observe your commandments. As you heard her prayers from heaven in all her persecutions, so may you always hear us as we call out to you from the earth.

text: Domine Iesu Christe cuius in fame pascimur verbo cuius in siti recreamur alloquio tu et ieiunium nostrum sanctifica tuae gratiae incremento et vocem nostram exaudi e summo caelo;
translation_en: Lord Jesus Christ, by whose word we are fed in hunger and refreshed in thirst, we humbly ask that you sanctify our fasting through your grace's increase and hear our voice from the highest heaven.

text: Domine Iesu Christe qui pro nobis carnem de virgine suscepisti et praecepta nobis tribuisti orandi tu ea quae nos te docente exposcimus propitiatus exaudi ut qui dies istos incarnationis tuae summa cum veneratione suscipimus dono Sancti Spiritus muneremur;
translation_en: Lord Jesus Christ, who for us took flesh from a virgin and commanded us to pray to you, we humbly offer what we present to you, taught by you. Grant that we may receive these days of your incarnation with the highest veneration, and be endowed with the gift of the Holy Spirit.

text: Domine Iesu Christe qui sic virginem matrem honorificasti quousque assumptionis gratia eam coram te suffragatricem pro nobis effecisti incomparabilem indigni quaesumus divinitatis tuae clementiam quatenus per obtentum illius beatissimae genetricis quam coelibem hodie fecisti in caelestibus regnis emundati ab universis contagiis audeamus exclamare et dicere e terris;
translation_en: Lord Jesus Christ, who honored the Virgin Mother to such an extent that through the grace of assumption you made her our advocate before you incomparable, we humbly ask for the kindness of your divinity. May it be that through the merit of the most blessed Mother whom today you have made a celibate in heavenly kingdoms, cleansed from all contagions, we dare to exclaim and say to her from earth:

text: Domine qui Agrii tui carnibus acquisitum tibi populum et mundas et saturas ne patiaris nos ultra esu draconis pollui cuius caput pro salute hominum contrivisti sed tu nos populum tuum et oves gregis tui Verbi tui cibo confortante imbue et Agrii tui vestigiis quae consequamur adiunge;
translation_en: Lord, who by the flesh of your sheep made a people for yourself and cleansed and satisfied them, may you not allow us to be defiled any further by the devouring dragon, whose head you have fashioned for the salvation of mankind; but rather fill us, your people, and the flock of your Word with the food that sustains us, and add to the footsteps of your sheep that we may follow.

text: Domine qui magnus dies es angelorum parvus in die hominum Verbum Deus ante omnia tempora Verbum caro opportuno in tempore conditus sub sole conditor solis da nobis diei huius iri tuis laudibus ecclesiasticae dignitatis sollemnem conventum ut qui initium anni talibus primitiis tibimet consecrasti totius temporis spatium tibi placitis excursibus atque operibus facias immolari quia te iubente oramus e terris;
translation_en: Lord, who art great among the angels but small in the day of man, Word of God before all time, Word made flesh suited to the time, created under the sun, creator of the sun, grant us that we may go through this day with your praises of ecclesiastical dignity. Since you have consecrated the beginning of the year with such beginnings, make the whole space of time pleasing to you by our excursions and works, because we ask that you rule from the earth.

text: Dominum Deum nostrum fratres carissimi toto corde deprecemur et humili oratione poscamus ut festivitatem hanc quam hodierno die in honorem sancti ac beatissimi illius devotissime celebramus illustret et nos consortes sanctis effectos propositum nostrum vitamque consummet ut cui sumus in hac nostra devotione fautores esse mereamur eidem donante Christo participes;
translation_en: We humbly beseech our dear brothers the Lord God, with all our heart, that this festival which today we are devoutly celebrating in honor of the holy and most blessed one, may be illuminated. May it fulfill our common purpose for which we have gathered, and complete our life, so that we may deserve to be supporters of Him in this devotion and participants given by Christ.

text: Dum sacrosancti sacrificii fratres carissimi dona tractamus omnipotenti Deo concessa oratione placeamus. Agnoscat pater filii sui verba atque ad aures clementiae suae unita prece concordem populus clamorem attollat et dicat;
translation_en: As we, the dear brothers, handle the offerings for the sacred sacrifice, may we be pleasing to the almighty God through the prayer granted to us. May He recognize His Son's words, and let a united people raise up their voices in harmony with our plea, and say:

text: E caelis Deus audi vocem nostram qui Stephanum martyrem tuum pro inimicis orantem audisti de terra quique eius spiritum in confessione tui nominis suscepisti orationem suscipe qua a nobis patrem invocati iussisti;
translation_en: From heaven, God, hear our voice, who heard the voice of your martyr Stephen praying for his enemies from the earth, and who received his spirit in the confession of your name. Receive also the prayer that we, summoned as fathers, have been commanded to invoke.

text: Ecce carorum fratrum sacra sollemnia celebrantes te Deum pietatis intentione rogamus ut quorum condicione corporum Iberam dedicas terram eorum precibus in pace omnem tuo sanguine redemptam tuearis ecclesiam quo eisdem suffragantibus a te promereamur audiri a quo praeceptum suscepimus exorandi ut dicamus;
translation_en: Behold the brethren of cars celebrating your sacred solemnities with pious intention, we humbly ask you to grant the land to those whose condition is in the body. May their prayers protect all the redeemed earth by your blood in peace. We pray for your church that it may be heard by you, as promised for them whom we hope to receive favors from you; we have taken the commandment to beseech you, so that we may say:

text: Ecce dilectissimi fratres fideli relatu cognovimus beatissimum Saturninum et gradu pontificalis sacerdotii functum et a tergo tauri illigatum pedibus martyrio consecratum.  Unde omnipotentem Deum qui ei geminam coronam sacerdotii scilicet atque martyrii largitus est deprecemur ut vel fides nos apud eum commendet qui supplicium nullum patimur propter fidem ut spes non destituat miseros quos non efficit effusio sanguinis gloriosos ut qui <sumus> recreati per momenta divinis consolemur sermonibus cum ad eum proclamaverimus;
translation_en: We have learned of the dearest brothers, a reliable report about the most blessed Saturninus, who was appointed to the pontifical order of priesthood and consecrated by martyrdom bound to the back of an ox. Therefore, we humbly ask the almighty God who has bestowed upon him both the double crown of priesthood and martyrdom, to recommend our faith to Him, since we suffer no punishment for our faith. May our hope not abandon the miserable ones whom His glorious blood does not make holy. We pray that those who are comforted by moments of divine grace will find solace in words with us as we proclaim Him.

text: Ecce dilectissimi fratres mecum oculos in sublime attollite hoc a domino specialiter precaturi ut qui gratia fidei christianae cor beatae Lupariae dignatus est illustrare repente nos in hoc momento ab omni criminum labe dignetur efficaciter expurgare proclamantes ad se e terris atque dicentes;
translation_en: Behold, my dearest brothers, lift up your eyes towards the sublime, for this is particularly prayed for by the Lord, that He may worthy of the grace of the Christian faith have illuminated the heart of Blessed Luparia to suddenly enlighten us in this moment, and cleanse us effectively from all guilt of sin. Proclaiming ourselves to Him from the earth and saying:

text: Ecce Domine redemptor noster et conditor hodierno die incumbente festo Cypriani martyris tui copiosius iucundamur et tamen pro ablutione nostrorum criminum suspiramus. Illius quippe gloriosos cineres retinet Africana Carthago sed lingua toto paene claret in mundo.  Unde quia hic vir etsi loculo teneatur in corpore beneficiis tamen patet ubique te rogamus et petimus ut eius nobis suffragio ea quae tibi debemus dimittas cuius nos doctrinis ut te oremus illustras;
translation_en:
Behold, O Lord, our Redeemer and Creator, on this day, the festival of your martyr Cyprian approaching, we are abundantly delighted but at the same time we sigh for the cleansing of our sins. Indeed, his glorious ashes are held by African Carthage, yet everywhere in the world it is almost clear that he prays for us.
Since this man is contained within a body but prayers on our behalf are open to you everywhere, we ask and beseech you to remit from us what we owe to you, whom you have enlightened through your teachings so that we may pray to you.

text: Ecce Iesu bone qui nos patri tuo per sanguinem tuum reconciliasti pro nobis patiendo innocens crucem et solus inventus inter mortuos liber tuum sicut ipse docuisti deitatis natura et nostrum adoptionis gratia patrem poscentes affectu quo possumus imploramus ut resurgentes a malorum nostrorum sepulcris a tuis Christe non recedamus vestigiis;
translation_en: Behold Jesus, good one who reconciled us to your Father through your blood for us, suffering innocently on the cross and found alone among the dead freeing your own, just as you taught concerning the nature of your deity and our adoption's grace. With affection as we can, we implore you that rising from the tombs of our sins, we may not depart from your Christlike footsteps.

text: Ecce Salvator noster et Domine; qui per paginam veteris instrumenti offerri tibi decimas rerum praecipimur annuales tibi dierum decimas consecrare conamur praelargissimam tuae pietatis clementiam implorantes ut in congressione viae huius instruas nos documentis iustitiae et praeceptionibus legis tuae quibus instructi et hodierni diei suscepta sollemnia expleamus et devotissime a crastino instituta ieiunia inchoemus;
translation_en: Behold, our Savior and Lord; who through the pages of the old instrument are commanded to offer you annual tithes, we strive to consecrate daily tithes, invoking your most plentiful mercy. We implore that in the assembly of this way (pilgrimage), you guide us with documents of justice and teachings of your law by which we may be instructed, and complete today's solemnities, and from tomorrow begin the devout fasts.

text: Educ Domine de carcere animas nostras qui beatissimum Ioannem Herodiano gladio consecrasti. Detur per eum nobis paenitentiae optio qui paenitudinis exstitit praedicator. Conservet in fide populos qui arguit de infidelitate superbos. Deferat ad te confessionem humilium qui reargutor factus est contemptorum. Quique nuntius exstitit Verbi gratiam nobis praeroget nuntiati cum ad te nunc proclamaverimus e terris;
translation_en: Lord, from prison release our souls, whom you consecrated the blessed John Herodian with a sword. May he grant us the option of penitence, who became a preacher of repentance. May he preserve the people who accuse the proud for unfaithfulness. Let him bring to you the confession of the humble, who have become the accuser of the contemptible. And may he, as a messenger of the Word's grace, intercede on our behalf when we now proclaim to you from the earth.

text: Emunda Domine conscientias nostras fidei catholicae confessione sincera et cordis contritione continua ut semper a te exaudiamur e caelis cum pro nostris delictis ad te proclamaverimus e terris;
translation_en: Purify, Lord, our consciences with the sincere confession of the Catholic faith and continuous heartfelt contrition, so that we may always be heard by you from heaven, after we have declared our sins to you on earth.

text: Erige nos ante conspectum tuum omnipotens Deus in quo vivimus cui sollemnes sumus cuius beneficio nostra salus est cuius donum nostra festivitas cuius munus vita credentium cuius redemptio resurrectio mortuorum.  Adesto sacrificiis quae docuisti; adesto gaudiis quae dedisti qui spem resurrectionis ac redemptionis nostrae Filii tui resurrectione signasti.  Conserva in nobis inter omnia ac super omnia hoc munus tuum ut hunc resurrectionis dominicae diem dignis conci10 nentes carminibus ad te e terris sic dicere mereamur;
translation_en:
Erect us before your omnipotent God, in whom we live, to whom we are solemn, whose benefit is our salvation, whose gift is our festivity, whose service is the life of believers, whose redemption is the resurrection of the dead.
Assist at the sacrifices which you taught; assist at the joys which you gave, who have marked the hope of our resurrection and redemption with the resurrection of your Son.
Preserve in us above all things and especially this gift of yours, that we may be worthy to sing fitting hymns on this day of the resurrection from the earth to you.

text: Erigite fratres oculos ad caelum petentes a Deo perenne auxilium qui hunc beatissimum Sebastianum martyrem suum insutum ictibus sagittarum post exceptum supplicium aeternum convocavit ad regnum.  Clamate ad illum et nullo modo detis ei silentium; nam ostendet in nobis indulgentiae pietatem si pia eum invocaverimus ex voce proclamantes atque ita dicentes;
translation_en: Lift up, brothers, your eyes to heaven, seeking eternal help from God who called his most blessed martyr Sebastian, untouched by arrow strikes after receiving punishment, to the kingdom. Call out to him and do not give him silence; for he will show us mercy if we invocate him devoutly with voice proclaiming, and thus saying:

text: Erubescimus Domine te patrem vocibus appellare qui filiorum amisimus dignitatem. Sed quia paterno affectu nos salvas cum de propriis delictis non iudicas ideo etsi indigni filii paternae tamen precem fundimus pietati petentes ut in hoc nostrae afflictionis tempore nostrum iubeas peccatum omittere quo etsi meritis nequimus saltem affectu cordis te patrem invocemus atque dicamus;
translation_en: We blush, Lord, to call you Father who have lost the dignity of Sons. Yet, because as a loving Father you save us despite not judging us for our own sins, therefore even though we are unworthy sons, we pour out our prayerful plea to your mercy. We ask that during this time of our affliction, you command the sin to be omitted, so that although we cannot merit it, at least with affection in our hearts, we invoke you as Father and say:

text: Ex tuo Christe Deus admonemur praecepto ut spirituum temptamenta malorum per salubre devincamus te opitulante ieiunium. Sed quia nihil valet fragilitas nostra si nos non adiuvaverit misericordia tua rogamus ut in omne quod agimus tua nos misericordia subsequatur et in omne quod petimus a te audiri promereamur;
translation_en: From You, Christ God, we are admonished by Your command to overcome the temptations of evil spirits through healthy fasting, with Your help. However, since our fragility is of no avail unless Your mercy supports us, we humbly ask that Your mercy follows us in all that we do, and we promise to beseech You to hear our prayers in all that we ask.

text: Exaudi Domine supplicantes famulos tuos et devotionem eorum benignus assiste ut misericordiam tuam nec ab eis exoratus subtrahas nec a nobis offensus avertas sed celeriter te placari emendatione concedas cum ea quae Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus orare docuit oraverint e terris;
translation_en: Hear us, O Lord, your supplicating servants and benignly assist their devotion that you may not withdraw your mercy from them who ask for it nor turn away from us because we have sinned. Rather, grant that you be quickly appeased with the amendment they make as our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, taught to pray. They prayed on earth.

text: Exaudi Domine vocem precis nostrae et huius ieiunii litationem propitiatus acceptare dignare quo semper te propitium habeamus cum te patrem piissimum invocaverimus ita dicentes;
translation_en: Hear us, O Lord, the voice of our supplication and this Lenten fasting's entreaty. Be gracious and accept it, that we may always have you propitious when we invoke the most kind Father. So let us say:

text: Exaudi Domine voces et populi tui preces non merito poscentium sed sanctorum causa praesentium cum tibi tuis institutis omnes proclamamus e terris;
translation_en: Hear us, O Lord, the voices and prayers of your people, who are not worthy to ask but through the cause of the saints present with you. We all proclaim this to you from the earth.

text: Exaudi omnipotens aeterne Deus supplicem plebem tuam ob honorem Mariae beatissimae genitricis et ita preces nostras benignus intende ut cum fiducia dicere mereamur orationem quam nos Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus orare sic docuit dicens;
translation_en: Hear, O almighty everlasting God, your humble people's supplication, on behalf of the most blessed Virgin Mary, our Mother, and so incline your benevolence to attend to our prayers. May we merit confidently to say the prayer that our Lord Jesus Christ, Your Son, taught us when He said:

text: Excellentissimam in hac nocte tuae Christe resurrectionis celebrantes sollemnitatem in qua ipse novus dies novo de tumulo surgens veternosam antiquae noctis caliginem caelestem convertisti in claritatem te quibus possumus lacrimosis rugitibus imploramus ut qui nos redemisti pretio tui sanguinis instituta a te praecepta acceptes nostrae orationis cum ea quae nos docuisti proclamaverimus e terris;
translation_en: Celebrating this night's solemnity of your excellent resurrection, Christ, where you yourself rose on a new day from the ancient tomb, and transformed the dark gloom of the celestial old night into light. We implore you with tearful cries that you who have redeemed us with the price of your blood, accepted by you the precepts instituted, proclaimed our prayers along with those which you taught us from earth.

text: Eximio eminentiae munere immensa tua pietas eminet Christe in quo saepe indignis digna largiris dum et praevenis misericordia nolentes et provehis laureaudos in caelis quique sanctum tuum Christophorum martyrem dum iuxta quod in omnibus mansueta species manet dissimilis exstaret positione tanto fidei cremasti ardore ut tuo fretus munere et inimicis eum ostenderis in terrore et victorem illum faceres in passionis agone praebe nobis quaesumus similem te sequendo obtinere amorem ut qui nostro ex merito indigni sumus servi vocari eius suffragio te patrem mereamur adoptive habere ut libera voce semper ad te clamemus e terris;
translation_en: By your eminent gift, your great mercy, Christ, shines above all. You often give what is worthy to the unworthy, and you surpass in mercy those who do not desire it, and you help the unwilling ones to reach laurels in heaven. Those who venerate your saint Christopher, the martyr, may also exist in such a faith-fueled ardor that, trusting in your gift, they would show him to their enemies as a terror and make him victorious in the struggle of passion. Grant us, we ask, a likeness of you when following him, so that we who are unworthy servants by our own merit may be called by his intercession worthy to call you our Father adoptively. May we always cry out to you with a free voice from the earth.

text: Exsultantes de tuorum parvulorum Iusti et Pastoris Deus pater triumphis quorum laetantis infantiae aetas relictis scholae tabulis ad suscipiendum alacriter pervolavit bravium passionis tibi creatori nostro et vota cum gaudiis et scelera pandimus cum lamentis poscentes tuam piissime maiestatem ut qui illorum innocentiam consecrasti martyrio nostram miseriam repares innocentiae bono quo eorum adiuti suffragiis ad te proclamare mereamur e terris;
translation_en: Exulting in your righteous little ones and God, Father, triumphs whose joyful childhood has flown away from school tables to embrace eagerly the reward of your passion, we present to you, our Creator, our vows along with our joys and sins, pleading with your most merciful majesty. May you who consecrated their innocence through martyrdom repair our misery with the good which they attained, so that with their assistance we may deserve to proclaim ourselves worthy of you from the earth.

text: Fac nos aeterne Deus ut unusquisque nostrum vas suum in honore et sanctificatione possideat qui virgines tuas Ius.tam et Rufinam ex conquestu fictilium vasculorum passionis perduxisti ad gloriam quo emundatis conscientiis ad te proclamemus e terris;
translation_en: Make us eternally, God, that each one of us may possess his vessel in honor and sanctification who brought your virgins Justa and Rufina from the triumphant vessels of passion to glory. So we cleanse our consciences on earth, proclaiming them to you.

text: Fons vitae perennis Iesu Filius Dei vivi in aeternum da nobis aquam vivam; da sitientibus vitam aeternam. Efficiamur quaesumus templum tuum in quo habites in aeternum ut et ipsi intra nos habeamus regnum tuum. Tu nos Christe Iesu exaudi de summis cum patrem sicut nos iussisti exoraverimus e terris
translation_en: Fountain of eternal life, Jesus Son of the living God, give us living water; give eternal life to those who thirst. May we be made effective, we ask, your temple in which you dwell forever, so that we too may have your kingdom within us. Hear us, Christ Jesus, from the heights with the Father, as you have commanded us to pray from earth.

text: Fratres carissimi martyrum parvulorum exempla incitent nos ad virorum fortium acta et sicut illorum vox sanguinis clamavit ad Deum ita nos unita pietatis voce exclamemus ad caelum et dicamus;
translation_en: Dear brothers, the examples of these child martyrs inspire us to act like men of great courage. Just as their voice of blood cried out to God, so let us exclaim with the voice united by piety to heaven and say:

text: Gloriosi levitae exemplis et beatissimi martyris Stephani magisteriis instituti aeterno regi et patri Deo precem fratres carissimi cum omni humilitate fundamus ut dato nobis fidei calore vel munere ad martyrii nos desiderium amoris sui igne succendat eiusque imitatores efficiat qui non solum pro sui gloria verum etiam pro exemplis eruditionis nostrae passionem sustinuit et cui conferre dignatus est in passione virtutem intercedendi pro nobis tribuat facultatem et orationem quam praecipere dignatus est dicere sine cunctatione permittat;
translation_en: With the shining examples of the glorious Levite and the most blessed martyr Stephen, we humbly present our prayer to the eternal King and Father, God. We ask our dearest brothers that they establish for us a burning faith or gift, so that the desire for martyrdom inspired by his love's fire may ignite in us. May he make us imitators, who not only suffered for his glory but also for the examples of our education, and to whom it was deemed worthy to grant virtue in suffering intercession on our behalf. May he grant us the ability and prayer which He deems fit to command without hesitation.

text: Gratias tibi agimus omnipotens aeterne Deus et domino Iesu Christo filio tuo qui nos per sanguinem crucis suae redemit qui pro delictorum nostrorum indulgentia ad te de cruce clamavit qui discipulos suos antequam ad crucis passionem veniret sic docuit orare et dicere;
translation_en: We give thanks to you, almighty eternal God and Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who redeemed us by your blood shed on the cross, who before coming to his passion taught his disciples how to pray and say:

text: His precibus te Deus Pater omnipotens deprecamur quibus nos Dominus noster Iesus Christus Filius tuus orare praecepit dicens;
translation_en: With these prayers we humbly entreat you, God the Almighty Father, as our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, commanded us to pray, saying:

text: Iesu esto nobiscum in hac via ne in hoc mundo tepide nos agentes aut crapula vel ebrietate corda nostra graventur aut curis huius saeculi dimergantur. Sed potius fac nos ita ieiuniis vel vigiliis dies istos passionis tuae amabiliter praestolare ut tunc nos placabiles reddat et nunc cum ea quae nos docuisti protulerimus gratiae nobis donum infundat. Quia te iubente dicimus;
translation_en: Jesus, be with us on this way, that in this world we do not act faint-heartedly because of wine or drunkenness, and our hearts are burdened or because of the cares of this world we are distracted. But rather, make us so observe these days of your passion lovingly through fasting or vigils, that then you may render us pleasing, and now with her whom you have taught, grant us the grace-filled gift. Because it is by your command that we say:
