text: Iesu praeceptor occurre nobis ambulantibus viam cupientibus pervenire ad patriam ut praecedente luce tua ambulemus in viam rectam nec oberremus in tenebram istius noctis horrendam te in nobis lucente qui es via veritas et vita.  Da igitur nobis ut sicut caecus iste per confessionem verae credulitatis obtinuit donum indultae salutis ita nos adipiscamur in tuis verbis effectum piae petitionis cum ea quae nos docuisti proclamaverimus e terris;
translation_en: Jesus, our guide, meet us as we walk, desiring to reach the homeland by following the path. Let us walk in your light, so that we do not stumble in this dreadful night's darkness. You in us shine who are the way, truth, and life. Therefore, give us such that, like a blind man who obtained the gift of forgiven salvation through confession of true faith, we may acquire the effect of pious petition with what you taught us, which we have proclaimed from the earth.

text: Iesu redemptor piissime cura vulnera nostra stigmate crucis tuae. Hodie nos oratio quam ipse docuisti reddat idoneos et cras passio tua efficiat in tuae mortis unione connexos. Hodie bone Iesu exaudi nos de caelis cum ea quae nos docuisti proclamaverimus e terris;
translation_en: Jesus, most merciful Redeemer, care for our wounds caused by the stigmata of your cross. Today let the prayer that you yourself taught us make us fit, and may tomorrow your passion unite us in the union of your death. Today, good Jesus, hear us from heaven with what we on earth have proclaimed according to what you taught us.

text: Illis te Domine sancte Deus Pater omnipotens precibus deprecamur quibus nos per sanctos apostolos tuos orare docuisti;
translation_en: To them, Lord, holy God, all-powerful Father, we humbly beseech You with prayers, through whom You have taught us to pray to You through Your holy apostles.

text: In hac tuorum martyrum Servandi et Germani Christe Deus passionis die laetantes oblatis tibi victimis veniam te nostris dare flagitamus offensis poscentes ut qui eorum gladii animadversione non terruisti constantiam nostra eisdem intervenientibus et abluas crimina et suscipias postulata. Quia te iubente dicimus;
translation_en: On the day of your martyrs Servandus and Germanus, Christ God, rejoicing, we offer you victims, we implore you to grant us forgiveness for our offenses, asking that who among them were not terrified by the gaze of their swords strengthen our constancy; may they intervene on our behalf and wash away our sins, and receive our petitions. Since we say this by your command.

text: Inaestimabilem tuae magnificentiae bonitatem iri hac resurrectionis Filii tui sollemnitate cum veneratione deposcimus Domine sancte Pater aeterne omnipotens Deus cuius bonitatis imago est Christus per quem nobis tale munus condonare dignatus es ut nos eius passione ac resurrectione ex servis filios adoptares.  Per ipsum te Domine supplices exoramus ut nos ab omni infestatione adversarii tutos atque defensos custodias ut numquam tuum contristemur Spiritum Sanctum sed ipsum semper habeamus advocatum ut officiis misericordiae et humilitatis insistentes divitias caelestes ab eo in futuro percipere mereamur;
translation_en:
We implore your inestimable goodness, O divine majesty, during this solemnity of the Resurrection of your Son, with reverence. Lord, holy Father, eternal and omnipotent God, whose image is Christ, through whom you were pleased to grant us such a gift, that we might be adopted as sons from servants because of his passion and resurrection.
Through Him, Lord, we humbly entreat You to protect and defend us from every adversary's attack, so that we may never grieve Your Holy Spirit. May He always be our advocate, that by persevering in the works of mercy and humility, we may merit to receive celestial riches from Him in the future.

text: Inclinemus Deo fratres carissimi corda nostra cum lacrimis et confitentes peccata nostra clementissimo conditori iugi obsecratione clamemus e terris;
translation_en: We incline our dear brothers' hearts to God with tears and confessing our sins to the most merciful Creator we implore Him with supplications from the earth.

text: Indigni quidem sumus nomine filiorum omnipotens Deus sed iuvante domino nostro Iesu Christo filio tuo licet trepidantes tamen oboedientes humili mente oramus et dicimus;
translation_en: Indeed, we are unworthy to be called the sons of Almighty God, but with the help of our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, although trembling, we obey with a humble mind; we pray and say:

text: Intendite dilectissimi fratres sacerdotis Babilae inconvulsae spei virtutem triumque puerorum robustiorem animi fidem quam valentem corporis qualitatem quos praedictus doctor egregius gladio continuo percussurus sacris ulnis congeminando complectit gratias flebiliter referens creatori quod eos quos de manu eius acceperat coronandos obtulerit illi.  Horum igitur exemplum constantiae imitantes corrigamus mores in melius caritatem teneamus ad invicem per dilectionem acceptum ministerium expleamus et ad servitutem Dei ceteros inflammemus; operari iustitiam delectemur noxia fugiamus spiritu oremus atque dicamus;
translation_en:
Pay close attention, my dearest brothers, priests of Babylon, the unbroken strength of hope and the greater faith of the robust three boys, which is stronger than their powerful bodily quality. The esteemed teacher, who will continually strike them with his sword, humbly offers thanks to the Creator for offering them, whom he received in his hand to crown, to Him.
Therefore, let us imitate the constancy of these examples and correct our behavior for the better, let us hold on to love for each other through mutual affection, let us complete our accepted service, let us kindle a desire for servitude to God in others, and let us delight in justice, flee from wickedness, pray and say:

text: Intuere Deus famulos tuos qui tibi fideliter decimum suarum rerum persolvunt et sicut promisisti horrea eorum impleantur frumento et redundent torcularia vino et oleo ut non in eis sit morbus neque casus sed cum eis in nobis semper tuus vivat affectus nec desit tuae gratiae virtus cum ad te nunc proclamaverimus e terris;
translation_en: May God look upon your servants who faithfully pay you the tithe of their possessions, and let their barns be filled with grain, their wine presses overflow with wine, and their olive presses with oil. May there never be sickness or accident among them, but may your love always live among us, and may your grace not cease among them. For we now proclaim you from the earth.

text: Investigabilis omnium creaturae occultorum secretissime munda quaesumus nos in huius diei excessu tuae genitricis ab omni noxiorum labe ut ita demum nostra purificati conscientia saltem per eam deportatricem tibimet nostrae paupertatulae deferamus votum ut quandoque tuum valeamus adipisci regnum atque idcirco hunc catholicum gregem de tua misericordia fidentem te patrem valeat iubilo personare in laudem ut tuo quamquam indigni eruditi magisterio patulo ore proclamare possimus e terris;
translation_en: We humbly ask that you make us thoroughly investigable of all hidden creatures on this day of your mother's departure, and cleanse us from any stain of evil. In this way, we may finally present our purified conscience to her as a carrier of our humble poverty, and through her may be able to offer our vow to you. We hope that one day we may worthily acquire your kingdom, and therefore, let this Catholic flock confidently sing your praise with joy from your mercy, so that we, though unworthy, can proclaim your generous teachings widely with open mouths from the earth.

text: Ipsius praeceptum est Domine quod agimus (in) cuius nunc te praesentia postulamus; da sacrificio auctorem suum ut impleatur fides rei in sublimitate mysterii ut sicut veritatem caelestis sacrificii exsequimur sic veritatem dominici corporis et sanguinis hauriamus per eundem Christum Dominum nostrum dicentes;
translation_en: It is Your commandment, Lord, that we are doing (this) in whose presence we now beseech you; grant a sacrificer for its own offering, so that the faith of the mystery may be fulfilled in its sublimity. Thus, as we carry out the truth of the heavenly sacrifice, so let us partake of the truth of your Lord's body and blood through the same Christ our Lord, saying:

text: ( ... deest incipit ...) invocato sancto nomine suo iubeat liberari et iam eos nostris precibus adiuvemus qui ignorantes adhuc iter verum a diabolo in erroribus saeculi detinentur ut omnes agnitione suae maiestatis illuminet per Iesum Christum Dominum nostrum cuius mandata retinentes oramus et dicimus;
translation_en: (... missing start ...) when the holy one is invoked by his own name, he commands to be freed and now let us assist with our prayers those who are still led astray by the devil in the errors of this world, unaware of the true path. Let all be enlightened with the knowledge of their majesty through Jesus Christ our Lord, whose commands we hold. We pray and say:

text: Libera nos omnipotens ab omni malo vel auctore vel opera malo ut animos noster ad peccatum nec apetitum facilli sit haec consensum eius. Solum ministerii studeat fieri per quem desiderant liberare quo te iubente dicimus e terris;
translation_en: Deliver us, Almighty One, from every evil and its author or deed that our souls may not easily be led to sin through this consent of his. May only the ministry be done by whom they desire to set free, whom we say are sent from you on your command from the earth.

text: Malorum nostrorum fratres carissimi memores lacrimosas preces domini dirigamus ad aures quo mundati a vitiis libera ad eum voce proclamemus e terris;
translation_en: To our dearest brothers in affliction, we direct the tearful prayers of the Lord to His ears, so that He may cleanse them from sins and on earth we proclaim our voice to Him.

text: Memento Domine quod terra sumus et adspice contritionem nostri spiritus ut qui carnis infirmitate ad terram prosternimur ad caelos castigatione spiritalis ieiunii sublevemur et quia ex nostro est ut cadamus ex tuo sit ut surgamus;
translation_en: Remember, Lord, that we are earth and look upon the contrition of our spirit, so that we who are brought low by the weakness of the flesh may be lifted up to heaven through spiritual penance, and because it is from us that we fall, may it be from you that we rise.

text: Memor apud te Christe Iesu virtutis aeternae et apud me imbecillitatis humanae vix audeo commemoratione dominicae passionis effari qui tremebunda non sustinet humanis conscientia quod libere maiestatis poscit auctoritas ( ... cetera desiderantur ... )
translation_en: Remembering you, Christ Jesus, eternal power, I dare not within my humble self recount the memory of your Lordly Passion which trembling humanity cannot bear to acknowledge what freely demands authority from majesty (... the rest is desired ... ).

text: Memores dilectissimi fratres Romani beatissimi interritam fidem et inconcussae spei soliditatem qua se praedixit paratum sibi incendium nullis modis esse visurum cor nostrum armis spiritalibus perarmemus et ea quae a Deo postulaverimus posse nos promereri credamus.  Nam idem qui tunc propitius affuit sui martyris voto erit procul dubio nostrae confessionis acceptor ut qui illi tribuit martyrii palmam non reiciet nostram in honorem tanti martyris obsequelam. Extendamus ergo cum palmis ad aethera vocem et ea quae nos ipse instituit orare proclamemus e terris cum summa meritis intentione;
translation_en: Remembering, dearest brothers of Rome, the blessed faith and unshakable steadfastness of hope with which you foretold yourself to be unwilling to see your heart kindled by any means, let us arm our hearts with spiritual weapons. And we believe that what we have asked from God will be granted to us. For the same One who was favorable then to his martyr's vow will certainly be an acceptor of our confession. He who gave a palm to the martyr will not reject our offering in honor of such a great martyr. Therefore, let us extend with palms our voice to heaven and proclaim on earth what you yourself instituted for us to pray with supreme merits.

text: Memores praeceptorum tuorum Domine oramus et dicimus ...
translation_en: Remembering Your commandments, Lord, we pray and say...

text: Minuetur Domine in visceribus nostris mundana cupiditas et caelestium praemiorum nutriatur magis ac magis caritas ut in universa quam Christus dilexit ecclesia clamemus tibi ex totis praecordiis et cum tremore mentis et corporis dicamus e terris;
translation_en: Lord, may mundane desires be minimized within our hearts and let the love for celestial rewards grow more and more, so that we may cry out to you as the Church did when it loved Christ throughout all things. From all our innermost parts we shall say this with trembling mind and body, from earth.

text: Minuetur Domine in visceribus nostris per intercessum sanctae Marinae virginis et martyris tuae humana cupiditas et caelestium praemiorum nutriatur magis tua caritas ut in universa quam Christus dilexit ecclesia clamemus omnes ex totis praecordiis et cum tremore mentis et corporis dicamus e terris;
translation_en: Lord, may there be a change within our hearts through the intercession of the holy Virgin and Martyr Marina, that human desires be fed more by your charity rather than worldly rewards. In all that Christ loved his church, we cry out from the depths of our being, with trembling mind and body, we say it from the earth.

text: Miserere nostri fili David ne decidamus in via nec laboris subruamur pressura nec sine fructu perveniamus ad patriam ut parsimoniae nostrae propitiatus ex victimis exaudias vocem nostrae confessionis cum ad te proclamaverimus e terris;
translation_en: Have mercy on our son David, that we may not stumble in the way, nor be overwhelmed by labor under pressure. May we not reach our homeland without fruit. Through the favor of our parsimony, hear the voice of our confession as we have cried out to you from the earth.

text: Munda Domine a cuncta piaculorum colluvione cor meum et ab omni noxiae contagione purifica ut fulgida mentis acie te oraturus assistens sincerissimae dilectionis affectu cum omnibus filiis tuis tibi merear proclamare a terris;
translation_en: Purify, Lord, my heart from every stain of sin and cleanse it from all contagion of wickedness, so that with the purest affection of my most sincere love, I may approach you with a radiant mind while assisting all your sons on earth, to merit proclaiming you.

text: Munda nos Domine muneribus sacris et salutem nobis conferat ista participatio sanctitatis. His armis dominicis muniamur et salubribus defensaculis circumdemur. Purifica corda et labia nostra ut mundi corde et corpore mereamur tibi dicere;
translation_en: Purify us, Lord, with sacred rites and may this participation confer salvation upon us. Let us be armed with the Lord's weapons and encompassed by wholesome defenses. Purify our hearts and lips so that we may deserve to say to you with a clean heart and body.

text: Nate patris ingeniti Christe qui ab arce sedis aethereae telluris infima petens inter alma sacrae monita iussionis quibus nostri sensus obtusionem exacuis precem etiam qua 1 delictorum veniam impetremus ostendis; respice placatus orata quae docuisti; vota suscipe quae mandasti; corda sanctifica quae creasti.  Et quia nemo mortalium in hac flebili peregrinatione sic durat ut cottidie non delinquat ita miseris nobis per suffragia patroni praesentis et pietatis tuae praesta gratiam favoris ut ad te semper exaudiamur e caelis quo praecipiente iugiter proclamemus e terris;
translation_en:
Born of the Father before all ages, Christ, who from the height of your heavenly throne sought even the lowest parts of the earth according to the sacred commands with which you sharpen our dulled senses and grant us the prayer for pardon of our sins; have mercy on us as we pray and plead what you have taught us. Receive our vows, fulfill our requests, sanctify the hearts that you have created.
And since no one among mortals endures in this weeping pilgrimage without daily sinning, grant us through the intercession of your present patron and the favor of your mercy, so that we may be heard always from heaven where we constantly proclaim you on earth.

text: Non agnoscentes Domine meritum sed praeceptum quia iubere dignatus es audemus dicere;
translation_en: Lord, we do not acknowledge merit but commandment, because you have deemed it fit for us to dare to say.

text: Non nostro merito omnipotens Deus sed Iesu Christi Filii tui oboedientes praecepto audemus dicere;
translation_en: We, not by our own merit but by obeying the command of Almighty God through Jesus Christ His Son, dare to say;

text: Non nostro praesumentes Domine merito sed Domini nostri Iesu Christi Filii tui quem ut nos a tenebris et umbra mortis liberaret misisti oboedientes imperio indigni quidem sumus nomine filiorum sed iubemur dicere;
translation_en: Lord, we do not presume to come to you in our own merit, but by the merits of our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, whom you sent to free us from the darkness and shadow of death. Although we are unworthy, we are commanded to say;

text: Non nostro praesumentes pater sancte merito sed Domini nostri Iesu Christi Filii tui oboedientes imperio audemus dicere;
translation_en: We do not presume to speak on our own authority, Father holy, but rather obeying the command of our Lord Jesus Christ, His Son, we dare to say;

text: Non renuas Christe Deus contritorum precem qui esurientium pascis esuriem nec miseris nobis pietatis deneges opem qui fons es misericordiae sempiternae sed refice spiritali pane quos voluisti filios esse adoptionis tuae; quibusque orandi dedisti praeceptum da orationis effectum ut tibi soli et ieiuniis corporibus et spiritu serviamus;
translation_en: Do not refuse, O Christ, God of the contrite heart, who feeds the hungry with bread, nor deny us help in our piety. You are the everlasting fount of mercy; refresh the spiritual bread to those whom you have chosen to be your adopted children. To them, whom you have given the commandment to pray, grant the effect of prayer that we may serve you alone, both in body through fasting, and in spirit.

text: Non sufficimus tibi gratias agere Domine sancte Pater omnipotens aeterne Deus pro tantis misericordiae tuae donis quibus nos vivificas sanctificas aeternitati praeparas sed et institutis unigeniti tui Iesu Christi domini ac Salvatoris nostri indulgentiam pietatis tuae cum immerito poscendi orare concedis cuius praecepta recolentes dicimus;
translation_en: We are not enough, Lord holy Father almighty eternal God, to express our gratitude for such great acts of mercy that you bestow upon us, which revive, sanctify and prepare us for eternity. Yet, through the institutions of your only-begotten Son Jesus Christ, our Lord and Savior, you grant us the indulgence of your pity, whose commandments we recall, saying:

text: Nostis dilectissimi fratres dominum Iesum incarnatum fuisse in terris pro salute humani generis; et ideo petamus ab eo ut iustificet miseros qui suos coronavit electos ut illis intercedentibus culpas nostras diluat veternosas ob quorum triumphos has libaminum offerimus hostias quo per hanc dominicam orationem et in adventu suo digni eius habeamur in oculis et martyrum suffragiis nostrorum peccatorum absolvamur a vinculis cum ea quae nos docuit proclamaverimus e terris;
translation_en: We, your most beloved brothers, know that the Lord Jesus was incarnate on earth for the salvation of the human race; and therefore we ask him to justify the miserable ones who he has crowned as elect, so that through their intercession, our ancient sins may be washed away because of whose triumphs we offer these incense-laden offerings. By this divine prayer and on his coming, may we be worthy to be in his sight, and may our sins be forgiven by the prayers of the martyrs along with what we have proclaimed from the earth.

text: O Iesu bone amabilis et admirabilis auctor suscipe sacrificium servorum tuorum et qui praestitisti Lazaro ut audiens vocem tuam surgeret e sepulcro praesta nobis ut te auditu capientes interno resurgamus per gratiam a proprio sceleris nostri profundo quo vocem piae orationis qua nos te exorare docuisti in terris sicut eam nunc coram te fiducialiter prompserimus ita quoque effectum ipsius petitionis a te percepisse nos gratulemur;
translation_en: O Jesus, sweet and admirable Author, receive the sacrifice of your servants, and as you provided that Lazarus rose from the tomb upon hearing your voice, grant us that we may internally rise up through your grace from our own depth of sin, just as we now confidently promise before you such effect of this petition. Thus, let us also thank you for receiving the fruit of this same petition from you.

text: O Verbum patris quod caro factum es ut habitares iri nobis praesta nobis ut qui te venisse iam credimus et venturum adhuc speramus ab omni peccatorum eluamur contagione cum praeceptionis tuae oraculis proclamaverimus e terris;
translation_en: O Word of the Father, who became flesh to dwell among us, grant that we may believe in him whom we already believe has come and hope he will still come. Cleanse us from all sin contagion as we have proclaimed with your precepts' oracles from the earth.

text: Omnes fratres carissimi qui conditos nos ac redemptos domini pietate gaudemus orationis dominicae memores precibus indefessis eiusdem domini misericordiam imploremus clamantes e terris;
translation_en: All dearest brothers who rejoice in us being enclosed and redeemed by the pity of the Lord, let us remember the prayers of the Lord's Sunday with unwavering petitions. Let us implore His mercy tirelessly, crying out from the earth.

text: Omnes qui redemptionis nostrae mysterium colimus iniquitatum pondera devitemus et qui abluti sumus vulnere crucis praedicemus gloriam resurgentis quo fide mundatis cordibus nostris exclamemus e terris;
translation_en: Let us all who venerate the mystery of our redemption shun the weight of sins, and those washed clean by the wound of the cross proclaim the glory of the risen one. With faith purified within us, let us exclaim from the earth.

text: Omnipotens aeterne Deus qui Filium tuum pro nostra redemptione misisti Verbo editum virginali utero procreatum ut carnem indueret et nos de peccatorum vinculis liberaret poenas crucis pertulit diversa tormenta sustinuit et nos sua passione salvavit simulque resurrectione redemit miserere igitur nostri ut orationem quam nos ipse docere dignatus est sic dicere mereamur;
translation_en: Almighty eternal God, who sent Your Son for our redemption, born of the Virgin's womb by the Word made flesh, to clothe Himself in flesh and free us from the bonds of sin through His passion, who suffered various torments on the cross and saved us with His suffering, and also redeemed us with His resurrection. Have mercy upon us, that we may deserve to say the prayer which You were pleased to teach us in such a way.

text: Omnipotens Domine qui es auctor felicitatis aeternae impetrante quaesumus sancto tuo Felice squalorem a nobis nostrae infelicitatis absterge ut apud te in aeternum cum ipso feliciter gaudeamus cuius congaudentes felicitati festa hodie sollemnia celebramus quia te praecipiente oramus;
translation_en: Almighty Lord, who art the author of eternal happiness, we humbly ask that you remove from us our infelicity through your saint, Felicity. May we rejoice with her forever in your presence, for whose felicity we celebrate today's solemn feast, as we pray to you according to your command.

text: Omnipotentem Deum fratres carissimi deprecemur ut propinquante termino saeculi sollicitiores nos efficiat memores nominis sui ut assumens hostiam quam ei in hoc fine diei offerimus severitatem a nobis futuri examinis arceat quam timemus quo fiducialiter ad eum praeconio  oris et vocis proclamemus e terris;
translation_en: We humbly beseech the Almighty God, our dearest brothers, that as the end of the age approaches, may He make us more vigilant, mindful of His name. May He protect us from the strictness of the judgement we fear, which we confidently proclaim to Him with voice and mouth. Let us call upon Him from the earth.

text: Omnipotentem sempiternum dominum deprecemur ut qui in Domini nostri Iesu Christi circumcisione tribuit totius religionis initium perfectionemque constare det nobis in eius portione censeri in quo totius salutis humanae perfectio summa consistit et orationem quam nos Dominus noster edocuit cum fiducia dicere permittat;
translation_en: We implore the Almighty everlasting Lord that He who, in the circumcision of our Lord Jesus Christ, granted the beginning and perfection of our religion, may cause us to be considered worthy in His portion where all the perfection of human salvation is summed up, and may allow us to pray the prayer which our Lord has taught us with confidence.

text: Omnis conventus dominicae plebis qui ad peragenda paschalis laetitiae sollemnia convenistis pace illa qua hodie dudum ianuis clausis intrante domino discipulorum corda firmata sunt vestrorum etiam abdita pectorum roborentur quo in peragendis paschalium sacramentorum officiis pacificati per sanguinem crucis proclamemus e terris;
translation_en: All the assembly of the people who have gathered for the celebration of the joy of Easter, may you enter with the peace that your hearts were strengthened when the Lord entered through closed doors, and even the hidden parts of your breasts may be fortified. Thus, in performing the sacraments of Easter, let us proclaim peace from the earth through the blood of the cross.

text: Omnis conventus ecclesiae qui tolerantiam et virtutem sanctorum apostolorum et martyrum Simonis et Iudae audistis mentis oculos mecum in intima ducite et quid contemptus mundi valeat pie perpendite. Ecce divitiae dantur et respuuntur; ecce vindicandi de persecutoribus licentia conceditur et contemnitur.  Et hinc est quod daemonibus imperandi facultas et finitur et obtinetur. Non alias namque diabolus vincitur quam cum mundus cum suis opibus temnitur. Respuamus igitur temporalia ut devicto diabolo praemia possimus perfrui sempiterna et orationem quam nos docuit habitator in caelis libere possimus clamare e terris;
translation_en: All assembly of the church who have heard of the tolerance and virtue of the holy apostles and martyrs Simon and Jude, lead your minds' eyes with me into the depths and ponder what the contempt of the world is worth. Behold, wealth is given and refused; behold, permission to avenge against persecutors is granted and disregarded. And thus it is that the power to command demons ends and begins. For indeed, the devil is not vanquished otherwise than when the world with its possessions is subdued. Therefore, let us reject temporal things so that we may enjoy eternal rewards after defeating the devil, and let us freely call out the prayer which the inhabitant of heaven taught us from the earth.

text: Orationem dicturi dominicam fratres carissimi nihil nostris mentibus cogitatio terrena subripiat nihilque turpe vel lubricum horrendae vanitatis occurrat sed paenitentes de praeteritis et petentes veniam de futuris cum timore et fiducia clamemus e terris;
translation_en: When about to pronounce the Lord's prayer, dear brothers, let no earthly thought steal into our minds, let nothing shameful or slippery appear from abhorrent vanity. Instead, let us humbly lament for past sins and beg forgiveness for future ones with fear and faith, crying out from the earth.

text: Orationem dominicam nemo audeat dicere nisi magisterio edocti regis perpetui. Et licet sit sermonum compendio breviata omnium tamen necessariorum petitionem concludit quam non audemus divina traditione tacere sed cum ingenti timore clamare et dicere;
translation_en: No one dares to say the Lord's prayer unless taught by the king eternal in his ministry. And although it is abbreviated as a summary of all sermons, nonetheless it concludes the necessary petition which we dare not omit speaking according to divine tradition but with great fear proclaim and say;

text: Orationem fratres dicturi dominicam propter haec votiva primum nos postulare convenit sacrificia ut divina bonitas oblatorem simul cum oblatis praeveniens in benedictione dulcedinis nos quoque sequenter exaudiat ad se proclamantes e terris;
translation_en: It is fitting for the brothers about to pronounce the Lord's Prayer for these vows, first to ask for sacrifices so that divine goodness, overtaking the offerer together with the offerings, may hear us subsequently in the blessing of sweetness, as we also call out to Him from the earth.

text: Oremus Deum dilectissimi fratres ut nos efficiat coram se exorabiles quo puras manus cum conscientiis ad eum levemus proclamantes e terris;
translation_en: Let us pray to the dearest brothers that God may make us approachable before Him, fervent in our supplication, with clean hands and clear conscience, lifting them up towards Him from the earth.

text: Os interminabile patris et lingua dulcissimi genitoris suavitas aeternitatis in hoc deposito tui vatis lacrimas ac nostra suspiria intende iam mitis.  Et quia merito supernam amisimus patriam quin imo per condicionem filii dicebamur proni appetivimus infima; nec est qui clamandi ad te vocem possit habere liberam.  Tu huc ad nos auditum tuae clementiae flecte qui dudum pro miseris es inflexus ad mortem. Nam quantum praestabis redemptis qui olim te exhibuisti peremptis?  Ob inde quia ab aevo desperationis frustratu tuo sumus ad spem reducti oraculo te habentes apud patrem advocatum in quo audiri mereamur in caelo cum ad te orationem quam docuisti clamaverimus ex humo;
translation_en:
The unmoving mouth of the Father and the sweetest tongue of the loving Genitor's sweetness of eternity, pay heed to this deposited vessel of your prophet. Now, since we have justly lost our heavenly homeland and indeed, by the condition of the Son, we were eager to seek the lowest depths; yet there is none who can freely voice a call to you.
You, heard here by your mercy, bend towards us, who in ancient times were bent low for the wretched unto death. How great is your power that you show to those redeemed, whom you once revealed to the perished?
Therefore, since we are brought back from eternal despair by your intervention, we have hope, having prophecy of you as our advocate before the Father. We deserve to be heard in heaven when we call upon you with the prayer that you have taught us, raised up from the earth.

text: Paraclite spiritus qui cum patre et filio unus in Trinitate permanes Deus nostris hodie illabere sensibus ut te postulante pro nobis cum magna fiducia proclamemus e terris;
translation_en: Comforter Spirit, who with the Father and the Son remains one in the Trinity, God, today make us aware of Your presence so that we may boldly call upon You on our behalf.

text: Pietatem Dei patris poscamus fratres carissimi ut praestet nobis indignis servis suis corpus hoc Domini nostri Iesu Christi filii sui ad remedium animae nostrae percipere et hune sacrosanctum sanguinem eius sine ullo conscientiae reatu libare quatenus requiescente in cordibus nostris suae pietatis dilectione orationem quam apostolos suos docere dignatus est dicere mereamur;
translation_en: Let us beseech the piety of God our Father, dearest brothers, that He may grant to us, unworthy servants, to perceive this body of our Lord Jesus Christ, His Son, for the remedy of our soul and to freely drink this most sacred blood of His without any guilt of conscience. May the love of His piety rest in our hearts so that we may deserve the prayer which He deigned to teach through His apostles.

text: Praeceptionis divinae memores dilectissimi fratres orationem quam Christus suos patrem docuit semper orare discipulos nos quoque e terris proclamemus ad caelos;
translation_en: Remembering the divine precepts, dearest brothers, let us declare to heaven the prayer that Christ taught His disciples to pray always from the earth.

text: Praeceptis salutaribus moniti et divina institutione formati audemus dicere;
translation_en: Having been admonished by the salutary precepts and formed by divine institution, we dare to say;

text: Praeceptorum domini memores fratres carissimi orationis dominicae verba dicturi maiestatem eius deprecemur adclines ut peccatorum nostrorum misericorditer obliviscens dono gratiae suae corpora nostra cordaque sanctificet quatenus omnium criminum labe purgati libera voce dicamus e terris;
translation_en: Remembering the precepts of our Lord, dear brothers, we humbly beseech His majesty to incline towards us, mercifully forgetting our sins, and to sanctify our bodies and hearts with the gift of His grace, so that, purified from all guilt, we may freely say on earth: "we are clean."

text: Praeceptum orationis quod Christus suis commendavit discipulis nos quoque fratres cum gemitu cordis exclamemus e terris et dicamus;
translation_en: The commandment of prayer which Christ entrusted to His disciples, let us also brothers cry out from the heart and say:

text: Praesta Domine supplicantibus nobis ut per haec piae oblationis libamina fideles animae defunctorum illorum et a tartareis vinculis absolvantur et aeternae quietis amoenitate donentur quo et sepultis refrigeria et vivis impetrantes tutelam ad te semper fiducialiter proclamemus e terris;
translation_en: Grant, O Lord, to us who are supplicating, that through these holy offerings the faithful souls of those departed may be released from the chains of Tartarus and granted eternal peace, so that both the buried and the living may continually seek protection in you. From earth we proclaim our trust in you.

text: Praesta nobis omnipotens beatissimi martyris Vincentii et Laeti testis tui assiduum patrocinium ut eorum quoque praeclarum assequi mereamur exemplum ut eo sentiamus impensissime suffragantes quo sequamur fortissime proeliantes;
translation_en: Grant us, Almighty one, the steadfast patronage of the blessed martyr Vincent and your witness Laetus, that we may also deserve to follow their distinguished example. May we feel their fervent intercession as we vigorously engage in battle.

text: Precamur nunc Domine Deus ut quemadmodum Filius tuus Dominus noster in illa gratiarum actione mortem nostram suscepturus auditus est ita nunc et nos qui ipsum et vitam eius quaerimus audiri mereamur in oratione quam nos paterno alloquio orare docuit dicens;
translation_en: Now we ask you, Lord God, that just as your Son, our Lord, was heard in that act of giving thanks when he was about to take upon himself our death, so now let us who seek him and his life be heard in the prayer which you taught us to pray by the fatherly address, saying;

text: Pretiosam in conspectu tuo Domine mortem sanctorum apostolorum annuis recursibus honorantes damus gloriam laudi tuae quia luminaria pretiosa a te vero lumine indeficiente succensa non solum dum leguntur sed dum coluntur illustrant; atque in universa terra exiit sermo oris eorum quorum intercessionibus exoratus dum suscipis devotionis officium precum quaesumus largiaris effectum. Ob hoc quippe clamamus e terris;
translation_en: We present to you, Lord, the precious death of your holy apostles whom we honor with annual returns, giving glory to your praise, for the precious lights, kindled from your true and inexhaustible light, not only when they are read but also when they are venerated, illuminate; and throughout the whole earth, the message of their mouth has gone forth, whose intercessions we ask that you grant us as we call upon them. Therefore, we beseech you to give the effect of our devotion's office of prayers. For this reason, we cry out from the earth.

text: Quis loquetur potentias tuas Domine aut quis enarrare poterit omnes laudes tuas? Ad humana descendisti caelestia non relinquens; ad superna regressus <es> humana non deserens. Ubique totus ubique mirabilis. Non interceptus carne ut non esses in patre; non ereptus adscensione ut non esses in homine.  Respice ad orationem plebis tuae sancte Domine misericors Deus ut in hac die sacrae adscensionis tuae sicut data est tibi gloria in excelsis ita nobis gratia praestetur in terris qui nos orare docuisti et dicere;
translation_en: Who shall speak of your power, Lord, or who shall recount all your praises? You have descended to the human from the heavenly and did not abandon; returning to the supernal you did not forsake the human. Wondrous everywhere and everywhere. Not enclosed in flesh so as not to be in the Father; not seized by exaltation so as not to be in man. Look upon the prayer of your holy people, Lord merciful God, that on this day of your sacred ascension, just as glory was given to you in the heavens, so grace may be bestowed on us on earth, whom you have taught to pray and say:

text: Quod via ut sequeremur ostendit; quod vita ut loqueremur edocuit; quod veritas ut teneremur instituit; tibi summe pater cum tremore cordis proclamemus e terris;
translation_en: Who showed us the way to follow; who taught us how to speak in life; who established us in truth, we declare with trembling heart to you, highest Father, from the earth.

text: Recensito dilectissimi fratres symbolo nostrae credulitatis Eulaliae virginis intueamur robur fidei vel aetatis quae inter flammas iam in consummatione suppliciorum unum et verum Deum in Trinitate praedicat adorandum.  Et ideo accedamus ad eum cum lacrimis ad quem illa accessit cum consummato supplicio passionis conquerentes apud eum de infirmitate nostra qui eius roboravit infantiam; petentes ab en quod praecepit ut ipse tribuat quod promisit; invocantes eum ea pietate intentionis parcendum misero riae nostrae qua miseratione nos docuit orare semper et dicere;
translation_en:
Let us review, my dearest brothers, the symbol of our faith in Eulalia the virgin. Let us consider the strength of her faith or age which she proclaimed as one and true God in Trinity to be adored, even in the midst of consuming tortures.
And therefore, let us approach him with tears, to whom she approached with her suffering completed; appealing to him for our weakness, from whom he strengthened her childhood; requesting from him what he commanded that he himself may grant what he promised; invoking him with such compassionate intention to have mercy on our miserable plight which he taught us to pray for always and to say;

text: Redemisti primitus Domine quos occisi redemptoris sanguis innocens comparavit. Nunc propitius visita quos anniversaria resurrectionis eius sollemnitas congregavit.  Repleamur universi benedictione dulcedinis liberati de molestia sempiternae formidinis ut cum Christo resurgentes a peccatis omnibus eruamur et futurae vitae gaudia consequamur quia <te iubente dicimus>?
translation_en: First, O Lord, you have redeemed those whom your Redeemer's innocent blood had earlier made worthy of redemption. Now, propitious Lord, visit those who have been gathered together on the anniversary of his resurrection. Fill us all with the blessings of sweet liberation from eternal fear, so that, rising with Christ, we may be freed from all sins and attain the joys of future life, for we say it as you command us.

text: Redemptor noster et conditor cuius in sepulcro caro non vidit corruptionem sed glorificata surrexit Dei patris roborata virtute tu omnia corruptionum carnalium in nobis vulnera propitiatus interime et gloriosae castitatis cingulo nos adstringe quo devictis vitiorum carnalium incentivis ea quae nos docuisti exclamemus e terris;
translation_en: Our Redeemer and Creator, whose flesh did not see corruption in the tomb but was glorified by rising with the power of God the Father, strengthen us with all the wounds inflicted by carnal corruptions, and bind us with the girdle of glorious chastity so that, vanquishing the incentives of carnal vices, we may exclaim what you have taught us from the earth.

text: Redemptor noster fortissime Deus qui inspicis contritionis nostrae affectum probabile tibi effice hoc ieiunium nostrum ut qui te patrem habere dignoscimur paternitatis affectu a te exaudiri promereamur;
translation_en: Our Redeemer most mightily God, who observes the probable effect of our contrition, we ask that you make this our fast acceptable to you. May we, worthy to call you Father, promise to be heard through the affection of paternity from you.

text: Respice Domine tuorum fidelium multitudinem quam per adoptionis gratiam filio tuo facere dignatus es coheredem. Erue cunctos de faucibus vorantis gehennae pro quibus idem redemptor clementissimus tribus diebus latuit in inferioribus terrae. Tolle a nobis mortis durae perniciem et beatae resurrectionis quam in fine speramus redde mercedem quia te iubente <dicimus>?
translation_en: Look upon, O Lord, the multitude of your faithful ones whom you have been pleased to make co-heirs with your Son through the grace of adoption. Save all from the jaws of ravening hell, for whom the same most merciful Redeemer lay hidden for three days in the depths of the earth. Deliver us from the harsh death we dread and grant us the blessed resurrection which we hope for at the end; because you command it, do we say so?

text: Rutilat ecce dies Christe Domine Iesu redemptor bone mundi mirabilis in quo beatissimus Thomas apostolus tuus gemina laureatus corona feliciter meruit scandere regna; qui et verbo praedicationis suae mundo claruit et per effusionem sanguinis gladio percussus martyrium consummavit. . Per eum nobis subvenias miseris per quem lumen fidelitatis et credulitatis infundere dignatus es infidelium catervis. Eoque inter ( ... cetera desiderantur ... )
translation_en: Behold, the day shines, Christ Lord Jesus, Redeemer of the good world, marvelous in which your apostle, most blessed Thomas, doubly laurelled, ascended happily to the kingdoms; who also enlightened the world with his word of preaching and completed martyrdom through the pouring out of blood by a sword. Through him you help us wretches, through whom you were deemed worthy to infuse the light of faith and credulity among the unbelievers' ranks. (... other parts are missing ...)

text: Salutare orandi praeceptum tuos magister bene docuisti discipulos quorum principatum te iubente indeptus est Petrus; ut reiecto orationis multiloquio tuum deitatis natura et nostrum adoptionis gratia patrem audeamus invocare et dicere;
translation_en: You, master, have skillfully taught your commandments to your disciples, among whom the principality was indebted to you and granted by your command to Peter. Therefore, casting aside the multitude of words in our prayer, may we dare to invoke and say your divinity, whose nature is Father, through the grace of our adoption.

text: Sanctorum tuorum Domine exoratus suffragiis absolve miseros a delictis. Da ut habeant obsequendi praemium qui devotionis impendunt tuis martyribus famulatum ut per eos qui tibi suo in certamine placuerunt et orandi tribuas votum et orationis commodes clementer effectum cum ad te ea quae filio tuo docente didicimus patulo in terris oris officio proclamaverimus;
translation_en: Lord, with the intercession of your saints, we humbly ask that you forgive the miserable from their sins. Grant a reward for obedience to those who have served your martyrs in devotion, so through them whom you found pleasing in their contest and granted their petition, may the prayer and ease of our request be graciously accomplished as we publicly proclaim with open mouth on earth what we have learned from your Son.

text: Satia nos Deus cibo iustitiae aeternitatis amore qui Theophilum martyrem tuum ad te converti fecisti ex adspectu delectabilis pomi quo sicut menti eius in tribus malis totidemque rosis sacramentum insinuans Trinitatis ad culmen eum perfectae fecisti pertingere passionis supplicio eum glorificans crucis sic nos odore caritatis tuae reficiens et actu fac tibi esse placabiles et corpore fortiores ut utraque virtute valentes post te in odorem unguentorum tuorum curramus et paternis affectibus imploratum te erga nos placabilem semper sentiamus cum ad te proclamaverimus e terris;
translation_en: Fill us, God, with the food of eternal justice, a love that you turned Theophilus your martyr towards you, from the delightful sight of a fruit, as you guided his mind in three evils and as many roses of the sacrament of the Trinity to its culmination. You made him reach the peak of perfection through the suffering of passion, glorifying him on the cross. Refresh us with the fragrance of your love, make us pleasing to you and stronger in body, so that with both virtues we may run towards you like incense from your ointments, always feeling a pleasing Fatherly disposition towards us, which we proclaim to you from the earth.

text: Satia nos Domine misericordia tua et ciba nos pane lacrimarum in hac ieiunii nostri aerumna ut attritum per abstinentiam corpus tibi deserviat tibique praeceptionis tuae orationem anima cum lacrimis offerat et sic a te effectum capiat petitionis sicut te patulo officio invocat oris;
translation_en: Satiate us, O Lord, with your mercy and feed us with the bread of our tears in this our affliction of fasting, that a humbled body may serve you through abstinence. May the soul offer to you a prayer with tears, and thus may it receive an answer to its petition as it invokes you with an open mouth.

text: Satis dulcis est Domine sollemnitas ieiuniorum qua vivi homines perducantur ad caelum. Dona ergo nobis Christe Deus semper illa sectari per quae a te mereamur facillime audiri;
translation_en: Lord, the solemnity of the fasting ones is most sweet to us, by which living men are led to heaven. Therefore, give us, O Christ God, always to seek after those things through which we may easily be heard by you.

text: Scimus Domine quod nullus apud te innocens est quia saepe insidia inimici oves condicionis tuae persequitur. Sed quia humana fragilitas quae frequenter dilabitur in culpa ex suo merito non potest diaboli vitare muscipula nisi eam tua pietas eripuerit sancta petimus ergo omnipotentiam tuam ut protegas nos miseros gratia tua et maerore anxios vel in angustia positos liberet nos citius dextera tua ut libera voce et mente tibi mereamur dicere;
translation_en: We know, Lord, that no one is innocent before you, for often the snares of the enemy pursue the sheep of your condition. But since human frailty, which frequently collapses into guilt due to its own merit, cannot avoid the snare except by the holy mercy of your piety that we ask for. Therefore, we implore your omnipotence to protect us, wretched ones, with your grace and release us more quickly from anxiety or distress placed upon us. May your right hand free us, so that we may deserve to speak freely and sincerely before you.

text: Septeno nos Domine dono perlustra spiritus qui septem Macchabaeis fratribus pro tua lege certantibus et tolerantiam dedisti ut vincerent et coronam effuso illis tribuisti pro sanguine.  Sicque nobis Felicis tui felicitate laetantibus tribuas quod rogaris ut iustificationem per id nostris impertias votis per quod te iubente ad te proclamaverimus e terris;
translation_en: Lord, we beseech you to illumine us by the Holy Spirit, as you did for the seven Maccabees brothers who fought for your law and showed endurance, that they might win and you bestowed a crown upon them in return for their blood. May you grant us, rejoicing in your happiness, what we ask for through our prayers, by which we have proclaimed you just before all people.

text: Si facta omnium adspicias Domine nemo est qui te digne patrem appellet; si conscientias discutias nemo est qui reus non sit; si verba metiris nemo ad loquendum ante te idoneus invenietur.  Sed quia non suffragantur nobis verba facta vel merita solam tenemus obsidem vocem Domini nostri Iesu Christi qui nos exorando sic docuit orare et dicere;
translation_en: If you observe all that is done, Lord, there is no one who calls you worthy Father; if you weigh consciences, no one will be found innocent; if you measure words, no one suitable for speech will be found. Yet, since we cannot rely on our own words or deeds alone, we hold fast to the voice of our Lord Jesus Christ, who taught us to pray in this way:

text: Sit iugis ad Deum fratres carissimi nostrae humilitatis intentio et pro cottidianis peccatis indefessa precatio ut corde creduli et devotione strenui fidenter clamemus e terris;
translation_en: May our dearest brothers' intention be steadfast to God on the yoke, and an unwavering prayer for daily sins. With hearts full of faith and devotion, we cry out confidently from the earth.

text: Si nostis fratres carissimi Deum sibi decimas rerum velle offerri noveritis etiam hos dies de diebus vitae nostrae de expleto scilicet anno decimarum loco nos debere Deo persolvere.  Ideoque praeteritorum veniam implorantes simus orationi et ieiunio unanimiter insistentes atque orationis dominicae memores cordis simul et oris officio clamemus e terris;
translation_en: If you know that your dear brothers wish to offer the title of goods to God, you will also understand that on these days of our life, we should complete the place for paying the tithe of ten years. Therefore, having implored forgiveness for past sins, let us be united in prayer and fasting, and at the same time let us call upon God with the service of both heart and mouth from the earth.

text: Simus ad Deum fratres carissimi pro salute nostra solliciti qui de meritorum nostrorum non sumus felicitate securi. Et quia omnibus opus est indulgentiam redemptoris ad sperandam eius misericordiam omnes unanimitate clamemus e terris;
translation_en: Let us be brothers, dearest friends, mindful of our salvation who are not securely happy with the merits of our own. And because it is necessary for all to seek the indulgence of the Redeemer for the hope of his mercy, let us all cry out in unity from the earth.

text: Sit Christe Deus Iacobus apostolus tuus apud te emundator facinoris nostri qui carne frater exstitit tibi. Sit pro nostris advocatus piaculis qui tibi fuit adfinis. Sitque nobis patronus qui tuus fuit ex advocatione discipulus.  Ut praecepta orandi quae in terris positus discipulis ostendisti hic tuus martyr tibi commendet prece qui ea a te propria percepit in aure quo effectum capiamus in his verbis cum ad patrem proclamaverimus e terris;
translation_en:
May Christ be our God, James the apostle be with you as a purifier of our sin, who became your brother in flesh. May he be our advocate in our pleas, who was related to you. May also we have you as our patron, who were from your disciple by invitation.
That your teachings on prayer, which you showed to the disciples placed on earth, may this your martyr recommend to you with prayer, who received them from you personally in that ear through which we can achieve their effect, when we proclaim these words to the Father from the earth.

text: Sit licet fratres carissimi peccatorum nostrorum plurima multitudo non tamen est de domini misericordia diffidendum si totis ad eum nisibus convertamur.  Quia ergo melius cordis humilitate et oris confessione placatur quam victimis humiliemus nos ante eum omnes et toto mentis affectu clamemus e terris;
translation_en: It is fitting that our dear brothers, though a great multitude of sinners, are not to be distrusted from the Lord's mercy if we turn ourselves entirely towards Him. For indeed He is more pleased with a humble heart and confession of the mouth than we offer Him all victims before Him; and with whole mind's affection we cry out to Him from the earth.

text: Sit nobis ad Deum dilectissimi fratres deprecandi pura devotio et confitendi omnimoda plenitudo. Vestiet enim nos ille vestimento iustitiae qui sponsam suam Agnetem induit stola claritatis aeternae. Abluat maculas sceleris nostri qui per eam ab inferis iuvenem suscitavit. Dabit effectum orationis nostrae si nos devotissime ad se prospexerit clamare et dicere;
translation_en: May we, the most dear brothers to God, have a pure devotion and the fullest confession. Let him clothe us with the garment of justice who dressed his bride Agnes with the robe of eternal clarity. May he wash away the stains of our sins who through her brought forth the youth from hell. He will grant effect to our prayers if he looks upon us devoutly and makes us say and call:

text: Summe et omnipotens Deus pater ingenite qui unigeniti tui in adsumptione carnis adventum reconciliationis nostrae voluisti esse remedium ut per eum gratiam reciperemus adoptionis qui a te ante omnia saecula sine initio ineffabiliter genitus in natura deitatis exstat aequalis et efficeremur tui per adoptionem filii qui servi esse ex nostro merito eramus indigni dignos quaesumus nos effice tantae dignitatis sollemnitate ut possimus ad te non immerito proclamare et dicere;
translation_en: Most high and almighty God, Father, who in the incarnation of your only-begotten Son desired to be our reconciliation's remedy, so that through him we might receive grace and adoption which you have begotten before all ages without beginning, ineffably. May we, who by our merit were unworthy to be your sons, become worthy through adoption, we humbly ask. Make us worthy of such great dignity, that we may be able to proclaim to you not undeservedly and say:

text: Suscipe omnipotens Deus huius preces fidelissimi conventus qui se tuis cottidie adclinis commendat conspectibus quo hunc martyrem tuum Pelagium quem prompta celebrat obsequela apud te habeat interventorem cui tu largiri dignatus es martyrii palmam.  Rescinde quaesumus dura nostrae mentis praecordia et caritatem irriga benedictionis ubertate gratuita quatenus te favente libera nostra tibi serviat vita quae malae consuetudinis more indesinenter labitur ad illicita.  Erue nos de manu insidiantis ac tuis semper serva in castris. Non nos abicias a facie tua quos consueta bonitate e terris docuisti orare et dicere;
translation_en:
Receive, Almighty God, the prayers of this most faithful congregation who daily bow themselves before your sight, that they may have your martyr Pelagius as an intercessor whom you have been pleased to grant the palm of martyrdom.
We humbly beseech you to soften our hardened hearts and irrigate them with the abundance of freely given blessings so that while you favor us, we may serve our life which keeps slipping into bad habits because of its accustomed inclination towards illicit acts.
Deliver us from the hand of the insidious one, and always keep us in your camp. Do not cast us away from your face, those whom you have taught by your customary kindness to pray and say on earth.

text: Tolle Deus gladium de manu diaboli persequentis ut pax tua abundet in sanctis. Non sinatur amplius vulnerare temptator quibus talia remedia voluit providere Salvator ut in domo pacis inter filios pacis exclamemus e terris;
translation_en: Take, O God, the sword from the hand of the devil who is pursuing [you], so that your peace may abound in the saints. Let it not be permitted any longer for the tempter to wound those whom the Savior has willed to provide with such remedies; instead, in the house of peace, let us exclaim from the earth.

text: Totis sensibus hodiernum Domine sacrificium celebramus quo nobis ipsius sacrificii sunt nata primordia per eundem Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum cuius orantes verba recitamus dicentes;
translation_en: Today, Lord, we celebrate the entirety of the sacrifice offered to You, from which the beginnings of self-sacrifice were born in us through our same Lord Jesus Christ, whom we now pray, repeating the words we say:

text: Tribue nobis Domine veritatis apprehendere viam et dimicandi tenere audaciam ut qui sanctorum illorum festa excolimus per sanctos tuos te interpellare valeamus quo per eos te nobis parcendo ostendas per quos nobis affectum te rogandi insinuas ut effectum largiaris e caelis cum ad te cum gemitu proclamaverimus e terris;
translation_en: Grant us, Lord, the power to comprehend truth and to hold boldness in combat, so that we may celebrate their festivals through your saints. May we be able to call upon you, through them, as they show us your mercy by interceding for us. Through them, may we understand our desire to pray to you, so that you may grant us blessings from heaven, which we have cried out to you with a groan from the earth.

text: Unigenite Dei Filius qui nos non carne sed corde cupiens circumcidi omne praeceptum circumcisionis in suscepto homine adimplesti tu a cordibus nostris omne quod tibi non militat gladio verbi tui desecando abscide et virtutibus spiritalium actionum nos clementer accinge quibus potentialiter roborati ad te proclamare possimus ea quae nobis petenda instituisti ut dicamus;
translation_en: The Only-begotten Son of God, who desired to circumcise us not by flesh but by heart, has fulfilled all the precepts of circumcision in the man assumed. You, from our hearts, remove everything that does not fight for your word with the sword of your truth, sever and cut off. By spiritual actions gently arm us, by which we are potentially strengthened, to be able to proclaim those things that you have instituted for us, so that we may say:

text: Vere haec est praeclara illa et admirabilis super aurum et creaturarum aeterna laudatio quae et magnis magna largitur et parvis interiora conceditur; illos premento divinae gratiae divites retes nos pro miseratione tua inopes non relinquens; illis quoque ut regnum obtineant attribuis nobis ut salvemur; universa indulgere nos praecipis ut cum timore tuo dicamus;
translation_en: Verily, this is the glorious and wonderful praise above gold and eternal creation's laudation, which not only gives much to the great but also grants the interior to the small; these I press with divine grace as wealthy nets, we who are poor, you do not abandon for your mercy; likewise, you grant them a kingdom, so that we may be saved; you command all to forgive us, that we might say it with fear.

text: Vide vide Deus quibus gravati delictis obruimur qualiterque nobis ipsi cottidie efficimur et causa veneni et poena supplicii dum et cottidiano carnis nostrae veneno polluimur et de reparatione melioris vitae nullo modo cogitamus. Sed quia certum est quod hoc videas qui semper es clemens et ideo per confessionem nos ad te reddituros exspectas adeo suggerimus ut apostolo tuo Ioanne intercedente qui invocato nomine tuo letale ebibens virus non solum ipse evasit sed etiam alios eodem exstinctos poculo suscitavit procul a nobis efficias et incentivam carnis nostrae libidinem et virus persuasionis antiquae ut fide te colentes sicut Ioannem apostolum tuum non nocuit oblatum venenum ita nos non noceat latentium vitiorum virus occultum proclamantes atque ita dicentes;
translation_en: Behold, behold, God, with what sins we are overwhelmed, and in what ways we make ourselves worse day by day. We are poisoned daily by the venom of our flesh and do not consider any way of repair for a better life. But since it is certain that you see us who are always merciful, we suggest that through confession you await us coming back to you with your apostle John interceding. May he, called upon by your name, drink the lethal virus, not only escaping himself but also raising others from the same deadly cup. Keep us far away from this, and dull the desire of our flesh and the old persuasion's virus, so that as those who faithfully follow your apostle John, the poison offered does not harm us, but rather the hidden sins are proclaimed.

text: Videte videte dilectissimi fratres mirabilia operum dei qualiter Eugenia virgo pro nomine Iesu martyrium sustinens nec undis subicitur nec ardoribus concrematur.  Haec sane fides agebat pro qua Dominus noster praedixit quod in ea se rogantibus nihil difficile est. Unde hac fide quae per dilectionem operatur rogemus pii patris clementiam ut nostras respiciat lacrimas diluat culpas impertiat gratiam et arceat quaeque nobis videntur esse adversa.  Si enim rogaverimus eam fiducialiter spes nobis est quod exaudiat nostri clamoris vocem cum ad eum ea quae domino Iesu Christo edocente didicimus proclamaverimus e terris;
translation_en: Behold, behold, dearest brothers, the wonders of God's works, how Eugenia, the virgin, sustained martyrdom for the name of Jesus and was not submerged by the waves nor consumed by the fires. This indeed is faith for which our Lord promised that if we ask in it, nothing will be difficult. Therefore, with this faith that operates through love, let us implore the mercy of the loving Father to look upon our tears, to forgive our sins, grant grace and shield us from whatever seems adversarial to us. For if we have asked for it confidently, hope is ours that He will hear our cry, when we proclaim on earth what He taught us concerning Jesus Christ.

text: Venerabilibus informati praeceptis incitati munere pietatis qui Mariae flentis lacrimas non spernis Lazaro dignanter cognomentum fratris imponis ecclesiae suboles appellas ore gratiae coheredes tibi supplices clamamus et dicimus;
translation_en: Having been encouraged by the worthy commands, moved by the duty of piety, you who do not disdain the tears of Mary, Lazarus, you give a worthy name as brother to the church's seedlings. We, who are your supplicants, call out with the mouth of grace, and we say:

text: Venisse te Domine pro nostra in terris salute credimus; venturum quoque te ad iudicium sustinemus. Et ideo cum fiducia quae docuisti proclamamus;
translation_en: We believe that you, Lord, have come to our world for salvation on earth; we shall also sustain your coming for judgment. And therefore, with the faith you taught us, we proclaim

text: Via quae nos duxit ad te; veritas quae nos confirmavit in te; vita quae nos vivificavit in te sacro ore constituit quid petamus a te piissime;
translation_en: The way which led us to you; the truth which confirmed us in you; the life which made us live in you, establishes with sacred mouth what we are asking from you, most merciful one.

text: Vivi panis alimenta et sacri sanguinis dona sumpturi dominica prece mentes et corda firmemus. Agnoscat altissimus filii sui vocem et verba Christi ad aures paternas concordis populi clamor attollat et dicat;
translation_en: We live by the bread which you give, and we receive the gift of sacred blood. Through the prayer of the Lord's day, we strengthen minds and hearts. May the Most High hear the voice of his Son, and may the words of Christ rise to the Father's ears in unison with the cry of the devout people, and say:

text: Voto alacres et fide ferventes fratres carissimi accedamus ad domini mensam et quibus possumus studiis spiritalibus celebremus apostoli sui illustrissimum festum. Semotis paululum saecularibus curis caelestibus dilatemur in gaudiis et domino nostro vota reddamus cum lacrimis et orationibus sanctis.  Aderit profecto clemens rogantibus qui beato apostolo Bartholomaeo concessit imperare daemonibus. Suscipiet contritionem humilium qui in passione se sequendi apostolo suo dedit exemplum. Nec irrita licet indigne ministrantium sacerdotum efficiet munera qui apostoli sui obsequia se habere ostendit miraculis gratiosa. Dabit sumpturis dignitatem sumendi qui sancto Bartholomaeo apostolo gratiam conferre dignatus est Spiritus Sancti. Exaudiet orationem nostram e caelis qui nos orare sic docuit proclamare e terris;
translation_en: With eager vows and fervent faith, dearest brothers, we approach the Lord's table, and as much as possible, we celebrate the most illustrious feast of the apostle. Letting go for a moment our worldly cares, let us dilate ourselves in joys and let us offer to our Lord vows with tears and holy prayers. Indeed, the merciful one who granted the blessed apostle Bartholomeo to command demons will be present. He will receive the contrition of the humble ones who gave an example by following their apostle in his passion. The ministry of the unworthy priests shall not remain fruitless, who showed obedience to their apostle with gracious miracles. To those who are worthy, the Holy Spirit has granted to bestow dignity on taking sumptuous gifts, who considered it fitting to confer grace to Saint Bartholomew, the apostle. He who taught us to pray from heaven will hear our prayer from earth.

text: Ab omni malo nos eripe omnipotens Deus et praesta ut iubar<e> apostolici luminis circumdati omne aevum criminis cum pompis saeculi respuamus.
translation_en: Deliver us from all evil, Almighty God, and grant that we, enveloped by the yoke of the apostolic light, may reject throughout every age crimes with the paraphernalia of this world.

text: Adesto Domine fidelibus tuis et quos caelestibus instituis sacramentis a terrenis conserva periculis.
translation_en: Be present, Lord, to your faithful ones and those whom you institute with heavenly sacraments, and preserve them from earthly dangers.

text: Domine Deus omnipotens libera nos a malo et in tempore accepto salva nos ut sicut in condemnatione Filii tui perfidorum piaculum salus omnium fuit sic per misericordiam tuam communis sit cultus iste credentium.
translation_en: Lord God Almighty, free us from evil and, at an acceptable time, save us. So that, just as the forgiveness of sin was salvation for all in the condemnation of Your treacherous Son, may this act of worship be common through Your mercy to those who believe.

text: Exerce liberator in nobis iuris proprii facultatem qui Lazaro virtutem Mariae pietatem Marthae laborem remuneras; favorem plebis excitas et patris voce concina gloriaris.
translation_en: Exercise in us the power of your own righteousness, who rewards Lazarus' virtue with Mary's devotion, Martha's labor; you stir up the favor of the people and sing the glory of the father with a fatherly voice.

text: Libera Domine libera nos ab omni malo et a fortissimis adversariis diabolo et morte ea quae cunctis fortior est virtutis et dexterae tuae proiectione defende.
translation_en: Lord, free us from every evil and from our greatest adversaries - the devil and death, which is stronger than all, protect us with your power and right hand's projection.

text: Libera Domine libera nos ab omni malo et constitue nos in omni opere bono.
translation_en: Lord, free us from all evil and establish us in every good work.

text: Libera nos a malis auctor bonorum omnium Deus libera nos ab omni temptatione ab omni scandalo ab omni haeresi ab omni opere tenebrarum et constitue nos in omni opere bono et da pacem in diebus nostris auctor pacis et veritatis.
translation_en: Deliver us from evils, O God, who is the author of all goodness; deliver us from every temptation, from every scandal, from every heresy, from every work of darkness and establish us in every good work. Grant us peace in our days, O author of peace and truth.

text: Libera nos a malis omnibus auctor bonorum Deus ab omni temptatione ab omni scandalo ab omni opere tenebrarum et constitue nos in omni bono et da pacem in diebus nostris auctor pacis et caritatis.
translation_en: Deliver us from all evils, O God, the author of good, from every temptation, from every scandal, from every work of darkness and establish us in all that is good and grant us peace in our days, O author of peace and charity.

text: Libera nos a malis omnibus misericors Deus et praesta ut haec sacrificia tibi offerentes beatorum martyrum et confessurum tuorum illorum auxiliis adiuvemur et exempla eorum imitari valeamus.
translation_en: Deliver us from all evil, merciful God, and grant that as we offer these sacrifices to you in honor of your blessed martyrs and confessors, we may be aided by their assistance and have the ability to imitate their examples.

text: Libera nos a malis praesentibus et futuris omnipotens Deus libera nos a periculis ab infirmitatibus ab scandalis et praepara nos ad omne bonum.
translation_en: Deliver us from present evils and future ones, Almighty God, deliver us from dangers, from weaknesses, from snares and prepare us for every good.

text: Libera nos a malis praesentibus et futuris propitiusque concede ut quae nobis poscimus relaxari ipsi quoque proximis remittamus.
translation_en: Deliver us from the present evils and grant us your favor, that what we ask for may also be forgiven to those who are near to us.

text: Libera nos a malo Domine Christe Iesu. Corpus (sanctum) tuum pro nobis crucifixum edimus et sanguinem sanctum tuum pro nobis effusum bibimus. Fiat nobis corpus sanctum tuum in salutem et sanguis sanctus tuus in remissionem peccatorum.
translation_en: Deliver us from evil, Lord Christ Jesus. We eat your holy body crucified for us and drink your holy blood shed for us. May your holy body be our salvation and your holy blood the forgiveness of sins.

text: Libera nos a malo nostra libertas quia tibi soli licet augere merita et dimittere peccata. Evacua nos vitiis et reple nos virtutibus ut <oblatio> sanctificata atque aucta sanctificet corda dum creditur deleat peccata dum sumitur ut hic et in aeternum salvi esse mereamur.
translation_en: Deliver us from our evil, for to you alone it is right to increase merits and forgive sins. Free us from vices and fill us with virtues, so that the sanctified offering may be increased and further sanctify hearts while it is believed that sins are deleted, when it is taken so that here and forever we may be worthy of eternal salvation.

text: Libera nos a malo omnipotens Deus et dominare tu nostri qui mortis a nobis dominia repulisti ut tua semper Domine cogitemus cum alacritate mandata cum timore iudicia cum exsultatione promissa.
translation_en: Deliver us from evil, almighty God, and drive away the rule of death over us, which you have repelled from us, Lord, that we may always remember your commands with joy, the judgments with fear, and the promises with exultation.

text: Libera nos a malo omnipotens Deus et custodi in bono. Evacua nos vitiis et reple virtutibus et bona nobis tam praesentia quam aeterna concede.
translation_en: Deliver us from evil, Almighty God, and keep us safe in good. Cleanse us from sinfulness and fill us with virtues, and grant us both temporal and eternal blessings.

text: Libera nos a malo omnipotens Deus et praesta ut incisa mole facinorum sola in no(bi)s proficiant incrementa virtutum.
translation_en: Deliver us from evil, almighty God, and grant that the impression of our deeds may bring about growth only in good works within us.

text: Libera nos a malo omnipotens Deus et tribue nobis supplicibus tuis tam promptum pro Christo tuo ad patiendum animum ut probemur non nos martyrio sed nobis defuisse martyrium.
translation_en: Deliver us from evil, almighty God, and grant to us, your suppliant ones, a quick mind for Christ's sake, so that we may be proven not by our martyrdom but by our lack of it.

text: Libera nos ab omni malo ab omni delicto auctor omnium bonorum et conditor Deus et intercedente beata Maria genitrice tua contra cottidiani hostis insidias cottidiana nos protectione defende.
translation_en: Deliver us from all evil, from every sin, author of all good and Creator God, and with the intercession of your blessed Mother Mary, protect us daily against the daily plots of our enemies, defend us daily.

text: Libera nos ab omni malo omnipotens Deus et quia tibi soli est praestandi potestas tribue ut sollemne hoc sacrificium sanctificet corda nostra dum creditur deleat peccata dum sumitur.
translation_en: Deliver us from all evil, omnipotent God, and since it is only to you that power should be given, grant that this solemn sacrifice may sanctify our hearts as sins are believed to be erased when it is received.

text: Libera nos ab omni malo propitiusque concede ut quae nobis poscimus relaxari ipsi quoque proximis remittamus.
translation_en: Deliver us from every evil, and graciously grant that what we ask for ourselves be also forgiven to those who are near to us.

text: Libera nos aeterna pietas et vera libertas neque sinas ab inimico capi qui a te cupiunt possideri.
translation_en: Free us, eternal kindness and true freedom, do not allow us to be captured by the enemy who desire to possess us from you.

text: Libera nos Domine ab omni malo et custodi nos iri omni bono Iesu Christe auctor omnium bonorum.
translation_en: Deliver us, Lord, from all evil and protect us in every good thing, Jesus Christ, author of all goods.

text: Libera nos Domine ab omni malo praeterito praesenti et futuro et intercedentibus pro nobis beatis apostolis tuis Petro et Paulo da propitius pacem in diebus nostris ut ope misericordiae tuae adiuti et a peccato simus semper liberi et ab omni perturbatione securi.
translation_en: Deliver us, Lord, from all evil past, present and future, and through your blessed apostles Peter and Paul, grant us Your mercy so that we may always be free from sin and secure from any disturbance in these our days.

text: Libera nos omnipotens Deus a malis et constitue nos in bonis; evacua nos a vitiis et reple virtutibus tuis.
translation_en: Deliver us, almighty God, from evils and establish us in goods; drive out sins from us and fill us with your virtues.

text: Libera nos omnipotens Deus ab omni malo ab omni periculo et custodi nos in omni opere bono perfecta veritas et vera libertas.
translation_en: Deliver us, Almighty God, from every evil and every danger, and keep us in every good work completed by the perfect truth and true freedom.

text: Libera nos omnipotens Deus ab omnibus malis et praesta ut natus hac nocte Salvator mundi sicut divinae nobis generationis est auctor ita et immortalitatis sit ipse largitor.
translation_en: Deliver us, almighty God, from all evils and grant that the Savior of the world, born this night, may also be the author of our divine birth, and may himself be the giver of immortality.

text: Libera nos quaesumus Domine ab omnibus malis praeteritis praesentibus et futuris (et) intercedente beata et gloriosa semper(que) virgine Dei Genitrice Maria et beatis apostolis tuis Petro et Paulo atque Andrea da propitius pacem in diebus nostris ut ope misericordiae tuae adiuti et a peccato simus semper liberi et ab omni perturbatione securi. Per Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum Filium tuum qui tecum vivit et regnat Deus in unitate Spiritus Sancti per omnia saecula saeculorum. Amen.
translation_en: Deliver us, we beseech You, Lord, from all past, present, and future evils (and) with the intercession of the blessed and glorious ever-virgin Mother of God, Mary, the holy apostles Peter, Paul, and Andrew, may You be propitious, granting peace in our days. May we, helped by Your mercy, always be free from sin, and secure from every disturbance. Through Our Lord Jesus Christ Your Son who lives and reigns with You in the unity of the Holy Spirit forever and ever. Amen.

text: Libera nos quaesumus Domine ab omnibus malis praeteritis praesentibus et futuris et intercedentibus sanctis tuis anima famuli tui illius pro abundantia clementiae tuae pium te sentiat in inferis quae multorum forsitan tormentorum cruciatus pro iustitiae merito sentit in poenis.
translation_en: Deliver us, we beg Thee, Lord, from all past, present, and future evils; through the intercession of Thy saints. May the soul of Thy servant feel Thy mercy abundant in the depths, which perhaps for justice's sake feels the torments of many cruelties in penalties.

text: Per Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum in quo tibi est cum quo tibi est honor laus gloria magnificentia potestas cum spiritu sancto a saeculis et nunc et semper et in omnia saecula saeculorum. Amen.
translation_en: Through our Lord Jesus Christ, in whom you have peace, honor, praise, glory, majesty, power, with the Holy Spirit, from the ages past, now and forevermore, and to the ages of ages. Amen.

text: Commixtio consecrati corporis et sanguinis Domini nostri Iesu Christi nobis edentibus et sumentibus proficiat ad vitam et gaudium sempiternum.
translation_en: The mixing of the consecrated body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ may profit us who eat and drink, for eternal life and everlasting joy.

text: Commixtio corporis et sanguinis Domini nostri Iesu Christi sit nobis salus in vitam perpetuam.
translation_en: The mixing of the body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ be to us salvation for eternal life.

text: Fiat commixtio et consecratio corporis et sanguinis Domini nostri Iesu Christi accipientibus nobis in vitam aeternam.
translation_en: Let there be a mixing and consecration of the body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, which is given to us for eternal life.

text: Fiat haec consecratio et commixtio corporis et sanguinis Domini nostri Iesu Christi omnibus accipientibus nobis salus in vitam aeternam.
translation_en: Let this consecration and mixing of the body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ be for all who receive us salvation for eternal life.

text: Fiat nobis et omnibus sumentibus quaesumus Domine commixtio et consecratio corporis et sanguinis Domini nostri Iesu Christi in remissionem omnium peccatorum tutamentum quoque mentis et corporis et ad vitam capessendam aeternam praeparatio salutaris.
translation_en: We humbly ask You, Lord, that the mixture and consecration of the body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ be granted to us and all who partake, for remission of all sins, preparation also of mind and body, and for obtaining eternal life, a salvific readiness.

text: Haec sacrosancta commixtio corporis et sanguinis Domini nostri Iesu Christi fiat (mihi et) omnibus sumentibus salus mentis et corporis et ad vitam capessendam aeternam praeparatio salutaris.
translation_en: May this most holy mixture of the body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ be (to me and) to all those partaking, preparation for salvation of mind and body, and for obtaining eternal life.

text: Praesta nobis omnipotens Deus ut haec communicatio sacri corporis et sanguinis tui non ad iudicium sed ad remedium proficiat mentis et corporis.
translation_en: Grant us, almighty God, that this communion of your sacred body and blood may not lead to judgment but to the remedy for mind and body.

text: Pacem mandasti pacem dedisti pacem dereliquisti. Pacem tuam Domine da nobis de caelo et pacificum hunc diem et ceteros dies vitae nostrae in tua pace disponas.
translation_en: You have commanded peace, you have given peace, you have left peace. Grant us your peace, Lord, from heaven; make this day peaceful and all the days of our life in your peace.

text: Domine Iesu Christe qui dixisti apostolis tuis: »Pacem relinquo vobis pacem meam do vobis« ne respicias peccata mea sed fidem Ecclesiae tuae eamque secundum voluntatem tuam pacificare et (co)adunare digneris.
translation_en: Lord Jesus Christ, who said to your apostles: "I leave you peace, my peace I give to you," do not look upon my sins but grant faith to your Church and deem it worthy to pacify and unite it according to your will.

text: Acceptare digneris quaesumus piissime Deus huius salutaris sacrificii munus oblatum et nobis famulis tuis intercedente beato confessore tuo Mauro omnium concede veniam peccatorum.
translation_en: We humbly ask you, most gracious God, that you may deign to accept this sacred offering of the sacrifice and, through the intercession of your blessed confesser Maurice, grant us, your servants, forgiveness for all our sins.

text: Beati apostoli tui Iacobi in cuius hodie festivitate corpore et sanguine tuo nos refecisti quaesumus Domine intercessione nos adiuva ut eius precibus gubernemur cuius utimur te constituente doctrina.
